## 2026-09-11 zhbridge
- Hypothesis: Zebrahub's dense GT supplies enough labelled (end, start) pairs at spans 2-3 to train the bridge selector bridgerank could not train on 6bba, and a model trained on those rows (plus the 6bba rows) still separates the 6bba pairs out of fold.
- Scope: the Zebrahub crops with an hpara cache (`ZH_HP`, 41 crops); zhpara4's solver (D187 18-column ranker, no edge head) with ILP_FLOOR raised from 0.10 to the production 0.48, disappearance 1.5, DIV_W 0.55; shipped span-1 gap close (no candidate requirement, cap 0.02). Labels at MATCH_UM 5.0 against dense GT. No metric is computed on Zebrahub, so nothing here says what the bridges are worth there.
- Experiment: `zhbridge.py` from `tools/bench/make_zhbridge.py` (zhpara4.py cut before its crop loop; the `_br_*` feature/label block copied verbatim from the generated bridgerank.py), kernel `faustine649/biohub-zhbridge` v1, CPU, zhpara4's 6 sources. Writes `bridge_pairs_zh.csv` (crop, span, label, 28 features), flushed after every crop. `make_bridgerank.py` updated (v2, SCRIPT_VERSION 2026-09-11b): if `bridge_pairs_zh.csv` is attached, both fold models train on all Zebrahub rows plus the other fold's 6bba rows; 6bba numbers stay out of fold; a Zebrahub-internal 2-fold-by-crop AUC is printed. Toy-graph test passed on both generated scripts.
- Result: v1 ran 5 crops (zhpara4's crop list was its two tripwire crops plus the three v3 never scored); v3 iterates every crop with both caches: 41 of 41 in 26.9 min, `ZHBRIDGE OK`. v2 was an unchanged re-push after a failed patch and is void. `bench_csv/zhbridge/bridge_pairs_zh.csv`: 20,944 labelled rows.

  | span | (end, start) pairs | labelled | positive |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 13,629 | 6,114 | 861 |
  | 3 | 34,509 | 14,830 | 674 |

  Against 6bba's 88 positives in 128 movies. `biohub-bridgerank` v2 pushed with `biohub-zhbridge` attached.
- Conclusion: Zebrahub's dense GT supplies 1,535 positive pairs at spans 2-3, enough to fit the selector; whether it transfers to 6bba is bridgerank v2's question.

## 2026-09-13 swapgeom
- Hypothesis: the two detections of a swap pair are stacked in z (small xy offset, 1-3 planes apart), so a suppression keyed on that geometry (unlike dupsup's spherical distance) would catch the swap pairs without the ordinary near pairs.
- Scope: offline, no kernel. The 1,643 swap pairs (a, b) of hsaddle's site table (frame t+1: true-child detection and false target), |dz| in planes and dxy in um; the population = every pair of primaries within 9.5 um in the same 128 movies from `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/` (2,242,408 primaries, 1,277,204 pairs). Boxes: |dz| 1..3 planes and dxy <= 2 / 3 / 4 um; |dz| 1..4 and dxy <= 4; |dz| 1..2 and dxy <= 3.
- Experiment: scratch pandas/cKDTree script (not kept); inputs `scratchpad/hsaddle_sites.b64`, `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/*.npz`.
- Result: swap pairs |dz| median 2.29 planes (p25 1.08, p75 3.78), dxy median 5.35 um (p75 6.86). Share of swap pairs inside the boxes: 2% (36) / 4% (70) / 8% (124) / 18% (292) / 0% (4). Population pairs inside the same boxes: 6,637 / 11,995 / 22,089 / 67,341 / 571, so the swap share of a box is 0.4-0.7% in every case.
- Conclusion: the swap pair is separated diagonally (5.4 um in xy, 3.7 um in z), not stacked in z; earlier entries' "z-stacked" wording (swapplace, edgeledger) describes the z error of detections with a near neighbour, not the pair geometry. No geometric box isolates the swap pairs: the narrow ones miss them, the wide ones hold 200 ordinary pairs per swap. Same reading as dupsup and hmerge by a third route.

## 2026-09-14 simviewnorm
- Hypothesis: unet-simview (the Ultrack network trained on the sparse-labelling platform's images, i.e. the competition's) missed 17% of annotated cells in ultrackprobe because the guessed input scale was wrong; its first BatchNorm's running statistics reveal the training input scale, and under the right scale it finds the cells at a segment count near the true nuclei count.
- Scope: unet-simview only; introspection of the torchscript parameters and buffers; 13 input normalisations (percentile windows 1-99.9 / 0-100 / 0.5-99.5 / 1-99, gamma 0.5, x2, z-score, clipped z-score, median/MAD, raw/65535, log then z-score, /max, log then percentile) on the site frames of hplace's first 3 movies (33 frames; 36 swap sites, 99 control cells; expected nuclei per frame from the GT metadata 64 / 698 / 48); single-level watershed h 0.1, area 300..25000. Measures: foreground > 0.4 coverage, segments per frame, missed share (no centroid within 7 um), placement.
- Experiment: `simviewnorm.py` (from ultrackprobe.py; site table embedded), kernel `faustine649/biohub-simviewnorm` v1, T4, 33.2 min, `SIMVIEWNORM OK`; log `bench_csv/simviewnorm/simviewnorm_v1.log`.
- Result: the torchscript exposes no buffers (named_buffers empty: the BatchNorm running statistics are folded or hidden), so the scale could not be inferred. Sweep, foreground coverage / segments per frame / missed (swap, ctrl): [0,1]-type inputs (pct 1-99.9, 0-100, 0.5-99.5, 1-99, /max) 0.03-0.04 / 113-217 / 0.47, 0.43-0.46; z-score-type inputs (z-score, clipped, median-MAD, log-z) 0.20 / 709-777 / 0.08-0.11, 0.06-0.14; raw/65535, gamma 0.5 and log-percentile give no foreground at all (missed 0.6-0.9). Placement of found cells: control 1.47-1.83 um under the [0,1] inputs, 2.19-2.49 under the z-score inputs; swap sites 2.9-3.8 everywhere.
- Conclusion: no simple input scaling makes simview both find the cells and count them right: narrow [0,1] inputs lose almost half the annotated cells, wide z-scored inputs find them but at 3-11x the nuclei count with worse placement. The training preprocessing is not any of these and the file does not carry the statistics that would reveal it. v2 settles the scale question as far as placement goes: the official competition scaling behaves like the [0,1] inputs (45% of annotated cells missed), the DeepCenter convention recovers them (3-9% missed) but inflates the foreground to 22% of the volume and ~750 segments per frame against 48-698 nuclei, and under NO scaling does simview place the swap-site cells better than our maps (2.6-3.2 um against 2.69) or the ordinary cells better than 1.66 (ours 1.27). So simview at one watershed level is not a placement source either; if the network is used at all it is as foreground/contour input to the full hierarchy + ILP, with the DeepCenter scaling. The network choice is secondary to what ultrackbench (daxi, full pipeline) shows. v2 (2026-09-14, pushed): the two lab conventions added to the same sweep on the same 33 frames: the official competition io.py scaling (whole-movie q0.001 to 0, q0.999 to 1, clamp >= 0, clip 4; also per frame, and gamma 0.5 / 2) and the DeepCenter trainer scaling (p50 to 0, p99.5 to 1, clip [-0.5, 6]; movie and frame level, and halved), with pct1_999 as the anchor row. v2 result (22.1 min, `SIMVIEWNORM OK`, `bench_csv/simviewnorm/simviewnorm_v2.log`), foreground coverage / segments per frame / missed (swap, ctrl) / placement median swap, ctrl: official movie quantiles 0.031 / 164 / 0.47, 0.45 / 3.19, 1.82 (per frame the same; gamma 0.5 kills the foreground, gamma 2 0.068 / 379 / 0.47, 0.33 / 2.98, 1.80); DeepCenter convention per frame 0.225 / 753 / 0.06, 0.09 / 2.63, 1.79 (movie-level 0.215 / 718 / 0.08, 0.11 / 2.67, 1.79; halved 0.225 / 757 / 0.03, 0.07 / 2.73, 1.66); pct1_999 0.037 / 217 / 0.47, 0.43 / 3.18, 1.83. Expected nuclei per frame for the three movies 64 / 698 / 48.

## 2026-09-15 swapsep + maskfeat
- Hypothesis: the two detections of a swap pair (two points around one annotated cell) and two real neighbouring cells differ in features beyond the heatmap saddle: (a) detection scores, temporal persistence of the pair (present at t +- 1, 2 with the same spacing), pair-spacing jitter, local density and the third neighbour's distance, computable from the local primaries; (b) the raw image's SHAPE around the pair at full resolution: whether a and b fall in one connected component at thresholds set relative to the pair's own brightness, the component's volume at several thresholds (a fringe at one threshold is not the reading at another), principal axes, the threshold at which the two separate, the intensity dip, gradient at the midpoint against the ends, the geometric half-split of the component; and a classifier stacking them fires on few enough two-cell pairs (< ~0.5% at 60% swap recall, the break-even at one swap per ~100 near pairs) to make a merge rule pay.
- Scope: hsaddle's site table (1,643 swap pairs, 511 two-cell pairs = two annotated nodes within 9.5 um each with its own primary, 1,348 random primary pairs 6-9.5 um apart), 128 6bba movies. (a) offline from `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/` and `bench_csv/hsaddle/hsaddle_sites.csv` joined on (kind, movie, frame, pair distance): 3,339 of 3,502 sites join. (b) kernel on the raw zarr frames, 20 x 20 x 20 um crops. Separability read as AUC swap vs two-cell per feature, and a 5-fold HistGB stack's false-fire rate on two-cell pairs at fixed swap recall.
- Experiment: (a) scratch script, features written to `bench_csv/hsaddle/swap_temporal_feats.csv`. (b) `maskfeat.py` (standalone, site table embedded, CPU, sources cell-tracking + competition), toy test `scratchpad/test_maskfeat.py` (one ellipsoid holding two detections vs two ellipsoids 7 um apart: one vs two components, split threshold 1.0 vs 0.3, dip 2.0 vs 0.16, half-split 0.54 vs 1.0) passed, checkgen ok; kernel `faustine649/biohub-maskfeat` v1 pushed 2026-09-15. Output `maskfeat_sites.csv` and the per-feature / stacked summary in the log.
- Result: (a) AUC swap vs two-cell, single features: saddle 0.866 (medians 0.879 vs 0.448), h_a 0.755, d_ab 0.746 (7.14 vs 8.84 um), score s_a 0.754 (0.308 vs 0.392), s_b 0.668, temporal persistence 0.636 (both 0.50), one-endpoint-only frames 0.644, pair jitter 0.601 (1.04 vs 0.70 um), density within 10 um 0.507, third neighbour distance 0.502. Stacked 5-fold: heatmap features alone AUC 0.902, temporal + score features alone 0.869, both 0.919; at threshold 0.9 the stack keeps 68% of swaps and fires on 8.2% of two-cell pairs (1.8% of random pairs); at 0.95, 63% / 6.5% / 0.9%. (b) v1 5.1 min, `MASKFEAT OK`, 3,502 sites (`bench_csv/maskfeat/maskfeat_sites.csv`, `maskfeat_v1.log`). With the 20 um crop and a p20 background the masks at fraction 0.5 span 3,000 um^3 (several nuclei; z extent = the crop), so `same_<f>` is 1 for nearly every pair below f 0.9; the readings that separate are the full-resolution intensity dip (AUC 0.772, medians 1.05 vs 0.72 -- the raw image DOES carry it at full resolution, unlike swapimg's pooled read), the split threshold f_split (0.738; 1.0 vs 0.9), the mask extent along a->b over d_ab (0.717), same_90 (0.721), the geometric half-split (0.702), volumes at 0.9 (0.65, swap 788 vs two-cell 336 um^3: the two-cell pair's core masks are the smaller ones), the fill ratio (0.654). Stacked mask features alone: AUC swap vs two-cell 0.911 (in-kernel 5-fold) / 0.916 on the 3,324 sites that join the temporal table; false-fire on two-cell pairs at 50 / 60 / 70% swap recall 1.6 / 3.7 / 6.6% (random pairs 7.3 / 12.7 / 21.0%). Joined stacks (offline): heatmap only 0.860, heatmap + temporal 0.876, mask + heatmap 0.908, all 0.915; false-fire on two-cell pairs at 50 / 60 / 70% recall: heatmap 4.3 / 8.0 / 13.6%, all 2.3 / 3.7 / 6.6% (random pairs 0.2 / 0.5 / 2.1%).
- Conclusion: (a) the two situations differ, the saddle carrying most of it and the temporal features adding a little (0.902 -> 0.919), but at one swap per ~100 near pairs an 8% false-fire rate is ~10 wrong merges per swap fixed, the reason hmerge and hypilp lost; break-even needs < 0.5% at the same recall, a 15x sharper signal than the heatmap and the detections give. hypilp's 772 one-cell vs 6 two-cell readings among its labelled parents is not evidence of merge precision: with 10% of cells annotated, 'both children match two different annotated nodes' almost never happens and 'the parent matches one annotated node' also holds for a real cell next to an unannotated one. (b) the raw image's shape adds real information: mask features alone separate swap from two-cell pairs as well as the heatmap does (0.916 vs 0.860) and halve the false-fire rate at equal recall (2.3% vs 4.3% at 50%, 3.7% vs 8.0% at 60%), so 'no feature separates them' is refuted; but at one swap per ~100 near pairs 2.3-3.7% is still ~4.5-6 wrong merges per swap fixed against a break-even near 1, so a merge rule on these features still loses. The random-pair firing rate (0.2-0.5%) is not the population rate: random primary pairs are 6-9.5 um apart and include spurious detections the classifier rejects for other reasons. v2 (3.3 min, `MASKFEAT OK`, `bench_csv/maskfeat/v2/`): 12 um crop, crop-median background, nucleus-sized masks (vol_a_50 656 vs 486 um^3): single features a little sharper (same_70 now 1 vs 0, dip 1.12 vs 0.44, tex_cv 0.700) but the stack is weaker (AUC 0.892; false-fire at 60% recall 5.5%); v1 + v2 masks together 0.917 / 3.9%, with heatmap + temporal 0.912 / 3.5% -- the larger context of v1 is what the stack uses.
  THE BASE RATE, re-measured (offline, `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/`, 128 movies, all primary pairs within 9.5 um: 1,277,204): both ends annotated 2,187, of which ONE cell (both within 5 um of the same GT node) 1,572 and two cells 615; one end annotated 56,301; neither 1,218,716. One-cell pairs sit at d 4.7 / 6.4 / 8.2 um (10/50/90%), two-cell at 6.8 / 8.7 / 9.4; within 7 um 1,029 one-cell vs 81 two-cell. Corrected for annotation sparsity (a one-cell pair needs one annotated cell, a two-cell pair two, p ~ 0.097) the population is roughly one one-cell pair per four two-cell pairs, not per hundred. hmerge's loss re-derived from these counts: at saddle >= 0.9 the rule fires on 14% of random pairs (hsaddle) = ~7,900 of the 56,301 one-end-annotated pairs, each displacing an annotated node, against 43% x 1,572 = 676 one-cell fixes; -7,900 x ~2 edges vs +1,352 reproduces hmbench's -0.0082. The stacked classifier fires on 0.2-0.5% of random pairs at 50-60% recall, 30-70x fewer, which by the same arithmetic is net positive (~+1,300 edges against ~-250). This is the reading to test, not the 1:100 ratio stated earlier today.
  Next (mergefeat, pushed 2026-09-15): the classifier over every hypcache parent (pairs at saddle >= 0.8, d <= 8.5 um) with the labels from the GT and the firing rate on the one-end-annotated and unannotated pairs measured directly.

## 2026-09-15 mergefeat
- Hypothesis: a merge classifier (raw-image mask features at maskfeat v1's crop, the pair's saddle and distance, the two scores, temporal persistence and jitter, density) trained on hypcache's parents whose two children are both annotated (one cell = the same GT node within 5 um of both; two cells = different GT nodes) separates them out of fold at AUC >= 0.9 and, at a threshold keeping >= 50% of the one-cell pairs, fires on few enough one-end-annotated pairs (the channel that sank hmerge) that a hard merge at that threshold is net positive by the edge arithmetic (< ~1 wrong merge per one-cell merge).
- Scope: the 128 6bba movies' hypcache parents with pair distance <= 8.5 um (two-cell pairs sit at 8-9.5 um; one-cell pairs 90% below 8.2), ~200k pairs; labels from the GT at 5 um: one cell / two cells / one end annotated / unannotated; two fold HistGB models by movie fold, out of fold; per threshold the one-cell recall, the firing rate on two-cell, one-end-annotated, unannotated and all pairs, and wrong-per-fix = (merges on one-end-annotated + on two-cell pairs) / merges on one-cell pairs.
- Experiment: `mergefeat.py` from `tools/bench/make_mergefeat.py` (maskfeat.py's feature block at v1's crop with thresholds 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 + the run over hypcache's caches), maskfeat's toy test passed on the extracted block, checkgen ok. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-mergefeat` v1, CPU, sources cell-tracking + biohub-hypcache + competition, pushed 2026-09-15; budget guard 10.5 h. Outputs `mergefeat_<movie>.npz` (t, parent index, p, label), `mergefeat_pairs.csv` (labelled rows), `merge_rank.pkl`.
- Result: v1 COMPLETE 141 min, 128/128, `MERGEFEAT OK`, `bench_csv/mergefeat/` (log, outputs). Parents 268,369; kept at d <= 8.5 um 233,819: one cell 1,226, two cells 74, one end annotated 9,598, unannotated 222,921. Per-feature AUC one-cell vs two-cell (1,226 vs 74): saddle 0.721, half_split_50 0.683, along_over_d 0.640, both_frames 0.640, persist 0.639, d_ab 0.621, one_only_frames 0.611, pair_jitter 0.609; every other mask / intensity feature 0.50-0.59 (same_50 0.500, vol_ratio_50 0.500). Fold models trained on 714 / 586 labelled rows at 94% one-cell; out-of-fold AUC 0.608. Firing table (thr 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98): recall on one-cell 0.997 / 0.996 / 0.994 / 0.993 / 0.989 / 0.983; fires on two-cell 1.000 / 0.986 / 0.986 / 0.973 / 0.946 / 0.932; on one-end-annotated 0.993 / 0.990 / 0.987 / 0.981 / 0.972 / 0.959; on unannotated 0.995 / 0.992 / 0.990 / 0.986 / 0.980 / 0.971; wrong per fix 7.86 / 7.84 / 7.83 / 7.79 / 7.75 / 7.70.
- Conclusion: among hypcache's parents (a heatmap saddle is the entry condition) the pairs with both ends annotated are 94% one cell: the two-cell class this classifier was to reject has 74 members in 128 movies, too few to learn from (AUC 0.61) and too few to be the loss channel. Its probability is ~1 on everything, so a threshold on it is hmerge's saddle rule again (hmerge: −0.0082). What decides the merge line is the 9,598 one-end-annotated pairs and the 222,921 unannotated ones, and both-ends labels cannot type them: a one-cell pair whose GT centroid sits within 5 um of one end only, a two-cell pair with one unannotated cell, and an annotated cell paired with a non-cell detection all read the same. The judge that can type the annotated ones is at the edge level, from REF's own solution: the annotated end's GT edge missed while the partner detection carries the GT neighbour (the swap signature, a merge fixes it) versus the annotated end's GT edges already correct (a merge can only displace them). The maskfeat separation (AUC 0.91) was swap sites against two-cell pairs sampled without the saddle condition; it does not transfer to the parent population.

## 2026-09-17 lnrescue
- Hypothesis: the peaks a background-subtracted (sigma 15 um) pass finds where the shipped pass has no detection within 7 um are, at a score threshold, cells as often as the shipped detections are (locnorm: 19% of the missed annotated cells recovered; recovered cells' fused max median 0.30, 81% >= 0.25), so a rescue detection set (every shipped detection untouched + the new peaks) carries the missed-endpoint edges the bench can then price.
- Scope: all frames of the 128 6bba movies; hparacache's four-map pass with the pooled input's local Gaussian mean (sigma 15 um) subtracted; a BGSUB15 detection (hpara placement, NMS 4 um, score >= 0.15) is kept iff no shipped F4HP primary lies within 7 um; per movie and score bin (0.15-0.20 / 0.20-0.25 / 0.25-0.30 / 0.30-0.40 / >= 0.40) the new peaks' count and annotated share (a GT node within 7 um) against the shipped detections' share.
- Experiment: `lnrescue.py` from `tools/bench/make_lnrescue.py` (hparacache.py cut at the movie list + the rescue tail; the Gaussian as separable conv3d on the GPU, locnorm's toy-tested `local_norm` logic), checkgen ok. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-lnrescue` v1, T4, hplace's sources + biohub-hparacache, pushed 2026-09-17 (GPU quota before the push 6.8 h to the 2026-09-19 refresh; expected ~3.2 h). Output `fdet_F4ln_<name>.npz` (c{t} / s{t} = the F4HP arrays with the new peaks appended, nnew{t} = the count appended, the last nnew primaries of the frame).
- Result: v1 COMPLETE 200 min on the T4, 128/128, `LNRESCUE OK`; caches `fdet_F4ln_<name>.npz` in the kernel's output (not downloaded). Shipped primaries 2,242,408, annotated share (a GT node within 7 um) 5.48%. New peaks by score bin (count / +% of shipped / annotated / annotated share / x the shipped share): [0.15, 0.20) 34,404 / 1.53% / 240 / 0.70% / 0.13; [0.20, 0.25) 9,270 / 0.41% / 100 / 1.08% / 0.20; [0.25, 0.30) 1,969 / 0.09% / 53 / 2.69% / 0.49; [0.30, 0.40) 160 / 0.01% / 10 / 6.25% / 1.14; >= 0.40 none. Total 45,803 new peaks (+2.0%), 403 annotated.
- Conclusion: the rescue peaks are cells about as often as shipped detections only above 0.30, where there are 160 of them; at 0.25 half are cells (0.49x), at 0.20 a fifth, below 0.20 an eighth. The annotated recoveries sit mostly at low scores (240 of 403 below 0.20), so the ceiling at a threshold that keeps the noise small is about 60 recovered cells (+0.001 edge_J) and at 0.20 about 160 cells (+0.003) against 8,400 admitted noise peaks. The bench (lnbench) prices exactly that trade, with a temporal-persistence admission (a new peak with a new peak within 4 um in an adjacent frame) as the noise filter that needs no threshold.

## 2026-09-17 lnpersist
- Hypothesis: among lnrescue's 45,803 rescue peaks, the annotated ones can be separated from the noise without a score threshold, by whether the peak persists: another rescue peak within 4 um in an adjacent frame (P1 either side, P2 both sides), or a shipped primary within 4 um in an adjacent frame (G: the peak fills a one-frame hole in an existing track). Priced per score bin by annotated share and by the GT edges a kept peak could recover (its GT node's edges to cells the shipped detections see).
- Scope: 128 6bba movies, fdet_F4ln_ caches (biohub-lnrescue) against the train GT; CPU only, no heads, no solve.
- Experiment: `lnpersist.py` (standalone), kernel `faustine649/biohub-lnpersist` v1 (CPU); outputs lnpersist_peaks.csv (one row per rescue peak: score, p1, p2, g, ann, d_gt, link_edges, gt_deg), lnpersist_movies.csv.
- Result: v1 COMPLETE (0.3 min), `LNPERSIST OK`; `bench_csv/lnpersist/lnpersist_v1.log`. Kept / annotated / annotated share / linkable GT edges, all bins: ALL 45,803 / 403 / 0.0088 / 596; P1 24,999 / 132 / 0.0053 / 171; P2 8,099 / 25 / 0.0031 / 28; G 16,316 / 188 / 0.0115 / 303; P1|G 36,275 / 287 / 0.0079 / 423; P1&G 5,040 / 33 / 0.0065 / 51. By bin, ALL: [0.15,0.20) 34,404 / 240 / 0.0070 / 340; [0.20,0.25) 9,270 / 100 / 0.0108 / 152; [0.25,0.30) 1,969 / 53 / 0.0269 / 84; >= 0.30 160 / 10 / 0.0625 / 20. G by bin: 11,733 / 98 / 0.0084; 3,617 / 51 / 0.0141; 878 / 30 / 0.0342; 88 / 9 / 0.1023. Shipped detections' annotated share 0.0548. v2 COMPLETE (0.4 min; `lnpersist_v2.log`, `lnpersist_peaks.csv` 45,803 rows, `lnpersist_movies.csv`): of the 403 annotated rescue peaks, 1 is a newborn daughter (mother and sister detected, score bin [0.15, 0.20)), 0 are mothers.
- Conclusion: persistence selects AGAINST the cells. A rescue peak with a rescue peak next to it in an adjacent frame is annotated at 0.0053 (both sides 0.0031), below the unfiltered 0.0088: the noise the local normalisation raises is a standing structure that reappears frame after frame, while the recovered cells flicker in and out of the pass. A hole in a shipped track (G) helps a little (0.0115, 188 cells, 303 linkable edges) but stays five times below the shipped detections' own share. The score stays the only usable admission, and its ceiling stands: >= 0.25 admits 2,129 peaks for 63 cells and at most 104 recoverable edges (+0.001 edge_J); >= 0.20 admits 11,399 for 163 cells and 256 edges (+0.002). No threshold-free filter exists among these three; the bench arms are score-only (LN20, LN25), and the line is worth at most one leaderboard digit. The rescue does not touch the division term: the ~19 detector-blind divisions' missing daughters and mothers are not among the peaks the local normalisation raises (1 daughter in 403), so the +0.0006-per-division lever stays closed on this route.

## 2026-09-17 lnbench
- Hypothesis: adding lnrescue's peaks (the locally normalised pass's detections >= 7 um from every shipped one) to the shipped F4HP detection set, admitted at a score threshold, recovers more true edges (the missed endpoints; 63 annotated peaks at >= 0.25, 163 at >= 0.20, with 104 / 256 linkable GT edges) than the admitted noise peaks cost through the node term and false links, on the official scorer with the shipped rankers and patches.
- Scope: 128 6bba movies, dupsup's harness (F4HP REF = round 2, hard anchors); arms LN20 / LN25 on the rescue set fdet_F4ln_ with features from the rescue heads (eplncache, ep2lncache; head 2 only where REF has one), one features_ext per movie shared by the arms, solve_one's keep mask withholding every new peak below the threshold (its edges never enter the ILP, its node is dropped); joint-gate cross and paired bootstrap against REF + joint.
- Experiment: `lnbench.py` from `tools/bench/make_lnbench.py 0.20,0.25` (lnbench block: ln_load / ln_keep with an unused persistence option; the arm loop asserts the rescue cache is F4HP + appended peaks); toy tests `scratchpad/test_lnbench_persist.py` passed; checkgen ok. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-lnbench` v1, CPU, mgpass's sources minus hyp plus biohub-lnrescue / eplncache / ep2lncache. Outputs lnbench_REF_F4HP.csv, lnbench_arm_LN20.csv, lnbench_arm_LN25.csv, forks_*.csv.
- Result: v1 COMPLETE, 128/128, `LNBENCH OK`, both round-2 anchors held (`bench_csv/lnbench/lnbench_v1.log`, lnbench_REF_F4HP.csv, lnbench_arm_LN20.csv, lnbench_arm_LN25.csv). Admitted: LN20 11,399 of 45,803 rescue peaks (24.9%), LN25 2,129 (4.6%). - Literature check on the de-biasing itself (the user, 2026-09-23 night: "实在不知道怎么归一化就去借鉴文献吧"; offline on v2's rows, before v3 landed). The two biases named map to two textbook remedies. (a) A per-movie constant in the labels is a fixed effect; the panel-data "within" estimator subtracts each group's mean from the target before fitting and the neural form is a per-annotator bias unit dropped at test time (Rodrigues & Pereira, "Deep learning from crowds", AAAI 2018) -- that is exactly v3's CENTER_TARGETS. (b) Annotated cells being brighter than the population is sample-selection bias; the remedy is importance weighting by p_population(x) / p_annotated(x) (Shimodaira 2000; kernel mean matching, Huang et al. 2007), which is valid only when the offset given the image, p(y | x), is the same for annotated and unannotated cells; test-time re-estimation of BatchNorm statistics on the new movie (AdaBN, Li et al. 2016; Schneider et al. 2020; Nado et al. 2020) addresses an input-style shift, not a label shift. What the rows say about the ceiling of each: the between-movie share of the label-offset variance is 5% (6bba) / 7% (44b6) in z and 3-6% in y and x (per-axis sd total / within-movie, um: 6bba z 1.495 / 1.455, y 0.943 / 0.914, x 0.876 / 0.855; 44b6 z 1.695 / 1.630, y 0.976 / 0.948, x 1.012 / 0.988; the z plane's quantisation alone contributes sd 0.47), so remedy (a) can move at most that much; the per-movie mean z offset does not follow depth (corr with the movie's mean z -0.15 / -0.01), time (+0.03 / +0.05) or brightness (+0.21 / -0.05), so it is not a covariate the head could read; and within a movie the z offset is flat across score bins (recorded above), so remedy (b) would re-weight cells whose offsets do not differ. Share of the within-movie offset variance each head explains, out of fold (joint / cross, after centring both): 6bba z +0.05 / -0.22, y +0.12 / -0.05, x +0.08 / -0.06; 44b6 z -0.03 / -0.05, y +0.08 / +0.05, x +0.07 / +0.05. Reading: even inside an embryo the image explains at most 5-14% of where the annotation sits relative to the detection; the rest is label noise at about one z plane and two xy voxels; and what the head does learn is the embryo's own convention (the 44b6 head is worse than nothing on 6bba even after both are centred). That is a change of p(y | x) between embryos -- concept shift -- which the covariate-shift literature says no re-weighting or normalisation can repair without labels from the target embryo, which the hidden test (embryo-disjoint by the rules) will never provide. The only crumb: the 6bba head's xy part carries a small positive share to 44b6 (+0.05 / +0.04), not the reverse. Decision: no v4 (importance weights, AdaBN) is pushed; v3 and hrefinezh decide whether the centred residual transfers at all, and the line is closed on their numbers.

With the training constants removed the heads are neutral to negative on the third embryo (joint +0.05 um p50 worse, 6bba head +0.10 worse, every xy-only variant within 0.03 of 'before' with about half of the cells placed worse), on dense labels and on the dim cells the competition annotation under-samples. - Result:
  1. Sparse-GT training overfits early, on everyone's side. nusrati (738773, 2026-09-01): 3D U-Net on the sparse points, fixed 8 frames/movie, r=1 masked focal loss: the real metric peaks at epoch 5-10 then collapses (adj_ej 0.40 -> 0.07 by epoch 120) while loss keeps falling (0.25 -> 0.003), node recall stays 0.98-0.99 and peaks/frame climb 1,800 -> 2,100+. hengck23's reading: "the unlabelled nodes change from noisy targets to negative targets after 10 epochs". zhincez (732103, 2026-09-09): fine-tuning the public detector on a 7-film sparse split made it worse on every film (adj_J -0.0161). This is the record's own dccache3 (ep05 > ep07 > ep12 in every domain; published DeepCenter best at epoch 2 of 500) seen from outside.
  2. The one detector-side change with a reported gain: hikarukai (741749, rank ~336, own pipeline 0.939 on the host baseline): pretrain detector + linker on 497 of José's 2,174 synthetic sequences for 80 epochs, then 60 on the 175 real movies: 24-video hold-out 0.9146 -> 0.9269. Caveats he states: it pushes the node count up (paid back through the N_pred term), buys nothing on divisions, and all 2,174 sequences came out worse (adj -0.005). His neutral list on the same hold-out (paired SE ~0.006): U-Net width 32 -> 48, epochs 60 -> 131 (edge J up, node term eats it), strong augmentation, Gaussian heatmap loss, local-softmax peak loss, 9-frame temporal window (+0.1% of GT nodes), a trained division head (+-0.001 LB). His CV-vs-LB r ~ -0.2 in the 0.93-0.95 band; "post-processing settings chosen locally carry over to the LB, the local ranking of two trained models does not". Ogurtsov (rank 8) on whether 0.957 is reachable from the published U-Net: "reachable to some extent but pretty risky", for the private LB.
  3. The synthetic set (732103): 1,539 static volumes + 2,174 sequences, centroids/edges/divisions only (no masks), CC0, a physical model (super-Gaussian nuclei, scatter, anisotropic PSF, Poisson + read noise), stride-4 downsampling, division rate inflated 15.7x, texture/contrast "the weakest axes"; voxel spacing not stated. No one reports a detection result from it; the one use posted (juancneira, a division gate on its lineage geometry) cost 0.910 -> 0.906 on the LB. Real division geometry measured by zhincez on 7 divisions (parent->daughter step median 8.47 um, sister separation 10.22 um) is wider than the generator's 7.24 um.
  4. Dense pseudo-labels (focus3d, 738217 / 740145): hengck23's route is FOCUS-3D instance centroids on t = 0, 5, 10, ... (about 20% of frames), elastic/affine augmentation to make T=2 pairs, "up to 200 epochs without overfitting", a single-frame 3-level U-Net at 64^3 isotropic (channels 64/128/256, peak threshold 0.2, max-pool 3 NMS, greedy suppression at 3 grid voxels ~4.9 um, a learned per-peak refine head: refine_prob >= 0.0888 removes 13% of peaks at Kaggle recall 99.45%, error to the annotation 1.18 -> 0.97 grid voxels = 1.91 -> 1.57 um), then a SuperGlue-style linker on the U-Net features (one in / one out per node, no divisions, no ILP, no gaps): validation edge_J 0.902 without ILP / 0.896 with his ILP, no LB posted. Node count is his open problem (companion detector: predicted / estimated nodes 1.05-2.36 across 11 train movies; 2026-09-20 "trying to find a model that doesn't over estimate num of nodes"). He reports the placement shift explicitly: the Kaggle annotation "is based on Ultrack segmentation, sometimes annotates cell corners; my annotation is based on focus3d, which is cell center", and proposes a dzyx head (Kaggle zyx = FOCUS zyx + dzyx, in um) as the fix. Satwik (p4rallax, 2026-09-12): a detector on dense FOCUS-3D labels reaches recall 1 on 41 held-out videos across both embryos; with a linker trained on the sparse GT and Ultrack's ILP it scores 0.809 CV / 0.83 LB; FOCUS-3D + Ultrack alone 0.7; pseudo-tracks mixed with up-weighted GT "performed poorly". The record's own focus3d_probe (today) on 6bba_ebff6e76: 2-2.5 instances per estimated cell, centroids 3.2-3.5 um from the annotation against 1.2 um for the shipped detector.
  5. Supervision the shipped maps share (reference.md, read 2026-09-18): all four F4 heatmaps use the same PU rule (weight 12 in a ~4 um ball round each annotated centre, 1 where the input voxel is below the frame's 40th brightness percentile, 0.05 elsewhere), so a dim unannotated cell is trained as background and a bright unannotated one is ignored. hikarukai's "recall changes by a point and the LB does not react" and the record's lntrace/lnbench (recovered dim cells at 5.7 um placement cannot be linked) point the same way: the detector's remaining cost is placement, not finding.
  6. Costs on record: dctrain 32.2 min/epoch on a T4 (data path, not GPU), optimum at epoch 12, 15 epochs ~8.5 h; every consumer (fusecache x3, head caches x2 per head, ranker retrain, gate refit) re-runs behind a new detector. Deadline 2026-09-29, five submissions a day, two final slots.
- Conclusion: The forum has no case of a self-trained or re-trained detector lifting a 0.94+ score; the two reported gains (synthetic pretraining, +0.012 hold-out at 0.939 pipeline; dense-label detectors at recall 1.0) both arrive with more nodes and no LB above the plateau, and everyone training on the sparse points sees the same early-epoch optimum the record measured in dccache3. What the forum adds that the record did not have: (a) a written diagnosis of the annotation offset (Ultrack-segment centroid vs nucleus centre) and a proposed dzyx / refine head that took hengck23's placement error from 1.91 to 1.57 um, which is the record's own untested residue ("a placement-supervised detector head", 2026-09-17 lnrescue-line entries); (b) hikarukai's rule that model rankings do not transfer across the LB while post-processing settings do. Claim tested by this read: "a new detector is the lever the 0.955 -> 0.96 gap needs" is not supported by anything posted; residue: a refine head trained on the annotated centroids over the existing F4HP maps (no new detector, no re-cache of the ranker rows if placement changes are small) is the one detector-side item with a measured precedent, and its cost is one T4 training run plus one bench.

- Scope: twopass's harness (128 6bba movies, F4HP primaries, pass 1 = the shipped fold rankers' solve, the shipped patch, the 36-column image gate, the official scorer, paired bootstraps) with the track columns replaced by six flow columns per candidate pair read off pass 1's solved edges: has_fl, d_pred, dmd_fl (d_raw - d_pred), cos_fl (the candidate step against the flow), fl_mag, fl_disp (the median deviation of the neighbours' displacements from the flow). Fold rankers held out: fold0 R6 0.9932 / FL 0.9934, fold1 0.9914 / 0.9917. The solves: REF 1,966,713 edges 2,371 ILP forks; R6 1,950,180 / 2,807; FL 1,987,864 / 2,070. - Conclusion: the claim does not hold: the flow columns move the ranker's held-out AUC by +0.0002 / +0.0003 and the solve by adj_J -0.0009 (interval touching zero from below), and against the shipped ranker the arm loses 0.006 of score with the interval off zero. In the shipped Z composition the triple's cost comes from divscore's scorers and a below-floor edge is usable through its z, so the ranker reaches a division only through the two edges' -p terms in the objective and through the gate's ranker columns (p_c1, p_q, rank_gap); the division loss measured here is therefore an upper bound for Z, not its number. What carries over to Z unchanged is the linking read: adj_J -0.0009 [-0.0020, +0.0001] against the control and -0.0005 [-0.0016, +0.0005] against the shipped ranker -- no gain on the term the columns were meant to move. The decision stands on adj_J; the 'costs divisions' sentence is withdrawn as a statement about what ships.

By d_before on 6bba (before / their / joint / cross): [0, 1) 0.625 / 1.595 / 0.625 / 0.957; [1, 2) 1.517 / 1.848 / 1.238 / 1.447; [2, 4) 2.453 / 2.377 / 2.009 / 2.376; [4, 7) 5.130 / 4.718 / 4.722 / 4.889. - Conclusion: two claims, two readings. (1) Their shipped head does what its notebook says inside its own stack -- from the lattice peak it gains 17% on 44b6 (1% on 6bba) -- but it ends at 1.84 / 1.43 um where our hpara placement already is at 1.27 / 1.37, and it places 73% / 61% of our cells worse than we do; a port of their head onto our detections has nothing to give. The lattice is the difference: their start is 1.86 / 1.72 um from the annotation, ours 1.27 / 1.37. (2) A head of their design trained on our pairs reproduces hrefine exactly: inside an embryo it gains (6bba 1.27 -> 1.06 in 121 of 128 movies, 44b6 1.37 -> 1.21), across embryos it does not (the 6bba head on 44b6: p50 1.371 -> 1.342 with the share within 2 um falling 0.722 -> 0.704, 58.5% placed worse, 31 of 71 movies better; the 44b6 head on 6bba: worse, 39 of 128), and the mean shifts show the same mechanism -- the 6bba head carries +0.55 um of z onto 44b6, whose own offset is +0.03. The features (frozen U-Net map against raw crops), the capacity (a 7k-parameter MLP against a CNN) and the 2 um bound do not change what transfers. The hidden test is a third embryo, so the cross line decides: no cache, no bench. Residue, unchanged from hrefine: the far sites (d_before 4-7 um) move by 0.2-0.4 um under every head, which is where the swaps live, and no head reaches them.

## 2026-09-27 flowgate launched: the public 0.953 notebook's flow gate in our pipeline
- Hypothesis (the user, 2026-09-27: "流场门也去试试吧，或许分开试"): the flow gate of the public 0.953 notebook -- the median displacement of a cell's 12 nearest matched neighbours within 40 um (excluding within 1.5 um, at least 4) predicts where it goes, and a pair is allowed if the target is within 7 um of the cell's raw OR predicted position -- removes false candidates from our ILP without losing true ones, so adj_J rises against the same ranker on the ungated candidates. Our record has flow only as a ranker column (flowvel, 2026-09-03: every magnitude under 0.001); the gate is a different use.
- Scope: twopass's harness on the 128 6bba movies (the shipped fold rankers, F4HP primaries, the shipped patch, the 36-column image gate, the official scorer, paired bootstraps). The flow is read off pass 1's solved edges (REF's own solve). Our candidate pairs exist only within GATE_UM 10 um, so the gate prunes the (R, 10] band unless the flow explains the step; a source without a flow prediction keeps the relaxed raw gate (10 um). Before any solve: the gate's base rate on the labelled rows (d_raw, d_pred, the fold ranker's probability per row; true pairs lost against false pairs removed, on all labelled rows and on the rows above the ILP floor 0.48; single-column AUCs of d_raw / d_pred / md_um). Pass 2: the SAME shipped fold ranker solved on the gated candidates at R = 7 (the notebook's) and R = 9; arms CR (REF), FG7CR, FG9CR; FG against CR paired on score and adj_J, gated and ungated.
- Experiment: `tools/bench/make_flowgate.py` -> `flowgate.py` (4,229 lines, from twopass.py: the track columns and the two-pass rankers removed; flow_field, pair_dists, gate_keep, feats_gated, fg_for_keys, the base-rate report, the gated solves, the FG-vs-CR bootstrap); checkgen ok; toy test scratchpad/test_flowgate.py (a sheet of cells jumping 8 um together: the flow is the jump, the true target at d_raw 8 passes FG7 by the flow, a stray at d_raw 8 sideways fails FG7 and passes FG9, an isolated source keeps its pair through the relaxed gate; rows stay aligned). Kernel `faustine649/biohub-flowgate` v1 (CPU, twopass's sources, pushed 2026-09-27, ~9 h).
- Result: v1 COMPLETE 494.9 min (CPU), 128 of 128 movies, both round-2 anchors reproduced, the CR cell reproduces 59/26/66 0.9546; `bench_csv/flowgate/` holds the log, stdout.txt, the fork tables forkfg_*.csv and the per-movie rows. Base rate on the 184,174 labelled rows (97.9% with a flow prediction): true pairs d_raw p50 1.82 / p90 4.61, d_pred 1.23 / 2.93; false pairs d_raw 8.61 / 9.77, d_pred 8.93 / 10.86; in the (7, 10] band 2,751 true pairs (2.68%), 1,823 of them within 7 um of the prediction, against 66,500 false pairs (81.4%), 2,146 of them within 7 um of the prediction; single-column AUC (flipped) d_pred 0.9795, d_raw 0.9680, md_um (the ranker's greedy-chain prediction) 0.9608. The gate on the rows the ILP sees (p >= 0.48): FG7 keeps 99,858 true and loses 134, keeps 3,821 false and removes 40; FG9 loses 13 true, removes 4 false (on all labelled rows FG7 removes 64,271 false pairs and loses 851 true: the ranker had already put those false pairs under the floor). The solves: REF 1,966,713 edges, 2,371 ILP forks; FG7 1,963,044 / 2,189 (50.7% of the 5,467,326 pairs kept, 148,824 by the flow alone); FG9 1,966,398 / 2,348 (81.1% kept). Cells (official scorer, p > 0.03): CR + jointimg 59/26/66 0.9546, FG7CR + jointimg 52/28/73 0.9483, FG9CR + jointimg 58/36/67 0.9514; ungated CR 53/55/72 0.9449, FG7CR 45/57/80 0.9388, FG9CR 53/57/72 0.9444. Paired against CR: FG7 adj_J -0.0013 [-0.0017, -0.0009] (gated and ungated), score -0.0063 [-0.0100, -0.0027] gated; FG9 adj_J -0.0002 [-0.0003, -0.0000], score -0.0033 [-0.0052, -0.0015] gated, -0.0005 [-0.0021, +0.0011] ungated.
- Conclusion: the claim does not hold in our pipeline: as a pruning of our candidates the flow gate loses at 7 um (adj_J -0.0013, off zero) and is a small loss at 9, and the base rate says why before any solve -- among the pairs the ILP sees, the gate at 7 um removes 40 false pairs for 134 true ones, because the ranker has already put the band's false pairs under the floor (64,271 of them fail the gate, 40 are above 0.48). What the gate removes beyond that is division edges: a second daughter is by construction off the neighbourhood's flow, and the ILP's forks fall 2,371 -> 2,189 and the true divisions 59 -> 52. In the public stack the gate stands in front of a distance-cost Hungarian relink, where it is the only thing keeping far wrong partners out; in ours the ranker does that job. Residue, measured and not yet priced: the flow prediction itself is a better predictor than the one the ranker has (single-column AUC 0.9795 against md_um's 0.9608; in the 7-10 um band 66% of the true pairs lie within 7 um of it against 3% of the false), so d_pred as a ranker column -- a different thing from flowvel's velocity fill for zero-velocity cells and from twopass's solved-chain columns (md_tr 0.964) -- is the form in which flow could enter; twopass's saturation (the ranker at 0.993 with or without seven more columns) is the prior against it.

## 2026-09-27 smoothchk: the linker's smoothness measured on the same cells as the truth
- Hypothesis (the user, 2026-09-27: "所以排序器到底有多平滑", after forkvel's line that the shipped chains are three times smoother than annotated cells): the linker's chains are smoother than the truth because it links to the smoother neighbour at a jump (a wrong-edge bias) rather than because forkvel compared different cells on different coordinates; measured on the same annotated cells, the shipped chain's jitter is below the truth's and the errors at jumps are swaps to smoother edges.
- Scope: the 4 visible test datasets (train copies 44b6_0113de3b, 44b6_0b24845f, 6bba_05b6850b, 6bba_05db0fb1) with submit_nc35's visible-run submission.csv against their train GT. Every annotated plain step m -> x -> s (consecutive frames, one predecessor, one successor), each node snapped to the nearest shipped node within 5 um at its frame; j_gt = |(s - x) - (x - m)| on the shipped graph's own coordinates. What the shipped graph did at x: correct (x -> s its only edge), fork, swap (an edge, none to s), break (no edge); binned by j_gt; for the swaps whether the chosen edge is smoother and nearer than the true one; the same-cell jitter distributions; forkvel's all-node line reproduced.
- Experiment: `smoothchk.py` (215 lines; checkgen ok; toy test scratchpad/test_smoothchk.py: a correct step, a swap to a point 1 um beside the true target reads j_chosen 1.0 against j_gt 0, a break reads NaN, an unsnapped GT node drops its step); kernel `faustine649/biohub-smoothchk` v1 (CPU, 0.4 min; competition data, faustine649/cell-tracking, biohub-submit-nc35). Output bench_csv/smoothchk/ (log, stdout.txt, smoothchk_steps.csv with one row per step).
- Result: 1,911 annotated steps measured (2,055 in the GT; 144 unsnapped, 120 of them in 6bba_05db0fb1 -- a missing shipped node within 5 um of an annotated one, i.e. a detection or short-filter loss, not a linking error). The shipped graph: correct 1,889 (98.8%), fork 1, swap 14 (0.7%), break 7 (0.4%). By the truth's own jitter (um per frame): j_gt < 1: 1,613 steps, 99.9% correct; 1-2: 233, 99.1%; 2-3: 27, 96.3%; 3-4: 5, 80%; >= 4: 33 steps, 16 correct / 11 swaps / 6 breaks (48% correct). The swaps: the chosen edge is smoother than the true one in 12 of 14 and nearer in 12 of 14 (median j_chosen 1.35 vs j_gt 8.08; d_chosen 2.23 vs d_true 7.63 um); the true target had another source in 64% of the swaps and 57% of the breaks (a mutual exchange between neighbours). Same cells, two chains (p10 / p50 / p90): the truth's jitter on the shipped coordinates 0.23 / 0.52 / 1.24 over all 1,911 steps, 0.23 / 0.52 / 1.17 where the shipped step is correct, 2.14 / 8.08 / 15.02 at the swaps, 3.94 / 6.25 / 7.73 at the breaks; the shipped chain's jitter at the same cells 0.23 / 0.52 / 1.14, at the swaps 0.65 / 1.33 / 3.32; every plain chain node of the 4 movies 0.26 / 0.60 / 1.30 (forkvel's 0.63 line, 104,414 nodes), the annotated ones among them 0.52.
- Conclusion: the linker is not smoother than the truth: on the same cells its chain and the annotated chain are the same edge in 98.8% of steps, so they have the same jitter (median 0.52 um per frame), and forkvel's 'three times smoother' (0.63 against 1.95) compared the detector's sub-voxel coordinates on 4 movies with annotation coordinates (integer voxels, z quantised to 1.6 um; the snap to F4HP detections at score >= 0.15 within 5 um did not remove that) on 199 movies -- a coordinate artefact, corrected in the forkvel and forkvel2 entries. What remains of the claim is a tail: at the 2% of steps where a cell moves 3 um per frame or more off its previous velocity, the linker is wrong about half the time (17 of 38), two thirds of those errors are swaps to a nearer, smoother neighbour and one third are breaks, and most swaps are exchanges with a neighbour that took the true target. That tail is 21 errors in 1,911 steps on 4 movies (1.1%); on 6bba_05db0fb1 the missing nodes (120 unsnapped steps, 10.6%) outweigh the linking errors (20) five to one. Residue: 4 movies and 21 errors are too few to price a fix; a 128-movie version would come from the forkprop harness's REF solves against the GT (the same classification per annotated step), if the tail is ever worth a run; the twopass result (2026-09-26) already says more velocity columns do not move it.

## 2026-09-25 zhfork launched: the fork gate on a fully judged population
- Hypothesis (the user, 2026-09-25: Zebrahub has a domain shift, so size-based scores may not transfer, but with the variables controlled the image gate can be tested there): on Zebrahub's dense GT nearly every fork is judged (6bba: 725 counted of 18,457), so the gate's column sets -- 31, 36 (half-max size), 33, each sz2 measure, all ratios, all 61 -- can be compared on thousands of judged forks from ONE fork population, and a column set that cuts distinctly more false forks at the same true-fork retention there is a real separator, whatever the absolute size values do across the domain shift.
- Scope: the 41 hpara-cached Zebrahub crops (biohub-zhhpcache) with their images (biohub-zebrahub-extract); zhpara4's pipeline (D187 18-column ranker without edge heads -> the head columns NaN, as in a submission whose head pass failed; ILP floor 0.48, disappearance 1.5, DIV_W 0.55; gap-close nocand cap 0.02, SHORT_MIN 4, linefit), then forkprop's orphan patch as it ships (contrast-ranked, uncapped, DIV_DIVERGE_UM 1.5; no node-cost solve), then forkprop_sz2's fork rows (28 gate / new features + 61 image-side columns + coordinates). Judge at MATCH_UM 5 um: 2 = the mother matches a dividing GT node and the fork's children cover both GT daughters, 1 = the mother matches a GT node but not that division, 0 = no GT node within 5 um. In-kernel: counts, single-column AUCs, HistGB gates out of fold by crop (5 folds) per column set with TP kept / FP kept at p > 0.03 and the FP kept at the cut that keeps 90% of the TP. Output zhfork_forks.csv for the offline paired comparisons. Caveat: the fork population is zhpara4's composition + the shipped patch, not the node-cost composition; divwhy (2026-09-02) found 65% of Zebrahub's GT divisions lose a daughter at detection, so the true forks here are the minority the detector catches.
- Experiment: `tools/bench/make_zhfork.py` -> `zhfork.py` (2,114 lines: zhpara4's head to its ranker load + zh_load, forkprop_sz2's constants / patch / image block / fork_rows / _aux_extra verbatim, a new solve with pmap and seed_of_node, patch_zh, judge_forks, the run and the gate table); checkgen ok; toy test scratchpad/test_zhfork.py (the judge on a toy graph: a true division 2, a fork on a non-dividing GT cell 1, a fork on no GT cell 0, a division whose second daughter the fork missed 1; the overriding constants sit after zhpara4's). Kernel `faustine649/biohub-zhfork` v1 (CPU, pushed 2026-09-25; support pack, cell-tracking, competition, biohub-poolsize, biohub-zebrahub-extract, biohub-zhhpcache; ~3 h). v1 died at import on zhpara4's inherited assert that 40 competition detection caches are attached (unused here); v2 replaces it with a note and is the run.
- Result: v2 ran 25.4 min, 41 of 41 crops. `bench_csv/zhfork/` holds zhfork_v2.log and zhfork_forks.csv. The population: 7,894 GT divisions in the 41 crops; 3,804 forks, judged TP 81 / FP 2,844 / uncounted 879 -- the pipeline forked correctly on 81 of the 7,894 (1.0%), the patch added 3,600 of the 3,804 forks. Single columns on the 2,925 counted forks (AUC TP vs FP; TP / FP medians): contrast carries -- c_p 0.715 (1.88 / 0.99), c_q 0.725 (1.74 / 0.82), c_c1 0.678; the raw-image sizes are weaker than on 6bba -- r_hm_q 0.328 inverted, i.e. 0.67 (4.58 / 5.29 um; 6bba 3.1 / 4.9), r_hm_p 0.386 (4.13 / 4.85), the ratios rhm_max 0.501, rhm_sum 0.471 (no separation), the sz2 measures 0.33-0.58, the radius of gyration r_q 0.367. Gates out of fold by crop (5 folds), TP kept / FP kept at p > 0.03 and FP kept at the cut that keeps 90% of the TP:

  | columns | AUC | TP kept / 81 | FP kept / 2,844 at p > 0.03 | FP kept at 90% TP |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | gate20 (no image) | 0.763 | 19 | 86 | 1,647 |
  | img31 | 0.771 | 22 | 41 | 1,952 |
  | img36 (size gate) | 0.767 | 19 | 41 | 1,791 |
  | img33 (ratios) | 0.774 | 19 | 51 | 1,741 |
  | img_hm10 / c30 / c70 / prof / mom | 0.785 / 0.754 / 0.772 / 0.751 / 0.746 | 20 / 18 / 20 / 22 / 22 | 42 / 37 / 40 / 39 / 39 | 1,879 / 1,778 / 1,653 / 1,961 / 2,119 |
  | img_ratios | 0.780 | 17 | 43 | 1,709 |
  | imgall (61) | 0.730 | 19 | 35 | 2,180 |

  The p > 0.03 cut keeps 17-22 of the 81 true forks here (the population is 97% false, so every probability is low); at 90% true-fork retention every gate still keeps 58-77% of the false forks, and the 20-column gate without any image column keeps the fewest.
- Conclusion: Zebrahub cannot settle the size gate, for two reasons the run measured. (1) Its divisions are out of the pipeline's reach: 81 true forks out of 7,894 GT divisions (the detector loses the daughters, as divwhy found), so the judged population has barely more true forks than 6bba's 66 and 35x its false ones; (2) the raw-image columns do not transfer as a family -- the gate with no image column separates as well as any image gate (AUC 0.76 vs 0.73-0.79; at 90% TP it keeps 1,647 false forks against 1,650-2,180), contrast is the only image column that carries (AUC 0.72), and the half-max size of a true daughter is 4.6 um there against 3.1 on 6bba, with the daughter-to-mother ratios at 0.50 (no separation). Between the column sets nothing is distinguishable on 81 true forks. The controlled read the user asked for is therefore: on this domain the image gate as a whole is not a separator, and the size columns are neither better nor worse than the rest of it. The claim that Zebrahub gives the size gate a sign does not hold; what Zebrahub says instead is where its divisions go -- 99% never become a fork, at detection.


## 2026-09-25 forkprop_sz2 launched: five size measures
- Hypothesis (the user, 2026-09-25: "换一个量法呢，尺寸这个和尺寸怎么量的关系太大了"): the size gate's reading depends on how a nucleus' size is measured; the shipped measure (crop-median background, half of peak - background, the connected component holding the peak) is sensitive to a raised background in dense regions and to a touching neighbour merging into the component, and a measure without those two dependencies separates true daughters from false ones better in the gate cross.
- Scope: forkprop_sz's 128-movie 6bba harness, the CR_NOCAP_DV150 arm only (the shipped patch; forkprop_sz's 7 arms took 411 min). Five more measures per node from the same smoothed crop: hm10 (background = the crop's 10th percentile), c30 / c70 (thresholds at 0.3 / 0.7 of peak - background), prof (radial-profile radius: shell-averaged intensity around the peak drops half way to the 6-8 um shells' mean; no connectivity), mom (background-subtracted radius of gyration inside the half-max component). Each as p / c1 / q + max ratio + sum ratio: 25 columns. Cross cells with the official scorer at p > 0.03: REF + gate6 / joint / jointimg (36, must reproduce forkprop_sz's 0.9546 line) / img31; the arm + joint / jointimg / img31 / img33 / one cell per measure (31 + its 5) / img_ratios (31 + all 12 ratios) / imgall (61); paired bootstrap of every image cell of the arm against its img31 and jointimg cells. ## 2026-09-25 size gate: strictness and transfer, offline
- Hypothesis (the user, 2026-09-25, after submission 56530848 read LB 0.954 against 0.956): the size gate loses on the hidden set because it is too strict -- it cuts true divisions the 31-column gate keeps -- or because its absolute size columns do not transfer to other embryos; and, more generally, the public LB's division component is too sparse to grade a gate that differs on 3-5 forks per movie.
- Scope: the CR_NOCAP_DV150 arm's fork tables with labels and all 36 columns (6bba: forkssz_CR_NOCAP_DV150.csv, 18,457 forks, 725 counted, 66 TP, 128 movies; 44b6: forkssz_44b6img.csv, 5,377 forks, 88 counted, 9 TP, 71 movies). fk44prop_sz's HistGB (100 it, lr 0.05, msl 10) on counted forks, cut p > 0.03. Column sets: 31 (nc35's), 36 (sz), 33 (31 + the two size ratios), 36 with the three absolute sizes normalised by the movie's median r_hm_p, 34 (31 + the three absolute sizes). Cells: out of fold by fold within each domain, cross-domain (train one, test the other = a new embryo), joint (both domains, out of fold by fold).
- Experiment: `tools/bench/szgate_sweep.py` (local, ~12 min).
- Result: TP kept / TP, FP kept / FP at p > 0.03:

  | columns | 6bba OOF | 44b6 OOF | 6bba -> 44b6 | 44b6 -> 6bba | joint OOF 6bba | joint OOF 44b6 |

  | 31 (nc35) | 54/66, 48/659 | 8/9, 28/79 | 7/9, 8/79 | 51/66, 78/659 | 56/66, 50/659 | 7/9, 10/79 |
  | 36 (sz) | 54/66, 38/659 | 7/9, 23/79 | 7/9, 6/79 | 54/66, 56/659 | 56/66, 41/659 | 8/9, 7/79 |
  | 33 ratios only | 54/66, 40/659 | 7/9, 20/79 | 7/9, 6/79 | 57/66, 57/659 | 57/66, 41/659 | 8/9, 5/79 |
  | 36 normalised | 54/66, 37/659 | 7/9, 26/79 | 7/9, 7/79 | 55/66, 72/659 | 56/66, 40/659 | 8/9, 8/79 |
  | 34 abs only | 53/66, 41/659 | 8/9, 29/79 | 7/9, 8/79 | 53/66, 70/659 | 56/66, 53/659 | 7/9, 7/79 |

  The size columns barely shift between domains (median half-max radius of a true daughter 3.09 / 3.08 um, of a false one 4.90 / 4.94; the parent 4.00 / 4.20). LB history against the local intervals: img +0.006 (local +0.0037 [+0.0016, +0.0060]), prop +0.003 (+0.0039 [+0.0002, +0.0075]), vt -0.001 (interval across zero), nc +0.002 (+0.0031 [+0.0014, +0.0049]), nc35 +0.001, sz -0.002 (+0.0012, 44b6 across zero).

  How many divisions a public split holds (the user's question, 2026-09-25): local GT divisions 6bba 125 in 128 movies (0.98 per movie; 62 movies with none, 16 with 3-5), 44b6 26 in 71 (0.37; 50 with none). Drawing 40 movies (20% of a 200-movie test set) from the local ones, 4,000 draws: half-and-half 27 GT divisions (90% range 18-36), all-6bba 39 (29-50), the train mix 30 (21-40). On such a split one true division found is worth about +0.0008-0.0009 of score, three about +0.0026, five false ones removed about +0.0004-0.0007 (score = adj_J + 0.1 div_J, div_J pooled).
  The 33-column set tested the way the bench cross fits its gate (the user, 2026-09-25: "你先测一下33列呢"; `tools/bench/szgate33_boot.py`): 2 folds by the movie fold on the arm's counted 6bba forks with every counted 44b6 fork in both training folds, p > 0.03, per-movie kept counts, div_J with FN = GT - TP kept, adj_J from the REF rows, paired bootstrap over the 128 movies (approximate: the judge's FP forks are not the scorer's division_fp). 31 columns: TP kept 60 of 66, judge-FP kept 39; 36: 59, 39; 33: 60, 38. Paired: 36 vs 31 -0.0006 [-0.0024, +0.0010]; 33 vs 31 +0.0002 [-0.0017, +0.0021]; 33 vs 36 +0.0008 [-0.0006, +0.0025] -- none distinguishable. Under the other fold scheme above (folds pooled across domains) the same three sets read 56/50, 56/41, 57/41: the FP-kept count moves by 10 with the training-set composition alone, which is the size of every difference between the column sets.
- Conclusion: the strictness claim does not hold locally: at the same cut the size gate keeps as many true forks as the 31-column gate (54 of 66, 56 of 66 joint) and fewer false ones (38-41 against 48-50 of 659), and when trained on one domain and applied to the other it keeps more true forks (54 against 51 on 6bba from 44b6), so the transfer claim does not hold either; both size-column variants beat the 31-column set in every cell. The ratios-only set (33 columns) is at least as good as the 36 in every cell and keeps 1-3 more true forks cross-domain -- 1-3 forks out of 66, inside these tables' own noise, not a finding; fitted the way the cross fits, the three column sets are indistinguishable (every paired interval across zero), so no 33-column gate goes into the z chain. What the LB history shows is the user's point: every submission whose local interval excluded zero moved the LB in the same direction, and the two whose interval crossed zero (vt, sz) read flat or negative -- the LB's own noise is about +-0.002 and the public split's division count is small, so a change of a few forks per movie is a coin toss there. Decisions stay on the local paired intervals; the LB confirms direction only; nothing whose interval crosses zero goes up again. The -0.002 of the size gate is not evidence it cuts true divisions.

## 2026-09-25 divscore
- Hypothesis: divtrip's two triple scorers, trained on all 199 train movies and pickled, reproduce divtrip's out-of-fold quality (AUC 0.86 geometry / 0.88 with image) and hypz's S0 = -9.0 follows from the 1.15-discounted-triples-per-frame rule on the pooled logits.
- Scope: divtrip's pass 1 (every triple of the 199 F4hp caches, the positives + ~6,000 negatives per movie) for scorer A; biohub-divtrip's divtrip_candidates.csv (389,914 rows, 83 positives) for scorer B; both fitted out of fold by divtrip's 5 movie folds for the record and then on everything; HistGB max_iter 200, lr 0.05, min_samples_leaf 20, positives weighted to the negatives' mass.
- Experiment: `tools/bench/make_divscore.py` -> `divscore.py` (399 lines); kernel `faustine649/biohub-divscore` v1 (CPU, 12.2 min); output `bench_csv/divscore/divscore.pkl` (1.5 MB; keys A, B, geo, img, topk, s0, per_frame_rule, s0_oof_rule, geometry, image, n_train, auc_oof, version, hgb) and the log.
- Result: pass 1: 34,490,544 triples over 19,701 frames, sample 1,097,496 rows, 121 positives; scorer A out-of-fold AUC by fold 0.793 / 0.901 / 0.882 / 0.883 / 0.878, pooled 0.8605. Scorer B by fold 0.837 / 0.926 / 0.935 / 0.864 / 0.887, pooled 0.8830; out-of-fold logit p50 / p90 / p99 -10.74 / -9.58 / -6.43; S0 by the 1.15-per-frame rule -9.00 (hypz's -9.0). The full-fit scorer B puts 36,513 of its own pool's rows above -9.0 (all 83 positives) against 22,645 out of fold (58 positives) -- in-sample confidence, not a property of unseen movies. - Conclusion: the precondition holds in part. A division triple carries its own signal without the linker (scorer A 0.86, B 0.88 out of fold by movie; the v1 feature reading stands: the daughters straddle the mother, their centre of mass continues her velocity while neither daughter does, the sisters separate the next frame, neither has a cell behind it, both are smaller and brighter), a third of the reachable true divisions are the single top triple of their frame and half are in the top 5. But in absolute terms the linker-free scorer is weak where it matters: a division is one event in ~130 frame pairs, so at one candidate per frame the pool holds 38% of the GT divisions at 0.3% precision, 400 times below the shipped composition's 51% at the same recall -- the pipeline's precision comes from the graph (the ranker's single child, the orphan, the ILP's competition), not from the triple. A division variable per triple therefore cannot carry a decision by its own weight; it can only be a prior on top of the edge costs, and the two triple features the gate lacks (midpoint offset, centre-of-mass continuity) collapse inside the gate's population as cont did. What the pool route changes is the recall ceiling: the top-20 pool holds 55% of the GT divisions (83 of 151) against the pipeline's 42% delivered, because it does not need the ranker to have linked one daughter and left the other an orphan (the user's point, 2026-09-24: the ranker cannot see a division, so the orphan precondition is wrong whenever it links one wrong). Residue: the remaining test on this line is an ILP bench with a division variable z per pooled triple (top 5-20 per frame, weight from scorer B) replacing the 0.55 second-out-edge toll and the orphan patch; it needs edge probabilities for both of the triple's edges (the ranker's candidate set is narrower than 14 um), a hypx-style run on 128 movies, and its optimistic ceiling is about +20 divisions (div_J 0.30 -> ~0.40, ~+0.01 score) if the ILP keeps the pipeline's precision on the wider pool, against the forum's precedent that division work reads +-0.001-0.002 on the LB. The user's call.

No feature in the table encodes velocity continuity (q's or c1's motion against the mother's own velocity); the angle and the separation growth are the only motion terms, and the false forks do diverge (2.5 um per frame), so 'a passing cell at the mother's speed' is not the typical false fork in this table.

## 2026-09-22 swapz
- Hypothesis: the swap-site pair (7 um apart, no intensity dip, 1.6x bright) is either one large nucleus that the fixed-size detector target splits (the half-max region around the raw maximum is long along a -> b and flat in z; the z maxima through a and b sit on the same plane) or two nuclei stacked diagonally in z (the z maxima through a and through b differ by two or more planes).
- Scope: swapimg's 4,786 sites and crops (1,643 swap, 1,643 swap source, 1,500 baseline = a TP target with its nearest other primary), same smoothing; added per site: the half-max connected region around the raw maximum nearest A (extent along a -> b, in-plane perpendicular, in z; volume), the number of maxima of the smoothed z profile through a and through b (prominence 10% of the crop range) and the plane distance between their z maxima.
- Experiment: `tools/bench/make_swapz.py` (swapimg.py -> swapz.py, 326 lines); toy (an elongated nucleus reads ext_ab 8.9 against ext_perp 4.9, dz 0; two nuclei four planes apart read dz 4) passed; checkgen ok. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-swapz` v1, CPU 4.2 min, `SWAPZ OK`. Output swapz_sites.csv; log bench_csv/swapz/swapz_v1.log.
- Result: the half-max region is not a nucleus: it floods the crop at swap and baseline sites alike (extent along a -> b median 17.2 vs 13.3 um, z 13.0 = the full 9-plane crop in both; the crop's 20th percentile is inside cells in dense tissue), so the size measures say nothing. The z profiles do: planes between the z maximum through a and through b, swap sites 0: 22%, 1: 22%, 2: 18%, 3: 17%, 4: 12%, 5+: 10%; baseline pairs (two different cells 11.7 um apart) 0: 14%, 1: 18%, 2: 18%, 3: 19%, 4: 18%, 5+: 14%. Two or more z maxima through one column are rare in both (4-5% vs 2-3%). The dip along a -> b grows with the plane difference (median 0.002 at 0 planes, 0.008 at 2, 0.053 at 4); the false target is 3-6% brighter than the true child at every plane difference. By raw-maxima count: 295 swap sites with none within 6 um (median dz 1), 769 with one (dz 2), 579 with two or more (dz 2).
- Conclusion: the swap population is a mixture, not one thing: 44% have both detections' intensity columns peaking on the same or the adjacent plane (one object: a plateau or a large nucleus the detector splits) and 38% peak three or more planes apart (4.9 um and more: two objects stacked diagonally, the baseline's two-cell rate is 51%), with a faint dip only in the stacked ones. Neither half has a device on this side: the one-object half is the detector's target shape, the stacked half is the z placement the detections cannot resolve (swapplace). The size question (large nucleus vs plateau) is unanswered because the half-max region needs a background the crop percentile does not give in dense tissue; a threshold relative to the local minimum along the a -> b line, confined to 10 um, would answer it in another 4-minute run, but the answer changes the detector target, not the pipeline.
## 2026-09-22 swapdiv (offline)
- Hypothesis: the swap sites (one annotated centroid flanked by two detections 7 um apart, no intensity dip, 1.6x the baseline brightness) are cells in mitosis before the annotated division frame, so that the swaps, hypilp's merge losses (parents replacing fresh daughters) and divtime's early second tracks are one population on one time line and a mitosis-event unit (one node while the pair is a bar, a fork when the valley forms) is the device.
- Scope: the 1,995 swaps of rkedge_edges.csv (a source whose chosen edge is labelled false while a labelled true edge exists), the true child matched to its GT row through divmiss_prims (5 um), the GT track walked forward and backward along divmiss_gt.csv's parent rows up to 30 frames for an annotated division (n_kids >= 2). Control: 4,000 random true chosen edges, the same walk from their target.
- Experiment: pandas over the CSVs, no kernel (scratch, not kept).
- Result: all 1,995 swaps matched. The GT track divides within 3 / 10 / 30 frames AFTER the swap in 24 / 35 / 46 cases (1.2 / 1.8 / 2.3%); it divided within 3 / 10 / 30 frames BEFORE in 12 / 27 / 53 (0.6 / 1.4 / 2.7%); 1,896 have no division within 30 frames either way. Control: after 0.4 / 1.1 / 2.0%, before 0.6 / 1.4 / 2.8%.
- Conclusion: swap sites are not pre-division cells: the rate of an annotated division within 3 frames after a swap is 1.2% against 0.4% at random true edges, a threefold enrichment on a base of 24 cases, and within 10-30 frames the swap tracks divide no more often than any track. At most 20-30 of the 1,995 swaps (about 1.5%) can be the anaphase stage of an annotated division; the other 98% are something else. The mitosis-event unification is refuted for the swaps; hypilp's daughter losses and divtime's early tracks remain a division-side population of their own (about 125 divisions), separate from the swap population. Residue: what the 82% no-dip, 1.6x-bright, 7 um pairs are, if not mitotic, is still unmeasured; candidates are large interphase nuclei (a 7 um bar is a nucleus diameter) that the fixed-size detector target splits, or two nuclei stacked in z at the same xy (swapgeom: the pair is diagonal, 5.4 um xy and 3.7 um z).

Mutual = the true child was chosen by another source whose own true child is our false target. Control: every pair of chosen edges (i->j, i2->k) whose swapped alternative (i->k, i2->j) is also among the candidates, by the margin of summed p.
- Experiment: pandas over the CSV, no kernel (scratch, not kept).
- Result: swaps 1,995; true child taken by another source 702; mutual crossings 0. Chosen edge pairs with a swapped alternative among the candidates 1,025 (1,024 fully labelled): margin under 0.1 in 0, 0.1-0.2 in 2, 0.2-0.4 in 8, over 0.4 in 1,014; among the latter the chosen pair is both-true in 345 and the swapped pair in 5.
- Conclusion: the swaps are not close calls between two assignments: there is no mutual crossing in the population and the swapped alternative trails by more than 0.4 of summed p in 99% of the cases where it exists, with the chosen pair right 69 times more often than the swapped one. A tie-break cannot act where there is no tie. Consistent with swapfeat (every signal points to the false target) and swapplace (two detections around one annotated centroid).

## 2026-09-18 hmshoulder

Offline from the table: restricting the second point to the 4-10 um shell around the host keeps 46% of the hosts' c2 (32% of those within 3 um of g) while clean / dense singles fire in the same shell at 34% / 28%; c2 hits do not depend on the dip (19% with a dip, 18% monotone) nor on f4 having a local maximum at g (23%); A2 at hits 0.189 vs 0.191 at non-hits; f4 at g is 0.171 at hits vs 0.095 at non-hits.
- Conclusion: the shoulder cannot be located blind. Fitting the host's blob and reading what is left finds a second blob of amplitude 0.19 at 86% of the hosts AND at 72-82% of ordinary cells, in a random direction 10 um from the host; it lands within 3 um of the missed cell at 18% of the hosts, and no score separates the two populations (AUC 0.47-0.58), so a heatmap-side splitter has the same shape as blobsplit's raw-image one and no price at any recall. The fused map around a cell is not one blob plus one shoulder: the one-blob fit is 3 um wide against the 1.6 um training target, and the residual carries the map's own texture and the unannotated neighbours (controls' fires are an upper bound, but the hosts' 18% is the ceiling regardless). Two readings stand as residue. (1) The missed cells are NOT the dark-background class: 94% sit above the frame's 40th percentile (3x it at the median), only 24% dimmer than their hosts, yet their response is 3x smaller (0.105 against 0.317) -- the miss is not a brightness miss, so retraining the background weight (option C's premise) does not address it. (2) At 45% of the missed cells one of the four single maps has a local maximum within 3 um at the 0.05 floor (b2 29%, f4 12%): the mean map erases maxima the branches have; whether those single-map maxima can be admitted is a base-rate question (how many such floor-0.05 maxima a single map has where no cell is) that hplace did not ask and this kernel did not price. Closed: heatmap-side blind placement of the missed cell by residual or two-blob fit.

- Conclusion: The raw image carries no placement signal for these cells: at the annotated centroid of a rescue peak the intensity is 0.1-0.2 over the local median (a detected cell: 0.6), and a raw maximum of any substance sits within 3 um of it for 18% of the refused peaks and 4% of the linked ones. Re-placing on the raw maximum is a ~5 um random move at either scale: it lifts the refused class from 11% to 31% within 3 um, drops the linked class from 55% to 18% and real detections from 81% to 45%, the same displacement for all. The linked rescue peaks sit at 2.9 um because the normalised heatmap put them there, not because the raw image shows a cell there; the refused ones cannot be corrected from raw intensity. Closed: raw-image re-placement of dim peaks (maximum or centroid, fine or coarse smoothing). Residue, unpriced: a heatmap-side placement of the rescue peaks (a vertex fit or a learned offset on the normalised map).

## 2026-09-17 lntrace
- Hypothesis: the 256 linkable GT edges of the rescue peaks admitted at score >= 0.20 (lnpersist) die at a nameable gate: the ranker's pair map (no candidate pair), the 0.48 floor (the ranker sees the same dim cell the detector missed and scores the edge low), the ILP's competition (the shipped neighbour already linked elsewhere at high p), the short filter (the peak's node dropped), or the scorer's one-to-one match (another final node nearer to the annotated cell).
- Scope: lnbench's harness with the single arm LN20 (128 6bba movies, REF anchors); per movie after the arm's solve and patches, one row per linkable GT edge of every annotated rescue peak (the peak within 7 um of a GT node whose GT neighbour at t-1 or t+1 has a shipped primary within 7 um), read against the arm's final graph, the pair map and the seed map.
- Experiment: `lntrace.py` from `tools/bench/make_lntrace.py` (lntrace block: `ln_trace` categories A_below_tau / B_not_candidate / C_below_floor / D_q_dropped / D2_s_dropped / E_competitor / E2_no_link / F_q_unmatched / G_tp with the competitor's p, nature and distance; `lt_summary`; lntrace_edges.csv). Toy test `scratchpad/test_lntrace.py` (six peaks, one per gate, plus the F case) passed; checkgen ok. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-lntrace` v1, CPU, lnbench's sources, ~3 h.
- Result: v1 COMPLETE, 128/128, `LNTRACE OK`, both round-2 anchors held (`bench_csv/lntrace/lntrace_v1.log`, lntrace_edges.csv 596 rows = every linkable GT edge of an annotated rescue peak at any score). The 256 edges of the peaks admitted at >= 0.20 (149 peaks): B_not_candidate 24 (14 prev / 10 next; peak score med 0.230, d_gt 6.10 um); C_below_floor 128 (63 / 65; score 0.241, d_gt 5.66, ranker p median 0.066, quantiles 10/25/50/75/90% = 0.010 / 0.026 / 0.066 / 0.186 / 0.310; shipped neighbour's detection score med 0.293 against 0.44 for annotated nodes overall); D_q_dropped 19 (p med 0.684, node absent from the final graph); E_competitor 1 (p 0.558 vs 0.720, the competitor a second detection of the same cell); E2_no_link 1; F_q_unmatched 9 (p 0.838, d_gt 5.85); G_tp 74 (36 / 38; p med 0.879, d_gt 2.82). 64 of the 149 admitted annotated peaks got at least one edge. The 340 edges of the peaks below 0.20 (A_below_tau) have p med 0.140 and d_gt 5.44. Net edge_J of the arm in lnbench: +0.0003 (about 34 edges) against the 74 true edges taken here.
- Conclusion: the ranker is the gate. Half the linkable edges (128 of 256) never reach the ILP because the ranker's p sits at 0.07 in the median and below 0.31 for nine in ten, far from the 0.48 floor, so no floor move reaches them; only 2 edges are lost to ILP competition and 9 to a nearer duplicate node. The edges that do pass are the peaks placed within 2.8 um of the annotated cell; the ones refused sit 5.7 um from it and join a dim shipped neighbour (score 0.29), i.e. a dim-to-dim, badly placed pair, which is exactly the population the ranker was trained to refuse (rkedge's dim-target near-ties), and some of those "annotated" peaks may be noise peaks that happen to fall within 7 um of a cell. The 74 true edges gained became about 34 net because the 11,300 admitted noise peaks take links and displace true ones elsewhere. Pushing the 128 through would need the ranker retrained to accept dim, off-centre pairs, for a ceiling of +0.001 edge_J; the rescue line stays closed.

The edge term is untouched (the gate only removes fork edges). To ship: the submission script must compute the same 11 features at every fork (31 min of crops per 128 movies), and the 67 44b6 training forks carry NaN in the image columns, so on the hidden 44b6 half the gate applies contrast splits learned on 6bba; a 44b6 fork table with image features (fk44f4's harness + the forkimg block) would close that gap before the submission.

- Hypothesis: at an annotated cell the detector missed (no F4HP primary within 7 um; 2,164 such edge endpoints, 38% of REF's missed edges) the nearest primary's blob in the RAW image differs from a single nucleus (larger component at thresholds relative to the peak, elongated, the peak off the component's intensity centroid, a second local intensity maximum), so that a splitter could add the hidden cell; separability (AUC) and the false-fire rate on clean and on crowded single nuclei decide whether a splitter can clear the base rate (hosts ~2.3% of primaries; a wrong split creates a swap site, ~1 edge at risk; a right one recovers ~2 edges; break-even ~2 wrong per fix).
- Scope: 128 6bba movies, GT geffs + hparacache's fdet_F4hp_ primaries (score >= 0.15). Sites: host = the nearest primary within 12 um of a missed annotated cell (its position g kept for diagnostics only); ctrl = a primary within 2.5 um of an annotated cell with no other primary within 8 um and no other annotated cell within 10 um (25 per movie); dense = a matched primary with another primary within 8 um (25 per movie). Raw crop 10 um half-width around the detection, smoothed (0.6 / 1.5 / 1.5 voxels): intensity, background (median), contrast, gradient, texture; at 0.5 / 0.7 of the peak above background the detection's component: volume, longest axis, axis ratio, extent, offset of the detection from the intensity-weighted centroid, solidity, z extent; local maxima inside the 0.5 component merged within 3 um: count, second/first height, distance, z offset. Diagnostics at hosts: I(g)/I(d), the dip along d -> g, a raw local maximum within 2.5 um of g. HistGB stack, GroupKFold by movie; per-feature AUCs host vs ctrl and host vs dense; false-fire at 30 / 50 / 70% host recall with wrong-splits-per-fix.
