Host diagnostics (the missed cell g): d(host, g) median 8.12 um; I(g)/I(d) median 0.750 (p25 0.566, p75 0.884); the dip along d -> g median 1.283, below 0.9 in 33%; a raw local maximum within 2.5 um of g in 7%. Feature medians host / clean / dense and AUC host-vs-clean, host-vs-dense: I_bg 462 / 200 / 316, 0.728 / 0.615; contrast 0.41 / 1.81 / 1.10, 0.763 / 0.686; vol_50 1,717 / 1,029 / 1,159 um^3, 0.656 / 0.616; ax_long_50 5.96 / 4.73 / 5.20, 0.705 / 0.616; extent_50 25.0 / 19.7 / 22.0, 0.706 / 0.618; off_centroid_50 5.88 / 1.83 / 4.22 um, 0.697 / 0.616; ax_ratio_50 1.46 / 1.46 / 1.53, 0.501 / 0.550; n_max 5 / 2 / 3, 0.709 / 0.609; max2_ratio 1.12 / 0.95 / 1.06, 0.642 / 0.533; tex_cv 0.11 / 0.15 / 0.14, 0.660 / 0.616; solidity, gradient, z extent 0.52-0.67. Stack (GroupKFold by movie): AUC host vs all singles 0.737, vs clean 0.768, vs dense 0.698; at 30 / 50 / 70% host recall the stack fires on 7.0 / 16.4 / 30.3% of clean and 9.0 / 22.0 / 41.7% of dense singles = ~16 / 24 / 32 wrong splits per hidden cell found (break-even ~2; hosts ~1.6% of primaries).
- Conclusion: the hidden cell is not visible in the raw image as a separate object: at 93% of the sites the smoothed raw intensity has no local maximum within 2.5 um of it, it reads 25% dimmer than the host, and the path from the host to it has no dip (median 1.28). What the shape features pick up is the surroundings, not a second nucleus: hosts sit in brighter, denser background (contrast 0.41 against 1.81) with larger, off-centre thresholded components that span neighbours; the separation is AUC 0.70-0.77 and a splitter would make 16 wrong splits per cell found at 30% recall. The mask / raw-image route to the 2,164 undetected-endpoint edges is closed together with the mask route to the swaps (maskfeat): in both geometries the raw intensity does not carry the second nucleus at this resolution. Restricting a rule to movies above an N_pred threshold (10k-40k) never turns it positive (score < 0.20: −0.0037 to −0.0009).
- Conclusion: on 6bba no ground-truth-free description of a node gets its annotated rate under the deletion break-even: the lowest-scoring tenth of the primaries still sits on annotated cells at 0.97% (a fifth of the average), short components at 0.95%, track ends at 2.4%; every rule priced loses edge_J faster than the node term pays, the best is +0.0002 of adj_J. The break-even is NOT a constant and annotation density does NOT help: deleting a node earns 0.1 J / N_est and a deleted annotated cell costs about 2 / (annotated edges), so gain over loss is about 0.045 J / k with k = the deleted bucket's annotated rate relative to the movie's average; the density cancels, and a bucket pays only when it is 25 times less likely to be a cell than average (k < 0.04). Our least cell-like bucket has k about 0.18; measured, the rules lose MOST on the sparsest movies (few annotated edges make each lost one expensive) and are near zero on the densest. So the earlier reading that a 0.77%-annotated domain would be 12 times cheaper was wrong, and the inferred node-term route of the public 0.947 pipeline needs its deleted nodes to be ~96% non-cells; nothing we can name comes close. Harness note: the official FP count corresponds to edges whose SOURCE node is matched (4,572 by the ledger against 4,305), not "either endpoint" (9,026).

## 2026-09-16 mergejudge
- Hypothesis: the 9,598 hypcache parent pairs with one annotated end (the population hmerge's loss came from) split, on REF's own final graph, into a part a merge can only lose on and a part it fixes: (a) the annotated detection A already carries its GT in-edge and all its GT out-edges while its pair mate B has an in-edge and an out-edge of its own to other nodes (B is a real unannotated cell: after a merge one node carries one in-edge and one track loses its edges), (b) the merged point, the midpoint, sits farther than 7 um (the scorer's radius) from A's GT node while A itself is within it (B is a ghost peak on A's far side: a merge moves A out of its match), versus (c) A misses a GT edge that B carries (the swap signature: a merge hands the edge to the merged node). The sizes of (a), (b), (c) decide whether any merge rule on this population can be net positive; (a) + (b) far above (c) reproduces hmerge's sign.
- Scope: dupsup's harness (F4HP, REF = round 2, hard anchors, no arms), 128 6bba movies; for every hypcache parent pair with children within 8.5 um: labels at 5 um as mergefeat (one cell / two cells / one end / unannotated), the annotated end A (the closer one when both match one GT node), distances A / B / midpoint to the GT node, whether REF's final graph carries A's GT in-edge and each GT out-edge, whether B carries one of those GT neighbours, B's in / out edges to other nodes and its chain length backward / forward (up to 5 frames), whether A and B both have in-edges from different nodes or both have out-edges; a summary per label with the shares of (a) / (b) / (c) and the agreement of the labels with mergefeat's.

One-cell pairs: A alive 0.778, B alive 0.707; B a track of its own 0.486; both full tracks 0.272; A right 0.581; A missing a GT edge 0.419, of those B carries it 0.834 = 407 pairs, but A alive in only 177 (A dead 230: the scorer at 7 um matches B, median 4.42 um from the GT node, so those edges are already TP); B carries a GT neighbour while A is right 271 (a parallel duplicate track, its edges FP); midpoint 1.65 um from the GT node, never beyond 5. Two-cell pairs: both full tracks 0.689, A right 0.892. Unannotated: B a track of its own 0.389, both full 0.399, B dead 0.307. No isolated live node exists in any class (the short filter removes them). Rules on REF's graph (share firing: one cell / one end / two cells / unannotated; and of one-cell fixes / of one-end case 2): "edges shared out between A and B" 0.013 / 0.006 / 0 / 0.010 (fixes 0.029, case 2 0); "one end has no edge" 0.503 / 0.292 / 0.149 / 0.377 (fixes 0.565, case 2 0.105); "not both full tracks" 0.728 / 0.507 / 0.311 / 0.601 (fixes 0.850, parallel duplicates 0.277, case 2 0.207, one-end A right 0.406).
- Conclusion: hmerge's loss channel is case 2 as the graph shows it: in half of the one-end pairs the mate B carries a persistent track of its own, and a merge leaves one node for two tracks. Whether B is an unannotated neighbour cell or a persistent duplicate peak of A the labels cannot tell: among the pairs known to be one cell, B carries its own track in 48.6% as well, so "a track of its own" means a persistent detection, not a proven cell. Case 3's displacement is small (the midpoint leaves the 7 um radius in 5.5% of one-end pairs). The fixable swaps are few: at most 177 one-cell pairs whose annotated end is alive on a wrong track (the 230 with a dead annotated end are already scored through the other detection), plus 271 parallel duplicates whose FP edges a merge would remove; the oracle ceiling of merging exactly those is about +0.009 edge_J. The both-full-tracks pattern marks 69% of two-cell and 79% of case-2 pairs against 27% of one-cell pairs, so a merge vetoed on "both full tracks" keeps 85% of the fixes and 21% of case 2; the 21% that survive share a predecessor (a predicted fork) or sit at track ends. What this buys on the bench needs a two-pass kernel (solve, decide the merges from the graph, merge, re-solve); the count arithmetic (about 300 fixable edges against about 950 surviving case-2 merges) does not promise a positive sign, and the maskfeat / mergefeat classifiers are not the instrument.

- Conclusion: the parents' damage is indirect. Three quarters of the lost true edges (185 of 247) join two children that are both still present: the parents act as extra candidate targets and pull the solve away from the children's true edges around them, not at them; the merged-division case (constraint 1) accounts for 2 lost edges and 1.8% of the selected parents, so it is not the mechanism; the chain in the children's weakness is real but shallow (median best in 0.37 vs 0.53), so a 'weak children' gate at 0.5 still keeps 89% of what the solver already picks. The ceiling is now priced: the parents gain 43 true edges on these 16 movies (0.37% of the 11,597 carried), about +0.003 edge_J over the bench if every loss were removed, against -0.004 as run. Residue: a parent restricted to the edges its children could have taken (u -> P only when u -> a or u -> b is a candidate, likewise out) removes the pull on unrelated cells and is the one constraint the ledger points at; it caps at that +0.003.

## 2026-09-14 skipilp
- Hypothesis: span-2 candidate edges (i at t, j at t+2) offered to the SAME ILP the shipped linker solves, weighted by their own out-of-fold selector, recover the annotated 2/3-frame interior gaps that bridging track ends after the solve could not (bridgerank: 423 of the 511 gaps ran on through a wrong link at the missing frame and were never (end, start) pairs), because inside the solve a skip competes with the wrong consecutive link for i's out-slot and j's in-slot under the shipped costs; a chosen skip realised as two edges through a node inserted at t+1 (the NMS-suppressed candidate near the midpoint when one exists, else the midpoint) gains edges on the shipped composition (REF + joint gate).
- Scope: 128 6bba train movies, dupsup's harness (DET_SRC F4HP, +BIDIR fold rankers, floor 0.48, disappearance 1.5, DIV_W 0.55, shipped post-link patches incl. the span-1 gap close, gate6 / joint fork gates, official scorer). Labels: i matched (5 um) to a GT node with grandchildren, 1 iff j matched one of them; the middle GT node's matched / missed flag. Two fold HistGB(300) models by movie, out of fold. Arms, each a fresh full solve: SK50 / SK80 (weight p, offered at p >= 0.50 / 0.80), SK50H / SK30H (weight 0.5 p, offered at 0.50 / 0.30); a skip leaving a node with another out-edge is dropped. Ceiling before the run: bridgerank counted 511 annotated 2/3-frame gaps, at most ~1,500 edges of 113,362 scored (+0.013 adj_J if every one lands with no node cost).
- Experiment: `skipilp.py` from `tools/bench/make_skipilp.py` (dupsup.py + the skip block, stage A2, solve_one(skip=...)), toy test `scratchpad/test_skipilp.py` (proposals, features, labels, middle flag, insertion incl. snap and fork-drop) passed, checkgen ok; tracksdata's ILPSolver builds flow constraints per node with no consecutive-frame check (`_ilp_solver.py` read), so a t -> t+2 edge is an ordinary edge to it. Sites where the four peaks sit within 1.5 um of each other: d -> A median f4 2.13 (swap, n 419) / 1.03 (control, n 1,822); spread over 3 um: 3.18 (swap, n 789) / 2.19 (control, n 657). - Conclusion: no single map places better than the mean: at swap sites the four sit within 0.14 um of each other at the median and which one is nearest per site is spread evenly (20-30% each), so a "use map X in dense regions" rule has nothing to pick; even an oracle choosing the best map per site (which needs the answer) gains 0.65 um and leaves the median at 2.0 um. The placement error at swap sites is shared by all four networks, and all four see two maxima within 7 um of the one annotated centroid at 68-88% of these sites against 17-22% at ordinary cells: what is wrong there is upstream of the fusion, in the image or the annotation. Choosing among the existing heatmaps is not a placement lever. Where the peaks are relative to each other (v2): at half the swap sites all four maps put their peak in one place, and that place is still 2.1 um from A; at the other half they split between two places 4 um apart, A sits 2.5 um from the nearer one, and the mean map's peak coincides with one of the four maps' peaks (0.33 um) rather than landing between them (7%). Averaging does not manufacture the swap-site position; the four networks either share one displaced centre or divide between two, and the annotated centroid is off both. The one un-run measurement is whether those second maxima are real unannotated nuclei (sparse annotation) or split responses to one nucleus; the score cannot tell them apart either, since only the annotated one is scored.

- Conclusion: merging every primary pair with saddle >= 0.9 loses 708 true edges and adds 236 false ones, and the node term (5% fewer nodes, worth about +0.004 adj_J) does not cover it. The base rate decides: the bench has 1,805 swap edges in total, and the rule merged 118,820 pairs on these movies, so even if every swap were fixed it would be at most 1.5% of the merges; the other 98.5% are pairs the linker was tracking correctly, and hsaddle's 4% two-cell rate is 4% of a very large population. HM80 (twice the merges) is not run. A saddle-keyed merge cannot be applied blind; if it has a use it is as a candidate signal restricted to the sites where the linker is already uncertain, which is a different experiment.

## 2026-09-12 hmerge
- Hypothesis: replacing each pair of hpara primaries whose heatmap saddle is at least 0.9 (or 0.8) within 9.5 um by one detection at the segment mass centroid gives a detection set on which the shipped linker loses fewer swap edges than it gains false merges, i.e. edge_J rises on the round-2 bench.
- Scope: the 140 hpara movies (128 6bba scored by the bench + 12 44b6), all frames, the shipped F4 heatmap pass anchored frame by frame against the shipped fdet_F4_ cache; only primaries (score >= 0.15) are paired and merged, the sub-threshold pool is untouched; each primary merges at most once, highest saddle first; the merged point takes max(score) and goes through the same `_refine` as every detection. This kernel only writes the caches; the score needs both edge heads re-run on the merged points (the pair set changes, so cached (t, i, j) rows do not join) and then the bench.
- Experiment: `hmerge.py` from `tools/bench/make_hmerge.py` (hparacache.py with the caching loop replaced), kernel `faustine649/biohub-hmerge` v1, T4, sources: support pack, dctrain-175 weights, xiaoleilian unet3d weights (x2), cell-tracking, fusecache + fuse6bba (anchor), competition. Synthetic test `scratchpad/test_hmerge.py` (a ridge pair merges to the ridge centre with the higher score, a two-Gaussian pair does not, sub-threshold peaks are never paired, three primaries on one ridge merge only once) passed. Outputs: `fdet_F4hm90_<name>.npz`, `fdet_F4hm80_<name>.npz`, per-movie and total counts of primaries, pairs, merges.
- Result: v1 T4 203.5 min, 140 movies, all frames, `HMERGE OK`; anchor: every frame of every movie reproduced the shipped `fdet_F4_` cache exactly. Primaries 2,596,494; pairs of primaries within 9.5 um 1,515,680. HM90 merged 138,903 (5.35% of primaries, 9.16% of pairs); HM80 merged 239,306 (9.22% / 15.79%). By dataset: 6bba (128 movies) HM90 5.30% of primaries, HM80 9.06%; 44b6 (12) HM90 5.67%, HM80 10.24%. Per-movie HM90 rate min 0.33%, median 2.94%, max 16.33%. Log `bench_csv/hmerge/hmerge_v1.log`; caches in the kernel output (`fdet_F4hm90_`, `fdet_F4hm80_`, 140 each).
- Conclusion: the caches exist and sit on the shipped heatmap pass. The merge rate among all near primary pairs (9.2% at s >= 0.9) is above hsaddle's two-cell control (4%) and below its random primary pairs (14%), so the rule removes 5.3% of primaries whose composition (one-cell ridges vs two real neighbours) the bench has to settle: whether edge_J rises or falls is the hmbench read-out (heads first: ephmcache / ep2hmcache on the merged points).

## 2026-09-12 hsaddle
- Hypothesis: the fused F4 heatmap, unlike the raw image (swapimg), separates the two peaks of a swap pair from the two peaks of two real neighbouring cells: at a swap site the heatmap between the peaks is a continuous ridge (saddle near 1), between two annotated cells it dips; if so, a merge rule keyed on the saddle has a discriminator and the merged point (the mass centroid along the pair) lands nearer the annotated centroid than either detection (3.6-4.6 um).

Sites: 1,643 swap pairs (frame t+1: true-child detection a, false target b, GT child A), 511 control pairs (two annotated nodes within 9.5 um in one frame, both with a distinct primary within 5 um: two cells by construction), 1,348 random primary pairs 6-9.5 um apart drawn from the swap frames. Measures on the pooled 1.625 um grid: h at a, b, A; saddle = min(h along a->b) / min(h_a, h_b); number of blobs along a->b (dips of 10% of min(h_a, h_b)); distance between the two peaks' mass centroids at R 4 / 5 um and whether they fall under the 4 um NMS; the segment mass centroid's distance to A.

Output: `hsaddle_sites.csv` and a summary by kind.

## 2026-09-12 dupsup
- Hypothesis: suppressing the second detection of every primary pair closer than R um (greedy by score, 3D) before the ILP removes the two-detections-one-cell ambiguity behind the 1,643 swap edges and gains edge_J on the shipped composition, at R between 5.5 and 7.5 um where annotated nuclei are almost never that close (154 pairs within 7 um among 113,121 GT nodes) and GT sisters rarely are (9.6% under 6.5 um).
- Scope: 128 6bba train movies, round-2 harness (BASE fold rankers, hpara points, floor 0.48, DIV_W 0.55); each arm is a full re-solve with the suppressed primaries withheld from the ILP's candidate edges and dropped from the solved nodes; features, head cache and (t, i, j) indexing untouched, so a kept detection stays where it was (3.6-4.6 um off the centroid). The scorer rewards under-detection without a clamp (adj = J (1 - 0.1 ratio), REF ratio -0.023): removing 12% of nodes buys about +0.01 of adj_J from the node term alone, so edge_J (plain micro Jaccard) is the identity effect and is bootstrapped separately.
- Experiment: `dupsup.py` from `tools/bench/make_dupsup.py` (bridgerank.py with the bridge collection, model and replay removed; `_dup_keep` greedy suppression; `solve_one(keep=...)`; arms re-solved in stage B as hparabench's dw35 was). Arms SUP55 / SUP65 / SUP75 = R 5.5 / 6.5 / 7.5 um. Each arm's forks judged, gate6 and joint gates trained out of fold on its own forks, paired bootstrap of arm + joint against REF + joint on score, adj_J and edge_J. Kernel `faustine649/biohub-dupsup` v1, CPU, rkedge's 16 sources. Toy test `scratchpad/test_dupsup.py` (greedy mask, ties, empty frames, the candidate-edge filter and the node drop) passed. Anchors: REF 55/237/70 adj_J 0.9146, REF + joint 0.9433. Outputs: `dupsup_REF_F4HP.csv`, `dupsup_arm_<arm>.csv`, `forks_<arm>.csv`.
- Result: 276.5 min CPU, 128/128, `DUPSUP OK`; anchors held (REF 55/237/70 adj_J 0.9146 score 0.9298, REF + joint 0.9433, ANCHOR_D187 0.9204). Outputs in `bench_csv/dupsup/`.

  | arm | primaries suppressed | candidate edges withheld | forks | div tp/fp/fn (ungated) | edge_J | node_r | adj_J | score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF | 0 | 0 | 6,709 | 55/237/70 | 0.9118 | -0.0231 | 0.9146 | 0.9298 |
  | SUP55 | 37,979 (1.7%) | 50,245 | 6,251 | 54/215/71 | 0.9092 | -0.0335 | 0.9129 | 0.9288 |
  | SUP65 | 114,990 (5.1%) | 143,224 | 5,671 | 51/196/74 | 0.9003 | -0.0573 | 0.9059 | 0.9218 |
  | SUP75 | 264,597 (11.8%) | 314,512 | 4,583 | 43/159/82 | 0.8781 | -0.1071 | 0.8874 | 0.9025 |

  Edge deltas against REF from the per-movie CSVs: SUP55 TP -303, FP -20 (edge_J down in 59 movies, up in 25); SUP65 TP -1,240, FP +65 (87 / 20); SUP75 TP -3,801, FP +19 (99 / 17). True edges lost per suppressed primary 0.008 / 0.011 / 0.014; the per-movie edge_J loss correlates with the movie's suppressed share at -0.45 / -0.74 / -0.80. With the joint gate, arm + joint against REF + joint (2,000 draws): SUP55 score -0.0028 [-0.0050, -0.0008], adj_J -0.0016 [-0.0026, -0.0007], edge_J -0.0025 [-0.0035, -0.0015]; SUP65 -0.0116 / -0.0087 / -0.0115; SUP75 -0.0318 / -0.0272 / -0.0337 (all intervals exclude zero). The node term moved the way the metric promises (adj_J minus edge_J: REF +0.0028, SUP75 +0.0093) and did not cover the edge loss at any radius.
- Conclusion: Suppressing the lower-scored member of every primary pair under 5.5 / 6.5 / 7.5 um loses true edges monotonically (-303 / -1,240 / -3,801) and recovers nothing on the swap side (FP barely moves), so the pairs the swaps live in are not removable duplicates, or the survivor does not inherit the identity; either way the claim "a pair of primaries under 7 um is one scored cell" is refuted by the score. The inference behind it was wrong: 154 both-annotated pairs within 7 um among 113,121 GT nodes is rare because annotation is 9.7% sparse (both members of a close pair are annotated with probability about 1%), not because nuclei are; the base rate of a neighbour within 7 um is about 3%, and 5.5 um suppression already removes 1.7% of primaries. A local replay of the greedy mask at the 1,643 swap sites: at 5.5 um it removes the true-child detection in 15% and the false target in 2% (both survive in 83%); at 7.5 um 53% / 15% / 34%, after which the GT child's nearest survivor is the false target in 54% and the true child in 40% (another detection 3%, none within 7 um 2%). So even at 7.5 um the identity flips in only about half the sites while the whole movie pays. Residue: nothing at the detection-set level that the head cache allows (a midpoint merge would destroy two real cells wherever suppression did); a swap fix needs the detections at BOTH frames placed within about 1.5 um of Ultrack's centroid, i.e. a placement-aware detector (an offset head or a wider heatmap centroid), GPU, unpriced.

- Scope: 128 6bba train movies; 1,643 swap sites at t+1 (GT child A, true-child detection a, false-target detection b), the same 1,643 swap sources at t (GT parent, detection a), and 1,500 baseline sites (a random TP edge's target A, its detection a, and the nearest other primary b). A greedy suppression of the hpara primaries would remove 1.7% at 5.5 um, 5.1% at 6.5, 11.8% at 7.5.
- Conclusion: The swap site is one annotated centroid flanked by two detections about 7 um apart, each 3.6-4.6 um off it, the intensity flat across the pair (no dip in 82%, no raw peak at the centroid in 83%), the false target as bright as the true child. The profile test cannot separate one nucleus from two touching ones at this smoothing (the baseline's 11.7 um neighbour pairs read as one-peaked in 75% too), so the image does not decide the biology; the scoring rule does: annotated nuclei are almost never within 7 um of each other, so a pair of primaries under about 7 um is one scored cell carrying two detections, whichever way Ultrack drew it. The operational fix proposed here, one detection per such pair before the ILP, was tested the same day (dupsup) and loses edges at every radius; the sentence 'annotated nuclei are almost never within 7 um of each other, so a pair of primaries under about 7 um is one scored cell' is wrong: with 9.7% annotation the both-annotated pair count says nothing about physical spacing (see dupsup's Conclusion).

## 2026-09-12 swapplace
- Hypothesis: the 1,640 swaps (source linked to a false target while its annotated child was left below the floor) are a detection-placement problem, not a linking one: in these cases the detections sit far from the annotated centroids, so which of two nearby detections "is" the annotated cell is decided by sub-plane z differences, and the linker's nearest choice and the scorer's nearest match disagree.
- Scope: offline, no kernel; the swap pairs of `bench_csv/rkedge/rkedge_edges.csv` joined to `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/` (every primary with its nearest two GT nodes) and `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_gt.csv` (GT coordinates; GT z is integer planes). 1,643 swaps with coordinates. Baseline = all 108,983 primaries matched at 5 um.
- Experiment: scratch pandas scripts (not kept). Measured: the GT parent-to-child displacement against the detected one; the z error of detections against GT, split by whether another primary lies within 4 um xy and 1-3 planes; the distance of the source, the true child k and the false target j to the GT child A; whether j's nearest GT node is A.
- Result: GT parent-to-child |dz| median 1.62 um (p25 0.00, 13.3% at 2.5 um or more), xy 1.22 um, i.e. the annotated cell barely moves; the detections put the true child 3.42 um away in z from the source and the false target 0.74. Detection-to-GT offset: all matched primaries median 1.24 um (13.8% over 2.5 um), TP-edge sources 1.16; swap sources 3.57 um (71.2% over 2.5), swap true children 3.64 (73.2%). |z error|: primaries without a neighbour within 4 um xy 0.71 um median (p90 2.20); with a z-stacked neighbour (1-3 planes) 1.57 (p90 3.54), 1.0% of matched primaries; swap source 1.67, swap child 1.63. In 56.4% of swaps the false target's nearest GT node is A itself (j 4.63 um from A, k 3.64; j and k 5.35 um apart in xy and 2.3 planes in z); in 37.1% j is the closer detection to A in 3D. When j's nearest GT node is another cell (n = 5) it is 7.3 um from A.
- Conclusion: The swap edges sit where the detector's placement is three times worse than usual (3.6 um from the annotated centroid against 1.2), typically two detections about 5 um apart around one annotated cell, each 3.6-4.6 um off it; the annotated cell moved about 2 um, and which detection the scorer calls "the cell" turns on a fraction of a z plane. No feature of a pair can carry that, which is why the ranker, the image head, smoothness and normalisation all failed (swapfeat, crowdnorm). The lever is placement in dense regions, upstream of every linking stage; ceiling about 1,640 FN plus their mirrored FP, roughly +0.03 adj_J, the largest measured. Residue: whether the raw image is bimodal at these sites (two nuclei) or unimodal (one nucleus, two heatmap peaks on its shoulders) decides between a proximity-adjusted centroid target for the detector and a merge-and-re-place rule; a CPU kernel reading image crops at the 1,643 sites would settle it. Not run.

## 2026-09-12 crowdnorm
- Hypothesis: the ranker's weakness in crowded frames is a feature-scale problem, so per-movie or per-frame normalisation of its inputs, or a model fitted on crowded rows only, ranks the true child first more often there.
- Scope: offline, no kernel; the 184,174 labelled candidate pairs of `bench_csv/rkedge/rkedge_edges.csv` (128 6bba movies), HistGB(300, lr 0.05, msl 20) on the 18 harness columns plus the head's three, 2-fold by movie, out of fold. Crowded = source has 3 or more candidates (20,130 sources with a true child). Metric: share of sources whose top-ranked candidate is the true child (what the ILP mostly takes), and AUC. Local fits reproduce the ranking, not the calibration.
- Experiment: scratch scikit-learn script (not kept). Arms: raw features; every feature z-scored within its movie; geometry divided by the movie's median pair distance; geometry scaled by n_curr^(1/3); a model trained on crowded rows only; crowded rows weighted x3.
- Result: top-1 on crowded sources: raw 0.9311, z-scored 0.9304, / median d 0.9308, x n_curr^(1/3) 0.9312, crowded-only 0.9312, x3 weight 0.9311; sparse sources 0.9907 in every arm; AUC on crowded rows 0.9836-0.9839. The 1,387 crowded failures: the true child crosses 2.5 um or more in z in 65.9%, has p < 0.48 in 89.9%; the picked target crosses in 20.3%.
- Conclusion: Normalisation, whether per movie or per frame, and crowd-specific training change nothing (all arms within 0.001 of each other on 20,130 crowded sources). The crowded deficit (93.1% against 99.1%) is the z-stacked pairs of swapfeat concentrated where cells are dense, not a scale mismatch between sparse and crowded regions. Residue: none on the feature side; the failing pairs need a signal that says the cell moved two planes, which no column, the image head included, carries.

## 2026-09-12 edgeledger
- Hypothesis: some bucket of the shipped arm's 5,698 missed edges is recoverable by a post-link rule on the final graph (joining a free track end to a free track start below the ILP floor; extending a track one frame past an undetected start or end), i.e. has a precision above the Jaccard break-even (about 0.48: one added false edge costs J, one added true edge gains 1).
- Scope: offline, no kernel; `bench_csv/rkedge/rkedge_edges.csv` (labelled candidate pairs = sources matched to an annotated GT node with children; in_C_ilp = ILP edge, in_C = final edge) and `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_gt.csv` (every GT node with its nearest primary). Freeness of a target is a lower bound (an unannotated predecessor is invisible). Extension precision is estimated from GT structure only (a track start whose GT parent is undetected against a GT start inside the annotated range), not from a run.
- Experiment: scratch pandas scripts (not kept).
- Result: FN with both endpoints detected 3,534 = 2,438 below the 0.48 floor + 1,096 above it; the other 2,164 of the 5,698 have no candidate pair (an endpoint undetected or beyond the 10 um gate). Post-link ledger on labelled pairs: the short filter removes 169 true / 23 false ILP edges (whole fragments, neither endpoint survives); the patch adds 44 true / 95 false direct pairs. Above the floor: 169 removed by the short filter, 480 with source and target both free in the ILP solution (p median 0.69; source has an ILP predecessor in 26.5%, is in the final graph in 10.8%: fragments too short to pay the 1.5 disappearance), 168 whose source took another edge (that edge false in 96.4%, p 0.60 vs 0.53), the rest target taken. Below the floor (p median 0.16), partitioned by what the graph did instead: 1,640 (67.3%) the source took a false edge (these ARE the swaps of swapfeat, not a separate bucket; their true edge has p median 0.125); 37 the source took another true edge (a division); 761 the source is a dead end, of which 444 have a free target and 317 a target already reached by a true edge from another detection (294 of 317: two detections within 5 um of the same GT parent, so the scorer's one-to-one match counts one of them, not a miss). Join rule = not in the final graph, source free, target free, mutual best by p, p in [tau, 0.48): tau 0.10 joins 1,219 precision 0.239; 0.20: 836 / 0.295; 0.30: 520 / 0.367; 0.40: 259 / 0.448. True and false joins have the same geometry (d 5.4 vs 6.0 um, |dz| 3.2 vs 3.5, target score 0.32 vs 0.32). One-frame extension: backward at a detected node whose GT parent is undetected 2,082 against 2,925 GT starts inside the annotated range, precision 0.416 (and the 2,082 include gaps the span-1 patch already bridges); forward 2,061 against 2,985, 0.408.
- Conclusion: No post-link rule on the final graph clears the break-even on any bucket: of the 2,438 below-floor true edges only the 444 free-end-to-free-target ones are reachable by a rule (the rest are the swaps, divisions, or duplicate-source pairs the scorer does not count), and joins on them reach 0.45 at best (259 joins, net about zero), extensions 0.41 before counting the already-bridged gaps, the short fragments the ILP and the short filter refuse were swept on 2026-09-0x (SHORT_MIN 4), and the swaps have no dissenting signal (swapfeat). The missed edges that remain are decided upstream: 1,805 swaps between z-stacked cells (ranker, image head and geometry all agree on the wrong target), 2,438 edges the ranker puts below 0.48 with the same geometry as false pairs, and about 2,000 with an undetected endpoint. Residue: none on the post-link side; the swap population (about 1,800 FN plus their mirrored FP) is the one bucket whose ceiling is large (about +0.03 adj_J) and it is a z question, either the detector's z placement or the annotation's z identity.

## 2026-09-12 divadmit

## 2026-09-11 swapfeat
- Hypothesis: the 1,805 swap edges of the shipped linker (source linked to a false target while its annotated child was left) carry a signal the pairwise ranker does not see, either in the image edge head (p_fwd / p_rev / h_fused) or in the solved graph's topology (target continuation, track smoothness), so a second-stage vote could reverse them.
- Scope: offline, no kernel; `bench_csv/rkedge/rkedge_edges.csv` (237,512 candidate rows of the 128 6bba movies: every labelled pair plus every pair where arms C and D differ; a pair is labelled when its source matched an annotated GT node with children) joined to the hpara primary coordinates in `bench_csv/divmiss/divmiss_prims/`. Topology is visible only through labelled sources, so continuation of an unannotated target cannot be read from this table.
- Experiment: scratch pandas script (not kept). Solved graph = rows with in_C = 1 (129,871 edges; 98,927 TP, 3,381 FP). Swaps = sources with a label-1 edge not in C and a label-0 edge in C (1,805 pairs). Kink = |(x_j - x_i) - (x_i - x_h)| in um over the solved predecessor h.
- Result: (1) target continuation: TP targets are visible as sources in 96.2% and continue in 99.0% of those; FP targets are visible in 33.2% and continue in 94.5% of those. Counting invisible targets as dead ends gives 68.6% for FP edges, which is the 69% recorded on 2026-09-11 in the loss map; it measures annotation, not topology. (2) Swaps: false target p_C median 0.803, true child 0.146, margin under 0.1 in 7.4%; true child under the 0.48 floor in 91.0%; ranked second for its source in 1,362 of 1,805. Distance to false target 1.94 um (|dz| 1.13), to true child 6.55 um (|dz| 3.31); scores 0.347 vs 0.309. 56.1% of false targets are themselves annotated cells with children, 94.6% of those continue in C; 38.9% of true children are taken by another labelled source. (3) Image head on swaps: h_fused false 0.711 vs true 0.181, prefers the true child in 4.2%; p_fwd 6.5%, p_rev 4.3%. Head AUC on all labelled pairs 0.9913 against the ranker's 0.9924 and distance alone 0.9680. (4) Smoothness: kink at source TP median 1.93 um (p90 4.51), FP 2.63 (p90 6.19), AUC 0.625 alone; on the 1,302 swaps with a predecessor the path through the false target has kink 2.24 um, through the true child 6.86 um, the true child smoother in 9.4%.
- Conclusion: On the swap edges every available signal points to the same wrong target by a wide margin: the ranker (0.80 vs 0.15), the image head (4-6% for the true child), distance (1.9 vs 6.6 um), z (1.1 vs 3.3 um) and track smoothness (9%). A vote among these models cannot reverse a unanimous choice, and the "dead-end target" feature does not exist in the data (94.5% of the visible FP targets continue). Residue: whether some of these GT edges are themselves annotation swaps between z-stacked cells is not testable from our side; the 39% mutual swaps (true child taken by another annotated source) are the place to look if it ever is.

- Conclusion: v1: the sparse competition GT yields 88 positive (end, start) pairs at spans 2-3 across 128 movies against 186,571 proposals, too few to fit a selector; the distance rule at span 2 makes 14,478 bridges and loses adj_J -0.0022 [-0.0028, -0.0016] on the shipped composition. v2: a selector trained on Zebrahub's dense labels ranks 6bba's labelled pairs at AUC 0.93-0.94 and makes no wrong pick above p 0.5 on them, but 6bba's true bridges are twice as long per frame as Zebrahub's, so it accepts 31% of them at 0.5 and 6% at 0.8. No threshold moves the shipped score: at 0.5 the 2,388 accepted pairs with an unannotated endpoint add nodes whose penalty equals the 40 edges gained (adj_J +0.0001 [-0.0002, +0.0004]); at 0.8 the 393 bridges gain 11 edges at zero FP (adj_J +0.0001 [+0.0000, +0.0002]). The ceiling of any selector on these proposals is 297 edges, +0.0026 adj_J before node cost. Residue: divmiss counts 511 annotated 2/3-frame interior gaps but only 88 of them are (end, start) pairs after the ILP and the span-1 pass, so the rest continued through a wrong link and are a linker question, not a bridging one.

## 2026-09-11 divmiss
- Hypothesis: (1) the 29 divisions the shipped arm loses to `mother_absent` / `daughter_absent` have a peak near the missing cell in the sub-threshold band [0.05, 0.15) or a primary the ILP dropped, rather than no peak at all; (2) the 1,805 swap edges (true child 6.5 um away, false target 1.9 um away along the source's velocity, 51% two or more z-planes off) are GT identities absorbed by a second cell inside the 5 um match radius.
- Scope: 128 6bba train movies, hpara peaks (`fdet_F4hp_`), GT geffs; no ranker, no ILP, no solved graph. `MATCH_UM` 5.0 throughout (the scorer matches at 7.0).
- Experiment: `divmiss.py` from `tools/bench/make_divmiss.py` (rkedge.py cut before its feature stage, one GT-vs-peaks pass appended), kernel `faustine649/biohub-divmiss` v1, CPU, rkedge's 16 sources. Writes `divmiss_gt.csv` (every GT node: nearest primary distance/score/index, second-nearest primary, nearest pool peak, nearest any peak, mother/daughter flags) and `divmiss_prims/<movie>.npz` (every primary with its two nearest GT nodes), to be joined locally with `bench_csv/rkedge/rkedge_edges.csv` on (dataset, t, i).
- Result: 1.2 min, `DIVMISS OK`, 113,121 annotated GT nodes, 125 GT divisions, 2,242,408 primaries. Output in `bench_csv/divmiss/`.

  GT nodes against the hpara peaks (nearest within 5 um):

  | | n | primary (s >= 0.15) | pool only [0.05, 0.15) | no peak at any score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | mothers | 125 | 120 | 0 | 5 |
  | daughters | 250 | 234 | 2 | 14 |
  | all annotated nodes | 113,121 | 107,425 (95.0%) | 629 (0.6%) | 5,067 (4.5%) |

  Divisions by daughters with a primary: 2 daughters 111, 1 daughter 12, 0 daughters 2. Of the 14 divisions missing a daughter primary, 2 have a pool peak for her, 12 have nothing. Daughter primaries score median 0.399 against 0.441 for all annotated nodes; a second primary within 5 um of a daughter occurs in 1.7%. Against the shipped funnel (`mother_absent` 8, `daughter_absent` 21, both measured on the solved graph): 5 mothers and about 14 daughters have no peak, so roughly 3 mothers and 7 daughters had a primary the ILP dropped as unlinked; 2 daughters are reachable from the pool.

  Swap edges (1,805; the source took a false target while its labelled child sits 6.5 um away), joined on (dataset, t, i):

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | source's nearest GT node A | 3.48 um (median) |
  | source's second-nearest GT node | 24.08 um; within 5 um in 0.2% |
  | source -> true child, z-planes | 2.0 (median) |
  | source -> false target, z-planes | 0.7 |
  | false target within 5 um of A's child | 1,006 (55.7%), median 4.67 um |
  | false target with no GT node within 5 um | 794 (44.0%) |
  | false target near some other GT cell | 5 |
  | scores: false target / true child / source | 0.347 / 0.309 / 0.352 |

  So in 1,006 swaps two detections sit inside the match radius of one annotated child, the annotation nearer the one 6.5 um and two z-planes from the source; the linker took the other. In 794 the false target has no annotation within 5 um.
- Conclusion: Of the 29 divisions the funnel calls absent, about 19 have no peak at any score (detector-blind), about 10 had a primary the ILP dropped, and 2 are in the sub-threshold pool; drawing daughters from the pool is worth at most 2 divisions. Of the swap edges, 56% are two detections within the match radius of one annotated child, which no linking rule can resolve, and 44% link to a detection with no annotation near it. 4.5% of annotated cells have no peak within 5 um at any score; that, not the ranker, is the largest single bucket left on the edge term.

So 101 of 254 (40%) fell under the 0.48 floor in D; 153 were above the floor and the ILP still did not take them. Of those 153: the target got a different parent in D in 63 cases (32 of those competing edges are themselves true), the source got a different child in 20 (5 true), and in 73 neither endpoint is linked in D at all. Mirror image for the 224 gained: 76 under C's floor, 148 above it, of which 59 target-parent conflicts (29 true), 38 source conflicts (1 true), 55 unlinked in C.

  Lost true edges by target detection score (lost / kept in D):

  |---|---|---|---|
  | [0.00,0.24) | 52 | 1,787 | 2.83% |
  | [0.24,0.30) | 68 | 4,423 | 1.51% |
  | [0.30,0.36) | 74 | 9,380 | 0.78% |

  | [0.50,1.01) | 0 | 5,997 | 0 |

  Over all true edges the median p_D - p_C is 0.000 in every score_j band, and the share above the 0.48 floor differs by at most 0.012 between arms (0.824 vs 0.812 in the lowest band, 0.991 vs 0.992 in [0.36,0.50)). The two rankers disagree only on a thin band of dim-target, multi-candidate edges (p around 0.6, 2-3 candidates per source), and there the disagreement runs both ways.
- Conclusion: The hypothesis is half right: the lost edges do have dim targets (median score_j 0.31, none above 0.50), but only 40% fell under the floor; 60% were above it and lost to the ILP's choice of a competing edge or to the node being dropped. The retrain does not shift probabilities on any score band; it swaps 254 true edges for 224 other true edges of the same kind and removes 60 false edges, net -30 true. The C-vs-D gap is ILP tie-breaking on near-equal low-confidence edges, not a systematic error in the retrained ranker, and nothing in this table points to a fix that would prefer C's 254 over D's 224.

  | 56086066 | control (what ships) | — | 0.944 | — |

  | 56135603 | F4 ranker + DIV_W 0.35 | +0.0023 / +0.0019 / n/a | 0.944 | +0.000 |

The retrain removed 0.55% and read +0.000.
  - `submit_hp` v1 and `submit_rk` v1 were both pushed without `"machine_shape": "NvidiaTeslaT4"` and were handed a P100 whose sm_60 the installed torch refuses. Both were re-pushed as v2 with the pin, and v2 of each carries the scores above.

The retrain reads +0.000, which at three-decimal resolution cannot resolve a claimed +0.0023; it is neither confirmed nor killed, and its local gain is entirely divisions on a channel whose interval is wide in every domain. ## 2026-09-09 jointgate
- Hypothesis: the joint gate's incoherent 44b6 fork population materially understates hpara's score.
- Scope: offline, no kernel. Pruning-curve arithmetic only; B's own-fork row is unavailable until `fk44f4` runs. 44 to 51 counted forks sit within 2x of the `p > 0.03` cut, so a fork either side flips on any numerical difference.
- Experiment: `gatelab` established that the pruning curve is a pure function of (label, gate p), because `div_J = TP/(TP+FP+FN)` with `FN = N_GT − TP` and N_GT fixed at 125. Every arm's fork table is in its kernel output. `fork_gate_joint.pkl` is fitted on 128 6bba counted forks plus 67 44b6 ones, and the 44b6 half comes from `divbench5`, generated under the shipped BASE ranker on refine coordinates. The user chose not to submit until the follow-up measurements were in.
- Result:

  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | A ships | none (6bba-only) | 42/47/83 | 0.2442 | 42/47/83 | EXACT |
  | A ships | SHIPPED (divbench5) | 46/39/79 | 0.2805 | 46/39/79 | EXACT |
  | B retrain | none (6bba-only) | 45/52/80 | 0.2542 | 45/52/80 | EXACT |
  | B retrain | SHIPPED | 45/46/80 | 0.2632 | 45/49/80 | 3 forks |

  | C hpara | SHIPPED | 49/52/76 | 0.2768 | 49/51/76 | 1 fork |
  | C hpara | its OWN (88 hpara 44b6 forks) | 47/43/78 | 0.2798 | — | NEW |

  | arm | joint gate on SHIPPED forks | on its OWN forks | Δ div_J | ~Δ score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | A ships | 0.2805 | its own ARE the shipped ones | 0 | 0 |
  | C hpara | 0.2768 | 0.2798 | +0.0029 | +0.0003 |
  | B retrain | 0.2632 | waiting on `fk44f4` | | |

  - The coherent gate keeps fewer forks of both kinds (49/51 -> 47/43), losing 2 TPs to gain 8 FPs removed. div_J rises because FPs outnumber TPs nine to one in this population.

    D is at or below A in every column. In the shipped configuration only C gains (+0.0009, one constant changed); B needs DIV_W 0.35 and then gives the highest cell anywhere (0.9449, +0.0025 over what ships).
  - `ANCHOR_HARD` and `ANCHOR_SOFT` are never read anywhere in this script lineage — declared, documented, mutated by the F4HP demotion block, and consulted by nothing; the real anchors are literals next to the print. The re-arm at round 2's F4HP values was a no-op and the log printed `want 0.9216 -> MISS (-0.0012)`. The numbers match round 2 exactly by inspection: `ANCHOR_D187` 0.9204 / div_J 0.0667 and `+BIDIR pkl` 0.9252 / div_J 0.1389, both to four decimals, on fixed pkls that cannot see `RANK_TRAIN`.
- Conclusion: the two changes interfere; together they read 0.9282, below hpara alone (0.9298) and the retrain alone (0.9290), where additive would be 0.9321. Adding the retrain on top of hpara is distinguishably negative (P 0.043). The best cell has the largest train/deploy mismatch, so mismatch removal does not explain the retrain's gain; the ranking, the training pool and output size do not order the cells either. The effect runs through the ILP rather than the ranking.

## 2026-09-09 zhpara4 result
- Hypothesis: that the zebrahub OOM kill is a single dense `N_pred x N_gt` float64 cost matrix inside `compute_metric`; and, as rivals, a cgroup limit far below the advertised box size, or a native segfault.
- Scope: zebrahub crops only, one run (~6 min to the kill). The bias check covers the 38 crops that scored out of 41. Says nothing about which allocation is actually quadratic.
- Experiment: `zhpara4` kernel with a probe printing `MemTotal` / `MemAvailable` and pred/GT node counts plus dense size in GB before every `compute_metric`, plus two small tripwire crops. Offline size/effect join: `tools/zhsize.py`, reading zhpara v3's own CSV (`n_gt`, `num_pred_nodes`). `tools/klog.py` fixed to fetch logs.
- Result: `MemTotal 32,870,492 kB` (32.9 GB), `MemAvailable 31,686,692 kB` — no cgroup limit far below the advertised size. Log survived (21,397 chars, not zero) and its last line is `Killed` (SIGKILL); a native segfault would print `Segmentation fault`. Kill is inside `compute_metric`, where zhpara3's `rss.log` put it.

  Probe:

      tripwire crop 1   pred  8,966n / gt  5,051n   dense  0.4 GB   scored
      tripwire crop 2   pred  6,164n / gt  5,320n   dense  0.3 GB   scored
      ZSNS001_z2y2x7    pred 40,936n / gt 54,073n   dense 17.7 GB   KILLED

  Against the crops that did score:

  | crop | n_gt | n_pred | dense | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ZSNS001_tail_z2y3x2 | 56,167 | 46,633 | 20.95 GB | scored |
  | ZSNS005_z1y6x8 | 47,527 | 51,282 | 19.50 GB | scored |
  | ZSNS001_tail_z2y0x3 | 47,455 | 43,611 | 16.56 GB | scored |
  | ZSNS001_z2y2x7 | 54,073 | 40,936 | 17.7 GB | killed, twice |

  A larger allocation succeeded and a smaller one failed in the same run. The 38 that scored span 0.18–20.95 GB, so the lost crop sits inside the working range. It killed zhpara v3 after 38 crops and zhpara4 after 2, entering the metric at 2.1 GB both times.

  Bias check on the three lost crops (the three largest by cache size: 39/41, 40/41, 41/41):

  | | value |
  |---|---|
  | Spearman(dense size, d adj_J), n=38 | −0.093 |
  | Spearman(dense size, \|d adj_J\|) | −0.219 |
  | weighted d adj_J, largest 12 crops | +0.00077 |
  | weighted d adj_J, smallest 12 crops | +0.00065 |
  | weighted d adj_J, all 38 | +0.00098 |

  `tools/klog.py` fix: kagglesdk writes the downloaded log with `open(path, "w")` and no encoding, so on this box it gets gbk and any kernel whose stdout contains `⚠` fails to download. It now re-execs itself under `-X utf8`.
- Conclusion: both rivals (hidden cgroup limit, native segfault) are eliminated; the dense `N_pred x N_gt` hypothesis is contradicted, since node counts do not order the outcome. What remains measured is an OOM kill inside `compute_metric`, reproducible on `ZSNS001_z2y2x7` across two runs at low resident memory. The zebrahub hpara arm (+0.0011 [+0.0005, +0.0017], P 0.998, 38 of 41 crops) is not biased by the three missing crops, and keeps its existing caveat that it runs dcmerge's solver.

  1. Churn is four times the net: net −652 forks, retrain drops 2,955 and adds 2,303.
  2. Overlap hypothesis dead: of the forks the retrain drops, 83.1% sat below the gate's cut, against 77.5% of the ones it keeps and a base rate of 79.8%. Gate-p medians of dropped and kept forks: 0.0050 and 0.0049.

  4. Join exact: `pf_c1`, `pf_q` from the same cached head must be identical on a correct join, and are — max |d| = 0.000e+00 over 3,898 and 3,621 matched forks.

  | | BASE | F4 | d |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `p_c1` (mother -> first daughter), TP | 0.8525 | 0.8575 | +0.0050 |
  | `p_c1`, FP | 0.8604 | 0.8581 | −0.0024 |
  | `p_q` (the edge that makes it a fork), TP | 0.4591 | 0.4442 | −0.0149 |
  | `p_q`, FP | 0.2602 | 0.2505 | −0.0097 |

  On the primary edge the signs are opposite (separation); on the fork-making edge both fall (a downward shift of scale, same direction as 652 fewer forks offered).

  Correction to the gate reading (corrected 2026-09-09; earlier text said "the joint gate is worth +0.0037 on the old ranker and +0.0004 on the new one" as if the gate collapsed — those are the joint gate's margin over the 6bba-only gate):

  | | BASE | F4 |
  |---|---|---|
  | ungated -> + gate6 | 0.9266 -> 0.9387 = +0.0121 | 0.9290 -> 0.9406 = +0.0116 |
  | gate6 -> joint | 0.9387 -> 0.9424 = +0.0037 | 0.9406 -> 0.9410 = +0.0004 |

  The fork gate itself is undamaged by the retrain. What is lost is the extra value the joint gate got from adding 71 44b6 movies' counted forks to its training set: those 44b6 forks come from divbench5, i.e. the BASE ranker's fork population, while the 6bba forks now gated come from the F4 one.

  Housekeeping: `biohub-rkpool` shows ERROR — the inherited `assert not ANCHOR_FAIL` fires at the end on `REF_FORKS` (52/225 against the control's 50/249); those anchors must miss in the treatment arm and should have been gated on `RANK_TRAIN`. The assert is accumulated and checked once at the end, so all 128 movies were scored and `rkpool_F4.csv` written before it fired.
- Conclusion: at the shipped floor 0.48 on 128 out-of-fold 6bba movies, the F4 retrain gains +0.00231 score [+0.00067, +0.00396], P(>0) 0.990, and eprank3's 12-movie verdict is overturned. The retrain cannot be shipped by swapping the pkl alone: the gain survives in four of five configuration cells and is −0.0014 in the deployed one (REF + joint). Best local cell is F4 pkl + DIV_W 0.35 + joint gate = 0.9449 against today's shipped 0.9424. Stated order of work: `rkfloor` first (whether 0.48 is the retrained ranker's argmax), then re-run the 44b6 fork population under the F4 ranker so the joint gate is joint in the same sense, then a submission with the byte delta recorded before it goes.

## 2026-09-09 zebrahub kill diagnosis
- Hypothesis: that the repeated zebrahub SIGKILL is a single quadratic allocation inside `compute_metric` rather than a gradual leak; rivals were a native segfault (rustworkx / scipy) and a cgroup limit far below the advertised ~30 GB.
- Scope: zebrahub crops, `ZSNS001_z2y2x7` specifically. Four kills across `biohub-zh-pipeline` (10 of 41 crops, progress.md:425), `zhpara` v1 (9), `zhpara` v3 (39), `zhpara2` (9); until this night none left a readable error — Kaggle returns a zero-byte log for a SIGKILLed session.
- Experiment: `zhpara` v3, `zhpara2`, `zhpara3`. `zhpara3` writes `_rss` samples to `/kaggle/working/rss.log` with `flush` + `fsync`. `zhpara2` printed a `VmRSS` / `VmHWM` trace that died with the process.
- Result: what each run establishes —

  | run | what it establishes |
  |---|---|
  | `zhpara` v3 (38/41) | 39 GT geffs against 38 CSV rows -> died INSIDE crop 39; the single leftover prediction geff names it `ZSNS001_z2y2x7` and shows the REF arm had already saved. `_checkpoint()` kept 38 crops of paired data. |
  | artefact count | 819 files / 7.6 MB under `ps_zh_gt` -> disk exhaustion eliminated. |
  | `zhpara2` (8 anchors, died on crop 9) | not accumulation: held only 8 small crops of state and still died on the first big one. Its 8 crops reproduce v3's rows bit for bit — 8 x 2 arms x 12 columns, 0 differ, worst \|d\| 0.000e+00 — so the harness is deterministic and rows from separate runs may be joined. |
  | `zhpara3` (`rss.log`, fsynced) | the stage. |

  Surviving trace on `ZSNS001_z2y2x7`:

       97s  REF after zh_load          1,201,936 kB
      312s  REF after solve_one        2,398,420 kB   peak 2,409,328 kB
      323s  REF freed, pre from_geff   2,132,648 kB
      323s  REF after from_geff        2,132,736 kB
                                       <- killed. The next sample would have
                                          been "REF after compute_metric".

  That crop's `solve_one` takes 215 s against 9–13 s on the two tripwire crops, roughly twenty times the work of a small one. RSS entering the metric was 2.1 GB, peak 2.4 GB, on a box with about 30 GB — not a gradual climb into a ceiling. `zhpara3`'s one blind change (freeing `nodes0 / edges0 / pool` right after `patch_and_save`) is visible as 2,398 MB -> 2,132 MB and was not the problem.

  (corrected 2026-09-09 by zhpara4; earlier text gave a dense `N_pred x N_gt` float64 cost matrix via `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` — 60,000 x 60,000 = 28.8 GB in one allocation — as the hypothesis fitting every fact. A crop needing 20.95 GB dense scored and the one that kills needs 17.7 GB, so `N_pred x N_gt` does not order the outcome. The 38 successful crops' node counts were in the kernel output when that paragraph was written.)

  Both rivals eliminated by zhpara4: `MemTotal` 32.9 GB with 31.7 GB available (no hidden cgroup limit) and the log's last line is `Killed` (SIGKILL), not `Segmentation fault`. See 2026-09-09 zhpara4 result.

  Conditional note on record: if the quadratic story holds, the fix is a sparse or blocked matcher rather than a bigger box, and it would explain why this domain has killed runs since the beginning while the competition domains never have — zebrahub is the only one with dense ground truth, so `N_gt` is every cell rather than the 0.77–9.71% an annotator labelled.
- Conclusion: the kill is an OOM SIGKILL inside `compute_metric` on `ZSNS001_z2y2x7`, at 2.1 GB RSS with peak 2.4 GB, so it is one allocation and not a slow leak. Which allocation is unidentified: node-count-based dense sizing does not predict it.

## 2026-09-09 eprank3 result
- Hypothesis: whether retraining the production ranker on the F4 coordinates it is deployed on improves the pipeline; and, as a mechanism, whether BASE primaries act as augmentation so that removing the train/deploy mismatch removes a regularisation.
- Scope: 12-movie holdout (F4-6bba and F4-44b6), floor 0.10 — `eprank3` inherits `edgeprob_rank2`'s solver constants and has no `PROD_FLOOR` at all, while what ships is 0.48. Both intervals include zero. The direction was later reversed in sign at 128 movies and floor 0.48 (see 2026-09-09 rkpool result: +0.00085 adj_J [+0.00003, +0.00167], +0.0024 score, P 0.990, 77/128 up); what stands from this entry is the number as measured, 12 movies at floor 0.10.
- Experiment: `eprank3` (POOL_ARM=F4) and `eprank3-ref` (POOL_ARM=BASE), 102.2 min + ~100 min CPU. Three head-2 arms cut and an `ep2_path is None` guard added. Artifact `edge_ranker_ep175v4_bidir_f4.pkl`. Companion 128-movie control `rkpool_ref`, 134.6 min stage B. Both pkls unpickled to compare intercepts. Floor evidence: `eprank3.py:203 ILP_FLOOR = 0.10`, `eprank3.py:1849 if pr >= ILP_FLOOR:`, `grep -c PROD_FLOOR eprank3.py` -> 0; `rkpool.py:1848` sets `PROD_FLOOR = 0.48`.
- Result: control exact —

      ANCHOR_D187  F4-6bba   adj_J 0.9216   want 0.9216 HARD -> OK (+0.0000)
      +BIDIR       F4-6bba   adj_J 0.9261   want 0.9261 soft -> OK (-0.0000)
      +BIDIR       F4-44b6   adj_J 0.8515   want 0.8515 soft -> OK (+0.0000)

  and it re-read `HEAD1` 0.9245 / 0.8453 and `HEAD12` 0.9238 / 0.8438. `ANCHOR_D187`, `HEAD1` and `HEAD12` use no retrained ranker and are byte-identical between the two arms on all 24 datasets; only `+BIDIR` moved.

  | | BASE pool (ships) | F4 pool (retrained) | delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | D175 training rows | 217,688 (0.497 pos) | 216,209 (0.501 pos) | −1,479 |
  | `+BIDIR` val AUC | 0.9926 | 0.9926 | 0.0000 |
  | edge AUC F4-6bba | 0.9929 | 0.9929 | 0.0000 |
  | edge AUC F4-44b6 | 0.9871 | 0.9872 | +0.0001 |
  | stage B adj_J F4-6bba | 0.9261 | 0.9250 | −0.0011 |
  | stage B div_J F4-6bba | 0.1515 | 0.1316 | −0.0199 |
  | stage B score F4-6bba | 0.9412 | 0.9381 | −0.0031 |
  | stage B adj_J F4-44b6 | 0.8515 | 0.8493 | −0.0022 |

  Per dataset, `+BIDIR` only:

  | | weighted adj_J (what is scored) | unweighted mean | 90% interval | up |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | F4-6bba | −0.0011 | −0.00129 | [−0.00303, +0.00031] | 2/12 |
  | F4-44b6 | −0.0022 | +0.00214 | [−0.00725, +0.01596] | 3/12 |

  44b6's unweighted mean disagrees in sign with its weighted one because of one movie: `44b6_0b24845f` reads 0.9167 -> 0.9961, +0.0794, against a median move of −0.0002. That dataset is on record as unstable — `edgeprob_rank2` measured it at 0.9167 / 0.9937 / 0.9979 / 0.8148 across four linker arms, a ±0.18 swing. Set aside, the per-dataset picture agrees with the weighted one.

  `HEAD1` identical in both arms, so `+BIDIR` minus `HEAD1` is what the 18 coordinate columns are worth on top of the head:

  | ranker's gain over the head alone | BASE pool | F4 pool |
  |---|---|---|
  | F4-6bba | +0.0016 | +0.0005 |
  | F4-44b6 | +0.0062 | +0.0040 |

  The augmentation/regularisation mechanism was retracted the same night by this run's own AUC — both that story and plain overfitting are about generalisation, and edge AUC is flat in five independent readings:

  | | BASE pool | F4 pool |
  |---|---|---|
  | fold0 held-out AUC (rkpool, 128 movies) | 0.9935 | 0.9935 |
  | fold1 held-out AUC (rkpool, 128 movies) | 0.9917 | 0.9918 |
  | val AUC on its own primaries (eprank3) | 0.9926 | 0.9926 |
  | F4-6bba (eprank3) | 0.9929 | 0.9929 |
  | F4-44b6 (eprank3) | 0.9871 | 0.9872 |

  What moved are the threshold-sensitive outputs:

  | 6bba | BASE | F4 | relative |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `edge_J` | 0.9242 | 0.9230 | −0.13% |
  | `div_J` | 0.1515 | 0.1316 | −13% |
  | `node_r` | −0.0199 | −0.0203 | fewer nodes kept |
  | `node_r` 44b6 | −0.1113 | −0.1120 | fewer nodes kept |

  Two thirds of the 6bba score loss is divisions (0.1 x −0.0199 = −0.0020 of −0.0031). The safe-division patch and the capacity-2 ILP both accept on probability values; the ILP reads the value against `PROD_FLOOR` 0.48 and `ILP_DISAPP` 1.5.

  The simple calibration story is measured and false:

      BASE pool   baseline logit -0.012710  -> p 0.496823
      F4 pool     baseline logit +0.003145  -> p 0.500786

  0.016 logit apart, exactly the training base-rate difference (0.497 -> 0.501 positive), i.e. class balance; and it points the wrong way, since a higher intercept raises probabilities while fewer nodes survived. If calibration is the mechanism it is a change in tree shape, which needs both models' probabilities on the same rows.

  Floor confound: the whole comparison ran at floor 0.10 while what ships is 0.48 (ref 56030644), and `ilpsweep` measured that move as 6bba +0.0000 but 44b6 −0.0131. This is the same freezing error as `divradius`, which froze the fork gate and read +0.0088 for a sister radius that became −0.0005 once the gate was retrained per cell. (An earlier draft of the eprank3 write-up named the wrong constant, `PROD_FLOOR = 0.48`, before the source was read.)

  Four anchor cells across two floors:

  | BASE pkl | F4-6bba | F4-44b6 | source |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | floor 0.10 | 0.9261 | 0.8515 | eprank3-ref, ilpsweep REF |
  | floor 0.48 | 0.9261 | 0.8384 | ilpsweep's F48 delta (+0.0000 / −0.0131) |

  (corrected; an earlier draft wrote "0.9261 / 0.8515" for floor 0.48 — 0.8515 is the floor-0.10 value, 0.8384 is 0.48's. 6bba is 0.9261 at both because its F48 delta is +0.0000.)

  Floor 0.48 ships because it won on LB (+0.001, ref submit-f48, −1.43% bytes), not because it is the local optimum: locally it is +0.0000 / −0.0131.

  `+BIDIR` permutation drop: `h_fused` +0.1765 against `p_fwd` +0.0019 and `p_rev` +0.0020. This weakens reading `HEAD1`'s 6/6 per-movie split as two near-equal disagreeing predictors. The 18 columns alone (`ANCHOR_D187`, no head) still read AUC 0.9894 and adj_J 0.9216.

  128-movie control `rkpool_ref` reproduced four recorded numbers exactly:

      ANCHOR_D187  F4-6bba(12)   adj_J 0.9216  want 0.9216 HARD -> OK (+0.0000)
      +BIDIR pkl   F4-6bba(12)   adj_J 0.9261  want 0.9261 soft -> OK
      REF          F4-6bba(128)  50/249/75  div_J 0.1337  adj_J 0.9133
                                 score 0.9266 (divbench3) -> OK
      POOLED F4 edge AUC 0.99256 over 183,966 rows  (hparabench round 2: 0.99256)

  Fold AUCs flat between arms at 128-movie scale: BASE 0.9935 / 0.9917 against F4 0.9935 / 0.9918.

  hparabench round 2 established the day before that a 12-movie holdout can disagree in sign with the 128 containing it (adj_J −0.0012 on the 12 against +0.0013 on the 128); `F4-6bba` is that holdout.

  Consequence recorded for the TTA line: retraining the ranker on tta4 features is the same move (fit on the exact features deployed), so the prior on "retraining rescues TTA" was lowered; the `ttacache2` arm will still be run.
- Conclusion: on the 12-movie holdout at floor 0.10 the retrained ranker is worse on both domains — adj_J −0.0011 on 6bba (2/12 datasets up) and −0.0022 on 44b6 (3/12 up) — with both intervals crossing zero. Edge AUC is flat in five readings, so the loss is downstream of ranking, in the threshold-sensitive ILP/patch stages. The measurement was taken at a floor that does not ship, and rkpool at floor 0.48 on 128 movies reverses the sign.

## 2026-09-09 zhpara v3 result
- Hypothesis: whether hpara's effect holds on zebrahub, the third domain and the only one with dense ground truth.
- Scope: 38 of 41 crops (killed at crop 39), paired crop by crop. The three missing crops are the largest and adj_J is weight-averaged, so the number will move when they land. div_J's interval includes zero (P = 0.922). `zhpara` runs dcmerge's solver — no edge head and no fork gate — so the result answers "does better placement help the linker", not "does it help the shipped submission", and is not a number that can be added to a submission's expected gain. Absolute scores are 0.68 rather than 0.93 because zebrahub labels every cell.
- Experiment: `zhpara` v3, ~3.8 h CPU, killed at crop 39 of 41 with 38 crops of paired data saved by `_checkpoint()` (CSV rewritten after every crop). Crops ordered smallest-first behind the 8 anchor crops.
- Result: anchors exact, REF arm over the 8 dcmerge-v2 crops —

      edge_jaccard      got 0.8036  want 0.8036  OK (+0.0000)
      adj_edge_jaccard  got 0.8093  want 0.8093  OK (+0.0000)
      division_jaccard  got 0.0230  want 0.0230  OK (+0.0000)

  | `edge_J` | 0.6826 | 0.6836 | +0.00101 | [+0.00040, +0.00161] | 0.995 |
  | `adj_J` | 0.6828 | 0.6839 | +0.00102 | [+0.00042, +0.00162] | 0.996 |
  | `div_J` | 0.0064 | 0.0072 | +0.00077 | [−0.00014, +0.00182] | 0.922 |

  27 of 38 crops up on adj_J, median +0.00116. Division counts: REF 44/853/5929 -> HP 49/823/5924, TP +5, FP −30, FN −5. Same direction hparabench round 2 found on 6bba (7,004 -> 6,709 forks proposed while true ones rose); every test in `_add_safe_divisions` is a distance.

  | domain | Δ score | 90% interval | P(>0) | sample |

  | 6bba | +0.0031 | [+0.0014, +0.0049] | 0.998 | 128 movies |

  (corrected 2026-09-09 by hp44full; earlier text said 44b6 −0.0002 [−0.0064, +0.0051], P 0.509, on 12 movies with 2 GT divisions. On all 71 movies the point estimate is +0.0013, its interval contains 6bba's +0.0031, and the division channel moved for the first time, +0.0174 against 6bba's +0.0182. See 2026-09-09 hp44full result.)

  Finishing the three missing crops is a ~30-minute job on 3 crops, not a re-run. `divbench5` v2 showed the 12-movie 44b6 draw reads 43% high on this kind of quantity (+0.0020 on 2 events against the full 71's +0.0014 on 26); `hpara44` (GPU) + `ephp44` were running/queued to give all 71 movies hpara coordinates.
- Conclusion: hpara is positive on zebrahub, score +0.0011 [+0.0005, +0.0017], P(>0) 0.998, across 27 of 38 crops. The ledger reads two domains positive with intervals excluding zero, one null, none negative, which meets the record's three-domain rule. The division-count movement matches the 6bba mechanism (distance-based tests in `_add_safe_divisions`).

## 2026-09-09 rkpool / rkpool-ref pushed
- Hypothesis: The shipped ranker is trained on BASE primaries and deployed on F4 primaries; does training it on F4 instead change held-out AUC and score?
- Scope: 175-movie training pool, 128 scored 6bba movies; held-out-fold AUC read on F4 rows in both arms (a cross-domain read for the BASE arm). Two CPU kernels. Says nothing about zebrahub or 44b6.
- Experiment: `edgeprob_rank2.py:1608` builds the production pool as `_jobs = [(n, "BASE", "pool") for n in POOL175]`, so `edge_ranker_ep175v3_bidir.pkl` (loaded by every submission) learned on BASE primaries (xl three-branch mean, LB 0.922) and is deployed on F4 ones (that mean plus ep05 DeepCenter as a fourth equal-weight map, LB 0.925, ref 55889500). `hparabench_ref` has the same shape: stage A's two fold rankers train from `LAB`, built with `EP_OF["BASE"]`, and stage B solves F4. Two kernels, identical movies, folds, columns, estimator, seed and stage B; one line differs.

  | kernel | `RANK_TRAIN` | the fold rankers learn on | stage B solves |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `rkpool_ref` | `BASE` | the xl three-branch mean | F4 |
  | `rkpool` | `F4` | that mean + ep05 DeepCenter | F4 |

  Enabling condition: `fuse44b6` (59 of 59, 90.1 min) and `ep44b6` (59 of 59, 45.3 min) landed F4 primaries and F4 head probabilities for the 59 44b6 train movies that lacked them, so all 199 movies now carry both. hparabench never attached them (its log reads `199 BASE + 140 F4`). With `biohub-fuse44b6` + `biohub-ep44b6` attached, the F4 pool is the same 175 movies as the BASE pool: no pool-size confound, no new GPU.
- Result: Anchors inherited unchanged from `rkpool_ref` = hparabench_ref's path with `LAB_TRAIN` bound back to `LAB`: divbench3 REF over the 128 = 50/249/75, div_J 0.1337, adj_J 0.9133, score 0.9266, plus gate cross cells 0.2442 / 0.2805 / 0.2591. The control arm is run rather than reused from round 2's CSV so those asserts fire if attaching two cache datasets perturbed the BASE path.

  Amendment to ttabench (see 2026-09-09 ttabench): its override replaced `EDGEPROB_F4` while training reads `EDGEPROB`, so the fold rankers there were 100% noTTA-trained (corrected 2026-09-09; earlier text said "90%+ noTTA"). Its adj_J −0.0051 / edge_J −0.0074 is train/test mismatch plus TTA with no way to separate them. The matched test needs tta4 in the training rows; `ttacache` (140 movies) is running on 6bba.

  Outcomes recorded against the three registered branches: F4-beats-BASE fired on 128 movies at floor 0.48; BASE-beats-F4 fired only on the 12-movie read at floor 0.10. On eprank3 the direction of the BASE-beats-F4 branch fired but its augmentation explanation did not: held-out AUC is flat in five readings, i.e. same ranking, different downstream behaviour at constants tuned for the other calibration. Constants tuned against the mismatched ranker's calibration: `PROD_FLOOR` 0.48, `ILP_DISAPP` 1.5, `DIV_W` 0.55, and the fork gate.

  Head-and-ranker-as-peers arm (not run, not previously rejected). Previously tried and rejected: `+BIDIR2` / `+BOTH` / `+AVG` (more head columns inside the ranker, 1/11, 5/7, 4/7 per movie) and `HEAD1` / `HEAD12` (head replacing the ranker, 0.9245 / 0.8453). A convex blend of the two probabilities at the same level was never run; `make_submit_ep2.py:72` forbids it structurally:

      assert (RANKER_NAME is None) != (HEAD_ONLY_COL is None)

  `HEAD1` loses only 0.0016 / 0.0062 yet splits 6/6 per movie on both domains. `progress.md:4692` records that the ILP's costs were tuned against the ranker's calibration, not h_fused's, so HEAD1's −0.0016 was measured at a floor belonging to the other scale and is a lower bound on the head's value. A blend arm would have to sweep the floor with the weight. Held back until `rkpool` reports, since training on F4 moves the ranker's probabilities and would stale any blend weight measured against the old one. Counter-evidence on head-heavy configurations: `progress.md:104` — both official edge heads were trained on all 199 train movies, so every local head number is in-sample; `progress.md:46` — `submit_off` (official nodes + head only, no ranker) read +0.004 / +0.057 locally and scored LB 0.895, the worst on record (that run changed the detector too, so it does not isolate the head).
- Conclusion: Every score in the record was produced by a ranker reading coordinates it was not fitted on, and no arm had isolated the cost. The user agreed to retrain the ranker first and asked about treating the edge head and the ranker as peers. Removing the mismatch costs no GPU and was impossible before 2026-09-07 because the F4 caches did not exist for 59 movies.

## 2026-09-09 divradius + divradius2
- Hypothesis: Does the public 0.946 notebook's division parent / sister radius (9.0 / 14.0 vs our 12.0 / 15.0) gain score, and what is the ceiling on fixing `DIV_PARENT_UM` 12 vs `GATE_UM` 10?
- Scope: 6bba only, 128 movies, 299 counted forks, 50 true, 125 GT divisions. Laptop CPU. `tools/divradius.py` filters the fork proposals a run at the shipped radii already made; it does not re-run `_add_safe_divisions` at a smaller radius, so the caps (`DIV_GLOBAL_CAP`, `DIV_FRAME_CAP`, `used_p` / `used_q` exclusivity) mean a dropped proposal can free a slot for another. Proposals sort by `d_pq + 0.15 * d_s`, so far ones sort last and win contested slots least often, which bounds but does not zero the effect. The joint gate was retrained here on the 12.0-radius fork population; an arm at 10.0 would retrain on its own, and retraining cannot recover a fork never proposed, so that works against the tightened arms in the direction they already lose.
- Experiment: `hparabench_ref` already writes `forks_dw55.csv`, one row per fork with all 20 gate features, `d_pq`, `d_s` and the label. Gate reproduced locally with divbench9's recipe: `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=100, learning_rate=0.05, min_samples_leaf=10, random_state=0)`, 20 features, two alternating movie folds, out of fold, cut `p > 0.03`. `tools/divradius2.py` retrains the gate per cell. Paired bootstrap over the 128 movies, same resample for every cell.

  | `d_pq > 10`, four NaN features | 29 | 7 | 22 | 7 | 9 | 1.00 | 0.41 |

  Ceiling on supplying the missing features and playing that band perfectly (all 7 true forks kept, all 9 surviving false ones cut): 46 / 30 / 79, div_J 0.3020, +0.0215 div_J = +0.0022 score on these 128 movies. (Corrected 2026-09-09; the first draft called +0.0022 "about one noise width" and cited `accdiag` for a floor of 0.002-0.003. `accdiag` measured no such thing and there is no floor: eight `random_state` values give the identical 46 / 39 / 79, so repeat-run noise is zero.) Cost of the fix: a re-cache of the edge head at a wider pair gate for 128 movies plus a bench run. Distinct from widening the gate for the linker, which `gate-sweep`, `gate2` and `zgate` all closed.

  Two further nulls off the same table. Per-source gate cut: forks come from the ILP's own stage (`src` 0, 112 counted, 22 true) and the geometric patch's (`src` 1, 187 counted, 28 true), sharing one threshold; best of a 10 x 10 split grid is ILP 0.05 / patch 0.03 at +0.00017 score, worse than moving the single cut. At 0.03 the gate keeps 0.91 of true ILP forks vs 0.93 of true patch ones, and 0.13 of false vs 0.17; `src` is already one of the twenty features. Single-threshold sweep: 0.03 (ships) 0.2805, 0.04 0.2848 (+0.00043 score), 0.05 0.2675, 0.02 0.2686 — peak one grid step wide on 299 forks and 50 true events; divbench3 priced this axis at +0.0009 and closed it.

The parent cut has already taken the forks the sister cut would have taken, so only the square shows it. Nothing in the public 0.946 notebook is left to port. The −0.004 verdict on their 9.0 is far outside what the filter-vs-re-run approximation could flip; the sister 12.0 candidate was not, and it did not survive retraining.
