## 2026-09-09 ttabench
- Hypothesis: Does edge-feature D4 TTA change score through the full pipeline (ranker + ILP + patches + scorer), not just the edge head's own AUC?
- Scope: 12 holdout 6bba movies carrying a tta4 cache; 116 of the 128 movies are byte-identical between the runs by construction. First edge head only — `ttaprobe` cached `edgeprob_` and not `edgeprob2_`, so the second head stays single-view on the 12 movies that have one. 178 min CPU.
- Experiment: `tools/ttapair.py`, 4,000 draws, the same resample for both arms; the harness confirmed exactly 12 rows differ. `ttaprobe`'s `noTTA` arm is the same wrapper with averaging switched off and must reproduce `edgeprob_F4_` bit for bit: 12 of 12 movies, worst |dp| = 0.000e+00, checked in the first seconds of the kernel. `ttaprobe` held `det_logits` at view 0, so detections are byte-identical, the `(t, i, j)` rows are identical, and only two column values differ.
- Result:

  | | noTTA | tta4 | delta | 90% interval | P(>0) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `edge_J` | 0.9235 | 0.9159 | −0.00741 | [−0.01309, −0.00241] | 0.003 |
  | `adj_J` | 0.9265 | 0.9213 | −0.00507 | [−0.01051, −0.00023] | 0.040 |
  | `div_J` | 0.0769 | 0.0976 | +0.01933 | [−0.07094, +0.11475] | 0.632 |
  | score | 0.9342 | 0.9311 | −0.00313 | [−0.01370, +0.00932] | 0.312 |

  The score interval includes zero because of `div_J`: twelve movies contain twelve GT divisions, so its interval is 0.19 wide and it enters at one tenth the weight. Per movie, 5 of 12 up on adj_J; the aggregate is driven by `283bf9f1` (−0.027) and `7af54fde` (−0.010), both heavy. Diluted over all 128 the same numbers read adj_J −0.0005, exactly a tenth of −0.0052.

  Chain, end to end:

      D4-average the U-Net features
        -> the edge head's own AUC falls 0.00417        (ttascore, 12/12 movies)
        -> 10.6% of gated pairs swap order              (Spearman 0.85-0.97)
        -> through ranker + ILP + patches + scorer:
           adj_J  −0.0051  90% [−0.0105, −0.0002]
           edge_J −0.0074  90% [−0.0131, −0.0024]

  The ±0.005 previously quoted came from hparabench round 1's interval, a comparison that changed the coordinates (detections moved, the gate re-formed, the candidate pair set changed), so the arms shared almost nothing; it does not apply here.

  Amended 2026-09-09 by the rkpool entry: the fold rankers in this run were 100% noTTA-trained — the override replaced `EDGEPROB_F4`, and stage A trains from `LAB`, built with `EP_OF["BASE"]`. The arms therefore differ in the ranker's training distribution as well as its input. Tested claim that survives: bolting D4 feature averaging onto the shipped, non-TTA-trained ranker loses adj_J. Tested claim that does not survive: D4 feature averaging is worth nothing to this pipeline. The matched version needs tta4 in the training rows; `ttacache` (140 movies, tta4, ~4.1 GPU h) is caching them. The view-1 identity anchor, the row-set check and the per-movie table are unaffected.
- Conclusion: Edge-feature TTA costs adj_J −0.0051 and edge_J −0.0074 through the full pipeline, both intervals excluding zero, measured against a ranker fitted without TTA. The test was not underpowered. The last step of the chain had been asserted before it was measured; working-agreement.md records that offline edge AUC anti-predicted this pipeline three times running.

## 2026-09-09 hparabench round 2 + zhpara pushed
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: Three CPU kernels. Round 1 scored 128 6bba movies of which only 12 carried hpara coordinates, so every aggregate was diluted about tenfold and had to be re-read on the changed subset by hand; its AUC discriminator never ran (the Kaggle version was still round 1's). `hparacache` v3 at 140 movies, `ephpcache` and `ep2hpcache` have since landed.
- Experiment:

  | kernel | arm | scope |
  |---|---|---|
  | `biohub-hparabench` | `DET_SRC=F4HP` | 128 6bba + the 12 44b6 D187 rows, hpara coordinates |
  | `biohub-hparabench-ref` | `DET_SRC=F4` | the same, refine coordinates, hard anchors asserted |
  | `biohub-zhpara` | REF vs HP | zebrahub, both arms in one run, dcmerge's solver |

  Three domains: 6bba (128 movies, the scored set), 44b6 (the 12 D187 rows, printed by both arms), zebrahub (`zhpara`, every crop carrying both caches). `zhpara` runs a different pipeline — dcmerge's solver has no edge head and no fork gate — so it answers whether better placement helps the linker, while `hparabench` answers whether it helps the shipped submission.
- Result: v6 died in 60 seconds on its own new assert: `edgeprob2: only 12 of the 128 scored 6bba movies have an F4hp cache`. `edgeprob2` is the optional second head (divbench9 reads it with `.get(name)`) and only 24 movies have an `edgeprob2_F4_` cache at all, so 116 of the 128 scored movies are solved without it in both arms. `ep2hpcache` cached 140; merging all 140 in would have given the hpara arm a second head on 116 movies where the control has none, making the delta measure the second head instead of the placement. The override now replaces and never adds — the hpara dict is cut down to the keys the refine arm already has — and a movie with a refine cache and no hpara counterpart is a hard error.

  `zhpara` anchors: the REF arm must reproduce dcmerge v2's recorded zebrahub BASE (edge_J 0.8036, adj_J 0.8093, div_J 0.0230) on dcmerge's own 8 crops; the hpara cache must carry byte-identical ground truth; the detection count must match frame by frame, because hpara re-places and never re-detects. It also prints `|hpara − refine|` per crop so a null cannot be confused with a no-op.

  The discriminator is the fitted ranker's out-of-fold AUC on `poolsize`'s labels — same pairs, same labels, same model, the one difference being where the points were placed.
- Conclusion: All 128 scored movies now differ between the arms instead of 12. A change counts when the sign agrees across domains; a win in one domain is a property of that domain.

## 2026-09-09 edge-feature TTA verdict
- Hypothesis: The public 0.946 notebook averages the U-Net output over D4 views before reading the edge features and credits it with +0.005 (0.941 -> 0.946); does our edge probability become more informative under that averaging?
- Scope: 6bba only, 12 holdout movies. Measures TTA on the edge features with the detections held fixed; their step averages the detection logits and the features together in one pass. The ranker never ran, the ILP never ran, no graph was scored. Our U-Net is not theirs; a D4-augmented model would be a different experiment.
- Experiment: `ttaprobe` v3, 69 min T4, plus `ttascore` 2 min CPU. Patch `model.encode`, not `predict_video`: the U-Net output is averaged over `n` D4 views (forward transform, encode, inverse transform, mean) while the detection logits are left alone, so detections, their order and their identity are byte-identical across arms and the cached `(t, i, j)` rows join exactly. 36 passes = 12 movies x `noTTA/tta4/tta8`, 7,128 encode calls, 23,760 extra U-Net passes. Movie-level paired bootstrap, 2,000 draws.
- Result: The wrapper is not a no-op: `fwd>0.5` falls on 12 of 12 movies; median `p_fwd` falls on 11 of 12 (0.827 -> 0.728 on `2312ac41`, 0.669 -> 0.399 on `283bf9f1`).

  | arm | views | AUC `p_fwd` | AUC `p_rev` | AUC `prod` | vs noTTA | \|dp\| p50 / p90 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | noTTA | 1 | 0.99037 | 0.99073 | 0.99194 | +0.00000 | -- |
  | tta4 | 4 | 0.98548 | 0.98674 | 0.98777 | −0.00417 | 0.019 / 0.093 |
  | tta8 | 8 | 0.98589 | 0.98672 | 0.98786 | −0.00408 | 0.020 / 0.102 |

  14,636 labelled pairs, 0.6625 positive, `poolsize`'s own labelling rule, the same rows in every arm. Per movie, tta4 is worse on 12 of 12 and tta8 on 10 of 12. Bootstrap: tta4 −0.00415 90% CI [−0.00563, −0.00276], tta8 −0.00408 [−0.00599, −0.00232], P(>0) = 0.000 for both. tta8 is indistinguishable from tta4.

  AUC is invariant to any monotone transform, so a uniform squash would leave it unchanged; the order moved. Spearman between the noTTA and tta4 columns runs 0.85-0.97 per movie, and 10.6% of randomly drawn pairs swap order.

  The decision rests on two things: (1) their claimed mechanism is that the edge features get better, and here they get worse on 12 of 12 movies with P(>0) = 0.000, so the stated reason for the +0.005 does not reproduce on our features — that part is measured; (2) everything downstream is a cost argument: ~20 GPU hours to re-cache three edge-probability datasets. The CPU-only test is cheap (the 36 TTA probability caches exist; ranker, ILP and scorer run on CPU) but would score only the 12 movies that carry them. The chain `head AUC down -> the ranker's three probability columns get worse -> its edge ordering gets worse -> the ILP picks worse edges -> score down` had not been run at the time this entry was written; working-agreement.md records that an offline AUC is not a score and that on 2026-08-24 edge AUC anti-predicted the pipeline three times running.

  Mechanism: TTA is free only when the network is equivariant under the transforms being averaged; nothing in our training recipe makes the U-Net D4-equivariant, and the shift size (median |dp| 0.02, p90 0.10) says it is not close.

  Correction to the first draft, which said their +0.005 should be looked for in detection TTA "which we do not run": we do run it. `fuse6bba.branch_maps4` and `detfuse3` build every one of the four F4 heatmaps as the sigmoid of its 4-flip logit mean — identity, flip y, flip x, flip both — and the detector has worked that way since F4 landed (LB 0.925, 2026-08-31). The public notebook uses eight views there instead of four, on the official detector rather than our ensemble. `tta8` is indistinguishable from `tta4` here, and `_d4_fwd` views 0-3 are exactly `_flip`'s four transforms. Our detector averages logits and takes one sigmoid at the end; `model.encode`'s `unet_out` is averaged as it comes.

  Six of the seven differences from the public 0.946 notebook are closed (corrected 2026-09-09; the first draft of this paragraph said "all six" and dropped one — the comparison table's verdict column marks `division parent / sister um` open): three from the existing record (disappearance cost, ILP division weight, density-adaptive gap), two by `gapcross` (gap radius, short-track floor + rescue), edge-feature TTA here, and `divradius` closing the parent / sister radius (their 9.0 / 14.0 costs −0.004 score).

  Bug found and fixed: `ttaprobe` v3's own AUC table was wrong by one subscript:

  ```python
  prim = load_primaries(name, "F4")          # [ (N_t, 3) ] per frame
  mp = match(np.asarray(prim[t_][0], ...))   # <- row 0 OF THE FRAME
  ```

  `load_primaries` returns a list of arrays, not a list of `(coords, scores)` tuples, so `prim[t][0]` is the first detection of frame `t` and only detection index 0 could ever match, as source or target. It printed a table on 565 rows where the correct rule gives 14,636, and reported tta4 at −0.052. The bug is in the labeller, which runs after every cache is written, so the GPU work was intact and `ttascore` redid the readout on CPU in 2 minutes. What caught it was a known population size: 565 labelled rows across 12 movies is a quarter of one per frame, and `accdiag` had recorded ~14,817 for the same rule on the same holdout. `ttascore` now carries the gate anchor (rebuild `gated_pairs` from its own primaries, demand the cache agrees on the per-frame pair count and on every cached pair being inside `GATE_UM`; passed 12/12, worst distance 10.000 um; a wrong primaries index fails both) and a row-count floor (refuse to print a table on under 5,000 rows).
- Conclusion: Averaging the U-Net features over D4 views makes our edge probability worse, −0.0042 AUC, 12/12 movies, bootstrap P(>0) = 0.000. The tested claim is narrow: D4-averaging before the edge head makes the head's own forward, reverse and product probabilities less able to separate true children from gated non-children on 6bba. The ~20 GPU hours are refused on a cost judgement, not on a demonstration that TTA would lose score. Nothing in the public 0.946 notebook is left to port.

## 2026-09-09 gapcross result
- Hypothesis: Does the public notebook's tighter gap radius `GAP_CLOSE_UM` 5.0 interact with our gap budget, and do the short-track floor and rescue pay?
- Scope: 128 movies, 238 min CPU. Six arms in a 2x2 on radius x budget plus two short-track arms.
- Experiment: Anchor `ANCHOR_D187 F4-6bba(12) adj_J 0.9216 -> OK (+0.0000)`. Control `g9c3`, the pre-cap20 baseline, written into the script's own output before the run.
- Result:

  | arm | gate | cap | short | rescue | adj_J | div_J | score | d score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF | 9.0 | 0.02 | 4 | off | 0.9133 | 0.1337 | 0.9266 | +0.0000 |
  | g5 | 5.0 | 0.02 | 4 | off | 0.9132 | 0.1340 | 0.9266 | −0.0001 |
  | g5c3 | 5.0 | 0.003 | 4 | off | 0.9127 | 0.1344 | 0.9261 | −0.0005 |
  | g9c3 | 9.0 | 0.003 | 4 | off | 0.9124 | 0.1360 | 0.9260 | −0.0006 (CONTROL) |
  | s6 | 9.0 | 0.02 | 6 | off | 0.9133 | 0.1343 | 0.9267 | +0.0001 |
  | s6r | 9.0 | 0.02 | 6 | on | 0.9134 | 0.1343 | 0.9268 | +0.0002 |

  The control loses −0.0006, so the harness exercises the gap stage. At the loose budget, tightening the radius costs −0.0001 (REF -> g5). At the tight budget, tightening the radius moves g9c3 −0.0006 -> g5c3 −0.0005, i.e. nothing, and slightly the other way. Read one at a time, g5 alone reads "harmless" and g5c3 alone reads "−0.0005"; the square shows the budget carrying both. `SHORT_MIN` 4 -> 6 is +0.0001, consistent with the leaderboard record for the reverse move (6 -> 4 scored 0.000); adding the rescue is a further +0.0001. The rescue mechanism runs — the log shows it proposing 236 components and rescuing 114 of them, 503 nodes.

  How to read six rows inside ±0.0006 (corrected 2026-09-09; the original text said `accdiag` put this holdout's own noise at 0.002-0.003 and used that to call every row "no detectable effect"). `accdiag` measured how often the acceleration column is computable, not a noise floor. The pipeline is deterministic: eight `random_state` values through the gate give the identical 46 / 39 / 79, and the local reproduction of divbench3 and divbench8 hits both recorded rows exactly. Repeat-run noise is zero, so `s6r`'s +0.0002 is an exact property of these 128 movies. A bootstrap interval measures whether the sign would survive a different draw of movies, which is a transfer question, not a measurement-error one. The submission rule in force is local positive + LB positive is a real gain, however small.
- Conclusion: The radius does nothing at either budget, so our +0.002 leaderboard win came from the budget and cannot be un-bound by their radius. `GAP_CLOSE_UM` 5.0 buys nothing; ours stays at the public baseline 9.0. The short-track pair is worth +0.0001 / +0.0002. Of the six differences from the public 0.946 notebook, five were closed at this point — three from the existing record (disappearance, ILP division weight, density-adaptive gap) and two here — leaving edge-feature TTA (`ttaprobe`, queued behind Kaggle's two-concurrent-GPU-session limit).

## 2026-09-08 zprofile and hpara pipeline arm
- Hypothesis: the z-edge sag in detector response is caused by the network degrading at the z border of its own input (zero padding), branch (b), rather than by cells physically half outside the imaged volume, branch (a). Second line: hpara placement can be swapped for refine placement without retraining anything.
- Scope: zprofile is CPU, ~1 min, on gtsplit's CSVs (13,646 GT cells with `h_gt`, the F4 heatmap value at the annotated voxel, not just the 313). All 24 movies are Z=64 and every GT cell joined. Matched cells are 97.6% / 96.0% of GT and serve as the control. Caveat recorded before the numbers: a real biological gradient would also bend the curve, so only a symmetric sag at both ends points at the network. The hpara arm measures placement alone and does not retrain the ranker, so a positive result is trustworthy and a negative one is not decisive.
- Experiment: two lines, in the order the user set (hpara arm first).
  1. `hparacache` (GPU, 35.9 min T4) + `hparabench` / `hparabench_ref` (CPU). `fdet_F4_<name>.npz` stores only final coordinates and scores, so `hpara` — which needs the heatmap — cannot be recomputed from it; only the 24 bench movies are re-cached, at fuse6bba's 82 s/movie. Design choice: NMS runs once, on the `refine` coordinates, and the survivors are placed both ways, holding detection count, order and identity fixed so the cached edge-head probabilities stay validly joined by (t, i, j); this forgoes hpara's +0.0008 recall, which came from NMS acting on better coordinates. `hparabench` is divbench9 with 51 lines changed: `DET_SRC` repoints `FDET_F4` at the hpara caches, the F4 anchors demote to soft in that run only, and per-movie rows are dumped to CSV so the two runs pair for a bootstrap. `hparabench_ref` (`DET_SRC=F4`) keeps divbench9's 0.9216 hard anchor. `tools/test_hparacache.py` plants a Gaussian at a known sub-voxel position. The bench loads `edge_ranker_ep175v3_bidir.pkl`, fitted by `edgeprob-rank2` on the 175-movie pool's refine-based features, and applies it to hpara coordinates; re-fitting would mean re-caching all 187 movies (about four GPU hours against 35 minutes for the 24) plus re-running `edgeprob-rank2`.
  2. `zprofile` (CPU, ~1 min, `biohub-zprofile`): joins `h_gt` to each cell's z from the geff, against the true stack depth read from the zarr metadata.
- Result:
  - `hparacache` anchor: 24 of 24 movies, every frame of every movie reproduced the shipped `fdet_F4_` cache exactly, so the heatmap pass is bit-identical. Displacement |hpara − refine| p50 0.43 um, p90 0.75, max ~1.34, uniform across all 24 movies (per-movie p50 spans 0.427-0.488) — inside both the 4.0 um NMS radius and the 7 um match radius.
  - `tools/test_hparacache.py`: the shift cuts placement error 0.646 -> 0.044 um on clean blobs. The kernel's anchor cannot catch a no-op shift (the anchor is the control arm), which is why that test exists.
  - `hparabench_ref` took four pushes on its source list: v1 missed `biohub-edgeprob2`, v2 missed the pool's `fdet_F4_` caches, v3 missed `biohub-edgeprob-rank2`; each came from copying divbench9's docstring rather than its metadata. v4 pulls divbench9's real metadata (`py kag.py kernels pull <ref> -m`) and copies it verbatim; that list contains `biohub-zh-detect` and `biohub-edgeprob-rank2` and excludes `fuse44b6` and `ep44b6`. Corrected: `kernel_sources` does not cap at 10 — 12 sources pushed fine (corrected 2026-09-08; an earlier draft said it appears to cap at 10). The real constraint is that a named source kernel must have completed a run; naming one that has not prints a warning and pushes without it.
  - Pair gate: the first F4HP push died on `44b6_0b24845f t=0: 40 of 990 harness pairs have no edgeprob row`. Candidate pairs are distance-gated at `GATE_UM = 10.0` and hpara moves every detection by a median 0.43 um, so pairs cross that line in both directions per frame. Detections are identical but the pair set is not, so both heads were re-cached on hpara coordinates:

| kernel | writes | cost | check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biohub-ephpcache` | `edgeprob_F4hp_*` x24 | 15.2 min T4 | n_per_frame 24/24 exact |
| `biohub-ep2hpcache` | `edgeprob2_F4hp_*` x24 | 15.1 min T4 | n_per_frame 24/24 exact |

    `ep2hpcache` needed two versions: v1 inherited `edgeprob2_cache`'s job list, `[("base", n) for n in names] + [("F4", n) for n in names_f4]`, putting 199 base movies ahead of the 24 wanted — 70 minutes in it was still in the base pass, against 16 minutes for the whole job once cut. Cutting exposed two inherited-tail bugs from hard-coded label prefixes: `n_f4` counted `edgeprob2_F4_` when the label is `F4hp_`, and `complete` demanded `n_base == len(names)` = 199 outputs the version never writes. `ephpcache` has the first, so its landed run printed `EPHPCACHE INCOMPLETE ... NOT OK` on a run that cached all 24 and passed its check 24/24 — a false negative; the outputs are good. Both makers are fixed; `ephpcache` was not re-run.
  - Padding facts checked in the code: every 3D convolution in the repo is `nn.Conv3d(..., 3, padding=1)` and `padding_mode` appears zero times, so all use PyTorch's default zeros. That covers `UNet3D` (the three xl branches) and `_DCDeepCenterUNet3D` (the official DeepCenter and our ep05 retrain of it), and therefore the public 0.948 notebook. The whole volume goes through in one forward pass (`branch_maps4`), so the only boundary is the real one. Receptive field: 2 convs per block, `MaxPool3d(2)` pooling z as well, 64 -> 32 -> 16 -> 8; encoder reach in original planes 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 = 30, decoder about as much again, against a stack only 64 planes deep. Separate untested hole: a `state_dict` does not carry `padding_mode`, so if the original authors trained the official DeepCenter with reflect padding our reimplementation would load their weights without error and run inference with the wrong padding; checkable by comparing our heatmap against the public notebook's on one volume.
  - zprofile, among cells the detector found:

| | 6bba | 44b6 |
|---|---|---|
| h_gt, within 4 planes of an edge | 0.385 (n=2,096) | 0.205 (n=316) |
| h_gt, 12+ planes in | 0.366 (n=6,309) | 0.306 (n=2,064) |
| ratio | 1.054 | 0.672 |
| miss rate, 0-4 planes from an edge | 2.67% | 8.89% |
| miss rate, 10+ planes in | 2.13% | 1.90% |
| ratio | 1.26x | 4.68x |

    44b6's sag is symmetric in raw z (z 0-5 -> 0.219, z 55-63 -> 0.194, middle 0.30-0.32), which rules out simple light attenuation (monotone, one end dark).
  - shoulderfeat's 17-of-18 sign test stands as a fact about medians, but the miss-rate ratio is 1.26x on 6bba against 4.68x on 44b6.
  - Fix space had it been (b): inference-only — reflect-pad z and crop back, a measured z-calibration curve on the heatmap, or a depth-dependent detection threshold; retraining — random z-crop augmentation, reflect padding in the architecture, or partial convolutions. Reflect padding at inference is a distribution shift for a model trained with zeros; its control is that the interior must not move.
- Conclusion: branch (b) is refuted — one network, one architecture, one padding mode and Z=64 in every movie of both domains, yet the effect is present on 44b6 (ratio 0.672, miss ratio 4.68x) and absent on 6bba (1.054, 1.26x). The mirror-padding experiment is cancelled before it was pushed, along with reflect padding, z-calibration, depth-dependent thresholds, partial convolutions and z-crop augmentation. The symmetric raw-z sag on 44b6 fits branch (a): partially imaged cells at both ends of the stack. The z-edge effect is a 44b6 story, not a pipeline-wide lever. The hpara arm is pushed with both heads re-cached on hpara coordinates.

## 2026-09-08 shoulderfeat
- Hypothesis: the 313 shoulder cells carry a feature in the tracking graph's geometry or lineage that is knowable with no heatmap and no labels.
- Scope: geffs only, no images, no GPU. The 24 movies gtpeak measured (18 of them carry shoulder cells); z normalised inside each movie against p1..p99 of that movie's own GT z, then folded to distance from the middle of the stack. Cannot distinguish a cell physically half outside the imaged volume from a 3D UNet degrading at the z border of its own input.
- Experiment: kernel `biohub-shoulderfeat` v2. Run at `COMP_STRIDE = 1` (gtpeak).
- Result:
  - Per-movie z position (shoulder count, |z50 shoulder − .5|, |z50 all − .5|):

    | movie | shoulder | \|z50 sh − .5\| | \|z50 all − .5\| |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 6bba_3a1849c2 | 77 | 0.123 | 0.008 |
    | 44b6_a2bb48bb | 44 | 0.390 | 0.159 |
    | 6bba_3abfe10a | 40 | 0.331 | 0.144 |
    | 6bba_268e1230 | 33 | 0.123 | 0.025 |
    | 44b6_c96cfa10 | 22 | 0.473 | 0.176 |
    | 6bba_7b5d3b2c | 6 | 0.500 | 0.076 |
    | 44b6_0db75fae | 1 | 0.530 | 0.026 |

  - 17 of 18 movies put their shoulder cells nearer a z edge than their own cells, 0 against, 1 tie. Sign test p = 1.5e-5. Both ends: `44b6_c96cfa10` at 0.027 (near edge), `6bba_c27cba08` at 0.951 (far edge).
  - Distance to the nearer z edge (0 = at an edge, 0.5 = mid-stack), 13,646 measured cells:

    | bin | 6bba rate | 44b6 rate |
    |---|---|---|
    | 0.00-0.02 | 2.91% | 9.05% |
    | 0.02-0.06 | 1.12% | 7.27% |
    | 0.06-0.11 | 2.47% | 3.90% |
    | 0.17-0.23 | 2.36% | 2.01% |
    | 0.33-0.38 | 1.91% | 1.22% |
    | 0.44-0.50 | 1.30% | 1.18% |

  - 44b6 is a 7.7x gradient and nearly monotone; 6bba is 2.2x and noisy. In raw um: 44b6 14.00% in 0-9.75 um and 7.60% in 95.88-102.38 um against 0.36-2.3% in the middle.
  - (corrected 2026-09-08; earlier text tied this to 17 shoulder cells said to be "outside the volume" — that reading is withdrawn, see the SUPERSEDED note in the shoulderviz entry: a y/x index off-by-one in our own measurement, and 30 of the 48 such cells were matched by the detector.)
  - Run lengths, consecutive shoulder frames on one lineage, 155 runs over the 313 cells:

    | run | runs | cells | share |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 1 frame | 99 | 99 | 31.6% |
    | 2 | 26 | 52 | 16.6% |
    | 3 | 11 | 33 | 10.5% |
    | 4 | 7 | 28 | 8.9% |
    | 5-8 | 10 | 68 | 21.8% |
    | 12 | 1 | 12 | 3.8% |
    | 21 | 1 | 21 | 6.7% |

  - The run lengths are in real consecutive frames: GT is annotated on every frame of its own range, 23 of the 24 measured movies have zero missing frames, the exception being `44b6_87bba6c4`, which has no annotated cell at t=2. Several movies annotate only a sub-range (`3abfe10a` t=18-99, `0b24845f` 11-50, `33b596bf` 21-70, `c15fded2` 21-74, `e29f0176` 30-80, `0db75fae` 0-88), which shortens what a run can be but does not stretch a frame. 9.71% of 6bba's cells and 0.77% of 44b6's carry an annotation at all.
  - 99 cells (31.6%) are one-frame holes; at `GAP_SPAN = 1` a bridge can only reach those. 68% are holes of two or more frames, longest 21. The walk splits a run at a division rather than following both branches, which can only make runs look shorter, so 31.6% is an upper bound on the isolated share.
  - Track position, against the 24-movie control: shoulder cells are at a track START 8.9% / 4.5% of the time against 3.6% / 1.9% for all GT, and at a track END 7.6% / 7.9% against 3.7% / 2.0%.
  - 0 of 313 shoulder cells sits next to a division. Base rate 0.4% / 0.3%, so chance predicts about 1.2; zero is consistent with that.
  - Time: 44b6 rises from 0.33% in the third and fourth deciles to 5.0-5.7% in the last four. 6bba is flat around 2% with a 3.39% last decile. Confounded with z (the embryo moves in the volume), untested.
  - Crowding at the GT level is uninformative: GT annotates 9.71% of 6bba and 0.77% of 44b6, so the nearest annotated neighbour is a fact about the annotation. Both domains show U shapes with no interpretable ordering.
  - (corrected 2026-09-08; v1 had a denominator bug: it iterated every train movie in the two domains, 199 of them, but only 24 were ever measured by gtpeak. The other 175 contributed ~120,000 cells labelled "not shoulder", diluting every rate roughly tenfold. v1's decile tables are void; its per-movie table was unaffected, because each row uses only its own movie's cells.)
- Conclusion: shoulder cells sit at a z edge of the stack, at both ends, per-movie, with sign-test p = 1.5e-5; the effect is 7.7x on 44b6 and 2.2x on 6bba. This is knowable at inference with no labels. It does not distinguish "physically half outside the volume" (unrecoverable) from "3D UNet degrades at its input's z border" (a padding choice, fixable); the z sweeps rendered by `shoulderviz` v3 can, cell by cell. `gap_close` at `GAP_SPAN = 1` has a ceiling of about a third of these cells.

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: one variable (the fork gate pickle) on the 0.943 pipeline; hidden public split of unknown composition.
- Experiment: `submit_joint.py`, the production script. Fork gate retrained on both domains' counted forks (`fork_gate_joint.pkl`, 128 6bba + 71 44b6 movies, p > 0.03). Its only difference from `submit_gate.py` is the pickle name plus an assert that the loaded gate carries n_train 6bba 299 / 44b6 67 / tp 56, which stopped a silently-6bba-only gate from being submitted as the joint one.

  - LB 0.944, ref 56086066. Control: ref 56055405 = 0.943 (same code, 6bba-only gate). Δ +0.001.
  - divbench8 measured +0.0037 with a 90% interval of [+0.0016, +0.0060]; the entry predicted about +0.003 after the 85/15 domain weighting.

The competition score sums edge TP/FP/FN across movies and divides once, so a movie's weight in the aggregate is its edge count.

    | ref | change | control | LB | verdict |
    |---|---|---|---|---|

## 2026-09-08/09 public 0.946 notebook read
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: three public notebooks — `biohub-cell-tracking-0-946-lb` (Reyhan Ksatria, 2026-09-08), `biohub-harmonic-fusion` (120 votes), `biohub-942tta` (96 votes) — are the same code; harmonic-fusion is 942tta with the comments stripped and a new title. Source read only, no arm run here. Entry also records the three-domain hpara caches (6bba, 44b6, zebrahub).
- Experiment: read of the three notebooks' source. Their pipeline is driven by 57 `BIOHUB_*` environment variables; the official `predict_unet_transformer.py` reads 0 of them (checked: 0 occurrences) — the knobs are added by `_patch_text` rewriting the same official script at runtime, so none is a switch to flip. Kernels pushed off this read: `ttaprobe` (2026-09-09), `gapcross`. Caches: `hparacache` v3, `zhhpcache`.
- Result:
  Of eleven constants existing on both sides, five are byte-identical: 2.25, 10.0, 0.0076, 0.00375, 0.48. Six differ:

  | | theirs | ours | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | gap radius `GAP1_GATE_UM` | 5.0 | 9.0 | live; ours is the untouched public baseline, they moved it |
  | short filter | 6 | 4 | live only paired with their rescue |
  | division parent / sister um | 9.0 / 14.0 | 12.0 / 15.0 | rejected, measured (`divradius` 2026-09-09: their parent radius −0.0039 score, their sister radius an exact zero) |
  | ILP disappearance | 2 | 1.5 | rejected, measured |
  | ILP division weight | 1.2 | 0.55 | architectural, not a knob |
  | gap density adaptive | on | absent | not worth it, measured from their code |

  - disappearance 2: `ilpsweep` (2026-09-05) ran the notebook's ILP settings on our nodes: +0.0002 / −0.0115 / −0.0010, deleting 6-15% of our nodes where theirs deletes 39%, and the deleted chains are 62% / 91% / 58% true edges where the scorer looks. Their 2 is tuned for a node set far smaller than ours (18,618 against our 23,371 on the same movie).
  - ILP division weight 1.2: our constant's comment says it was "set from the fine sweep's argmax", swept with the fork gate present. The public baseline is 1.0; they went up to 1.2 to make the ILP emit divisions natively and filter them with geometry + DeepCenter, we went down to 0.55 and let the learned fork gate decide.
  - gap density adaptive: from their source, the radius moves by `clip(0.040 * (local_spacing - 6.5), ±0.125)` um, i.e. at most ±0.125 on a 5 um radius (2.5%), and `GAIN 0.04` needs a 3 um departure from the reference to reach that. It appears nowhere in their 0.934 -> 0.939 -> 0.941 -> 0.946 progression.

  Edge-feature TTA (+0.005, their 0.941 -> 0.946): the eight D4 views were already averaged into the detection logits, but the UNet feature map handed to the edge predictor came from the original orientation only. The code difference:

  ```python
  _,       det_flip = model.encode(imgs_flip)   # baseline: features discarded
  _u_flip, det_flip = model.encode(imgs_flip)   # theirs: kept, inverted, averaged
  ```

  `model.encode` returns both; the baseline throws the features away. Our `edgeprob_cache.py` comment: "det_tta only affects the detection logits, which are discarded here... Off saves three U-Net passes per window." That leaves our edge features single-view.

  `ttaprobe` (pushed 2026-09-09) decides whether that is worth ~20 GPU hours, for about one. It wraps `model.encode` so the D4 average happens inside it, leaving `predict_video` byte-identical and `det_tta` off; detections cannot move because `_detect_cells_pooled` is already injected. 12 holdout movies x 3 arms (1, 4, 8 views), labelling its own pairs, reporting single-column AUC of `p_fwd` — no bench, no ILP, no thresholds. It also prints how far the probabilities moved and the encode-call counts.

  `gapcross` (pushed) crosses the two live candidates: our only pre-fork-gate LB win was loosening the gap budget (0.003 -> 0.02, +0.002), which worked because the budget was binding — 30 of 83 datasets at the cap, 64% of demand unrepaired; their step tightened the gap radius, which proposes fewer repairs and can un-bind the budget. Six arms off one ILP solve per movie (`patch_final` rebuilds from a fresh copy): REF, g5, g5c3, g9c3 as a control that must lose, s6, s6r. Their rescue only considers components of length `[4, OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN)`; we run SHORT_MIN = 4, so that window is empty here and porting the rescue alone would change nothing. The unit under test is (SHORT_MIN 6 + rescue).

  Three-domain hpara caches, both anchors exact:

  | kernel | scope | cost | anchor |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `hparacache` v3 | 140 movies (128 6bba + 12 44b6) | 203 min T4 | every frame of every movie reproduces `fdet_F4_` exactly |
  | `zhhpcache` | 41 zebrahub crops | 44 min T4 | 4,100 of 4,100 frames reproduce `zhdet_` exactly |

  |hpara − refine|: 6bba/44b6 p50 median 0.460 um (p90 0.789, max 1.479); zebrahub p50 0.673 (p90 1.059, max 4.674, 1.28M detections). The larger zebrahub displacement is expected from a different instrument and voxel size; it is the first hpara number for a third domain.
- Conclusion: three of the six differing knobs are already measured and rejected on our own data, one (ILP division weight 1.2) is a different pipeline stage rather than a better number, and two (gap radius, short filter + rescue) remain live and are tested by `gapcross`. Edge-feature TTA is the only candidate with a stated delta (+0.005) and is tested by `ttaprobe`.

## 2026-09-08 hparabench round 1
- Hypothesis: whether hpara's better detection placement converts into score, with the ranker fixed and fitted on BASE coordinates.
- Scope: the bench scores SIX = all 128 6bba movies; the hpara caches cover the 24 evaluation movies, of which 12 are 6bba, so only 12 movies changed. The bench never scores 44b6 at all (the 71 44b6 movies are training data only, on BASE coordinates), so the other 12 caches produced nothing and this round says nothing about 44b6. The 116 untouched movies dilute the aggregate about 10x; tables below are the 12 that moved. n = 12 movies, 12 GT divisions.
- Experiment: `biohub-hparabench` v4 + `hparabench-ref`, ~170 min CPU each, control anchor exact. Round 2 pushed 2026-09-08: v5 both arms, ~170 min CPU each, no GPU, labelling the F4/F4HP pair rows with `label_rows` (reads the GT, CPU only) and scoring them with the same fitted model, out of fold, on the same 12 movies.
- Result:
  Control `hparabench_ref` (DET_SRC=F4) reproduces divbench9 on all four columns over its 128 rows — edge_J 0.9104, adj_J 0.9133, div_J 0.1337, score 0.9266.

  | | refine (ships) | hpara | delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | edge_J | 0.9235 | 0.9217 | −0.0018 |
  | adj_J | 0.9265 | 0.9248 | −0.0018 |
  | div_J | 0.0769 | 0.1250 | +0.0481 |
  | score | 0.9342 | 0.9373 | +0.0031 |

  | | div TP | div FP | div FN | edge TP | edge FP | edge FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | refine | 3 | 27 | 9 | 9,836 | 338 | 477 |
  | hpara | 5 | 28 | 7 | 9,828 | 350 | 485 |
  | delta | +2 | +1 | −2 | −8 | +12 | +8 |

  Twelve GT divisions across twelve movies; 3 caught became 5. div_J carries 0.1 weight; two events move it 0.048. Edge side: −8 TP, +12 FP, +8 FN out of ~10,650, every component the same direction; per movie 6 up 6 down. Paired bootstrap spans zero everywhere: CHANGED-only +0.0026 [−0.0023, +0.0077], all-128 +0.0003 [−0.0002, +0.0009].

  Cost of the decisive experiment, from the three cache kernels' own runtimes: hparacache 24 movies / 35.9 min, ephpcache 15.2, ep2hpcache 15.1 -> about 6 GPU hours to extend all three to 128 movies.

  Two process failures:
  1. `hparapair` aggregated the score wrong, caught by running the control through the anchor: adj_edge_jaccard is not `edge_J * (1 - 0.1 * ratio)` on the aggregate. The scorer applies the node penalty per sample and weight-averages the per-sample adjusted values by `tp+fp+fn`. The wrong form read 0.9126 against a recorded 0.9133 — 0.0007, four times the effect being measured. Fixed from `tracking_cellmot/metrics.py`; the anchor is now asserted in the output rather than printed.
  2. The F4HP arm was marked ERROR on a successful run: it scored 128/128, wrote its CSV, then died on `ANCHOR_D187 0.9204 want 0.9216` and `REF_FORKS`. The maker edited `ANCHOR_HARD`/`ANCHOR_SOFT`, but those two anchors never consult those dicts — both compare against a hard-coded number and append straight to `ANCHOR_FAIL`. Both anchors sit on HOLDOUT_6BBA, the 12 movies this arm changes, so a miss is the measurement. Now printed as `[expected]`; any other anchor still aborts. The CSV is written before the assert, so v4's data was usable and no re-run was needed.
- Conclusion: with the ranker fixed and fitted on BASE coordinates, swapping refine for hpara on 12 movies does not improve the 6bba score and moves the edges slightly the wrong way; the +0.0031 is two division events. It does not touch `refinecmp`, which measured placement. The edge regression is small but coherent in every component, which is also what a distribution shift would look like — this round cannot separate that from "does not convert". 44b6 is unmeasured here.

## 2026-09-08 refinecmp
- Hypothesis: whether an alternative sub-voxel placement rule beats the shipped `refine` in recall and in frame-to-frame jitter.
- Scope: 6bba (1,047 GT anchor points) and 44b6 (297 points). Placement only; whether reduced jitter converts into score is not tested. The ranker was trained on `refine` coordinates, so a direct swap changes its input distribution.
- Experiment: `biohub-refinecmp` v3, 36.5 min T4, both anchors exact. Five placement rules on the same peaks, so nothing is added or removed and recall can only move by a point crossing the 7 um match radius.

  | rule | what it does |
  |---|---|
  | `nore` | the bare pooled grid, no sub-voxel work — the floor |
  | `refine` | what ships: intensity centre of mass on the raw volume |
  | `refsm` | the same, smoothed |
  | `hcent` | centre of mass of the heatmap in a 3x3x3 window |
  | `hpara` | parabolic vertex of the heatmap, one axis at a time |

  Prior input: gtpeak measured F4 detections jittering 1.29 / 1.51 um p50 between consecutive frames against a real displacement of 2.72 / 2.10 um.
- Result:
  6bba (recall 0.9761 reproduced exactly):

  | rule | recall | \|offset\| p50 | jitter p50 | jitter >1um | >2um |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `nore` | 0.9772 | 1.65 | 1.46 | 62.9% | 21.8% |
  | `refine` (ships) | 0.9780 | 1.41 | 1.29 | 60.0% | 17.1% |
  | `refsm` | 0.9778 | 1.46 | 1.37 | 62.8% | 19.8% |
  | `hcent` | 0.9777 | 1.50 | 1.24 | 56.9% | 13.8% |
  | `hpara` | 0.9789 | 1.31 | 0.89 | 47.3% | 11.9% |

  44b6 (recall 0.9596 reproduced exactly):

  | rule | recall | \|offset\| p50 | jitter p50 | jitter >1um | >2um |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `nore` | 0.9620 | 1.75 | 1.72 | 71.7% | 33.9% |
  | `refine` (ships) | 0.9647 | 1.71 | 1.51 | 66.9% | 26.8% |
  | `refsm` | 0.9637 | 1.77 | 1.54 | 70.8% | 29.7% |
  | `hcent` | 0.9634 | 1.73 | 1.56 | 65.3% | 25.3% |
  | `hpara` | 0.9647 | 1.62 | 1.40 | 58.6% | 23.0% |

  Against the shipped rule: 6bba +0.0008 recall, −0.10 um offset, −0.40 um jitter; 44b6 +0.0000 recall, −0.08 um offset, −0.11 um jitter. Same sign on every column in both domains; `hpara` is the best arm in both. Jitter share above one micron falls 60.0% -> 47.3% and 66.9% -> 58.6%. The 0.40 um is removed from a 2.72 um real displacement, so on 6bba the manufactured share of apparent motion drops from 47% to 33%. It adds no nodes, so gtsplit's node-cost arithmetic does not apply and the penalty term cannot move.
- Conclusion: `hpara` beats the shipped `refine` on both domains in recall and jitter, at no node cost. The two rules that read the heatmap (`hpara`, `hcent`) are the two best for placement, and `hcent` also beats `refine` on 6bba jitter; an earlier use of dcpool's null result as evidence that heatmap-based point picking does not work is corrected by this. Whether the reduced jitter converts into score is untested.

## 2026-09-08 shoulderviz
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: 12 crops chosen dimmest-first out of the 313 shoulder cells, inspected by eye, with no control group of matched cells rendered the same way. A hypothesis with a picture attached, not a measurement. Does not contradict the density refutation, which asked a different question.
- Experiment: `biohub-shoulderviz` v1, 1.9 min CPU; v2 rendering fix; v3 2.8 min; v4; v5. CPU only, no detector. Four movies carrying 194 of the 313 (`6bba_3a1849c2` 77, `44b6_a2bb48bb` 44, `6bba_3abfe10a` 40, `6bba_268e1230` 33): one `_overview.gif` (100 frames, thin Z-slab MIP, GT circled thin blue, shoulder misses thick red) and six `_zoom<k>.gif` (~65 um crop around one miss, ±5 frames, slab centred on that cell's own z, ordered dimmest-first). 28 files. Also `biohub-nanwhere` (<1 min CPU) and the tests `tools/test_shoulderviz_depth.py`, `tools/test_shoulderfeat.py`.
- Result:
  - v1 rendering bug: the overview draws every GT node of the frame onto a slab fixed at `Z // 2`, so a cell at another depth appears as a circle on black. On `6bba_3a1849c2` t=50 that is 8 of 12 circles. v2 circles only in-slab cells and puts `GT in slab k/n` in the title; the zooms got the same filter. Nothing was concluded from v1's overviews.
  - Zooms: in every one of the 12 miss frames inspected the red circle sits immediately against a brighter neighbour — `6bba_3a1849c2` misses on the flanks of a bright chain of cells packed nose-to-tail; `6bba_268e1230` in the dim notch beside a bright blob; `44b6_a2bb48bb` in the dark seam between two elongated nuclei in dense tissue. Isolated cells in the same crops, circled blue, are found normally. Consistent with gtpeak's nearest real peak ~6 um away, on a neighbour.
  - Density refutation (2026-09-08, offline on gtsplit's CSVs): a movie's shoulder rate is not explained by that movie's detections per frame — corr +0.54 / +0.29 over 12 movies each, with `6bba_268e1230` at the second-worst rate and the lowest density. The crops suggest local crowding around the individual cell, which that test never measured.
  - `h_gt` is NaN in gtpeak exactly when the rounded GT index falls outside the heatmap array: 48 of 13,646 GT cells (0.35%), of which 30 are still matched and 17 are in the 313 shoulder bucket. Almost entirely 44b6, 34 of the 48 in one movie, `44b6_c96cfa10`, along what looks like a single lineage over t=64..94. (corrected 2026-09-08; earlier text read these as "the annotated position is outside the imaged field" and counted the 17 as information never recorded — refuted because 30 of the 48 were matched by the detector, which only runs inside the volume.) The mechanism is index arithmetic: gtpeak reads `yc = int(round(gt_vox[j, 1] / POOL))` with `POOL = 4`; the pooled axis has `Y/4` columns, so a cell in the last ~2 raw voxels of y or x rounds to index `Y/4`, one past the end, and reads NaN. z is not pooled and `round(z)` cannot leave `[0, Z-1]` for an in-volume cell.
  - `nanwhere` measurement: every one of the 24 movies is Z=64, Y=256, X=256, pooled to 64 x 64, and `Y % 4 == X % 4 == 0` so `pool_xy` discards nothing (0 GT cells in the truncated strip). Of the 48 NaN cells:

    | axis out of range | count |
    |---|---|
    | y | 26 |
    | x | 22 |
    | z | 0 |

    Their y or x is 254 or 255; z is ordinary (1, 5, 12, 17, 35, 51, 59, 60...). `round(254 / 4) = round(255 / 4) = 64` and the pooled axis has indices 0..63. Blast radius: none — `h_gt` is a diagnostic column only, the pipeline never indexes the heatmap at GT positions, so no score, bench number or submission is affected, and 64 pooled columns cover all 256 rows exactly. The "edge + out-of-volume ~= 14% of the 313" figure derived from the earlier reading is withdrawn; the z-edge attribution alone stands at ~27/313 ~= 9%.
  - v3: `.mp4` via libx264 (GIF fallback prints, so a silent downgrade cannot pass), contrast taken from the crop instead of the whole frame, and `<name>_zsweep<k>.mp4` — the crop at the miss frame, one z plane at a time from the top of the stack to the bottom, 64 planes. Motivated by `shoulderfeat`: the cells sit at a z edge in 17 of 18 movies, and "physically half outside the volume" and "the UNet degrades at its own z border" produce identical tables. On `44b6_a2bb48bb` the first sweep puts the missed cell at z=52 of 63.
  - v4 marker drop-out: v3 drew a circle only while the cell was within one voxel of the displayed plane, so each cell was visible for about three planes — 11 of 64 planes carried any blue on `44b6_a2bb48bb`, 17 of 64 on `6bba_3a1849c2`. v4 draws every marker and encodes distance instead: alpha `clip(1 - |dz|/10, 0.16, 1)`, line width in three steps, solid within 1.5 voxels and dashed beyond, marker size shrinking with depth; the red miss marker follows the same rule. The user chose the encoding over simply widening the tolerance to ±2-3 planes.
  - v5: v4's fade reached alpha 0.16 eight planes out, so on a 64-plane sweep distant markers were invisible over bright tissue — blue circles reached only 19 of 64 planes on `44b6_a2bb48bb` and 34 of 64 on `6bba_3a1849c2`, the red miss marker only 9. v5 floors alpha at 0.50, fades over 40 voxels instead of 10, carries the depth cue mainly in radius (down to 30% at distance) and dash, and draws a dark backing ring. 64 of 64 planes now carry every marker, blue and red.
  - `tools/test_shoulderviz_depth.py` renders one synthetic frame through the kernel's own drawing code and asserts that all five markers reach the canvas (v3 would draw two), that alpha is monotone in |dz| and floored above zero, and that matplotlib honours per-point `linewidths` and RGBA `edgecolors` alongside a per-collection `linestyle`.
  - Annotation density: GT annotates a median 9.71% of 6bba's cells and 0.77% of 44b6's, so a 44b6 crop showing fifty nuclei may legitimately carry one circle. In time the annotation is dense — every frame, in 23 of the 24 measured movies.
  - Follow-up pushed: `shoulderfeat` (CPU, geffs only, no images) measures depth in z, time, lineage run-length, position relative to divisions/track ends, and nearest annotated neighbour (labelled weak: GT covers 9.71% of 6bba and 0.77% of 44b6). The run-length column distinguishes 313 spread over 313 cells for one frame each (a `gap_close` problem) from 313 concentrated on 40 cells for 8 frames each. Its test, `tools/test_shoulderfeat.py`, plants a known lineage and a known depth effect, because there is no anchor for this run and the in-kernel `sum(runs) == len(sh_ids)` assertion would still pass on a walk that failed to back up.
- Conclusion: the 313 shoulder cells appear as cells pressed against a brighter neighbour in all 12 crops inspected, which is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and must not later be written as if gtpeak had proved it. The 48 NaN `h_gt` cells are ordinary cells against the y/x border read one index past the end by the diagnostic, not cells outside the volume, and nothing follows from them about recoverability.

## 2026-09-08 gtsplit
- Hypothesis: that splitting merged blobs recovers the 313 cells gtpeak found responding without a peak.
- Scope: 6bba (235 misses) and 44b6 (104 misses); detection stage only. `dets/fr` is the detection stage, not `N_pred` — the ILP candidate floor and `_short_filter` discard most surplus downstream, so a 3.5x detection increase is not a 3.5x node increase and this run cannot say what it would be.
- Experiment: `biohub-gtsplit` v1, both anchors exact. Shape split — threshold the heatmap, distance-transform the mask with the real voxel size, seed on maxima of the distance map, watershed — because gtpeak showed these cells have no intensity maximum.
- Result:

  | arm | mask | NMS | seed | 6bba dets/fr | recovered of 235 | 44b6 dets/fr | recovered of 104 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | BASE | -- | 4.0 | -- | 137.9 | -- | 310.1 | -- |
  | s05 | 0.05 | -- | 1 | 485.0 (3.5x) | 103 (43.8%) | 971.2 (3.1x) | 53 (51.0%) |
  | s15 | 0.15 | -- | 1 | 539.6 (3.9x) | 91 (38.7%) | 1,721.3 (5.6x) | 57 (54.8%) |
  | s15d | 0.15 | -- | 2 | 178.3 (1.29x) | 43 (18.3%) | 464.3 (1.50x) | 37 (35.6%) |
  | s15n | 0.15 | 4.0 | 2 | 142.8 (1.04x) | 30 (12.8%) | 321.4 (1.04x) | 24 (23.1%) |

  1. The ceiling is 44% / 55%, not 100%. The local test predicted this: on smooth merged Gaussians a shape split only separates the dim lobe in a narrow band of separation and amplitude ratio, and 4 of 20 synthetic configurations fell in it.
  2. Bucket breakdown: the `cold` bucket is never recovered (0/4, 0/1). The `1:1 gave it away` bucket is recovered completely on 44b6 (11/11). `nms-killed` comes back whenever NMS is off.
  3. NMS re-merges a third of what the split separates: s15d -> s15n costs 43 -> 30 (6bba) and 37 -> 24 (44b6) at the same seeding. No splitter can ship without changing `NMS_UM` too.
  4. At `s15n` — the only arm whose detection count the pipeline could absorb, +3.5% — 6bba's recall goes 0.9780 -> 0.9775: it recovered 30 of BASE's misses and lost 36 cells BASE already had, net −6. 44b6 nets +17 (recovers 24, loses 7). 6bba is 85% of the score weight.
  5. `reference.md`: an edge counts toward the denominator only if at least one endpoint matched a GT node, and "a fork lying entirely among unannotated cells enters none of the FP sets". So an edge between two unannotated detections is invisible to `adj_edge_jaccard` while `N_pred` counts every node. At 44b6's s15 the trade is +1,411 detections per frame for 57 recovered annotated cells over 964 frames — about 24,000 extra detections per annotated cell recovered.

  Design note on why no gate for shoulder points is possible, two independent walls: (a) a shoulder is defined as "not a local maximum", so any purely local criterion — value, shape, gradient, curvature — that fires on "a shoulder with a cell under it" must also fire on "the side of a cell"; (b) neither class is labelable — positives are visible only for the annotated fraction (6bba 9.71%, 44b6 0.77%), which gtpeak counted as 313, and negatives can never be confirmed because "no annotation here" does not mean "no cell here". The fork gate does have a negative class: every fork gets a TP/FP verdict from the official scorer. The only admissible evidence that a shoulder is a cell is external and topological — `_gap_close` asserts a cell must exist at a place and time (a track ends at t, another starts at t+2), which needs neither annotation nor a classifier.

  Correction, same day: an earlier version of that paragraph called the heatmap-placement route "largely already answered null" by `dcpool` and used its result as a prior. That transfer is invalid: (1) dcpool's stated mechanism is about the match radius, not position quality — a bridge insert's position "affects the metric only through whether the inserted node matches GT within 7.0 um", and a one-frame midpoint errs by about half a displacement (p50 1.82 um), so it lands inside the match radius essentially always; that is specific to bridge nodes, which `_gap_close` inserts after the solve, whereas an ordinary detection's position is decided before the solve and feeds the ranker's distance and velocity features. (2) DeepCenter ep05 is a deliberately non-converged checkpoint (`dccache3`: epoch 5 beats 7 beats 12, monotonically, in all three domains), and its peaks are still peaks — a shoulder in F4 is a shoulder in DeepCenter, because merged-blob geometry is a property of the image. dcpool's 20% snap rate is consistent with DeepCenter's peaks sitting where F4's already do. What remains true from dcpool: at span 1, post-link bridge position is metric-equivalent to the midpoint because 7 um swallows the error.
- Conclusion: splitting recovers at most 44% / 55% of the misses at 3.5-5.6x the detections, and at an affordable detection count it is net negative on 6bba (−6). Residue: 44b6's 11/11 recovery of the "two annotated cells, one detection" bucket, which is provable without a classifier (two GT cells inside one detection's radius) and is 11 cells rather than 313. `_refine` is unaffected by (4) and (5): it moves nodes that already exist, adds zero detections, needs no labels, and touches 100% of cells rather than 2.3%; `refinecmp` is that run.

## 2026-09-08 gtpeak
- Hypothesis: that F4's missed cells are cells the detector cannot see; also whether a peak survives NMS, and how large localisation error is.
- Scope: every annotated GT point in the 12 6bba holdout + 12 excluded 44b6, at every frame (detfuse3 used every 10th, giving n = 8 and n = 4 on its competition columns). Annotated cells only — 6bba labels 9.71% of its cells, 44b6 0.77% — so this is recall against a hand-picked sample.
- Experiment: `biohub-gtpeak` v1, 29.7 min, both anchors exact. Anchors on the `t % 10 == 0` subset: 6bba 1,047 GT / recall 0.9761, 44b6 297 / 0.9596. Full set: 10,699 and 2,947 points, recall 0.9780 and 0.9647.
- Result:
  Where the misses go:

  | bucket | 6bba (235 misses) | 44b6 (104) | the fix it implies |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | no peak, and the map is cold (h_win < 0.05) | 4 (1.7%) | 1 (1.0%) | a better detector |
  | no peak, but the map responds | 224 (95.3%) | 89 (85.6%) | peak extraction |
  | had a raw peak, NMS removed it | 6 (2.6%) | 3 (2.9%) | `NMS_UM` 4.0 |
  | a detection survived, the 1:1 gave it away | 1 (0.4%) | 11 (10.6%) | one detection, two cells |

  Five cells in 13,646 are genuinely invisible — 0.04% of annotated GT; the 2026-08-25 entry described this class as "the detector produces no response for them at all". At a missed cell, h_win p50 = 0.15 and h at the GT voxel p50 = 0.10 / 0.11 in both batches — above the 0.05 peak-finding floor, at or below the 0.15 gate. 98.3% / 99.0% are >= 0.05 within 3.25 um, against detfuse3's 99.6% on Zebrahub.

  The nearest raw `peak_local_max` output at any score is p50 5.84 um (6bba) / 6.91 um (44b6) from a missed cell: a response of 0.10-0.15 at the cell, nearest actual local maximum six or seven microns away, on a different cell. `peak_local_max` at threshold 0.05 would have emitted these if they were maxima. Same mechanism div-mass saw as 44.7% of divisions with both daughters in one watershed label; 44b6's 10.6% "one detection, two cells" bucket is 25x 6bba's. NMS accounts for 2.6% and 2.9%; `NMS_UM` 4.0 has never been swept and this says not to bother.

  Localisation, over the 10,464 / 2,843 cells F4 does find:

  | | 6bba | 44b6 |
  |---|---|---|
  | \|offset\| p50 / p90 / p99 um | 1.41 / 3.47 / 6.67 | 1.71 / 5.91 / 6.90 |
  | mean signed offset (z, y, x) um | −0.384, −0.018, +0.056 | −0.142, +0.210, +0.145 |
  | std per axis um | 1.533, 1.062, 1.074 | 2.205, 1.497, 1.517 |

  The only systematic term is 6bba's −0.384 um in z against a std of 1.533; a bias mostly cancels inside a link, jitter does not.

  Change in offset between a cell and its own next frame, along 10,009 / 2,729 GT track steps:

  | | 6bba | 44b6 |
  |---|---|---|
  | \|offset(t+1) − offset(t)\| p50 / p90 / p99 um | 1.29 / 2.41 / 8.16 | 1.51 / 5.76 / 10.49 |
  | steps above 1 um | 60.0% | 66.9% |
  | steps above 2 um | 17.1% | 26.8% |
  | real link length `d_pc1` p50 / p90 um (fork table) | 2.72 / 5.05 | 2.10 / 3.81 |
  | invented motion as a share of real, at p50 | 47% | 72% |

  At p90 in 44b6 the jitter exceeds the real displacement (5.76 against 3.81). The pooled grid is 1.625 um isotropic; independent quantisation at t and t+1 gives a difference with per-axis std 1.625/sqrt(12)·sqrt(2) = 0.66 um, about 1.15 um in magnitude, against 6bba's observed 1.29. `_refine` (centre of mass of the raw volume over ±2 z, ±5 yx) exists to remove that: p50 1.65 -> 1.39 um, while p75 goes 1.93 -> 2.00 and 44b6's p90 goes 4.19 -> 4.25 — it helps the median slightly and hurts the tail, and had never been validated until now. 44b6's 1.51 p50 and 5.76 p90 exceed quantisation, so a second term is present there.

  Caveats: `d_pc1` is measured at fork sites and is itself a detected distance, so it already contains the jitter — the true displacement is smaller and the 47% / 72% are understatements. The offset is to whichever detection the greedy 1:1 assigned; at 7 um that could occasionally be a neighbour, though a p50 of 1.41 um says most are the right cell.
- Conclusion: refuted on competition data with n = 13,646 — the detector responds at 95%+ of missed cells; what fails is turning a response into a local maximum when a brighter neighbour owns the blob. Two levers follow, neither requiring retraining: peak extraction (splitting merged blobs — watershed on the heatmap, or a lower-threshold second pass constrained to non-maximal ridges), target 224 + 89 = 313 cells, 2.3% of annotated GT; and sub-voxel localisation (a better `_refine`), target about half of 6bba's frame-to-frame jitter, which is 47% of real displacement.

## 2026-09-08 divbench9
- Hypothesis: that `DIV_W` 0.35 and the joint gate fix different forks and their gains add.
- Scope: 128 movies, 125 GT divisions. Two solves, four cells, three of them already measured as anchors; one new number.
- Experiment: `biohub-divbench9` v1, all three anchors exact. Paired bootstrap over the 128 movies, 2,000 draws, same resample for every cell.
- Result:

  | | gate6 (6bba only) | joint (+ 44b6's 67) |
  |---|---|---|
  | REF (0.55) | 42/47/83, 0.2442, 0.9387 (anchor, divbench3) | 46/39/79, 0.2805, 0.9424 (anchor, divbench8) |
  | dw35 (0.35) | 50/68/75, 0.2591, 0.9402 (anchor, divbench6) | 50/52/75, 0.2825, 0.9426 |

  All three anchors reproduce to four decimals; adj_J is 0.9143 in every cell, so the whole difference is the division term.

  Additivity:

      DIV_W alone  +0.0015     joint alone  +0.0037
      sum if independent  +0.0052     larger alone  +0.0037
      MEASURED TOGETHER   +0.0039   =  75% of the independent sum

  | cell | mean d vs REF+gate6 | 90% | distinguishable |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | REF + joint | +0.0038 | [+0.0016, +0.0061] | yes |
  | dw35 + gate6 | +0.0016 | [−0.0022, +0.0054] | no |
  | dw35 + joint | +0.0039 | [+0.0009, +0.0069] | yes |
  | dw35+joint vs REF+joint | +0.0002 | [−0.0032, +0.0036] | no |

  divbench6's +0.0015 does not survive its first interval: [−0.0022, +0.0054] straddles zero. divbench6 was cut from divbench4 before the bootstrap machinery existed and flagged this in its own words — "the effect size is at the resolution floor and has no interval around it". Passing the both-folds rule is necessary, not sufficient.

  Given the joint gate, DIV_W 0.35 is worth +0.0002, [−0.0032, +0.0036]. dw35 still finds 4 more true divisions under the joint gate (50 against 46) and pays 13 more false ones (52 against 39).

  History of the constant: `ranker-fine` chose 0.55 against a pipeline with no gate; divbench6 reopened it and chose 0.35 against the 6bba-only gate; divbench9 swaps in a better gate and 0.35 is worth nothing again. The 2026-09-08 argmax rule states that a constant is provisional whenever a stage changes the cost of the failure it was chosen against.
- Conclusion: refuted — `DIV_W` 0.35 and the joint gate fix the same forks. Residue: `DIV_W` 0.35 recovers 4 true divisions the joint gate misses, and the joint gate rejects 16 false forks 0.35 produces; something keeping the 4 without the 16 would be worth about +0.001, below what this bench can resolve on 125 GT divisions. What ships is unchanged: the joint gate alone, `DIV_W` stays 0.55. `submit_joint` (ref 56086066) is already the right submission and this run says not to follow it with a DIV_W one.

## 2026-09-08 divbench6

- Hypothesis: that `DIV_W = 0.55` is still the right price for a fork now that a fork gate cleans up behind the solver; and, from the opposite direction to divbench7, whether fork COUNT or the SOURCE that produces the forks governs the gated result.
- Scope: 128 6bba movies, four arms of `DIV_W` (0.55 REF / 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.20). Each arm gated by a fork gate trained out of fold on ITS OWN forks, because the arm changes the fork population. No paired bootstrap in this run — it was cut from divbench4, before that machinery existed — so effect sizes here carry no interval.
- Experiment: `divbench6.py` (built by make_divbench6.py), kernel biohub-divbench6 v1, 240.5 min, 128/128 movies, anchors exact. `DIV_W` is read by `solve_one`, so every arm is its own full ILP solve over all 128 movies: 4 solves. Fork gate cut p > 0.03, official scorer.
- Result:
  REF (0.55) reproduces 50/249/75, div_J 0.1337, adj_J 0.9133, score 0.9266 exactly.

  Mechanism check — where the forks are produced (ungated):

  | arm | forks | ILP forks | patch forks | div tp/fp/fn | div_J | adj_J | score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF (0.55) | 7,004 | 2,490 | 4,514 | 50 / 249 / 75 | 0.1337 | 0.9133 | 0.9266 |
  | dw45 | 9,955 | 5,692 | 4,263 | 61 / 369 / 64 | 0.1235 | 0.9130 | 0.9254 |
  | dw35 | 10,027 | 5,762 | 4,265 | 62 / 371 / 63 | 0.1250 | 0.9130 | 0.9255 |
  | dw20 | 10,169 | 5,903 | 4,266 | 62 / 375 / 63 | 0.1240 | 0.9129 | 0.9253 |

  Ungated, this reproduces the August shape: more forks, div_J falls because the false ones outnumber the true, every arm loses about -0.0012 of score. The arms find 12 more true divisions (50 -> 62).

  Gated, each arm by its own out-of-fold gate:

  | arm | div tp/fp/fn | div_J | adj_J | score | vs REF+gate | fold0 | fold1 | that gate's AUC |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF + gate | 42 / 47 / 83 | 0.2442 | 0.9143 | 0.9387 | -- | -- | -- | 0.9283 / 0.8326 |
  | dw45 + gate | 52 / 71 / 73 | 0.2653 | 0.9143 | 0.9408 | +0.0021 | +0.0060 | -0.0002 | 0.9176 / 0.8656 |
  | dw35 + gate | 50 / 68 / 75 | 0.2591 | 0.9143 | 0.9402 | +0.0015 | +0.0029 | +0.0012 | 0.9166 / 0.8862 |
  | dw20 + gate | 50 / 71 / 75 | 0.2551 | 0.9142 | 0.9397 | +0.0010 | +0.0029 | +0.0004 | 0.9198 / 0.8792 |

  Rule fixed in advance: a candidate iff it beats REF+gate in BOTH folds. dw35 and dw20 pass; dw45 fails on -0.0002 in fold 1 despite the largest gain and the most true divisions of any arm.

  Per-arm gate AUC averaged over folds: 0.8805 -> 0.9014 at dw35, almost all of it in the weaker fold (0.8326 -> 0.8862) while fold 0 gives up 0.0117. Against divbench7, which moved production the other way:

  | run | production moved to | forks added | mean out-of-fold AUC | gated result |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | divbench7 | the patch (precision 0.150) | +1,862 | 0.8805 -> 0.8656 | -0.0005, folds disagree |
  | divbench6 | the solver (precision 0.196) | +3,023 | 0.8805 -> 0.9014 | +0.0015, both folds up |

  ILP fork precision 0.196 against the patch's 0.150, re-confirmed on REF here.

  Effect size: dw35's div_J gain is +0.0149, inside the ±0.03 bar the bench resolves; adj_J unchanged (0.9143 against 0.9143). For comparison, divbench8 reads +0.0037 [+0.0016, +0.0060].

  (corrected 2026-09-08 by divbench9, same day; earlier text read the +0.0015 as a shipping candidate.) The paired bootstrap on the +0.0015 reads [-0.0022, +0.0054], so it is not distinguishable from zero, and given the joint gate `DIV_W` 0.35 is worth +0.0002. `DIV_W` 0.35 does not ship.

  August origin of 0.55: `biohub-ranker-fine` measured `DIV_W` on 12 GT divisions with no gate in the pipeline and picked the argmax 0.55, its own entry stating "0.45-0.65 are all defensible". What made 0.20 lose there was over-forking — 1,024 forks, 57 counted false ones — which is the failure the fork gate removes.
- Conclusion: the governing variable is which stage makes the forks, not how many are made; divbench6 adds more forks than divbench7 and comes out ahead. The mechanism finding rests on two runs pointing opposite ways. The constant change does not ship: after divbench9 the +0.0015 is indistinguishable from zero and the joint gate absorbs it. Residue: `DIV_W` 0.35 and the joint gate act on the same object (the fork population), so their gains may add (+0.0015 + 0.0037) or overlap; the cross is `divbench9`, which needs divbench8's bootstrap machinery.

## 2026-09-08 divbench7

- Hypothesis: that the division patch's per-frame cap is rationing away recoverable divisions.
- Scope: 128 6bba movies, arms on `DIV_FRAME_CAP` (REF 0.0076 / cap3x 0.0228 / cap8x 0.0608 / nocap 1.0). `DIV_FRAME_CAP` and `DIV_GLOBAL_CAP` are read inside `_add_safe_divisions`, which runs after the solve, so one solve per movie and one patch per arm. Says nothing about arrival-ordered budgets elsewhere in the pipeline.
- Experiment: kernel biohub-divbench7 v1, 122.6 min, anchors exact: D187 F4-6bba(12) 0.9216 / div_J 0.0606, +BIDIR 0.9261, REF 50/249/75, div_J 0.1337, adj_J 0.9133, score 0.9266. Fork gate at p > 0.03, each arm gated out of fold on its own forks. Follows divbench4's finding of 1,672 of 6,194 geometry-passing proposals refused by the cap.
- Result:

  | arm | frame cap | forks added | refused by the frame cap | div tp/fp/fn | div_J | adj_J | score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF | 0.0076 | 4,514 | 1,672 | 50 / 249 / 75 | 0.1337 | 0.9133 | 0.9266 |
  | cap3x | 0.0228 | 6,072 | 323 | 54 / 283 / 71 | 0.1324 | 0.9129 | 0.9261 |
  | cap8x | 0.0608 | 6,374 | 2 | 54 / 289 / 71 | 0.1304 | 0.9128 | 0.9258 |
  | nocap | 1.0 | 6,376 | 0 | 54 / 289 / 71 | 0.1304 | 0.9128 | 0.9258 |

  After the fork gate at p > 0.03:

  | arm | div tp/fp/fn | div_J | adj_J | score | vs REF+gate | fold0 | fold1 | the gate's own AUC |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | REF + gate | 42 / 47 / 83 | 0.2442 | 0.9143 | 0.9387 | -- | -- | -- | 0.9283 / 0.8326 |
  | cap3x + gate | 44 / 56 / 81 | 0.2431 | 0.9141 | 0.9384 | −0.0002 | −0.0021 | +0.0021 | 0.8936 / 0.8409 |
  | cap8x + gate | 43 / 54 / 82 | 0.2402 | 0.9142 | 0.9382 | −0.0005 | −0.0038 | +0.0032 | 0.8841 / 0.8471 |
  | nocap + gate | 43 / 54 / 82 | 0.2402 | 0.9142 | 0.9382 | −0.0005 | −0.0038 | +0.0032 | 0.8841 / 0.8471 |

  Lifting the cap recovers 4 true divisions (50 -> 54) and adds 40 counted false forks; after the gate that is 2 more true and 9 more false, the score is a wash, and the two folds disagree in sign in every arm. No candidate.

  Mechanism against gap4 (2026-08-27, where the gap-repair budget bound in 24 of 32 datasets and raising it gained +0.002 at LB): `_gap_close` hands its allowance out in frame order; `_add_safe_divisions` sorts every proposal by `d_pq + DIV_W_SISTER * d_s` and walks that list, so the per-frame counter keeps the geometrically best proposals in each frame and refuses the tail — a quality-ordered budget. The cap was refusing the worst 27%, and the gate degrades when they arrive: out-of-fold AUC 0.9283 / 0.8326 falls to 0.8841 / 0.8471.
- Conclusion: the cap binds on 27% of proposals; lifting it recovers 4 of the 75 lost divisions and the cost exceeds the gain both raw and gated. Residue: those 4 divisions are recoverable and something better than "first 1 per frame by geometry" might keep them without the other 1,862 forks, but that is a selection problem on the population the fork gate already scores, and the gate got worse when handed them.

  2. Arms `steal_all`, `steal_m0`, `steal_m20` (mother's ranker p must beat the current parent's by more than 0 / 0.20). The orphan pass runs first and to completion, so REF is untouched by construction. Every arm is patched, written and scored by the official scorer, then pruned by the SAME out-of-fold 20-feature gate at p > 0.03.

  Instrumented: the patch's own budget per arm (orphan added / global cap hit / frame cap hit; steal proposals / added / no-probability / margin-refused / caps). Expected ~3 h CPU.

  v1 died at the first movie of stage B on `KeyError: 'orphan_frame'`, the bug `tools/test_divbench4_steal.py` had already found locally; v2 carries both fixes. The traceback shows the per-frame cap binds on the very first movie — `orphan_frame` is only touched when a proposal is refused because frame `t` already holds `max(1, int(0.0076 * n_frame[t]))` forks. Cost of the two bugs: the 35-minute features stage, once.

  `DIV_W` note made while designing the steal. `DIV_W` does NOT govern the 5a case:

  - `q` is an ORPHAN: either she appears (cost `appearance_weight` = 0.0) or the mother forks to her (gain `p_Mq`, cost `DIV_W`). The fork is taken iff `p_Mq > 0.55`. This is `reference.md`'s rule and the population `_add_safe_divisions` patches by geometry.
  - `q` already has a parent `R` (the 5a case): taking her means `R` loses its only child and must disappear, at `disappearance_weight` 1.5. So the fork is taken iff `p_Mq - p_Rq > DIV_W + 1.5 = 2.05`, and probabilities live in [0, 1], so it can never be taken. 5a is structural; the binding constant is the disappearance weight. `ilpsweep` (2026-09-05) measured loosening it — disappearance 1.0 lost 12 of 12 on 6bba.

  The `DIV_W` orphan-fork curve (`biohub-ranker-fine`, 2026-08-23):

  | div_w | ILP forks | div TP/FP/FN | div_J | adj_J | score |

  | 0.35 | 394 | 5/39/7 | 0.0980 | 0.9211 | 0.9309 |
  | 0.45 | 190 | 5/27/7 | 0.1282 | 0.9216 | 0.9344 |
  | 0.55 (shipped) | 111 | 5/23/7 | 0.1429 | 0.9220 | 0.9363 |
  | 0.65 | 49 | 4/19/8 | 0.1290 | 0.9222 | 0.9351 |
  | 1.50 | 0 | 3/16/9 | 0.1071 | 0.9224 | 0.9331 |

There was no gate in August. From divbench3's table: ILP forks are more precise than patch forks (0.196 against 0.150 on counted forks) and the ILP makes fewer of them (2,490 against 4,514). `DIV_W` is read by `solve_one` when the ILPSolver is constructed, so it is a SOLVE-TIME constant and needs one full solve per arm, roughly 3x divbench3's stage B (2026-08-28 rule).

  `divbench6.py` built and waiting for a slot (make_divbench6.py): `solve_one` takes `divw`, arms at 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.20 each re-solve all 128 movies, every arm is patched, scored by the official scorer, then gated by a fork gate trained out of fold on that arm's own forks. REF is div_w 0.55 and must reproduce 50/249/75. ~4 solves x 128 movies, expect 5-6 h CPU.
- Conclusion: the 5a steal is closed — the solver's choice is right, the mother's own edge is about 16x weaker (p 0.054 against 0.872) over a 9.39 um displacement at the edge of `GATE_UM` 10.0, and ten of the 23 have no ranker probability for the mother's edge at all; the residue is the RANKER, the same 10-vs-12 um blind spot gatelab found on the fork gate. The eight new features are closed on 125 events: none improves the ranking and two combinations are measurably worse; `sc_q` (AUC 0.842 alone) still carries the gate and nothing explains why the 47 surviving false forks look like true ones on every column (gatelab5). Next candidate class is IMAGE evidence at the fork (intensity, shape, a nuclear-envelope signal), which needs a GPU pass and has never been attempted for divisions. The per-frame cap is a binding constraint counted for the first time.

  The division term is worth 0.014 of local score at REF (0.1 x 0.141), recall 43%, precision 17%: five counted false forks per true one. Every false fork gone at constant TP would be div_J 0.43 (+0.029 of score); every lost division found at constant FP, 0.33 (+0.019). The orphan-fork patch buys +0.0030 of div term and costs −0.0009 of adj_J, net +0.0021: it adds 29 true forks and 157 false ones (16% precision) on top of the ILP's 25 / 101; 29 of 54 TP come from the patch.
- Conclusion: the geometry is at a local optimum in both directions — the notebook's tighter rule loses 19 TP to shed 95 FP (−0.0195), and relaxing divergence to 1.0 / 0 um adds ~200 FP and loses 8-17 TP because the extra proposals compete for the same orphans and the per-mother / per-orphan / cap slots. divgate2's "0% of real divisions pass 2.25 um" was measured on the divisions that reached that test (33 zh, 1, 1); on 125 competition divisions the test does precision work outweighing what it refuses. Tested claims: the notebook's tighter division geometry transplants (killed, −0.0195 div_J on 125); the divergence threshold is what refuses real divisions (killed as a lever); the patch is worth nothing (killed, +0.002 score, 29 of 54 TP). Residue: (a) the 258 counted false forks for 54 TP are the lever, with fork-time features available (ranker p for both edges, head forward probability, distances, divergence, detection scores, density) on 312 counted forks out-of-fold; (b) the 71 lost divisions have never been walked through the patch's conditions on competition data at this size; (c) 44b6 is not on the bench. A division rule needs both folds up to be believed, and a sub-0.02 div_J change is inside the bench's noise.

The node penalty is J × (1 − 0.1 × (N_pred − N_true)/N_true), signed, clamped at 0 below and not above (metrics.py line 362, reference.md "no upper clamp"): every 10% of nodes below the estimate is +1% of J. On the visible 4 the notebook is 0.026 below us (0.8952 vs 0.9214) while in-sample; on the hidden set it is 0.003 above us with 24% fewer rows. If its hidden node_r is roughly −0.25 to −0.30 against ours near −0.05 (its ILP deletes 39% on 44b6_0b24845f, and its hidden bytes say it deletes >27% of official nodes everywhere), that is +0.02 to +0.025 of adj_J from the node term alone — the size of its edge deficit here: worse edges by ~0.02, node term +0.025, net +0.003. This is inference from four in-sample movies and one byte count, not a measurement of the hidden set.

  On "our rejection has room": a deletion pays only if the deleted nodes carry counted edges at less than a tenth of the average rate (random deletion of x of the nodes costs x of J and returns 0.1x). D20F48 on 44b6 deletes 15% of nodes for 2% of TP lost — a depletion of 7.7x, just short of paying.
- Conclusion: no edge-level merge helps and the consensus submission was not built — ours_only precision 0.747 is above the 0.48 break-even (dropping those edges costs more than it sheds, both −0.0213) and theirs_only 0.445 is at break-even with 76 false edges (union −0.0274); their in-sample advantage here makes both their buckets look better than they would on the hidden set. The 24% of rows the notebook does not carry are rows the scorer never looks at; deleting them changes no counted edge, only the node term. The user's reading of that term: it is unclamped below by design, since deleting nodes already risks deleting tracked cells (their edges become FN), and its purpose is to punish node spam and wild linking that the edge term cannot see off the annotation; the numbers add that this self-penalty exists only inside the annotation (every deletion costs on zh; on 44b6 it costs for 0.2% of nodes), so on sparse movies a deletion outside the annotated tracks is riskless and paid 0.1 per unit. Residue: (a) the organisers may still clamp it (the hub-node exploit was patched 2026-07-17); (b) a deletion rule aimed at unannotated regions is testable locally only through the node term, never through edges.

Kernel biohub-submit-off v2, 21 min, 0 fallbacks. Pushed 2026-09-04 after zhoffrank; the user asked for the submission to see the final file size.

- Hypothesis: the 0.948 notebook's margin comes from an over-detecting detector paired with post-processing built to delete; official-detector nodes through our linker with the notebook's deletion rule should hold up on unseen data.
- Scope: 8 Zebrahub eval crops. The linker here is D187, not the notebook's linker, so the interaction under test is detector × deletion rule, not detector × its whole pipeline. The user approved the run.

For fusescore's 8 zebrahub eval crops (sorted zhdet stems [:8], asserted), predict_video's detection path on the crop's [::4] strided volume: crop-level 0.001 / 0.999 quantiles (detfuse3 used per-frame; the official path uses the dataset's), the 2-frame window in which the frame is first seen, 4-view flip TTA, `_detect_cells_pooled` with the 3 um kernel (3, 3, 3), sigmoid at the peak, coords × (1, 4, 4). Arms OFFP (primary) and OFF28 (the notebook's blend: secondary logits re-centred to the primary's per-frame mean, std ratio clamped 0.5-2, 0.2 / 0.8, retention guard 0.90 -> primary alone where the blend keeps < 90% of the primary's peaks), gates 0.965 / 0.99. Output zhoff_<ARM><gate>_<crop>.npz in the detcache layout. `zhoffrank.py` -> biohub-zhoffrank (CPU; from gap2_rank.py by make_zhoffrank.py; pushed when zhoff landed): per crop, arms F4 / OFFP965 / OFFP990 / OFF28965 / OFF28990 through the D187 linker (18 columns; no head cache on zh), one ILP solve each, then the patches at SHORT_MIN 4 (ships) and 6 (the notebook's) on copies; scored as fusescore scored zh. Hard anchor F4 × 4 = 0.8118.
- Result: adj_J −0.32 to −0.42 below F4 on all 8 crops under both deletion rules. At its production gate the official detector under-detects zebrahub by 27-41%.

  Official nodes per frame (OFFP 0.965 / 0.99, OFF28 0.965 / 0.99) per crop: tail_z2y0x3 410 / 356 / 423 / 389; tail_z2y1x2 328 / 270 / 316 / 273; tail_z2y2x3 130 / 106 / 129 / 105; tail_z2y3x0 210 / 164 / 209 / 163; tail_z2y3x2 221 / 154 / 220 / 154; z2y1x4 93 / 76 / 101 / 93; z2y1x5 108 / 87 / 132 / 120; z2y1x6 77 / 68 / 82 / 76. The retention guard fell back to the primary on 0-3 frames of the four bright crops and on 62-99 of 100 frames of the three dim tail crops (q_high 117-236), so on those the "dual-seed blend" is the primary. Crop-level q_low is 0 everywhere (zero padding at the crop edge).

  Ledger that motivated the run: official nodes + official head + our ILP + our patches = LB 0.895; the same nodes + the notebook's linker + its patches = 0.948; on our nodes its linker loses 0.010 / 0.033 (motionlink), its 3-frame bridge is zero (gap2strict), its division rule is weaker (motionlink div_J 0.054 vs 0.152), and its edge probabilities are less polarised than our ranker's. The remaining explanation of 0.948 is that the hidden embryo resembles the training embryos (where the official detector recalls 99-100% of annotated cells, in-sample) more than Zebrahub does — an explanation no local test can reach.
