## 2026-09-04 gap2strict design

- Hypothesis: the 0.948 notebook's 3-frame bridge, under its own conditions, recovers what span2's flood could not.
- Scope: F4-6bba, F4-44b6 (linker +BIDIR loaded), F4-zh (ANCHOR_D187, no head columns); one ILP solve per dataset, four post-link variants applied on copies.
- Experiment: `gap2_rank.py` -> `biohub-gap2` v3 (CPU; generated from edgeprob_rank2.py by make_gap2.py; sources as zhrank). Expected ~1.5 h CPU.
- Result:
  Prior, span2 (2026-08-28): same t -> t+3 bridge, two interpolated nodes, no condition but distance, 35,711 bridges: 6bba −0.0014 (edge_J unchanged, nodes +1.4%, div_J −0.0173), 44b6 +0.0066, zh +0.0068; signs disagreed, discarded.
  The notebook's gap2 conditions (read from its source this session): total ≤ 10.2 um, step ≤ 4.4 um; direction must agree with the track's previous OR next step (cos > −0.25, |Δstep| ≤ 6 um), else a penalty; proposals ranked by distance + 2·penalty; caps 0.45% of edges / 180 per movie and 0.6% of a frame's ends; runs after the one-frame gap close and before the short-track filter.
  Arms: REF (as shipped; soft 0.9261 / 0.8515, zh 0.8118), GAP2_NB (the rule verbatim, interpolated nodes; no intensity refinement, no image in the harness), GAP2_POOL (interpolated node replaced by the nearest sub-gate candidate within 3.2 um when one exists), GAP2_NOCTX (without the direction condition). ANCHOR_D187 solved again on 6bba as the hard anchor 0.9216.
  Bookkeeping per variant: candidates, context-rejected, selected, cap-skipped, pool-used, nodes added. Also printed on labelled eval rows: share of true edges ≥ 0.9 and false edges ≤ 0.1 for h_fused, p_fwd, the +BIDIR ranker and D187.
- Conclusion: Design entry for the gap2strict run; NOCTX vs NB prices the direction condition, POOL vs NB prices measured over interpolated positions.

## 2026-09-04 zhrank design

- Hypothesis: (1) a ranker trained on Zebrahub's dense labels transfers to the competition embryos; (2) re-normalising the shipped ranker's probability over each source's and each target's competitors (the head's structure) helps the ILP.
- Scope: judged on F4-6bba, F4-44b6 (transfer) and F4-zh (8 crops, in-domain, scored as fusescore scored zh, GT = the crop's own tracks). 18 columns only (no head cache on zebrahub). No brightness filter on the machine labels; dim GT points our detector misses produce no row.
- Experiment: `zhrank.py` -> `biohub-zhrank` v1 (CPU; generated from edgeprob_rank2.py by make_zhrank.py; sources add biohub-zh-detect and biohub-edgeprob-rank2). Expected ~4.5 h CPU.
- Result:
  Training-data arms: BASE18_D175 (soft anchors 0.9232 / 0.8346, rank v2), BASE18_ZH (the 33 zebrahub crops outside fusescore's 8), BASE18_MIX (both pools). The competition ranker's rows exist only where the source primary matched an annotated GT node with children (exclusion negatives; 44b6 annotates 0.77% of cells). Zebrahub's 41 crops (biohub-zh-detect: xl detections + machine tracks on the competition voxel grid, every frame, ~2.5% cells unlabelled) label every in-gate non-child as a true negative.
  Prior: pool 32 -> 187 competition movies moved LB 0.921 -> 0.920; div-train's Zebrahub-only classifier scored AUC 0.81 on held-out 6bba.
  Mechanism arms on the shipped +BIDIR ranker (loaded pkl): NORM = harmonic mean of p / Σ over the source's candidates and p / Σ over the target's candidates (a lone candidate becomes 1.0), MULT = sqrt(p × NORM). Reference +BIDIR soft 0.9261 / 0.8515, ANCHOR_D187 hard 0.9216. The ranker scores each pair alone (only rank_of_j_for_i / n_cand_i / n_cand_j describe the competition) and the ILP takes raw −p; the official head softmaxes over the sources of each target.
- Conclusion: Design entry for the zhrank run.

## 2026-09-04 motionlink design

- Hypothesis: the ranker + ILP are not earning their place; the notebook's velocity-predicted Hungarian with the learned probability as tie-breaker would do as well as our final linker.
- Scope: F4 primaries on the 24 competition sets (F4-6bba, F4-44b6), usual patches after the linker. Tests the notebook's linker on OUR nodes only; the 0.895 arm was official nodes + official head + our ILP.
- Experiment: `motionlink_rank.py` -> `biohub-motionlink` v1 (CPU; generated from edgeprob_rank2.py by make_motionlink.py). No pool, no training: +BIDIR loaded from biohub-edgeprob-rank2's `edge_ranker_ep175v3_bidir.pkl`.
- Result:
  Prior record: ILP over the official plain greedy +0.03 on 12 sets (2026-08-18, half of it the node penalty); ranker over distance-Hungarian +0.005 (2026-08-23); head columns +0.007 LB (edgeprob). Not previously tested: a velocity-predicted Hungarian as the final linker.
  The notebook's relink is per frame pair, gates 6 then 10 um, cost = |target − (source + 0.5 v)| + 0.05 |target − source| − 1.0 p, p = the ILP edge's probability (0 where the ILP chose otherwise), so the ILP is a ≤ 1 um tie-breaker. Our pre-pass `_link_sim` is the same shape (pred = P + 0.5 v, gates 6 / 10, plus a score-similarity term) and links the right parent 97.4% / 91.8% of the time where the parent is detected (p1head, layer 1).
  Arms: ANCHOR_D187 (hard 0.9216), +BIDIR (soft 0.9261 / 0.8515), HEAD1 (soft 0.9245 / 0.8453), MOTION0 (pure geometry, bonus 0), MOTION_H1 (bonus 1.0 × h_fused on every candidate pair), MOTION_H5 (bonus 5.0 × h_fused), MOTION_ILP (bonus 1.0 × the +BIDIR ranker's probability on the pairs +BIDIR's ILP kept, 0 elsewhere). Also printed: how many of each motion arm's raw edges coincide with +BIDIR's ILP edges. Paired per dataset vs +BIDIR, both groups.
- Conclusion: Design entry for the motionlink run.

The 3-4% disagreement — links the ILP's disappearance cost 1.5 refused and the Hungarian made — costs 0.010 on 6bba and 0.033 on 44b6; those links keep more nodes alive through the short filter (node_r −0.004 vs −0.020 on 6bba). Tie-breaker effect: head at 1 um 0.0002, at 5 um 0.0018 / 0.0043, our ILP's probability 0.0013 / −0.0006. One-to-one linking leaves the safe-division rule to find a third of the divisions (div_J 0.054 vs 0.152).
- Conclusion: The motion relink does 0.010 / 0.033 worse on 23 of 24 movies, so on our nodes the notebook's linker is the worse one and the linker is not the source of its margin over our 0.895 official-detector run. The ILP's refusal of low-probability links is the mechanism that wins, the same lever as the 2026-08-18 greedy-vs-ILP result. Untested of that notebook: its detection (dual-seed logit blend 0.20 / 0.80 at gate 0.965, minimum candidate retention 0.90) and post-processing (min track 6 with rescue, 3-frame gap2, stricter safe divisions, the DeepCenter veto on checkpoint_last.pt, which dcprobe found dead), and h_fused's calibration against our ILP costs (floor 0.10, disappearance 1.5, division 0.55) on the official detector's denser node set.

  Control (nopred): the pre-pass gives a readable cell the wrong predecessor in 2.9% / 6.1% / 0.8% of cases (6bba / 44b6 / zh), plus parent_taken.

ANCHOR_D187 hard 0.9216. Paired per dataset vs +BIDIR, both groups.
- Conclusion: Design entry for the p1head run.

## 2026-09-04 nb948 post-processing read

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: source read only, no run. The 0.948 notebook's post-processing as shipped; detection differs from ours too, so the linker's share is not isolated.
- Experiment: scratchpad nb948.txt, cell "bidirectional-production-postprocess", preset harmonic_v3_division_wide.
- Result:
  Official inference settings: dual-seed detection at 0.965, ILP appearance 0 / disappearance 2 / division 1.2, edge candidate threshold 0.48, bidirectional harmonic 0.15. Order per movie:
  1. Edge filter: drop edges not to the next frame or longer than 14 um.
  2. Motion relink (`OUTPUT_MOTION_RELINK` default on, not overridden): the ILP's edge set is discarded and rebuilt greedily. Per frame pair, two Hungarian passes (gate 6 um, then 10 um on the leftovers), cost = |target − (source + 0.5·velocity)| + 0.05·|target − source| − 1.0·p_ILP, velocity from the relink's own previous assignment, p_ILP the ILP edge's probability (0 for pairs the ILP did not pick; the bonus is worth at most 1 um). One-to-one, so every ILP division is dropped here. Skipped (raw ILP edges kept) only if some frame has > 2,600 nodes. Then single-parent repair (best edge per target).
  3. Gap close, 1 frame (max_gap clamped to 1 in code): track end at t to track start at t+2 within 2 × 5.8 um, adjusted ±0.125 um per step by local spacing (median of 3 nearest neighbours vs 6.5 um reference), Hungarian on distance. Middle node = an isolated node within 3.2 um of the midpoint if one exists, else a synthetic midpoint pulled to the intensity centroid (window z±1, yx±3, shift ≤ 3.2 um); synthetic middles spanning ≥ 8.5 um must score ≥ 0.25 on DeepCenter (pilkwang's center-prior checkpoint, not ours). Cap 5% of nodes / 2,000.
  4. Gap2: end at t to start at t+3, total ≤ 10.2 um, step ≤ 4.4 um, direction must agree with the previous or next step (cos > −0.25 and |Δstep| ≤ 6 um), two synthetic refined nodes; cap 0.45% of edges / 180, 0.6% of that frame's ends.
  5. Safe divisions (the only source of divisions after step 2): parent with exactly one child ≤ 10 um away, orphan candidate ≤ 7 um from parent and ≤ 12 um from the sister, candidate must be the sister's nearest orphan (mutual NN), both daughters need a single successor at t+2 with the grandchildren ≥ 2.25 um further apart than the sisters, and DeepCenter ≥ 0.12 at the candidate. Score parent_dist + 0.15·sister_dist; caps 0.76% of sources per frame, 0.375% of edges global.
  6. Division geometry filter: off. Prune isolated nodes.
  7. Short-track filter: components < 6 nodes removed unless they contain a division; if that would remove ≥ 10% of nodes, rescue 4-5-node components whose mean p_ILP ≥ 0.88 and mean edge length ≤ 3.0 um, budget 1.2% of nodes / 120.
  8. Linefit: window ±2 along single-successor chains, position moved 80% of the way to the fitted line.

  Differences from ours: our patches (gap bridge, SHORT_MIN 4, linefit, safe divisions) are the same family with looser division rules and no DeepCenter veto; the structural difference is step 2, where the notebook's final links are a velocity-predicted greedy assignment with the ILP as a ≤ 1 um tie-breaker and its divisions are all geometric. With the same official detector, "official nodes -> our ILP on h_fused" scored 0.895 and this recipe scores 0.948, but detection differs too (dual-seed blend, gate 0.965 vs 0.99).
- Conclusion: Source-level record of the notebook's post-processing order and constants.

- Hypothesis: the official detection heatmaps, added to the four the pipeline averages, surface the undetected parents nopred charged to the detector.

Untested caveats: (a) on zh the official maps were normalised by per-frame 0.001 / 0.999 quantiles, not the dataset's (the crops carry none); (b) the blend is equal-weight in probability space, where the 0.948 notebook aligns logits to the primary's per-frame mean / std and weights 0.2 / 0.8.
- Experiment: `detfuse3.py` -> `biohub-detfuse3` v3, 26.6 min T4, 2026-09-03. (v1 and v2 died on a constant used before its definition; nothing ran.) Anchors digit-exact: zh FULL3 0.7774, F4 0.7903 (F1* at 7 um).
- Result: zh, dense GT, 101,615 points over 410 frames, 7 um, own best gate:

| arm (b0,b1,b2,dc,off_p,off_s) | gate* | dets/fr | recall | prec | F1* | F1@.15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL3 (1,1,1,0,0,0) | 0.15 | 260.9 | 0.7979 | 0.7579 | 0.7774 | 0.7774 |
| F4 (1,1,1,1,0,0) ships | 0.15 | 257.7 | 0.8060 | 0.7752 | 0.7903 | 0.7903 |
| F5p (+ official primary) | 0.30 | 250.5 | 0.7725 | 0.7642 | 0.7683 | 0.7484 |
| F5s (+ second seed) | 0.15 | 310.5 | 0.8444 | 0.6740 | 0.7496 | 0.7496 |
| F6 (+ both) | 0.20 | 312.1 | 0.8370 | 0.6646 | 0.7409 | 0.7381 |
| F6h (+ both at 0.5) | 0.20 | 297.0 | 0.8335 | 0.6955 | 0.7583 | 0.7534 |
| OFFp (official primary alone) | 0.60 | 327.7 | 0.8248 | 0.6237 | 0.7103 | 0.7069 |
| OFFs (second seed alone) | 0.40 | 319.7 | 0.7827 | 0.6067 | 0.6836 | 0.6813 |
| OFF28 (0.2 / 0.8, the notebook's mix) | 0.15 | 352.3 | 0.8427 | 0.5927 | 0.6960 | 0.6960 |

  At 5 um the order is the same (F4 0.7685; F5p 0.7458, F5s 0.7247, F6 0.7154, F6h 0.7353; OFFp 0.6787, OFFs 0.6526, OFF28 0.6661).
  - The official detector, either seed, is 0.08-0.11 F1 below the shipped F4 on the only all-cells denominator, and 0.07-0.09 below the three-branch mean. It buys recall (OFF28 0.8427 vs F4 0.8060) with 37% more detections per frame and precision 0.59.
  - Blended in it drags every arm down: F5p −0.022, F5s −0.041, F6 −0.049, F6h −0.032 against F4. Half weight does not undo it.
  - Cold-miss rescue against F4's 16,226 zh misses: window-max >= 0.15 within 3.25 um in the 4-map mean 85.6%, off_p 93.0%, off_s 86.7%, any 98.1%; at >= 0.05 the 4-map mean reaches 99.6%.
  - Competition side (sparse GT, 12 + 12 datasets, stride 10): official maps alone produce 168.8 / 368.8 detections per frame on 6bba / 44b6 against F4's 48.9 / 26.1, and recall over annotated cells 0.996 / 1.000 against F4's 0.698 / 0.242 at F4's own best gate 0.40. Adding one official map (F5p / F5s) lifts dets/fr 48.9 -> 63.9 and 26.1 -> 41.2. The no-surplus criterion (detfuse2) is failed.
  - OFF28 alone at its own best gate is 0.094 below F4.
- Conclusion: the claim is killed on this denominator. Residue: F4's misses are not cold in the heatmap (85.6% have a >= 0.15 response within 3.25 um), so the peak / NMS stage loses them — the line the 2026-08-25 nms4 entry closed ("2 of 3, none significant"); and the logit-aligned blend is untested. No pipeline test is bought; per detfuse2's protocol the line stops here.

## 2026-09-03 nopred

- Hypothesis: the zero-velocity (no-predecessor) primaries are linker failures a motion feature can repair.
- Scope: F4 primaries, 32 datasets, three domains, D187 ranker. `unmatched` is unverifiable on 6bba (9.71% of cells annotated) and 44b6 (0.77%) — there it means "not annotated", not "spurious"; only zh (~97.5% annotated) can be read as causes. 44b6's bucket column says nothing at all (99.7% unmatched). Nothing here speaks to hidden-set 44b6-like movies.
- Experiment: `nopred.py` -> `biohub-nopred` v1, CPU, 59.1 min, 32 of 32 datasets; rankwhy's / twopass's harness. Local `tools/test_nopred_buckets.py` passed before the push. Hard anchors exact in all three domains: F4-6bba 0.9216 / 0.0606, F4-44b6 0.8353 / 0.0000, F4-zh 0.8118 / 0.0215. Design: every primary at t >= 1 with pass-1 velocity exactly zero goes into ONE bucket, decision order `other/linked_zero_disp` (has a pass-1 predecessor at identical coordinates) -> `unmatched` (no GT node within MATCH_R at t) -> `gt_start` (GT track starts here; sub-split border < 10 um vs interior) -> `division_daughter` (sister took the parent / parent went elsewhere / parent undetected) -> `parent_undetected` (GT parent at t-1 has no matched primary; `subthresh` = a detection below 0.15 within MATCH_R of it, `cold` = nothing) -> `parent_taken` (pass-1 gave the parent's primary to another cell; competitor unmatched vs another GT cell) -> `parent_out_of_gate` -> `parent_free_but_unlinked`. `recovered` = the FINAL graph has an in-edge into this primary from a node at t-1 within 7 um of the GT parent (ILP edge, gap bridge or division patch; only buckets with a GT parent). Control = seeded random sample of NON-zero-velocity primaries, same size per dataset, same buckets, plus whether pass-1's predecessor IS the GT parent's primary.
- Result:
  Population, zero-velocity primaries at t >= 1 (flowvel's numbers): 21,524 of 170,079 (12.7%) F4-6bba; 29,448 of 350,570 (8.4%) F4-44b6; 9,058 of 214,186 (4.2%) F4-zh.

  Buckets (count and share of the zero group · in final graph · recovered):

  | bucket | F4-6bba | F4-44b6 | F4-zh |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | unmatched | 10,353 (48.1%) · 61.4% · - | 29,345 (99.7%) · 50.3% · - | 2,804 (31.0%) · 40.8% · - |
  | gt_start | 59 (0.3%) · 89.8% · - | 8 · 87.5% · - | 594 (6.6%) · 56.2% · - |
  | division_daughter | 6 · 83.3% · 40.0% | 2 · 100% · 50.0% | 181 (2.0%) · 53.6% · 40.2% |
  | parent_undetected | 38 (0.2%) · 60.5% · 17.4% | 26 (0.1%) · 53.8% · 42.9% | 4,897 (54.1%) · 50.2% · 31.3% |
  | parent_taken | 72 (0.3%) · 69.4% · 38.0% | 66 (0.2%) · 59.1% · 41.0% | 577 (6.4%) · 51.0% · 57.1% |
  | parent_out_of_gate | 5 · 100% · 0.0% | 1 · 0% · - | 5 · 100% · 0.0% |
  | parent_free_but_unlinked | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | other = linked_zero_disp | 10,991 (51.1%) · 96.8% · - | 0 | 0 |

  Sub-splits and distances (medians, um):
  - `gt_start`: border < 10 um in 43 of 59 (6bba), 8 of 8 (44b6), 576 of 594 (zh, 97.0%); median distance to the nearest face 3.13 / 1.40 / 1.98; z-face share 25.6% / 12.5% / 18.9%; 0 non-adjacent GT edges in these files. These cells enter the field; zero velocity is correct for them.
  - `division_daughter` (zh 181): sister took the parent 158 (87.3%, rec 41.4%), parent went to another cell 6 (rec 0%), parent undetected 17 (rec 33.3%); this -> GT parent 4.09, sister -> GT parent 2.76.
  - `parent_undetected` (zh 4,897): `cold` 4,208 (85.9%, rec 32.7%), `subthresh` 689 (14.1%, rec 22.3%); this -> GT parent 1.88 um. 6bba 19/19 and 44b6 11/15 split the same way at n ~ 30.
  - `parent_taken` (zh 577): competitor unmatched (spurious) 269 (46.6%, rec 44.4%), competitor another GT cell 308 (53.4%, rec 64.5%). competitor -> parent primary 2.18 vs this -> parent primary 4.88; competitor -> GT child 6.12 vs this -> GT child 1.52. Competitor closer to the parent in 465 of 577; closer to this cell's own GT node in 16 of 577 (2.8%). Same shape on 6bba (68 of 72) and 44b6 (61 of 66), where every competitor is unmatched (unverifiable).
  - `parent_out_of_gate`: 11 cells in all, raw distance to the parent primary 10.4-10.8 um, damped prediction 10.6-13.3.
  - `linked_zero_disp` (6bba only, 10,991): a predecessor exists with coordinates equal to this primary's, two frames running. Per movie: 268e1230 339 of 945 zeros, 3a1849c2 667 of 1,104, 3abfe10a 6,510 of 10,837, 61dd1e0d 763 of 1,267, 7af54fde 1,029 of 1,679, 7b5d3b2c 392 of 581, afb141ff 611 of 1,091, aeee7805 541 of 761, c27cba08 139 of 501; 2312ac41, 283bf9f1, 5c824876 have 0. 96.8% are in the final graph. Not diagnosed: whether these cells are immobile or the detection coordinates are quantised so a sub-voxel move reads as zero. They are 6.5% of every 6bba primary at t >= 1.

  Fate in the final graph, zero group vs control:

  | group | domain | in final | with parent | as start | not in final |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | zero | F4-6bba | 79.6% | 57.9% | 21.7% | 20.4% |
  | control | F4-6bba | 97.4% | 96.6% | 0.8% | 2.6% |
  | zero | F4-44b6 | 50.4% | 18.3% | 32.1% | 49.6% |
  | control | F4-44b6 | 95.4% | 94.8% | 0.6% | 4.6% |
  | zero | F4-zh | 47.8% | 15.5% | 32.3% | 52.2% |
  | control | F4-zh | 98.5% | 98.3% | 0.2% | 1.5% |

  Rates that differ, zero vs control (zh): unmatched 31.0% vs 9.1%, gt_start 6.6% vs 1.2%, parent_undetected 54.1% vs 2.1%, recovered 34.2% vs 99.1%. The control's pass-1 predecessor is the GT parent's primary in 1,176 of 1,211 (6bba), 216 of 230 (44b6), 7,811 of 7,875 (zh) matched cases; `linked_elsewhere` sits 6.4-8.4 um from the true parent and 2.0-3.3 um from the one it took.

  Degradation counters over the 32 datasets: acceleration undefined (no parent) 48,077 rows; one backward step only 37,001 rows.
- Conclusion: In zh, the readable domain, the causes split as parent never detected 54% (86% of those `cold`, nothing within MATCH_R of a GT node 1.9 um away; the gap bridge repairs a third), nothing to link to (spurious detection 31%, field entry 6.6%, division daughter 2%), and greedy pass gave the parent to a nearer cell 6.4% (half the competitors spurious; ILP + patches recover 57%). `parent_free_but_unlinked` is 0 in every domain, so the pre-pass never leaves an available parent unlinked inside the gate and a better velocity had nothing to act on. Claim tested and not supported: "the zero-velocity cells are linker failures a motion feature can repair"; residue: (a) the 6bba `linked_zero_disp` population, 6.5% of the domain's primaries, undiagnosed; (b) zh `parent_undetected cold`, 4,208 cells, a detector-recall question at 1.9 um from a detected cell (the same place M15 lost 0.008 on LB); (c) the zero group is dropped from the final graph at 20% / 50% / 52% against 3% / 5% / 2% for the control, so `_short_filter` and the ILP are the stages that price these cells.

## 2026-09-03 flowvel

- Hypothesis: a velocity built from neighbourhood flow (a source outside the linker) for the zero-velocity cells recovers their edges.
- Scope: F4 arm, three domains, twopass's harness, same anchors, D187 ranker (no retraining). FLOWFILL touches 6.1% / 7.5% / 3.8% of ranker rows.
- Experiment: `flowvel.py` -> `biohub-flowvel` v1, CPU, 157.2 min, 96 of 96 arm-datasets, pushed 2026-09-03; anchors exact in all three domains. Flow for a primary at t = component-wise median of the pass-1 velocity vectors of its K=8 nearest primaries within 25 um that have non-zero pass-1 velocity (K_MIN 3, else undefined). Arms: FLOWFILL (flow only where pass-1 velocity is zero, 12.7% / 8.4% / 4.2% of primaries), FLOWALL (flow everywhere defined). Prints flow-vs-own-velocity cosine per domain.
- Result:

  | arm | domain | adj_J | d adj_J vs ANCHOR | per-dataset up / down / same |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | FLOWFILL | F4-6bba | 0.9218 | +0.0002 | 5 / 6 / 1 |
  | FLOWFILL | F4-44b6 | 0.8359 | +0.0006 | 6 / 6 / 0 |
  | FLOWFILL | F4-zh | 0.8121 | +0.0002 | 7 / 0 / 1 |
  | FLOWALL | F4-6bba | 0.9221 | +0.0004 | 5 / 5 / 2 |
  | FLOWALL | F4-44b6 | 0.8328 | −0.0025 | 3 / 8 / 1 |
  | FLOWALL | F4-zh | 0.8124 | +0.0006 | 6 / 2 / 0 |

  Flow statistics (K 8, R 25 um, K_MIN 3), primaries at t >= 1:

  | domain | defined | pass-1 zero | filled (zero AND defined) | med \|flow\| | med cos(flow, own v) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | F4-6bba | 89.4% | 21,524 | 10,142 (47.1%) | 1.90 | 0.787 |
  | F4-44b6 | 99.7% | 29,448 | 29,184 (99.1%) | 1.48 | 0.693 |
  | F4-zh | 99.7% | 9,058 | 9,037 (99.8%) | 0.64 | 0.711 |

  FLOWALL touched 90-99% of ranker rows. Refeature self-check 0.00e+00 in all three domains.
- Conclusion: FLOWFILL passes the three-domain sign rule but every magnitude is under 0.001, a fifth of the +0.003 floor, and per-dataset it is a coin flip in the two competition domains; FLOWALL's signs disagree. The tissue moves coherently (cosine 0.69-0.79), so the filled cells received a sensible motion prediction and the ranker still did not turn it into correct edges; the 6bba zeros are half isolated cells (fewer than 3 linked neighbours within 25 um). Claim tested and not supported: "a velocity for the zero-velocity cells recovers their edges"; residue: none on the velocity line.

## 2026-09-03 twopass

- Hypothesis: a better velocity source exists inside the pipeline — rebuilding velocity from the ILP's own edges and re-scoring with the shipped ranker improves the result.
- Scope: F4 arm + D187 ranker, three domains. Distribution shift stated up front: D187 was trained on pass-1 velocities, so a negative closes only "the shipped ranker profits without retraining". Pushed while ref 55974245 rescored.
- Experiment: `twopass.py` -> `biohub-twopass` v1, CPU, 199.5 min, 96 of 96 arm-datasets, pushed 2026-09-03; anchors exact in all three domains (0.9216 / 0.8353 / 0.8118 hard). Solve once (ANCHOR, F4 + D187), rebuild velocity from the ILP's edges (predecessor = solved parent; no parent -> zero, as pass-1 does), recompute the three velocity-dependent ranker columns (4 `md`, 5 `d − md`, 16 `|v|`; the other 15 are velocity-free), re-score with the SAME D187 ranker, re-solve, patch, score. Arms: TWOPASS_SAME (pred = P + v), TWOPASS_HALF (pred = P + 0.5 v).
- Result:

  | arm | domain | adj_J | d adj_J vs ANCHOR | per-dataset up / down / same |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ANCHOR | F4-6bba / 44b6 / zh | 0.9216 / 0.8353 / 0.8118 | — | — |
  | TWOPASS_SAME | F4-6bba | 0.9217 | +0.0001 | 3 / 5 / 4 |
  | TWOPASS_SAME | F4-44b6 | 0.8352 | −0.0000 | 2 / 10 / 0 |
  | TWOPASS_SAME | F4-zh | 0.8119 | +0.0001 | 5 / 3 / 0 |
  | TWOPASS_HALF | F4-6bba | 0.9218 | +0.0001 | 5 / 3 / 4 |
  | TWOPASS_HALF | F4-44b6 | 0.8342 | −0.0010 | 4 / 8 / 0 |
  | TWOPASS_HALF | F4-zh | 0.8122 | +0.0004 | 7 / 1 / 0 |

  Both arms: signs disagree across domains, every magnitude inside noise. Node/edge counts move by tens to a couple of hundred per domain.

  Velocity table:

  | source | domain | primaries (t ≥ 1) | velocity zero | zero % | med \|v\| (all / non-zero) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | pass-1 (greedy) | F4-6bba | 170,079 | 21,524 | 12.7 | 2.14 / 2.31 |
  | pass-1 | F4-44b6 | 350,570 | 29,448 | 8.4 | 1.89 / 2.05 |
  | pass-1 | F4-zh | 214,186 | 9,058 | 4.2 | 1.37 / 1.39 |
  | solved tracks | F4-6bba | 170,079 | 24,050 | 14.1 | 2.11 / 2.30 |
  | solved tracks | F4-44b6 | 350,570 | 38,921 | 11.1 | 1.81 / 2.04 |
  | solved tracks | F4-zh | 214,186 | 11,339 | 5.3 | 1.36 / 1.39 |

  Of the solved-track zeros, 6bba: 6,404 primaries the ILP kept no node for + 6,930 track starts; 44b6: 23,106 + 15,815; zh: 6,765 + 4,574. Refeature self-check 0.00e+00 in all three domains (columns 4/5/16 are the only velocity-dependent ones; verified at runtime).
- Conclusion: The ILP's velocities equal the greedy pre-pass's — where pass-1 finds a predecessor the ILP picks the same edge, and where it does not the ILP mostly has no node or no parent either, so the zero rate rises rather than falls. The 2026-08-25 premise ("the greedy chain is exactly what fails; the ILP's tracks are far better trajectories") does not hold for velocity, and the 24% of 6bba rank>=1 misses with velocity exactly zero (velwhy) are cells with no predecessor in any linker, not a pre-pass artefact. Claim tested and not supported: "a better velocity source exists inside the pipeline"; residue: a velocity source outside the linker (neighbourhood flow) was untested at the time. The retrained-ranker follow-up was judged not worth running: its inputs would be the same numbers.

## 2026-09-02 edgeprob

- Hypothesis: the official edge head's probability carries information the ranker's 18 coordinate columns do not.
- Scope: first block is the BASE arm on the D32 pool — the shipped pipeline is F4 primaries + D187 ranker, neither measured there; no zebrahub arm anywhere (the head was not run on zh crops). Second block (2026-09-03) is the F4 arm on the D175 pool, both eval groups clean holdouts, and carries the submission and LB reading. 44b6 per-dataset spread is ±0.06 with up/down 7/5 in the D32 block; the group number is carried by the big movies.
- Experiment: two kernels.
  1. `edgeprob_cache.py` -> `biohub-edgeprob` (GPU, T4). Official weights, `predict_video` with `_detect_cells_pooled` monkeypatched to return OUR BASE xl primaries (`seeds_of`, score >= 0.15, order kept; full-res voxel coords / downsample (1,4,4) as float grid coords), `threshold` 2.0 so its own candidate loop keeps nothing, `model.predict_edges` wrapped to capture the raw logit matrix per consecutive pair; softmax over sources (the official activation) gated to the ranker's 10 um pairs. Reverse pass (frames remapped f -> T-1-f) scores t+1 -> t with the same model (the public 0.948 notebook's bidirectional fusion, harmonic mean at weight 0.15). Output per dataset: (t, i, j, p_fwd, p_rev, l_fwd, l_rev, n_per_frame), indices identical to `pair_features`' rows. Datasets: HOLDOUT_6BBA 12 + 12 44b6 drawn with dctrain's seed 20260827 from the 55 outside the D32 pool + the D32 pool 32 = 56. det_tta off (TTA touches only det_logits). v1 SMOKE (2 datasets) passed all round-trip asserts, 36 s and 44 s per dataset, both directions. v2 = all 56.
  2. `edgeprob_rank.py` -> `biohub-edgeprob-rank` (CPU). rankwhy's harness; labels verbatim from `poolsize.py`; retrains D32-pool rankers for arms BASE18 / +PFWD / +BIDIR (p_fwd, p_rev, h_fused) / +ALL, plus the shipped D187 pkl as ANCHOR_D187 (loaded, not judged). Stage A: AUCs + permutation importance; Stage B: full solve + patches + official scorer on the 12 6bba and 12 44b6 (both out of the D32 pool). Hard anchors: ANCHOR_D187 6bba 0.9293, BASE18 6bba 0.9251 (fusescore 2026-08-30).

  Runs: `biohub-edgeprob` v2, 56 of 56 cached, 40.1 min T4, every round-trip assert held (36-67 s per dataset, both directions). `biohub-edgeprob-rank` v1, 116.5 min CPU, 120 of 120 arm-datasets scored, join 100% matched (3,219,747 pairs, 0 NaN p_rev). BASE18 retrained on the D32 pool reproduces `edge_ranker_d32.pkl` to max |dp| 0.00e+00. Expectation stated before the result: the chimera (official head alone on xl nodes) lost 0.011 locally; as an added feature the ceiling is the rank>=1 population, 1.4% of 6bba edges.

Pushed as `biohub-submit-ep` v1. Visible-4 run (v1) clean: head pass ok on all 4 movies (29 / 36 / 36 / 58 s), 0 movies degraded; output nodes 126,488 / edges 121,593 (F4's visible-4 was 128,157 nodes, −1.3%); tracking wall time 1,041 s vs F4's 914 s (+14%) -> hidden ~8.2 h, under 12. The visible-set self-score block died on `ModuleNotFoundError: tracking_cellmot` (internet off; the scorer is not in the pack) after submission.csv was written and validated — same code path as submit_f4, no effect on the submission, but no local score.

  Submitted as ref 55974245 (2026-09-03). Control: 55889500 = 0.925. LB: 0.932 (+0.007). Hidden output 270,137,616 bytes vs F4's 270,740,009 (−0.22%).
- Conclusion: The head's probability carries information the 18 coordinate columns do not: head-alone edge AUC beats BASE18 in all three populations and the paired pipeline delta is positive in both clean groups for every arm. +BIDIR is the best arm in both groups and the only one where no 6bba dataset loses more than 0.0035; the reverse pass adds to the forward one (+BIDIR > +PFWD), the raw logits do not (+ALL < +BIDIR, and +ALL collapses 44b6 dataset 0b24845f by 0.088), so probabilities ship, not logits. On the F4 arm the weakest domain is +0.0028, below the +0.003 floor, but the dense domain moves 12 of 12 datasets the same way. The +0.007 LB move was not bought with more edges (output 0.22% smaller); the holdout is 2 for 6, and both successes had a measured mechanism (F4: the repair budget bound; edgeprob: a new information source whose standalone AUC beat the ranker's).

## 2026-09-02 velwhy

- Hypothesis: re-ordering the ranker's existing candidate list by velocity-predicted distance instead of raw distance puts the true target first more often.
- Scope: rankwhy's rank >= 1 population only (173 / 152 / 1,510 cases); a re-ordering measurement on a fixed candidate list, not a scored pipeline change. Filed unreviewed, tables only.
- Experiment: `velwhy.py` -> `biohub-velwhy`, CPU, 35.2 min. Source velocity magnitude and the true target's position under two orderings of the SAME candidate list: ranker column 0 (raw distance) and column 4 (distance from the velocity-predicted position). Case counts reproduce rankwhy exactly; anchors exact. Cost: 35.2 min CPU, no GPU quota, no submission slot.
- Result:

  | | F4-6bba (173) | F4-44b6 (152) | F4-zh (1,510) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | velocity EXACTLY ZERO | 42 (24.3%) | 8 (5.3%) | 121 (8.0%) |
  | where non-zero: median / p90 (um) | 2.17 / 4.60 | 2.16 / 4.79 | 1.61 / 3.59 |
  | true target first by RAW distance | 5 (2.9%) | 0 (0.0%) | 9 (0.6%) |
  | true target first by PREDICTED distance | 27 (15.6%) | 29 (19.1%) | 187 (12.4%) |
  | predicted beats raw | 36 (20.8%) | 36 (23.7%) | 246 (16.3%) |
  | predicted loses to raw | 13 (7.5%) | 20 (13.2%) | 199 (13.2%) |
  | median d_true / md_true (um) | 6.90 / 6.94 | 6.59 / 6.68 | 5.89 / 6.41 |
  | median d_top / md_top (um) | 3.32 / 3.56 | 2.29 / 3.14 | 2.13 / 2.68 |
  | median candidates | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.0 |
- Conclusion: Re-ordering by predicted distance puts the true target first in 12-19% of the rank>=1 cases against 0-2.9% for raw distance. `md_true` exceeds `d_true` and `md_top` exceeds `d_top` in all three domains, so the velocity prediction moves the source away from both candidates; the gain comes from the relative change, not from the prediction landing nearer the true target.

  Cap arithmetic, not binding in any domain: `DIV_GLOBAL_CAP` 0.00375 x final nodes = 616 (6bba, 164,287 nodes) / 1,236 (44b6, 329,636) / 784 (zh, 209,271), against 456 / 861 / 128 forks actually added.

  Denominators, the user's correction on reading these tables (2026-09-02): on Zebrahub every cell is annotated and the detector's recall there is about 0.80, so any question asked of that domain returns "detection" — the 65.5% `div_daughter_missed` is a statement about zh's detector recall, not about divisions, and does not transfer. The competition domains carry the opposite bias: a division enters their GT only if a human saw the mother and both daughters, so their rows can never show a detection loss (0 of 14 here). `div_J`'s denominator is annotated divisions, which is the competition-like population.
- Conclusion: v2 is the version to read. Across 1,095 GT divisions the ILP forked correctly on one; the patch recovered 2 (6bba) and 18 (zh). Emitted forks are overwhelmingly false in all three domains and the global cap binds in none.

## 2026-08-30 dc_gate + vetoscore

- Hypothesis: whether DeepCenter can veto xl detections it is silent on (xl leads, DeepCenter speaks only at extremes).
- Scope: dc_gate is a local offline analysis on judge_rows.npz, zero GPU. vetoscore tested a cheap proxy of the veto — drop xl points with no dcdet ep05 peak (score >= tau) within 3 um — not the heatmap-response rule itself. Three domains.
- Experiment: `dc_gate.py` (local, judge_rows.npz, zero GPU); `biohub-vetoscore` v1, 219.2 min CPU, anchor exact in all 3 domains. `biohub-dcsample` (T4) caching ep05's raw window-max response at every xl detection (hdval_*.npz, 12+12+8 sets); `vetoscore2` generated, not yet run, at tau 0.02/0.05/0.10.
- Result:
  dc_gate: RESCUE — xl-dropped candidates with ep05 >= 0.15 are only 24.3% real, 29.8% at 0.30, and ep05 >= 0.9 comp positives are 0.0%. VETO — among xl-kept candidates (mean3 >= 0.15), those with ep05 window-max hd < 0.02 are 90.2% fake at 0.31% collateral (6bba comp positives killed: 0.19%). Gated AUC 0.742 vs DCheavy 0.763.

  vetoscore, adj_J delta:

  | arm | 6bba | 44b6 | zh |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | V05 | -0.0619 | -0.0479 | -0.0558 |
  | V10 | -0.0642 | -0.0473 | -0.0597 |
  | V15 | -0.0649 | -0.0575 | -0.0676 |

  The proxy vetoed 12.24% (zh) / 15.66% (6bba) / 18.19% (44b6) of all cached points — 4-6x dc_gate's prediction (~3%) — and the excess is ordered by cell density, because dcdet's 4 um NMS erases the peak of any real cell in a stronger neighbour's shadow, so dense regions read as "DC silent" exactly where they are busiest. 44b6_0b24845f alone: -0.4788. 6bba edge_J 0.9233 -> 0.8519 with node_ratio -0.019 -> -0.135.
- Conclusion: Peak-list-within-3um is not a usable silence oracle: all three taus are negative in all three domains. The heatmap-response veto itself is untested. The pipeline already deletes points post-link (`_short_filter`), so a negative faithful veto would read as pre-ranker deletion at these taus not paying, leaving the veto signal usable only as a ranker feature.

## 2026-08-30 fuserows + judge audit

- Hypothesis: whether a trained evidence judge over the four heatmaps' response patterns beats a fixed weighted average.
- Scope: features are point responses only — per-map local shape, inter-map peak offsets, and raw-intensity context were never features. Brightness deliberately excluded from features. Held-out test set: every second zh crop, all rows, 223,746 of which 90,161 positive.
- Experiment: `biohub-fuserows` (28.3 min T4) collected 381,405 evidence rows — union candidates of the four heatmaps, 7 response-pattern features, 6,710 competition-GT positives from 36 pool datasets (18+18, seed 20260830), 374,695 zh rows from 33 non-eval crops — and trained two negative variants. Local CPU audit: `judge_audit.py` on judge_rows.npz. ~0.5 h GPU total.
- Result:

  | scorer | held-out AUC |
  |---|---|
  | mean3 (shipped) | 0.7380 |
  | hd alone (ep05) | 0.7466 |
  | F4 / W1101 / DCheavy fixed blends | 0.7557 / 0.7632 / 0.7633 |
  | judge_all (trained) | 0.7651 |
  | judge_dim_only | 0.7536 |
  | judge_dim+silent | 0.7002, degenerate (comp-pos q10 = 1.0) |

  fuserows' judge_filtered AUC 0.9956 was circular: its test negatives were selected by the model's own input features (ep05-silent + dim). On the honest test it reads 0.7002 and its score distribution is a point mass (uncalibratable).
  The negative-label problem is priced (zh gap 2.5-7%, each filter's cost measured); judge_rows.npz allows zero-GPU retests of any future feature idea.
- Conclusion: The trained judge clears the best fixed blend by +0.0018. The joint pattern of the four responses is exhausted, to GBM-visible precision, by a weighted average. No variant meets the bar set for spending fusecache2 + fusescore2, so the line stopped here.

## 2026-08-30 zhcomplete

- Hypothesis: whether zebrahub is fully labeled.
- Scope: two label-free measurements. Per-frame dropout over 41 crops; unmatched-peak forensics over 8 crops.
- Experiment: `biohub-zhcomplete` v1, CPU, 0.7 min.
- Result:
  1. Per-frame dropout ~zero: 927,424 mid-flight track-frames across 41 crops, 9 one-frame holes, 18 any-length (boundary-guarded at 5 um).
  2. Unmatched-peak forensics: 8 crops, 21,721 xl peaks >= 0.15, 9.6% unmatched. Of 2,090 unmatched peaks, 591 (28.3%) are bright (above the matched peaks' own q25) AND independently seconded by ep05 within 3 um; 351 (16.8%) are dim with no consensus; 1,041 (49.8%) are dim-with-consensus and ambiguous (the bright bar excludes 25% of real matched cells too).

  Completeness gap: 591/(22,675+591) = 2.54% as the defensible estimate; ~6.7% if every ambiguous peak is a cell.
  Consequences: zh precision for every detector is understated by roughly this amount; arm orderings are largely robust (all arms inflated the same way) but absolute zh precision/F1 carries a footnote. zh keeps the honest-denominator role for recall (a 2.5% incomplete denominator against the competition's 2.8% annotation). The fusion judge's negative mining is sound only in the filtered variant (negatives = unmatched AND dim AND ep05-silent); the all-negatives variant would train on several hundred unlabeled cells as counter-examples. fuserows trains both; the filtered one is the primary.
- Conclusion: Zebrahub is not fully labeled; the gap is ~2.5% (bounded above by ~6.7%) and consists of whole-track misses, not per-frame flicker.

- Hypothesis: whether the detfuse2 heatmap blends convert their offline detection F1 gain into adj_J in the pipeline.
- Scope: five arms x three domains, one solve per arm per dataset, D32 ranker for every judged arm (leak rule), BASE x D187 as the harness anchor. 32 datasets, these blend weights, global blending only.
- Experiment: `biohub-fusescore` v1, CPU, 256.9 min. No submission spent.
- Result:
  Anchor exact in all three domains (6bba 0.9293 / 44b6 0.8185 / zh 0.8093 = dcpool to the digit).

  | arm | 6bba adj_J | 44b6 adj_J | zh adj_J |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | BASE x D187 (anchor) | 0.9293 | 0.8185 | 0.8093 |
  | BASE x D32 (reference) | 0.9251 | 0.8250 | 0.8088 |

  adj_J deltas vs BASE x D32:

  | blend | 6bba | 44b6 | zh |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F4 | -0.0053 | +0.0054 | +0.0027 |
  | W1101 | -0.0108 | +0.0054 | +0.0024 |
  | DCheavy | -0.0145 | -0.0020 | -0.0028 |

  div_J deltas: F4 -0.0301/0/-0.0022, W1101 -0.0278/0/-0.0019, DCheavy +0.0571/0/-0.0016.

  1. detfuse2's +0.0155 detection F1 — recall and precision up, dets/fr down, dense GT, anchored — did not survive the pipeline. zh converted at ~1:6 (+0.0027) and 6bba went negative. That is the ninth anti-prediction by an offline detection number.
  2. The dcmerge pattern is the model's domain property, not the usage's: helps where xl is weak (zh, mildly 44b6), hurts where xl is strong (6bba), under all three usages tried — points as primaries (dcmerge), points in the repair pool (dcpool, null), heatmap in the blend (fusescore).
  3. What the direction still owns, unused: (a) three usages, one pattern, helps where xl is weak and hurts where it is strong, unexplained; (b) the 44b6 node deficit halved (-14.8% -> -7.3%); (c) F4/W1101 were positive in two domains; (d) ep05 solo beats the xl ensemble on zh; (e) the clean-eval machinery, the checkpoint, the undertraining dial.
  4. BASE x D32 vs BASE x D187: D32 is -0.0042 adj_J on 6bba (and -0.035 div_J), +0.0065 on 44b6, -0.0005 zh.
- Conclusion: What is measured and settled: global blending of ep05 into the average, at these weights, on these 32 datasets, is 6bba-negative. F4 and W1101 disagree in sign across domains; DCheavy is negative in all three. The D187 submission configuration stands.

- Result:

  | arm (b0,b1,b2,dc) | dets/fr | recall | prec | F1* |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | FULL3 (1,1,1,0) shipped | 260.9 | 0.7979 | 0.7579 | 0.7774 |
  | W110h (1,1,0.5,0) | 273.3 | 0.8217 | 0.7453 | 0.7816 |
  | F4 (1,1,1,1) | 257.7 | 0.8060 | 0.7752 | 0.7903 |

  - DCheavy: +0.0155 F1 over the shipped detector with fewer detections per frame; the no-surplus criterion is met.
  - ep05 solo beats the three-branch xl ensemble on dense GT (0.7879 vs 0.7774).
  - Cold-miss rescue: of FULL3's 15,774 zh misses, ep05 responds >= 0.15 near 89.9% (mean3 82.0%, either 93.5%).
  - W110hh and W2211 printed identical rows — they are the same normalised weights; a harmless arm-design slip that doubles as a determinism check.

  Competition-side section failed to inform: sampled frames left 8 (6bba) / 4 (44b6) cold misses — no n. Sparse-GT "own best gate" lands at 0.40 because the F1 is precision-dominated by the annotated-only denominator; those recall columns are not readable.

  Next: cache blended detections (F4 / W1101 / DCheavy computed from one shared 4-heatmap pass) for the 32 eval datasets (~1.5-2 h GPU), then a dcpool-style three-domain adj_J run (CPU), BASE anchored on the existing caches at 0.9293. Ranker frozen per thr5/dcmerge precedent.
- Conclusion: DCheavy gains +0.0155 F1 on the honest denominator with recall and precision up and fewer detections. Competition-domain judgment passes to the pipeline test.

  What attacks it, by existing evidence: training our own detector (never done; dctrain built the machinery — clean 175 split, PU loss, snapshot discipline, 32.2 min/epoch measured — and brightness jitter / dim-cell weighting are one flag each); detfuse's W110h weighting (+2.8 recall at equal F1); the 2.5% single-branch-visible miss headroom.
- Conclusion: On the honest denominator, detection cold-misses (14.49%) are ~8x the entire linking-side loss (no_cand + floor + absent + rejected + post = 1.8%). The ranker, the ILP and the post stages each lose under 1%; wrong links are 1.8% of final edges. The sparse domains understate the detection bucket by construction and it still leads on 44b6.

## 2026-08-29 divcurve

- Hypothesis: whether the division model's AUC is limited by the number of zebrahub crops used for training.
- Scope: div-train v3's protocol verbatim (same triples, 25 features, MATCH_UM 5.0, same GBM), the mixture sweep replaced by a crop-count learning curve. Eval set: 33,587 competition 6bba triples, 83 positives — AUC noise at this n is ~±0.02.
- Experiment: `biohub-divcurve` v1, CPU.
- Result:

  | crops | seeds' AUC on held-out 6bba | mean |
  |---|---|---|
  | 10 | 0.8029 / 0.7578 / 0.8215 | 0.794 |
  | 20 | 0.8075 / 0.8100 / 0.8249 | 0.814 |
  | 30 | 0.8326 / 0.8470 / 0.8292 | 0.836 |
  | 39 (all with divisions) | 0.8201 | 0.820 |

  10 -> 30 rises +0.042 (ranges barely overlap); the full 39-crop set lands below all three 30-crop draws. Zebrahub labels are machine-generated (~10% on near-background), so late-added crops plausibly carry label noise.

  Anchor did not reproduce and cannot: full-set AUC read 0.8201 against div-train v3's recorded 0.8083. Cause: in `div_train.py`, negative thinning seeds `np.random.default_rng(hash(name) % 2**31)`, and Python salts str hashes per process. v3's 0.8083 was one draw of a stochastic thinning and was never exactly reproducible. Within one run every arm shares one triple set, so the curve above is internally clean; across runs, zh-side AUCs carry ~±0.01-0.02 of thinning noise on top of eval noise. Any future assembly from `div_train.py` must replace `hash(name)` with a stable hash (e.g. `zlib.crc32` of the encoded name) before its numbers can anchor anything.
- Conclusion: The curve saturates by ~30 crops and the marginal crop at the top end is worth zero or less; extrapolating to 3x the crops is not supported. The constraint is the model / features / label quality, not crop count.

## 2026-08-29 dcpool

- Hypothesis: whether feeding epoch-5 DeepCenter points into the repair pool (visible to `_gap_close` alone) improves adj_J.
- Scope: DC points at score 0.12, repair pool only; one solve per dataset, arms byte-identical upstream; three domains. Speaks only to bridge inserts at span 1.
- Experiment: `biohub-dcpool` v1, CPU.
- Result:
  Every anchor held exactly: 6bba BASE adj_J 0.9293 / div_J 0.1316, zh BASE 0.8093, and the first clean 44b6 arm (dctrain's excluded 12) baselined at adj_J 0.8185.

  | DC_TAU | bridge inserts: midpoint | xl snap | DC snap | adj_J delta, all 3 domains |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | BASE | 3,017 | 1,348 | 0 | — |
  | 0.30 | 2,635 | 1,347 | 383 | ±0.0000 |
  | 0.15 | 2,179 | 1,345 | 841 | ±0.0000 |
  | 0.05 | 2,138 | 1,345 | 882 | ±0.0000 |

  117,691 DC points entered the pool (+29.2%); at tau 0.05, 20% of all bridge inserts moved from guessed midpoints onto measured positions and adj_J did not move at the fourth decimal in any domain. The cap never bound (17,460 made vs 55,188 allowed).

  Why zero: a bridge insert's position affects the metric only through whether the inserted node matches GT within 7.0 um. A 1-frame gap's straight-line midpoint errs by roughly half a displacement — p50 displacement is 1.82 um — so interpolation already lands inside the match radius essentially always. Measured positions are metric-equivalent to guessed ones at span 1. This also retro-explains the cap20 win's anatomy: the budget (how many bridges) was the entire effect; position quality never entered.

  DeepCenter ledger:

  | use | run | verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | primary add (published model) | dcmerge v2 | closed: breaks links, opposite signs |
  | primary add would need clean eval | dctrain/dccache2/3 | built it; epoch-5 is the right artifact |
  | repair-pool add (conditional, ep05) | dcpool | closed: true null, mechanism measured |
  | span-2 bridges (guessed positions) | span4 | closed: eats daughters |

  What survives: (1) the epoch-5 detector itself — clean three-domain eval, beats xl's recall on 44b6, cached for all 40 eval datasets — available if a future line needs a second detector for something other than bridge positions (e.g. division daughters); (2) the undertraining dial; (3) the detfuse finding that fusion signal exists at the peak-ranking level (+0.0215 AUC), which is a detection question, untouched by this null.
- Conclusion: The mechanism fired (20% of bridge inserts moved to measured positions at tau 0.05) and adj_J did not change at the fourth decimal in any domain. Bridge-insert position quality is metric-irrelevant at span 1.

## 2026-08-29 detfuse result
- Hypothesis: Combining the three detector branches (scalar weights or a learned per-peak combiner) improves detection over the mean.
- Scope: 41 Zebrahub crops, one domain, detection metrics only (no pipeline/adj_J run). Anchors digit-exact against det_ablate3 (FULL@5um 0.7738/0.7350/0.7539 at gate 0.15; B01 0.7585 at 0.20).
- Experiment: `biohub-detfuse` v1, 10 min T4, 101,615 GT points. Outputs `fuse_rows.npz` (128k peaks) and `fuse_miss.npz`, allowing offline fusion training with no new inference.
- Result: Scalar weights at the scorer's 7 um radius, each arm at its own best gate:

| arm (w0,w1,w2) | recall | prec | F1* |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL (1,1,1) | 0.7979 | 0.7579 | 0.7774 |
| B01 (1,1,0) | 0.7935 | 0.7701 | 0.7816 |
| W110h (1,1,0.5) | 0.8217 | 0.7453 | 0.7816 |
| W210h (2,1,0.5) | 0.8179 | 0.7482 | 0.7815 |
| W311 (3,1,1) | 0.8079 | 0.7563 | 0.7813 |
| W121 (1,2,1) | 0.8232 | 0.7362 | 0.7772 |
| W112 (1,1,2) control | 0.8247 | 0.7222 | 0.7700 |

  Four weightings tie at 0.7811-0.7816; the surface is flat once B2 is suppressed. W110h ties B01's F1 while keeping +2.8 points of recall.
  Branch disagreement band (det_ablate3's open question): peaks where branches disagree by >= 0.30 are 7.9% of 128k; score q25/50/75 = 0.204/0.230/0.261, only 2.0% sub-threshold against 16.5% for all peaks. The disagreement sits at the operating band, not below it.
  Per-peak fusion: logistic on the three branch logits, fit on even crops / scored on odd. AUC 0.7939 (mean score) -> 0.8153 (+0.0215). Learned weights (0.94, 1.68, 0.07).
  Miss headroom: of 15,774 GT cells unmatched at 7 um (floor 0.05), some single branch has window-max >= 0.15 near 98.3% of them, the branch mean near 82.0%. The 82% column is not pure "mean sees it and still misses": unmatched includes peaks lost to the 1:1 greedy competition and to the 4-um NMS, so only the 16.3-point gap (~2,570 cells, ~2.5% of GT) is fusion-specific recall a per-voxel combiner could recover.
- Conclusion: Scalar fusion is worth at most ~+0.004 detection F1, all of it from down-weighting B2; per-peak learned fusion ~+0.02 AUC, with B2's learned weight near zero. All numbers are detection, one domain. The line is held until the retrained DeepCenter lands, so that W110h, a learned combiner and DC-as-input can be tested in one run sharing the same re-cache + ranker retrain + three-domain solve.

## 2026-08-28 dctrain launched
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: 199 datasets split 167 train + 8 val + 24 excluded. Excluded set = the 12 6bba holdout (verbatim) + 12 44b6 drawn `random.Random(20260827).sample` from the 44b6 outside D32's pool. All three eval domains clean.
- Experiment: `biohub-dctrain` v1 pushed, T4, running. Recipe: the author's defaults verbatim (checked against their run wrapper line by line), except `--snapshot-interval 5 --snapshot-final` and epochs 30 not 50 (167 movies/epoch = 2.35x their per-epoch exposure; `--resume` continues if history says still improving). Labels read via `viz_cells.read_geff` (zarr-free); frames via the trainer's own per-chunk blosc2 path, matching the competition layout. Smoke-read asserted at startup. Waiter at 300 s.
- Result: All split names printed in the log. val: 4+4 drawn from the remaining 175, seed 20260828, excluded from training; best.pt selects on val, not on any eval domain. Cost estimate (not a measurement) ~5-7 h GPU; 8.8 h of quota remained at launch and the week refreshes 2026-08-29 00:00 UTC mid-run. Rationale: DeepCenter's shipped trainer's `split_samples` groups by name prefix, the prefix has two values (44b6/6bba), and "hold out 10% of groups" held out one whole batch — so 44b6 is its training set (eval forever nan) and 6bba its selection set (tainted), and dcmerge's opposite signs could not be settled.
- Conclusion: The user's call: retrain on our split and re-measure, or drop the model. Next after it lands: cache detections for the 24 excluded + 8 zh, detcmp-style coverage + recall, then dcmerge-style arms with the retrained weights, readable in all three domains.

The `estimated_number_of_nodes` figures are estimates.

## 2026-08-28 accdiag result
- Hypothesis: The acceleration column fails because it is rarely computable and because it measures camera/stage shake rather than cell motion; de-meaning per frame would fix it.
- Scope: 12 6bba holdout datasets, 173,269 seeds; AUC section uses `poolsize`'s own labels, 14,817 labelled pairs, 0.6588 positive. Single-column AUCs only.
- Experiment: `biohub-accdiag`, 9 min, CPU.
- Result: Computability, with the per-seed denominator:

| `acc_hist` | meaning | seeds | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | no backward link at all | 13,384 | 7.7% |
| 1 | one backward step, needs two | 8,703 | 5.0% |
| 2 | full, three positions | 151,182 | 87.3% |

  Corrected (this entry; earlier text said "for most candidates it cannot produce three"): acceleration is computable for 87.3% of seeds. The old claim compared a per-seed-per-frame counter (316,658) against a count of candidate pairs (225,861), so the fraction had never been measured. The run's own degradation counters, 31,594 and 25,885, are still per-seed-per-frame and accumulate across the sweep, stage B and the diagnostic; they are not comparable to 173,269.
  Stage motion vs cell motion — nothing in the pipeline subtracts global stage motion; a constant drift is absorbed by the velocity column, a changing drift appears as the same spurious acceleration on every cell, which the per-frame median of acceleration vectors estimates:

| | median | p90 |
|---|---|---|
| \|median acceleration\| per frame (stage) | 0.4845 | 1.9795 um/frame^2 |
| per-cell \|acc - median\| (cells) | 2.0187 | 2.8265 |
| ratio stage/cell | 0.240 | |

  1,176 frames had the >=5 usable seeds needed to estimate a median.
  Single-column AUC (below 0.5 means informative with the sign flipped; 0.5 means nothing):

| col | raw | de-meaned | flipped-equivalent (raw) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acc_len` | 0.4968 | 0.4919 | -- |
| `acc_cos` | 0.5136 | 0.5068 | -- |
| `md_acc` | 0.0624 | 0.0582 | 0.9376 |
| `md-md_acc` | 0.3013 | 0.3097 | 0.6987 |
| `acc_hist` | 0.5217 | 0.5217 | -- |
| for scale: `d` | 0.0319 | | 0.9681 |
| for scale: `md` | 0.0364 | | 0.9636 |
| for scale: `score_c` | 0.7955 | | -- |

  Every de-meaned column moves by at most 0.0084 and they disagree on direction (`md_acc` improves, `md-md_acc` and `acc_cos` get worse). `md` (distance from the constant-velocity prediction) is 0.9636 flipped; `md_acc`, the same distance from the acceleration-corrected prediction, is 0.9376.
  Arithmetic, with `vels[t+1][ci] = (C[ci] - P[pi]) * SCALE`:

```
pred     = 2.0*x_t - 1.0*x_{t-1}                        var  5.00 * sigma^2
pred_acc = 2.5*x_t - 2.0*x_{t-1} + 0.5*x_{t-2}          var 10.50 * sigma^2
```

  under independent per-detection position noise `sigma` — the acceleration term multiplies predictor variance by 2.1x (1.45x in standard deviation). Median real acceleration is 2.0 um/frame^2 against a 10 um gate.
- Conclusion: Acceleration is computable 87.3% of the time, the stage component is a quarter of the per-cell residual, and de-meaning changes nothing; the line closes on measurement. Adding acceleration moves the prediction away from the true child, so `md_acc` is a strictly worse version of a column the ranker already has. The variance argument is general and also explains `biohub-accel`'s permutation importance of +0.0000 to +0.0017 with the indicator column present and working.

## 2026-08-28 rank5 v2 result
- Hypothesis: Using the learned bridge ranker to reject low-ranked gap-closing bridges improves adj_J over `cap20` (no gate).
- Scope: 3 tau arms plus `cap20`, three domains (6bba, 44b6, zh).
- Experiment: `biohub-rank5` v2, 255 min CPU. Lookup healthy: 94.64% of seeds mapped, 0.90% of bridge pairs missing (v1 was 100% missing). Anchors held — `cap20` reproduced +0.0013 / +0.0085 / +0.0056.
- Result:

| arm | 6bba | 44b6 | zh |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cap20` (ref 55817630, LB 0.922) | +0.0013 | +0.0085 | +0.0056 |
| `tau0.2` | +0.0011 | +0.0080 | +0.0055 |
| `tau0.5` | +0.0012 | +0.0076 | +0.0052 |
| `tau0.8` | +0.0007 | +0.0030 | +0.0016 |

  Every threshold is below `cap20` in every domain, monotonically in how much it rejects. The ranker itself is strong: 0.9693 AUC against distance-alone's 0.8829 at exactly the decision gap closing makes.
  Five gates tried:

| gate | run | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| candidate required | `gap4` | loses |
| velocity cosine | `gap3` | loses |
| fragment length | `gap3`/`gap4` | loses |
| clearance radius | `gap3` | loses, fails the rule |
| learned, 0.97 AUC | `rank5` | loses, monotonically |

  Mechanism, from `_short_filter`: with no bridge the fragment falls below `SHORT_MIN` and is deleted whole, so every correct edge inside it disappears; with a wrong bridge the fragment survives and keeps all of its correct edges, and only the two bridge edges are false. A 2-frame bridge inserts two nodes, spans three frames, and is likelier to be wrong, so its cost doubles while the rescued fragment is the same — which is why `span2` adds more bridges and still loses.
  Instrumentation flaw, harmless here: `_GAP_LOG`'s key is `(need_cand, span, gate_um, cap_frac)` and does not include `GAP_RANK_TAU`, so all four arms sharing those four values summed into one row — 53,748 bridges is `cap20`'s 18,248 plus the three tau arms. Scores are unaffected.
  Standing of the gap-closing knobs:

| knob | verdict |
|---|---|
| `GAP1_CAP_FRAC` 0.003 -> 0.02 | the win, +0.002 on the leaderboard |
| the candidate requirement | drop it, part of the same win |
| `GAP_SPAN` 1 -> 2 | fails the rule, destroys divisions in 6bba |
| `GAP1_GATE_UM` 9 -> 12 | passes the rule, loses to `cap20` everywhere |
| four hand-made gates | all rationing, none selecting |
| a learned gate at 0.97 AUC | loses monotonically |

- Conclusion: The ranker separates bridge pairs well (0.9693 AUC) but rejecting the low-ranked ones costs score in every domain, monotonically. Every one-frame bridge is worth making; two-frame bridges are not. The shipped `cap20` is the end of this line.

## 2026-08-28 rank5 edge ranker
- Hypothesis: is the edge ranker informative beyond the physical distance that `_gap_close`'s Hungarian already sorts on, at the two-frame gap-closing decision?
- Scope: ranker trained on two-frame pairs from 116 6bba non-holdout datasets only. Label rule = `poolsize`'s with one extra hop through `child_of` (positive when j matches a GT GRANDCHILD of i's GT node). The three pipeline arms (`tau0.2`, `tau0.5`, `tau0.8`) measured nothing about the ranker; see Result.
- Experiment: `biohub-rank5`, 233 min CPU. Anchors: `cap20` reproduced +0.0013 / +0.0085 / +0.0056 exactly.
- Result:
  ```
  138,734 two-frame pairs, 60.65% positive
  18-feature ranker AUC   0.9693
  distance alone   AUC    0.8829
  the ranker buys         +0.0863
  ```
  Column 0 is the physical distance. Single-column AUCs (below 0.5 means informative with the sign flipped):

  | col | AUC | flipped |
  |---|---|---|
  | `d` distance | 0.117 | 0.883 |
  | `md` distance from the velocity prediction | 0.129 | 0.871 |
  | `rank` among the parent's candidates | 0.132 | 0.868 |
  | `n_cand_i` | 0.160 | 0.840 |
  | `dxy` | 0.170 | 0.830 |
  | `score_c` child detection score | 0.757 | — |
  | `score_p` parent detection score | 0.697 | — |
  | `d-md` | 0.612 | — |
  | `t/T`, `\|v\|` | 0.508, 0.491 | ~nothing |

  Three geometric columns sit at ~0.87 individually; the combination reaches 0.969. `score_c` at 0.757 is the strongest non-geometric feature.

  Probability quantiles (1/10/25/50/75/90/99%): 0.007 0.020 0.076 0.863 0.985 0.996 0.999 — bimodal, median 0.863.

  Pipeline arms void:
  ```
  bridge pairs looked up 54,744, of which 54,744 had NO probability (100.00%)
  ```
  `tau0.2` / `tau0.5` / `tau0.8` returned identical deltas +0.0001 / −0.0004 / −0.0006. Their 6bba `node_ratio` is −0.0223 against BASE's −0.0215, i.e. slightly fewer nodes than the shipped configuration.

  Cause: `solve_one` builds the ILP node coordinates with
  ```python
  coords = np.asarray(np.round(coords_rows), np.int16)
  ```
  so a graph node's xyz is the seed position rounded to an integer, while `seeds_of` returns the sub-voxel refined float. `_seed_to_node` matched at 1e-6 tolerance and never matched anything. Fixed at `SEED_MATCH_VOX = 1.0`: rounding moves a coordinate at most 0.5 per axis, i.e. at most √3/2 = 0.87 voxels, while `_physical_nms` already forces 4.0 µm between kept seeds — 2.46 voxels in z and 9.8 in xy.

  `_BRIDGE_MISS` instrumentation was added while writing the script and reported 100%.
- Conclusion: the ranker reaches 0.9693 AUC against distance alone at 0.8829, +0.0863, on two-frame pairs. The three tau arms measured "reject everything" because of the seed-to-node coordinate mismatch and carry no information about the ranker. The mismatch is fixed at `SEED_MATCH_VOX = 1.0`.

- Hypothesis: does DeepCenter cover our detector's misses by much more than our own sub-threshold repair band's 20.2%?
- Scope: one domain, 8 Zebrahub crops; does not satisfy the three-domain rule. Zebrahub is the only fair venue for DeepCenter (trained on all 71 44b6, model-selected on all 128 6bba) and also the domain furthest from the hidden test. Nothing here measures adj_J; recall is not the metric. The public solution has this mechanism and disables it, as a VETO rather than as a candidate source. Venue choice was the user's.
- Experiment: `biohub-detcmp` v3, 21 min GPU, 8 Zebrahub crops, `best.pt`. Prior runs: `detcmp` v1, `detcmp` v2, `dcprobe`, `dcprobe` v2. Comparison figures for our own band from `flicker.py`, same denominator.
- Result:
  Coverage:

  | DeepCenter | covers OUR misses | we cover ITS misses |
  |---|---|---|
  | @ 0.05 | 69.5% | 49.4% |
  | @ 0.10 | 64.3% | 51.2% |
  | @ 0.15 | 58.1% | 57.9% |
  | @ 0.30 | 28.6% | 84.2% |

  Our own sub-threshold band [0.05, 0.15) covers 20.2%. DeepCenter at 0.05 covers 69.5%, 3.4×; the bar was "much above 20.2%". Asymmetric: 69.5% vs 49.4%.

  Recall and flicker:

  | | recall | kept/frame |
  |---|---|---|
  | OURS @ 0.15 | 0.9642 | 272.7 |
  | DeepCenter @ 0.15 | 0.9644 | 281.3 |
  | DeepCenter @ 0.05 | 0.9784 | 296.4 |

  At 0.05 DeepCenter takes +1.42 points of recall for +8.7% output.

  | | always | intermittent | never | gap=1 | gap≥2 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | OURS @ 0.15 | 67.0% | 32.4% | 0.6% | 2,660 | 1,465 |
  | DeepCenter @ 0.05 | 76.5% | 23.2% | 0.3% | 1,889 | 835 |

  43% fewer gap≥2 dropouts.

  Correction: DeepCenter is not a temporal model. `_DCDeepCenterUNet3D` takes a single volume, exactly as ours does; the earlier temporal-model claim conflated it with the separate `biohub-temporal-unet3d-seed314159-v1` dataset. The measurement stands; the temporal mechanism offered for it does not.

  Run history:

  | run | result | cause |
  |---|---|---|
  | `detcmp` v1 | DeepCenter: 0.4 peaks/frame vs our 272.7, logit overflow | wrong checkpoint |
  | `detcmp` v2 | four normalisations, byte-identical logits | normalisation was never the variable |
  | `dcprobe` | 0–1 peaks on 6bba, DeepCenter's own val split | wrong checkpoint, isolated |
  | `dcprobe` v2 | `best.pt` 114–654 peaks, `checkpoint_last.pt` 0–1 | answered |

  `GroupNorm` after a bias-free convolution erases any affine input transform: v2's four normalisations returned identical logits to three decimals. v1 went 0.0017 → 0.0000 under 4-view flip averaging. Our arm reproduced `flicker3`'s Zebrahub figures exactly (32.4% intermittent, 0.6% never); the DeepCenter arm had no anchor.

  Checkpoint selection error: `reference.md` said "Do not read the 7x val_loss as 'got worse' — the loss is positive-unlabeled BCE that punishes finding unannotated cells." That was used as a positive argument for the epoch-500 checkpoint, whose weights have grown 2.5× and whose largest logit anywhere in a 64³ volume is −0.34. `reference.md` now carries the measurement.

  Next step costed: pipe DeepCenter into `_gap_close`'s repair pool as an add-only second candidate source; needs DeepCenter detections cached for 91 evaluation datasets (12 6bba + 71 44b6 + 8 Zebrahub), ~1.8 h GPU at the measured ~0.7 s/frame, then a CPU sweep.
- Conclusion: on 8 Zebrahub crops DeepCenter at 0.05 covers 69.5% of our detector's misses against our own repair band's 20.2%, and the coverage is asymmetric (we cover 49.4% of its). It shows 43% fewer gap≥2 dropouts at +1.42 recall points and +8.7% output. It is a single-volume detector, not a temporal one.

## 2026-08-27 edge ranker and divisions
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: fork split measured on the 4 visible datasets of ref 55817630's run; div_J figures from the 12-dataset 6bba holdout and gap4.
- Experiment: inspection of `solve_one` (capacity 2, `div_w = 0.55`), `_add_safe_divisions` and `_gap_close`; fork counts from ref 55817630's run.
- Result:

  | dataset | ILP forks | final forks |
  |---|---|---|
  | 44b6_0113de3b | 11 | 54 |
  | 44b6_0b24845f | 15 | 130 |
  | 6bba_05b6850b | 6 | 18 |
  | 6bba_05db0fb1 | 15 | 143 |
  | total | 47 | 345 |

  The ILP makes 14% of the forks; `_add_safe_divisions` adds 86%.

  Path 1, the ILP: the solve is capacity 2, and `div_w = 0.55` is the objective cost of opening a fork; whether it is worth paying depends on the ranker's probabilities for both child edges.

  Path 2, the orphan pool:
  ```python
  orph = [g for g in ids if not pred.get(g)]
  ```
  Which nodes have a predecessor is decided by what the ILP linked. The patch takes each node with exactly one child and looks for a nearby orphan as second daughter, subject to `DIV_CHILD_UM` 10, `DIV_PARENT_UM` 12, `DIV_SISTER_UM` 15 and `DIV_DIVERGE_UM` 2.25, with both daughters required to have exactly one successor each. `ranker_fine`'s header recorded the worry that a more confident 1:1 linker "steals second daughters into wrong continuations, draining the orphan pool the division patch mines".

  For D187 div_J moved 0.0909 → 0.1316, but that whole move is two events out of the holdout's twelve annotated divisions; the explanation offered (a more correct rather than more confident ranker feeds the mechanism) was never measured.

  Coupling to gap closing: `_gap_close` executes `pred[gs] = ng`. The user corrected the sign — `gs` is an orphan because its predecessor was missed, so turning it into a second daughter would manufacture a false division; bridging removes a false candidate, a benefit rather than a cost. Structurally,
  ```python
  ends = [g for g in by_t.get(t, []) if g not in succ and g in pred]
  ```
  a bridge starts only from a node with no successor, and a real mother has already linked at least one daughter, so she is in `succ` and can never be an `ends` node.

  Magnitude: 6bba at BASE is 5 TP / 26 FP / 7 FN, `div_J` = 5/38 = 0.1316. Removing three of the 26 false divisions would give 5/35 = 0.1429, +0.0113 div_J and +0.0011 score. gap4 measured +0.0000 for every arm in 6bba and 44b6, so not even three false divisions were touched.
- Conclusion: 86% of final forks come from `_add_safe_divisions` mining the orphan pool, which the ranker determines through what the ILP links; the ILP itself makes 14%. Gap closing removes false division candidates rather than true ones, and cannot reach a true mother by construction. Its effect on div_J is below three false divisions in 6bba.

## 2026-08-27 gap4 design

- Hypothesis: A bridge policy of "candidate exists OR both fragments long enough" (C or L) is a superset of BASE (C only) at the eligibility test, and its value is not derivable from gap3's arms.
- Scope: 8 arms × 3 domains, D187, `SHORT_MIN` 4. The budget-binding demonstration is on synthetic data. The len5/6/7 section is reasoning over gap3 numbers, not a run. The scoring allocator is designed, not built.
- Experiment: `biohub-gap4` pushed 2026-08-27, 8 arms × 3 domains, D187, `SHORT_MIN` 4. Local pre-check: 400 synthetic movies × 7 arms.
- Result:

The user set the policy: if a candidate point exists, bridge directly; if no candidate exists, require len 8. With C = a qualifying candidate exists and L = both fragments ≥ N:

| policy | bridges | |
|---|---|---|
| BASE | C | what ships |
| `nocand` | everything | gap3 |
| `len8` | L | gap3 — deletes C-and-short |
| the user's | C or L | superset of BASE at the eligibility test |

Partition by (C, L) into a = C∧L, b = C∧¬L, d = ¬C∧L, e = ¬C∧¬L:

```
nocand − BASE = d + e   = +0.0009 / +0.0012 / +0.0034
len8   − BASE = d − b   = +0.0013 / +0.0043 / +0.0019
the user's    = d       ← three unknowns, two equations
```

Not derivable from gap3. `len8 > nocand` in 6bba and 44b6 gives b + e < 0; Zebrahub gives the opposite; neither isolates `b`.

Budget: `_gap_close` walks `for t in range(T - step)` and `break`s the moment `n_added >= max_gaps`, so the budget is handed out in frame order.

| | |
|---|---|
| cap, `0.003 × nodes` | 476 bridges |
| eligible WITH the candidate rule | ~238 — never binds |
| eligible WITHOUT it | ~1,570 — binds at 30% of demand |

Synthetic demonstration:

| | superset held | BASE bridges LOST to `or8` |
|---|---|---|
| shipped budget 0.003 | 246 / 300 | 58 (both arms made exactly 600 — fully bound) |
| budget past demand | 300 / 300 | 0 |

The user's reading: raising the budget dodges the problem; ranking the bridges solves it, and under a binding budget scoring is the better route.

Scoring allocator (designed, not built) — two passes instead of one greedy sweep:

1. Collect. For every frame, run the same per-frame `linear_sum_assignment` and the same gates, but record `(score, t, ge, gs, picks)` and mutate nothing. With no bridges made, `ends`/`starts` are the original graph's endpoints.
2. Allocate. Sort by score descending; accept greedily while the budget remains and `ge ∉ succ`, `gs ∉ pred`, and every candidate the bridge wants is still unused.

Keeping the per-frame Hungarian assignment in pass 1 preserves existing matching quality; only the priority across frames changes.

| score | available for | note |
|---|---|---|
| `−D`, the bridge distance | every bridge | already computed, free |
| `cand_sc[tt][idx]` | candidate-backed only | needs a floor for midpoint bridges |
| `min(frag_len_a, frag_len_b)` | every bridge | `_frag_len` caps at 12 |
| the edge ranker | every bridge | strongest, and the most work |

The pipeline has a trained 18-feature pair scorer; gap closing uses raw Euclidean distance instead. gap3 recorded it as left out on purpose: its features are computed over the primary seed set (local density, rank among candidates, per-frame counts) and rebuilding them for a repair-pool point is not a small change.

Anchors: the assembly reverses the gate order — the candidate lookup runs before the length test, because "only when there is no candidate" cannot be expressed otherwise. BASE, `nocand` and `len8` must all reproduce gap3 to the digit. Proved locally first: 400 synthetic movies × 7 arms, byte-identical to gap3, every arm adding 1,580–12,284 edges so no arm compared two no-ops. The first version of that test was nearly vacuous (tracks too short for a length-8 gate to fire, candidates scattered so BASE made 4 bridges in 400 movies) and was rebuilt.

Test artefact: do not compare raw edge tuples across arms. Inserted nodes are numbered from `next_id`, so an arm making a different number of bridges renumbers all of them and every edge touching an insertion compares unequal. That reported the superset property failing 278 of 300 times — an artefact. Map back to the original `(ge, gs)` endpoints.

len5/6/7 (reasoned, not run): across gap3's gate 0 → 4 → 8 the binding domain is 6bba at every point (+0.0009, +0.0010, +0.0013) and rises monotonically, while Zebrahub at 8 is still +0.0019, above it. Crude linear extrapolation puts the weakest-domain peak near gate 10 at +0.00145, +0.0002 over len8. `_frag_len` caps at 12, so `GAP_MIN_LEN > 12` is unsatisfiable and silently disables gap closing entirely.

- Conclusion: The "C or L" policy's value equals partition cell d, which gap3's two equations cannot isolate. Under any loosened policy the gap budget binds and is allocated by frame order rather than bridge quality; a ranked two-pass allocator is the designed fix. len8 dominates len5/6/7 unless something non-monotone occurs between.

## 2026-08-26 thr5 result

- Hypothesis: Tightening `UNET_THRESH` above 0.15 trades edge quality for node count in a way that could win on the hidden test; and the node-count penalty asymmetry claimed in the earlier entry (see 2026-08-26 node-count penalty) holds.
- Scope: gates 0.15 / 0.18 / 0.22 / 0.26, `SHORT_MIN` 4, D187. The 44b6 arm is in-sample — all 12 datasets sit inside D187's training pool, so it reports fit, not transfer; the independent domains are 6bba and Zebrahub, two. What the official scorer uses for `N_true` on the hidden test is unknown from here.
- Experiment: `biohub-thr5`, 190 min. Anchor: g0.15 reproduced thr4's `g0.15_s4` exactly, 0.9279 / 0.8553 / 0.8037.
- Result:

The correction. `reference.md`: the penalty is `max(0, J * (1 - 0.1 * (N_pred - N_true)/N_true))`. The `max(0, ...)` floors the whole product; it does not clamp the ratio. Verified against thr5's own columns — 6bba g0.15, `edge_J` 0.9258 × (1 − 0.1 × −0.0215) = 0.92779 against the reported 0.9279.

(a) A move toward the target hurts, not helps. Under target means a negative ratio means a multiplier above 1; adding nodes moves the ratio up toward zero, which shrinks the bonus.

(b) There is no asymmetry, because the slope is constant. Adding ΔN nodes changes the multiplier by exactly `−0.1 × ΔN/N_true`, regardless of where the ratio sits:

| starting ratio | add 1.61% of nodes | multiplier | adj_J change |
|---|---|---|---|
| −0.0215 (6bba, actual) | → −0.0054 | 1.00215 → 1.00054 | −0.0015 |
| 0.0000 (hypothetical) | → +0.0161 | 1.00000 → 0.99839 | −0.0015 |

The only way the cost could differ between local and hidden is if the hidden `N_true` were a very different magnitude — about half, to double the cost.

(c) Both failed submissions' local gains were already net of the node cost. `SHORT_MIN` 4's +0.0025 / +0.0054 / +0.0045 and gate 0.12's +0.0055 / +0.0045 / +0.0121 are post-penalty numbers. The remaining explanation for the leaderboard's 0.000 and −0.002 is that the local gain is not present in the hidden data, as with windowing (+0.0019 → −0.001) and the ranker pool (+0.0073 → −0.001). The three-domain rule's first verdict is 0.920 → 0.920.

Open hole: `N_true` is the train geff's `estimated_number_of_nodes`, and `reference.md` records that the test split has no such field.

Tightening, adj_J deltas:

| gate | 6bba | 44b6 (in-sample) | zh |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 (shipped) | 0.9279 | 0.8553 | 0.8037 |
| 0.18 | −0.0042 | +0.0058 | −0.0236 |
| 0.22 | −0.0095 | −0.0095 | −0.0962 |
| 0.26 | −0.0166 | −0.0453 | −0.2204 |

Both independent domains fall monotonically.

Decomposition:

| | 6bba | | 44b6 | | zh | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gate | edge_J | ratio | edge_J | ratio | edge_J | ratio |
| 0.15 | 0.9258 | −0.0215 | 0.8473 | −0.0875 | 0.7976 | −0.0808 |
| 0.18 | 0.9193 | −0.0471 | 0.8465 | −0.1681 | 0.7709 | −0.1252 |
| 0.22 | 0.9102 | −0.0911 | 0.8214 | −0.2970 | 0.6924 | −0.2285 |
| 0.26 | 0.8975 | −0.1564 | 0.7768 | −0.4371 | 0.5631 | −0.3817 |

- `edge_J` is monotone decreasing in the gate in every domain; the node term is the only thing pushing back.
- Tightening deletes real cells. Zebrahub 0.15 → 0.26 loses 29% of `edge_J` relative. At 0.26 it emits 38% fewer nodes than there are cells, and a missed detection costs twice (the GT edge becomes an FN, the neighbour's predicted edge becomes an FP).
- Zebrahub's node-count bonus grows from +0.008 to +0.038 across that range — 0.03 against a 0.23 loss.

Loosening: local gain, leaderboard loss (ref 55780773, 0.918 against its control's 0.920). Tightening: local loss in both independent domains.

`SHORT_MIN` 4 sits at ratio −0.0215 on 6bba, so the shipped pipeline is 2–9% below the estimated cell count in every domain — a standing bonus of 1.002 to 1.009. The 0.977 figure recorded earlier was 6bba's alone; 44b6 is 0.913 and Zebrahub 0.919 (corrected 2026-08-26; earlier text quoted 0.977 as the holdout-wide ratio).

- Conclusion: The node-count term is linear with constant slope `−0.1 × ΔN/N_true`, so no local/hidden asymmetry exists and it explains neither leaderboard result. Tightening the gate loses in both independent domains; 0.15 stands, with the threshold line closed at both ends.

- Scope: 8 arms × 3 domains, D187 ranker, `SHORT_MIN` 4. `clear4` bridge counts were not printed, so its physical reading is unconfirmed. Weakest-domain gain sits against holdout noise of roughly 0.002–0.003, after six comparisons.

- Result:

`div_J` is +0.0000 in 6bba and 44b6 for every arm and +0.0001…+0.0010 in Zebrahub. Gap closing does not touch divisions in the competition domains.

`nocand` is the unconditional case, not the ceiling: its measured value is what survives after good and bad bridges cancel. `len8` is above `nocand` in two of three domains, and in 44b6 by 3.6× (+0.0043 against +0.0012).

44b6 is monotone in the length gate: nocand +0.0012 → len4 +0.0035 → len8 +0.0043. Zebrahub is monotone the other way: +0.0034 → +0.0028 → +0.0019. `_frag_len` is capped at 12, so len12 is the last testable point on that curve.

Velocity gate: in 6bba `vel0.0` is +0.0004, below the ungated +0.0009 and the worst of the surviving arms; in 44b6 the same gate more than doubles the gain (+0.0026 against +0.0012). The gate's sign is domain-dependent.

`clear4` (refuse a bridge when a primary node sits within 4 µm) is identical to `nocand` in 6bba and Zebrahub (+0.0009, +0.0034) and −0.0002 in 44b6. Inference, unconfirmed: the gate rarely fires in the sparse domains, and in 44b6 at 327 cells/frame the nearest neighbour is inside 4 µm often enough to block real repairs.

Node count: `max_gaps = max(1, int(GAP1_CAP_FRAC * len(nodes)))` with `GAP1_CAP_FRAC = 0.003`, and at span 1 each bridge inserts exactly one node, so node count can grow by at most 0.3%. The two leaderboard failures grew output by +1.61% and +10.3%. The adjustment term `(1 − 0.1 × node_ratio)` is worth ≤0.0003 here.

Downgraded the same day by thr5 (see 2026-08-26 thr5 result): the arithmetic above holds — len8 costs at most 0.0003 of the multiplier and gap3's +0.0013 is already net of it — but the node-count term is linear with a constant slope, so being clear of it explains nothing about the two leaderboard results.

Proposed submission, one variable from ref 55772253 (LB 0.920): `UNET_THRESH` back to 0.15 (0.12 cost three ticks and is the only clear LB loss of the three), `SHORT_MIN` stays 4 (0.920 vs 0.921 is one tick, and every gap3 arm was measured at 4), plus `len8`. That matches the measured configuration exactly.

- Conclusion: `len8` is the best arm, weakest-domain +0.0013, six of seven arms positive in all three domains; `clear4` is the one rejection. The weakest-domain gain is within holdout noise of 0.002–0.003 and the three-domain rule is 0 for 2.

## 2026-08-26 logbase result

- Hypothesis: A classical filter (tophat, LoG) can match the UNet detector, and the tophat preprocessing is load-bearing as a detector.
- Scope: 6bba, recall@7.0, every arm scored at matched detection count — top-N peaks with N set to what the UNet keeps on that frame — so no threshold enters the comparison.
- Experiment: `biohub-logbase`, 185 s CPU.
- Result:

| arm | recall@7.0 | vs UNet |
|---|---|---|
| UNet (shipped) | 0.9813 | — |
| raw brightness | 0.8434 | −0.1379 |
| tophat only | 0.8462 | −0.1351 |
| LoG σ=1.3 | 0.8925 | −0.0888 |
| LoG σ=1.6 | 0.9247 | −0.0566 |
| LoG σ=2.0 | 0.9032 | −0.0781 |
| tophat + LoG σ=1.6 | 0.9163 | −0.0650 |

raw 0.8434 → tophat 0.8462 is +0.0028. The recorded `val_recall` gap (0.573 no-tophat against 0.659 tophat) is between trained networks, not between preprocessings: the tophat changes the input distribution and the network learns better on it.

LoG scale prediction: matched σ for a blob of radius r is r/√3; cells are 7–9 µm across at a 1.625 µm isotropic heatmap voxel, so r = 2.2–2.8 voxels and σ = 1.25–1.6. Measured optimum σ=1.6.

- Conclusion: The UNet is worth +0.0566 over the best classical filter (LoG σ=1.6). Used directly as a detector the tophat is worth +0.0028, so the tophat-as-detector hypothesis fails.
