## 2026-08-26 _gap_close mechanism

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: Mechanism description plus two corrections to earlier accounts in this log; eligibility counts are across the 12 6bba datasets.
- Experiment: Code reading of `_gap_close`, plus eligibility counts.
- Result:

The candidate pool is a band cut from the detector's own peaks:

```
CAND_THR 0.05  ─────────────  UNET_THRESH 0.15  ─────────
   repair pool: 0.05 ≤ s < 0.15      primary nodes: s ≥ 0.15
```

A bridge is built only if all of these hold:

| test | value | swept? |
|---|---|---|
| endpoints within the gate | `GAP1_GATE_UM` 9.0 | no |
| the single nearest candidate to the midpoint | — | never |
| within the snap radius | `GAP1_SNAP_UM` 3.2 | yes → noise |
| candidate score at least | `GAP1_MIN_CAND_SCORE` 0.10 | yes → noise |
| under the cap | `GAP1_CAP_FRAC` 0.003 | yes → noise |

`GAP1_MIN_CAND_SCORE` cuts the usable pool in half — `[0.10, 0.15)` of a `[0.05, 0.15)` band. All four constants were inherited from the public solution and none was derived. Only ~20% of missed frames have any candidate in the band, so adjusting sub-constants inside a gate that seldom opens cannot move anything.

Correction 1 (corrected 2026-08-26; earlier text called the plain midpoint careless for ignoring velocity): `ge` is at t, `gs` at t+2, the missing node at t+1, so the midpoint is the constant-velocity prediction. The main linker is the cruder of the two — `pred = P + 0.5 * prev_vel` uses a damped half-velocity.

Correction 2 (corrected 2026-08-26; earlier text carried "the node-count penalty is the binding constraint" over from the submissions, where output grew +1.61% and +10.3%): gap closing is capped at 0.3% of nodes by construction. Across the 12 6bba datasets:

| | |
|---|---|
| cap, `0.003 × nodes` | 476 bridges |
| eligible WITH the candidate requirement | ~238 — the cap never binds |
| eligible WITHOUT it | ~1,570 — binds at 30% of demand |
| nodes `nocand` adds | +238 = +0.15% |
| its node-count penalty | 0.00014 of J — unreadable |

476 bridges add 952 edges, 0.77% of the total, a swing of about ±0.0077 — the magnitude gap2 measured (+0.0018 / −0.0016 / +0.0013), with signs disagreeing across domains.

Correction 3 (corrected 2026-08-26; earlier text called gap2's `nocand1` the upper bound of the line): `nocand1` is the unconditional case — every gap gets a node whether or not there is any reason — and its value is what remains after good and bad bridges cancel. A gated version can be above both: it accepts bridges BASE refuses and refuses bridges `nocand1` accepts. gap2 measured "always" and "only with a candidate"; the space between them was untested, and `biohub-gap3` tests it.

- Conclusion: The bridge mechanism fires rarely, which explains why every sweep of its sub-constants read as noise. The node-count penalty is two orders of magnitude smaller here than in the submission cases; what decides this line is whether the bridges are right.

- Hypothesis: gap3 — a gated bridge in the untested space between "always insert" and "only with a candidate" beats both. thr5 — tightening the detection gate could win on the hidden test even while losing locally, which adj_J alone cannot show.
- Scope: gap3: 8 arms × 3 domains, ~2.7 h. thr5: gates 0.15 / 0.18 / 0.22 / 0.26, `SHORT_MIN` 4, ~4.5 h. Both finished 2026-08-26; results in `2026-08-26 gap3 result` and `2026-08-26 thr5 result`.
- Experiment:

`biohub-gap3` — pure interpolation, gated. Each condition is its own arm:

| arm | candidate? | velocity cosine | fragment length | primary-node clearance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BASE | yes | — | — | — |
| nocand | no | — | — | — |
| vel0.0 / vel0.5 | no | ≥0 / ≥0.5 | — | — |
| len4 / len8 | no | — | ≥4 / ≥8 | — |
| clear4 | no | — | — | 4 µm |
| all | no | ≥0 | ≥4 | 4 µm |

`biohub-thr5` — the gate tightened for the first time, and the metric printed decomposed:

```
adj_J = edge_J × (1 − 0.1 × node_ratio)
```

- Result: The velocity gate passes a stationary endpoint rather than rejecting it — a zero vector has no direction. gap3's BASE anchors on short_sweep's `short_4` row (0.9279 / 0.8553 / 0.8037); gap2's BASE cannot be reused because its gate was divided by `span+1`, doubling `GAP1_GATE_UM` at span 1. Fixed. For thr5, `summarise()` does not aggregate `total_node_ratio`, so `_with_ratio()` adds it as a weighted mean using the same weights `adj_edge_jaccard` uses — purely additive, unit-tested, summarise's own keys untouched. Anchor: gate 0.15 must reproduce thr4's `g0.15_s4` exactly. The reading target is how far `edge_J` falls against how much `node_ratio` improves, not how far adj_J falls.

## 2026-08-26 node-count penalty (superseded)

- Hypothesis: The node-count penalty explains both failed submissions, because local sits under the target node count and so rewards what the leaderboard punishes.
- Scope: 12-dataset holdout. Superseded 2026-08-26 by thr5 (see 2026-08-26 thr5 result); the measurements below stand, the mechanism does not.
- Experiment: Analysis of two submissions plus the holdout node-count table; no new run.
- Result:

Superseded 2026-08-26 by `thr5`: (1) being under target does not make adding nodes free — moving toward the target shrinks the bonus, so adding nodes has always cost locally; (2) the term is linear with slope `−0.1 × dN/N_true`, independent of the current ratio, so local and hidden pay the same rate and the asymmetry this entry is built on does not exist. Both leaderboard results are therefore unexplained by it, and the local deltas below were already net of the node cost. The 0.977 figure is 6bba alone; 44b6 is 0.913 and Zebrahub 0.919.

| submission | change | local, three domains | output | LB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 55772253 | `SHORT_MIN` 6→4 | +0.0025 / +0.0054 / +0.0045 | +1.61% | 0.920 (0.000) |
| 55780773 | + gate 0.15→0.12 | +0.0055 / +0.0045 / +0.0121 | +10.3% | 0.918 (−0.002) |

The second was submitted with a prediction of 0.919, derived from the output growth alone; it landed at 0.918. The three-domain rule is 0 for 2.

`J_adj = max(0, J · (1 − 0.1 · (N_pred − N_true)/N_true))`, and on the 12-dataset holdout 11 of 12 datasets sit under the target node count:

| dataset | true/fr | N_true | N_pred | ratio | penalty factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7b5d3b2c | 58 | 5,780 | 4,990 | 0.863 | 1.0137 |
| 3a1849c2 | 70 | 7,003 | 6,223 | 0.889 | 1.0111 |
| 2312ac41 | 120 | 11,950 | 11,523 | 0.964 | 1.0036 |
| 283bf9f1 | 209 | 20,861 | 20,811 | 0.998 | 1.0002 |
| 3abfe10a | 521 | 52,065 | 53,504 | 1.028 | 0.9972 |
| TOTAL | | 164,698 | 160,857 | 0.977 | 1.0023 |

`corr(true cells/frame, N_pred/N_true) = +0.7498`, n=12, p≈0.005 — the dense dataset is the one over target.

The user set two limits on this: (1) the public split's composition is unknown and need not be adversarial to be skewed — taking the first or last N datasets is enough to give the public set a narrow density band, so LB 0.918 says only that adding nodes loses on that subset; (2) the penalty contaminates every judgement about edges and divisions, because node count and edge quality are multiplied together inside `adj_edge_jaccard`.

They are separable: `METRIC_COLUMNS` carries `edge_jaccard` (raw J), `total_node_ratio` ((N_pred − N_true)/N_true) and `adj_edge_jaccard` as three columns. Every sweep before this entry read only the third; all future sweeps report all three.

Direction opened (since falsified by thr5) — every threshold sweep so far went down (0.15 → 0.12 → 0.10 → 0.08); 0.18, 0.22, 0.26 had never been run:

| | local (ratio 0.977) | hidden (inferred: at/over target) |
|---|---|---|
| loosen | edges better + penalty better → helped twice | edges better − penalty worse → cancels |
| tighten | edges worse − penalty worse → hurt twice | edges worse + penalty better → cancels |

- Conclusion: The measurements here are sound; the asymmetry interpretation is superseded by thr5. The three-column reporting requirement stands.

## 2026-08-26 gap2 result

- Hypothesis: Widening the gap span and dropping the candidate requirement improve tracking, and the gap knob is independent of `SHORT_MIN`.
- Scope: 10 arms × 3 domains. The BASE anchor did not hold and the GAP arms are contaminated by a gate bug; the `SHORT_MIN` deltas are unaffected. Crossed with `SHORT_MIN` at the user's instruction, against the original one-at-a-time design.
- Experiment: `biohub-gap2`, 204 min CPU, 10 arms × 3 domains.
- Result:

Anchor:

| | recorded | gap2's BASE |
|---|---|---|
| adj_J | 0.9254 | 0.9253 |
| div_J | 0.1316 | 0.1282 |

The rewritten `_gap_close` normalised the gate by `step = span + 1`:

```python
D = D / float(step)      # span 1 -> step 2 -> gate 9 um becomes 18
```

At span 1 — the shipped configuration — it divided by 2 and silently doubled `GAP1_GATE_UM`. Fixed to divide by `span`, which is 1 at span 1 and therefore byte-identical to the shipped code.

- The `SHORT_MIN` deltas are unaffected — the same loosened gate sat under both halves and cancelled in the difference, which is why `sm4_base` reproduced `short_sweep`'s +0.0025 / +0.0054 / +0.0045 to four decimals.
- The GAP arms are contaminated, because they compare different spans and therefore different gates (×2, ×3, ×4 instead of ×1, ×2, ×3).

Each half is a delta against its own baseline:

| gap arm | 6bba sm6 | 44b6 sm6 | zh sm6 | | 6bba sm4 | 44b6 sm4 | zh sm4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| nocand1 | +0.0018 | −0.0016 | +0.0013 | → | +0.0010 | −0.0008 | +0.0005 |
| span2 | +0.0002 | −0.0001 | +0.0003 | → | +0.0003 | −0.0001 | +0.0003 |
| span2i | +0.0019 | −0.0016 | +0.0013 | → | +0.0011 | −0.0008 | +0.0005 |
| span3i | +0.0019 | −0.0016 | +0.0013 | → | +0.0011 | −0.0008 | +0.0005 |

Five arms, three domains, fifteen cells — every one shrinks by roughly half. The gap repair and the short filter are substitutes: a wider bridge leaves fewer fragments, so there is less for `SHORT_MIN` to delete. A one-at-a-time sweep would have overstated the gap arms by about 2×.

Every gap arm fails the three-domain rule: 44b6 negative in all of them, 6bba and Zebrahub positive in all of them. Three structural findings:

1. `span2i` and `span3i` are identical in every column. Bridging three frames finds nothing that bridging two does not.
2. `span2` — the honest widening, candidate still required — is +0.0002 to +0.0003. `flicker.py` predicted this: 79.8% of missed frames have no candidate in the repair band, so requiring one at both bridged frames fires on about 0.2 × 0.2 = 4% of dropouts.
3. `nocand1` ≈ `span2i` ≈ `span3i`. All of the movement comes from dropping the candidate requirement at span 1; the span never mattered.

Pure interpolation costs divisions: div_J −0.0032 in 6bba and −0.0025 in Zebrahub.

Not re-running: the fixed gate would loosen every arm equally, and 44b6's dissent is present at both `SHORT_MIN` values and in all five arms. The only thing that survived is `sm4_base`, which is already submitted.

Colab: the acceptance test did not finish again; the session is gone — zero assignments on the server and no keep-alive process, unlike three earlier cases where the VM was provably alive. `hold` does not actually hold: its background task reported "completed" while the keep-alive lingered for a further three hours and then died with it.

- Conclusion: Crossing the gap knob with `SHORT_MIN` was correct — every gap arm's gain halves when `SHORT_MIN` goes 6 → 4, so the two are substitutes. The gap line fails the three-domain rule and the span dimension is inert. The BASE anchor caught a `span+1` gate-normalisation bug.

- Hypothesis: Lowering the detection gate below 0.15 improves adj_J across all three domains.
- Scope: D32 ranker (`edge_ranker_d32.pkl`, pool 32) with the 16 `44b6` datasets inside that pool excluded, per the ranker-leak rule in `working-agreement.md`. Absolute numbers are not comparable to `post_sweep`, `short_sweep` or the submission, all of which ran on D187; only within-run deltas mean anything.
- Experiment: `biohub-thr3`, 179 min CPU. Baseline adj_J 0.9222, 0.0002 from `biohub-div-gate`'s recorded D32 row — anchor holds.
- Result:

Absolute:

| gate | 6bba | 44b6 | zebrahub |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 (shipped) | 0.9222 | 0.8603 | 0.7988 |
| 0.12 | 0.9243 | 0.8598 | 0.8068 |
| 0.10 | 0.9236 | 0.8596 | 0.8074 |
| 0.08 | 0.9236 | 0.8594 | 0.8075 |

Delta vs the shipped 0.15:

| gate | 6bba | 44b6 | zebrahub |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.12 | +0.0021 | −0.0006 | +0.0080 |
| 0.10 | +0.0014 | −0.0008 | +0.0085 |
| 0.08 | +0.0014 | −0.0009 | +0.0087 |

The script's pre-written verdict string says "6bba artefact", which names the wrong dissenting domain. 6bba gains and zebrahub gains, Zebrahub four times more (+0.0080 against +0.0021); Zebrahub has dense ground truth, so its adj_J is over all cells. 44b6 is the lone dissenter at −0.0006 to −0.0009, at or under the resolution floor. This differs from `poolsize` (6bba alone, +0.0073, LB −0.001).

Node/repair-pool columns:

| gate | nodes | repair pool |
|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 548,794 | 111,937 |

Exactly conserved: 0.15 → 0.08 adds 91,084 nodes and removes 91,084 from the repair pool. Lowering the gate moves detections from `_gap_close`'s repair pool into primary nodes rather than creating them.

`_gap_close` repairs a dropout by snapping to a candidate in `[CAND_THR 0.05, gate)`. At gate 0.08 that band holds 19% of what it held at 0.15, so lowering the gate progressively destroys the repair mechanism, and `biohub-gap2`'s arms would behave differently under a lowered gate.

## 2026-08-25 flicker
- Hypothesis: whether cells the detector misses are permanently invisible (a ceiling) or intermittently detected.
- Scope: 379 annotated GT tracks in the 12 `6bba` holdout datasets, followed along the GT's own edges so a track is one real cell's history. 6bba only, annotated cells only.
- Experiment: `flicker.py`. Prompted by the user's observation on the rendered movie of `6bba_3abfe10a`: cells detected in one frame, missing in the next, some flickering back and forth.
- Result:

| | tracks | |
|---|---|---|
| detected in EVERY frame | 270 | 71.2% |
| detected in NO frame | 0 | 0.0% |
| intermittent | 109 | 28.8% |

Dropout runs by length:

| length | runs | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 frame | 102 | 52.0% | the only length `_gap_close` bridges |
| 2 frames | 44 | 22.4% | unrepaired |
| 3 frames | 23 | 11.7% | unrepaired |
| 4+ frames | 27 | 13.8% | unrepaired |

48% of dropouts are beyond the reach of the existing repair.

Link to `SHORT_MIN`: a two-frame dropout splits a track in two; if either piece falls under 6 nodes, the shipped `SHORT_MIN = 6` deleted it. Lowering it to 4 gained adj_J in all three domains today.

`_gap_close` requires the inserted node to land on a real candidate from the repair band `[CAND_THR 0.05, UNET_THRESH 0.15)`. At the 465 missed frames:

| | |
|---|---|
| no candidate within 5 µm at all | 79.8% |
| there is one | 20.2%, median score 0.1226, p75 0.1352 |

(corrected 2026-09-08; earlier text said "four times in five the heatmap response does not dip below threshold, it vanishes".) The 79.8% counts "no CANDIDATE within 5 µm", and a candidate is a `peak_local_max` output; it says nothing about the heatmap value there. `gtpeak` (2026-09-08) read the value directly on the same domains: at F4's missed cells the 3.25 µm window max is p50 0.15 and 98.3% / 99.0% are >= 0.05, while the nearest raw peak is p50 5.84 / 6.91 µm away, on a neighbouring cell. The two measurements agree; the response does not vanish, it stops being a local maximum.

So the existing repair can fire on at most a fifth of dropouts, and a two-frame bridge needing a candidate at both missing frames would fire on roughly 0.2 × 0.2 = 4%. The remaining fifth sits just under 0.15, where `biohub-thr-sweep`'s winning gate of 0.12 lands.

`biohub-gap2`, queued: `_gap_close` rewritten with two parameters, crossed with `SHORT_MIN` at the user's instruction because a wider bridge leaves fewer fragments and moves `SHORT_MIN`'s optimum.
- `GAP_SPAN` ∈ {1, 2, 3} — how many missing frames to bridge; the gate is divided by the span so a longer bridge gets a proportional travel budget.
- `GAP_NEED_CAND` ∈ {True, False} — whether an inserted node may be purely interpolated with no detection evidence. For: the official metric matches nodes by centroid distance at `max_distance` 7.0 µm, so an interpolated node near a real GT cell counts as a match and brings two correct edges. Against: interpolating across a genuinely ended track manufactures false nodes, and the metric carries a node-count penalty.

10 arms × 3 domains, two must-reproduce anchors: `BASE` (span 1, candidate required, `SHORT_MIN` 6) must give `biohub-poolsize`'s D187 row; `sm4_base` must give `biohub-short-sweep`'s short_4 deltas. `post_sweep` swept this function's four constants and all four were noise; the span is the shape of the loop, not a constant, and had never been moved.
- Conclusion: no annotated cell is permanently undetected in this holdout, so the losses are intermittent rather than a detectability ceiling. 48% of dropout runs are longer than the one frame `_gap_close` can bridge, and 79.8% of missed frames have no candidate in the repair band.

## 2026-08-25 depth3
- Hypothesis: recall falls with imaging depth (z), i.e. the front/back difference visible on screen is depth attenuation.
- Scope: 8 z-bins per domain, three domains. Zebrahub's brightness column is `nan` throughout — brightness sampling only runs where a raw volume is mounted, i.e. the two competition arms — so the depth → dim link is tested only where GT is sparse. Zebrahub is the only arm whose GT is dense, so only there is `recall` recall over all cells.
- Experiment: `depth3`, three domains, correlations over 8 bin means.
- Result:

| domain | corr(recall, z) | p |
|---|---|---|
| 6bba | −0.6837 | 0.062 |
| 44b6 | −0.6800 | 0.064 |
| zebrahub | +0.5011 | 0.206 |

At 8 bins the 5% threshold is |r| ≥ 0.707, so none of the three is significant. Two domains fall with depth, Zebrahub rises.

Brightness link:

| | r | p | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6bba: GT brightness ~ z | +0.8048 | 0.016 | significant |
| 6bba: recall ~ GT brightness | −0.7788 | 0.023 | significant |
| 44b6: GT brightness ~ z | −0.0059 | 0.989 | nothing |

In `6bba`, GT-point brightness rises with depth (the opposite of attenuation), and brighter bins have worse recall.

The −0.7788 is a correlation over 8 bin means; the recorded recall 0.52 (dimmest GT-brightness quartile) vs 0.74 (brightest) is per cell. Different populations; a bin-level correlation can invert the individual-level one. Not in contradiction, not the same quantity. A per-cell version of this measurement has not been run.
- Conclusion: the depth hypothesis does not survive — signs disagree across domains and nothing reaches significance. The intermittent misses recorded in `2026-08-25 flicker` are not explained by cells being too deep to see.

- Scope: 7 values × 3 domains — `6bba` (12 holdout), `44b6` (12), Zebrahub (8 crops). Submission comparison is against the D187 pipeline only.
- Experiment: `biohub-short-sweep`, 168 min, CPU. Two must-reproduce anchors, both held; `short_4`'s deltas reproduced `biohub-post-sweep` to four decimals in all three domains (+0.0025 / +0.0054 / +0.0045).

|---|---|---|---|

Submitted: `biohub-submit-ranker` v5. Exactly one non-comment line differs from the deployed version, verified by diffing against the source pulled back from Kaggle (byte-identical to the local copy): `SHORT_MIN = 6` → `4`. The comparison is against ref 55757064, LB 0.920, not 0.921 — the deployed kernel prefers `edge_ranker_d187.pkl` and refuses the older one, so it is the D187 pipeline, which is also what `post_sweep` and `short_sweep` measured on.

The weakest domain's +0.0025 is the same scale as two local gains that failed to appear on the leaderboard (windowing +0.0019 → −0.001; ranker pool +0.0073 → −0.001), both measured on `6bba` alone. This is the first candidate the three-domain rule has produced.

Correction: this submission had been priced at "about 11.8 h of GPU quota" three times. A submission does not cost GPU quota; the 11.8 h is the hidden-test runtime against the competition's 12 h cap — a timeout risk, not a budget charge. Recorded in `kaggle-toolchain.md` section 9.
- Conclusion: `SHORT_MIN` is a smooth curve with its optimum at 4, and the pipeline is deterministic, so `post_sweep`'s table was real. `SHORT_MIN` 6 → 4 was submitted as a single-variable change.

## 2026-08-25 nms4
- Hypothesis: the fraction of GT lost to NMS rises with true cell density.
- Scope: three domains — 6bba (12 sets), 44b6 (12), zebrahub (8). True cells per frame counted per frame on Zebrahub and taken from the organisers' `estimated_number_of_nodes / T` on the competition arms. All three density ranges are ~10x wide, so the `NO RANGE` guard did not fire. `6bba` reachability is against annotated cells (9.71%); the correlation is within one domain so the annotation convention is roughly constant, unchecked.
- Experiment: `biohub-nms4`, 13 min, CPU.
- Result:

| domain | sets | density range | corr(lost to NMS, true density) | corr(reachable BEFORE NMS, true density) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6bba | 12 | 50–521 (10.3x) | −0.0633 | −0.5580 |
| 44b6 | 12 | 74–786 (10.6x) | +0.4856 | +0.0311 |
| zebrahub | 8 | 51–562 (11.1x) | +0.4067 | −0.0266 |

None of the six correlations reaches conventional significance; at n=12 the two-tailed 5% threshold is |r| ≥ 0.576, at n=8 it is 0.707.

| | r | p |
|---|---|---|
| 6bba before~density | −0.5580 | 0.059 |
| 44b6 lost~density | +0.4856 | 0.110 |
| zebrahub lost~density | +0.4067 | 0.317 |
| the other three | ≤ 0.064 | ≥ 0.84 |

`6bba`'s −0.5580 (p=0.059) says that in `6bba`, datasets with more true cells per frame have worse reachability before any suppression happens. The other two domains show nothing there (+0.031, −0.027). Candidate explanation for `6bba` showing no NMS density effect: the crowding damage is already done before suppression, so suppression takes an even share. Carried as unresolved, one point short of significance. The 12-dataset holdout this project measures everything on is entirely `6bba`.

The user pushed three times to have the density line tested where cells are crowded, against closing it on `6bba` alone.

Radius grid refined to (2.5, 3.0, 3.25, 3.5, 3.75, 4.0, 4.5) after nms3 put everything between two adjacent points; the curve is smooth and monotone in all three domains — no plateau, no kink, no optimum. Ceiling gain from the shipped 4.0 down to 3.0:

| domain | 4.0 | 3.0 | gain | extra points kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6bba | 0.9561 | 0.9564 | +0.0003 | +645 |
| 44b6 | 0.9527 | 0.9535 | +0.0008 | +1720 |
| zebrahub | 0.8947 | 0.8972 | +0.0025 | +1246 |

Reachability is monotone in the radius and always votes smaller, so it cannot choose one; only the official score, which pays for extra points through precision and the node-count penalty, can.
- Conclusion: the density hypothesis does not replicate — 2 of 3 domains show it at about +0.45, `6bba` shows −0.06 (p=0.85), so by the three-domain rule it is a property of some domains, not of the method. The ceiling gain from a smaller radius is +0.0003 and +0.0008 in two of three domains, before paying for the extra points, so the NMS radius line closes.

## 2026-08-25 nms3 partial
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: `6bba` and `44b6` only; the dense-GT Zebrahub arm did not run. `reachable()` counts GT nodes with a detection point within 5.0 µm, so its denominator is the labelled cells, not the cells that exist: 6bba keeps 9.71% of its cells, 44b6 keeps 0.77%, a 12x stricter sieve. Within-domain before/after differences are on the same annotated set and are clean; the cross-domain comparison is not available.
- Experiment: `biohub-nms3` v1 ran `6bba`, ran `44b6`, then died entering Zebrahub. The `6bba` anchor held: 0.0092 here against `biohub-nms-loss`'s recorded 0.0091. v2 queued.
- Result:

| domain | cells/frame | annotated | before | after | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6bba | 97 | 9.71% | 0.9652 | 0.9561 | 0.0092 |
| 44b6 | 327 | 0.77% | 0.9581 | 0.9527 | 0.0054 |

The first version of this entry read the two rows against each other as "the denser domain loses less, the opposite of the density hypothesis". Withdrawn; the user caught it within minutes on the grounds that recall and annotation are not the same thing. 0.9581 reads "95.81% of the two-or-three cells per frame that were annotated in 44b6". If annotation favours bright isolated cells — Zebrahub's recall-by-brightness-quartile is 0.52 dimmest vs 0.74 brightest — then `44b6`'s sample is the more purified, and isolated is the property that makes a cell safe from suppression. 0.0054 < 0.0092 is consistent both with 44b6 suppressing more gently and with 44b6 being annotated more selectively; these two rows cannot separate them. "Suppression costs 0.92% of 6bba's annotated cells" stands.

Radius sweep, recorded for later use, not read now: on `44b6`, 4.0 → 2.0 moves reachable-annotated from 0.9527 to 0.9535, flat below 3.0.

The crash:

```
T = max(int(k[1:]) for k in z.files if k.startswith("p")) + 1
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'arent_track_id'
```

`prenms2` writes the peaks as `p0…pN` / `q0…qN` and puts the ground truth in the same file, including `parent_track_id`, which also starts with `"p"`; `startswith` alone matched it. The prefixes `p`/`q` had been chosen to avoid colliding with the detection cache's `c`/`s`. Fixed in v2 by a shared `_frame_keys(files, prefix)` that requires the remainder to be digits, applied to all three frame-key scans and unit-tested against the real key set. Same family as `arm.lower()` on a float and `prev_of` as a dict.
- Conclusion: both sparse arms landed and the 6bba anchor reproduced. Only Zebrahub labels every cell, so only there is the denominator the true cell population; that arm is the experiment and it did not run.

- Experiment: `biohub-post-sweep`, 245 min, CPU. Seven constants, fourteen one-at-a-time changes. Both anchors held: BASE `6bba` reproduced `biohub-poolsize`'s D187 exactly.
- Result:

BASE, the shipped configuration:

| domain | score | adj_J | div_J |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6bba | 0.9386 | 0.9254 | 0.1316 |
| 44b6 | 0.8499 | 0.8499 | 0.0000 |
| zebrahub | 0.8014 | 0.7992 | 0.0221 |

| config | 6bba | 44b6 | zebrahub | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| short_4 (`SHORT_MIN` 6→4) | +0.0025 | +0.0054 | +0.0045 | same sign, positive |
| short_8 (`SHORT_MIN` 6→8) | +0.0007 | +0.0044 | −0.0056 | signs disagree |
| lf_w_0.5 | −0.0015 | −0.0027 | −0.0032 | same sign, negative |
| lf_win_1 | −0.0002 | −0.0007 | −0.0020 | same sign, negative |
| gap_minsc_0.15 | +0.0002 | −0.0003 | −0.0008 | signs disagree |
| lf_w_1.0 | +0.0014 | −0.0019 | +0.0007 | signs disagree |
| lf_win_3 | +0.0010 | −0.0027 | +0.0004 | signs disagree |
| the four `gap_*` gate/snap/cap rows | ±0.0000 | ±0.0006 | ±0.0001 | noise |

`_short_filter` deletes a whole predicted track with fewer than `SHORT_MIN` nodes unless it contains a division; shipped value 6. Lowering to 4 keeps the 4- and 5-node tracks and gains adj_J in every domain. `short_8` helps `44b6` and hurts Zebrahub, so the rule discards it.

Correction to the script's own verdict column: `gap_gate_7` printed "SAME SIGN, POSITIVE" with three deltas of `+0.0000` — all three positive but under `1e-4`, and the test as written had no lower band. `short_sweep.py` adds an explicit `TINY = 5e-4` floor; anything whose weakest domain is under it prints `TOO SMALL TO MATTER`.

Queued next: `biohub-short-sweep` (CPU, 7 configs × 3 domains), `SHORT_MIN` ∈ {1,…,7} where 1 switches the filter off, carrying two must-reproduce anchors, the second being `short_4`'s three deltas to four decimals. Then the leaderboard: `SHORT_MIN` is line 127 of `submit_ranker.py`, the script behind ref 55707206 (LB 0.921), so 6 → 4 is a single-variable submission; ~11.8 h GPU and one submission slot, needing the user's go-ahead because it is outward-facing.
- Conclusion: `short_4` is the only one of fourteen changes that survives the three-domain rule with a delta above the noise floor. The four `gap_*` rows are noise, and `44b6`'s div_J column carries no information.

## 2026-08-25 priority: divisions first
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: user's call; overrides the 2026-08-24 ordering below. Division FP/TP/FN counts are from the 12-dataset 6bba holdout.
- Experiment: —
- Result: the user's argument: divisions were being caught by the orphan fork, but morphology features are edge-correlated, so the orphan fork can no longer serve as the division criterion. The orphan patch is a linker-failure detector, not a division detector: its raw material is the ILP refusing the second daughter and leaving her unlinked, and `_add_safe_divisions` requires a parent with exactly one child (`div_train.py:418`, `if len(ch) != 1: continue`). Changing the linker changes what it catches.

| ranker becomes | what the ILP does | orphan patch | div_J |
|---|---|---|---|
| more fastidious (daughters "look different", edges pushed down) | refuses both daughters, `len(ch)==0` | never fires | falls |
| more correct | takes both daughters, `len(ch)==2` | never fires | rises |

The third regime, named by the user 2026-08-25, is the status quo: the patch fires on things that are not mother and daughter. Measured by `biohub-poolsize` and carried in ref 55757064's description:

| ranker | div TP | div FP | div FN |
|---|---|---|---|
| D32 | 3 | 21 | 9 |
| D187 (submitted) | 5 | 26 | 7 |

26 false divisions bought 5 real ones. A fork lying entirely among unannotated cells enters no FP set (user's observation, verified): 913 extra forks cost −0.0027 adj_J, about 30 visible edge FPs, so ~97% of extra forks are invisible; div_J is not blind to them and div_J is the 0.1 term. Across all 12 `gate_sweep` points (forks 0 to 1847) division FN never drops below 6 while division FP explodes — the missed divisions are not in the candidate set.

Bound on `div_mass`: its fake forks are built from GT (mother + true successor + any GT cell within GATE_UM), an easier population than the patch's actual false positives, which already survived sister distance, mutual-nearest, both-children-continue and divergence. A good AUC there does not say the 26 fall; testing that needs the patch's real survivors.

`poolsize` already ran the second regime: a better ranker moved div_J 0.0909 → 0.1316, so "a more confident linker drains the orphan pool" was too simple — correct and confident are different axes.
- Conclusion: divisions need a criterion that does not depend on the linker failing first. Mass conservation is a candidate — a real division sums to one mother, a mother-plus-passing-neighbour sums to two — and `div_mass.py` → `biohub-div-mass` is that measurement. If it lands, divisions decouple from linking and the 2026-08-24 ordering can resume.

## 2026-08-25 nms_loss
- Hypothesis: a fixed 4.0 µm NMS radius hurts where cells are crowded.
- Scope: 12 `6bba` holdout datasets only, at 97 cells per frame — the least crowded domain available (`44b6` runs 327, Zebrahub's crops span 45 to 809). `biohub-prenms-cache` was built before the three-domain standard and covers only the 12 `6bba` holdout. A null result on the sparsest data does not close a density hypothesis; "the radius is already right" is supported for 6bba and nowhere else. `nms3.py` runs all three. Corrected by the user immediately after the run. The user also identified where the test belongs: Zebrahub is the only domain whose GT is dense, so it is the only place true cell density per crop is known; on competition data `corr(annotation density, true density) = −0.20`, and with crops spanning 18x in density the right measurement is NMS loss correlated against true density across them.
- Experiment: `nms_loss.py` → `biohub-nms-loss` v1, 9 min on CPU, on `biohub-prenms-cache`'s pre-suppression peaks.
- Result:

| | |
|---|---|
| GT reachable BEFORE suppression | 0.9652 |
| GT reachable AFTER suppression | 0.9561 |
| cost of NMS | 0.0091 |

Per dataset the loss runs 0.0% to 3.8%, mostly under 1%.

| rule | recall | detections kept |
|---|---|---|
| fixed 2.0 µm | 0.9564 | 168,240 |
| fixed 3.0 µm | 0.9564 | 168,220 |
| fixed 4.0 µm (shipped) | 0.9561 | 167,575 |
| fixed 5.0 µm | 0.9554 | 166,609 |
| fixed 6.0 µm | 0.9519 | 163,411 |
| adaptive, beta 0.30 | 0.9564 | 168,205 |
| adaptive, beta 0.45 | 0.9561 | 167,657 |
| adaptive, beta 0.80 | 0.9320 | 155,454 |

Halving the radius buys +0.0003 recall for 665 more detections, and the adaptive rule — radius = beta × the frame's median nearest-neighbour distance — does not beat the fixed one anywhere. The adaptive rule was designed to matter where density varies, and 6bba alone barely varies.

Three measurement errors this run exposes:
1. The density correlation is computed against the wrong quantity. The `cells/fr` column reads 5–13, which is annotation density; `reference.md` records `corr(annotation density, true density) = −0.20` and that N_true cannot be inferred from the GT. So `corr(fraction lost to NMS, cells per frame) = +0.0041` says nothing about true density. The conclusion survives by magnitude instead: NMS removes 0.91% of reachable GT in total, so even if all of it landed on the densest datasets it could not produce `corr(adj_J, density) = −0.733`. The recorded explanation — the density penalty sits downstream of edge scoring, in near-ties among many candidates — still stands, and the NMS hypothesis is refuted.
2. `det_floor`'s "13.1% of cells have no peak at any threshold" is a Zebrahub number that was generalised to the competition; the 9.5% "has a peak but is discarded" had been called the largest recoverable loss on the board and NMS was pointed at it. That lead is now measured and empty.
3. The correction in (2) was itself a bad comparison, exposed when the user asked which dataset the NMS recall came from:

| | value | what the percentage means |
|---|---|---|
| Zebrahub | 0.8688 | dense GT: 86.9% of ALL cells have a peak |
| 6bba (competition) | 0.9652 | sparse GT: 96.5% of the 9.71% that are ANNOTATED |

Not the same measurement. The 6bba figure says nothing about the ~90% of cells nobody labelled, and the Zebrahub bench measured recall by GT brightness quartile at 0.52 for the dimmest against 0.74 for the brightest, so if competition annotation skews bright, 96.5% is optimistic by an unknown amount. Honest statement: among annotated cells on 6bba, 96.5% have a peak.

Which dataset each 2026-08-25 experiment ran on:

| experiment | data | GT |
|---|---|---|
| `nms_loss`, `thr_sweep`, `poolsize`, `node_filter`, `div_gate` | 12 `6bba` holdout | sparse |
| `post_sweep` | 12 `6bba` + 12 `44b6` + 8 Zebrahub | mixed |
| `det_floor`, `det_ablate3`, `tta_probe`, `node_bright`, `morph_*`, `div_mass` | Zebrahub crops | dense |

A percentage measured against sparse GT is not comparable to one measured against dense GT, even when both are called "recall".
- Conclusion: NMS costs 0.0091 of reachable annotated GT on 6bba, and neither a smaller fixed radius nor the adaptive rule beats the shipped 4.0 there. Detection on competition data is not where the loss is (96.5% reachable before NMS, 95.6% after); the gap between 95.6% and pipeline performance is downstream, in which candidate the linker picks, where `corr(adj_J, density) = −0.733` already pointed. The density hypothesis is not closed by this run.

- Hypothesis: —

Degradation: `zarr` was not installed, so `read_geff` fell back to its filesystem reader; a `.geff` is a zarr store, so that path matters even though the `geff` library is optional.

    | domain | datasets | GT edges | per dataset |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `6bba` | 12 | 10,313 | 859 |
    | `44b6` | 12 | 2,526 | 210 |

  - Three-domain rule (an effect counts only if its adj_J delta has the same sign in `6bba`, `44b6` and Zebrahub): if each domain independently shows the correct sign for a marginal effect about 65% of the time, all three agreeing happens ~27% of the time.

"Nothing survived the three-domain rule" and "these constants are optimal" are different claims; only the first is measured by that rule.

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: three prior multi-frame attempts recorded in one place; `biohub-accel`'s result had never been written down and survived only in a session scratchpad.
- Experiment: recap of `biohub-accel`, `biohub-hoct-score`, `biohub-div-kinematics`; plus a two-pass design note.
- Result:
  - 1. Acceleration lookahead (Togashi's item 4) -- `biohub-accel`. Five columns on top of the ranker's 18: `acc_len`, `acc_cos`, `md_acc`, `md-md_acc`, `acc_hist`.

    | arm | cols | score | adj_J | div_J | TP/FP/FN |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | BASE | 18 | 0.9386 | 0.9254 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |
    | ACC | 23 | 0.9319 | 0.9235 | 0.0833 | 3/24/9 |
    | delta | | -0.0067 | -0.0019 | -0.0483 | |

    Stage A agreed in advance: edge AUC 0.9867 against 0.9864, permutation importance +0.0000 to +0.0017 across all five.

    Degradation counters: `accel_no_parent` 316,658; `accel_one_step` 246,780; against 225,861 candidate pairs.
  - Two corrections to the original accel diagnosis, found 2026-08-28 (earlier text said the five columns were filled with 0 which the model read as "no acceleration", and that "for most candidates it cannot produce three"):
    1. The zeros are labelled. `accel_of`'s docstring: "return zero and say how many steps there were, so the model can split on the count instead of reading 0 as 'not accelerating'". The fifth column `acc_hist` is 0 = no backward link, 1 = one step, 2 = full, and the ACC arm used all 23 columns, so the indicator was present and the arm still lost by -0.0019. A later session built a proposed NaN fill on the wrong diagnosis; it would have changed nothing.
    2. Denominators do not match: `accel_of` is called once per SEED per FRAME; 225,861 is a count of candidate PAIRS, so 316,658 is not comparable to it.
  - Answered 2026-08-28 by `biohub-accdiag`: acceleration is computable 87.3% of the time. Stage drift is 0.240 of the per-cell residual, and subtracting it changes every column by at most 0.0084 with no consistent sign. `md_acc` flipped AUC 0.9376 against `md`'s 0.9636 -- the acceleration term doubles the predictor's noise variance. Closed on measurement.
  - -0.0019 sits inside the range where the holdout has inverted against the leaderboard twice, so "it hurt" is not supportable either.
  - 2. HOCT, higher-order cell tracking -- `biohub-hoct-score`: `similarity` AUC 0.7012 with images against 0.9091 for plain negative distance on the same 364 edges. Lost by 0.21. Training code is withheld so there is no fine-tuning path. Closed.
  - 3. Division model's forward features -- `biohub-div-kinematics`: `sep_slope` separates a true division from a random pair 1.155 against 0.082, a 14x gap, and is genuinely multi-frame. `biohub-div-gate` wired it into the pipeline and the prune sweep was monotone downhill. Closed as a post-hoc filter; the measurement stands.
  - Untried design: two passes. Every attempt above computes multi-frame features from a greedy backward chain (`pass1_tracks`). The ILP produces a globally optimal capacity-2 solution whose tracks are connected. Solve once, build the multi-frame features from the solved tracks, re-solve; the features are used for a second solve rather than to build the trajectories they come from. Cost: two ILP solves per dataset instead of one, roughly double `biohub-thr-sweep`'s ~10 min per configuration. Pure CPU on cached detections.
- Conclusion: Acceleration is closed negative on measurement: it is computable 87.3% of the time and `md_acc` is a worse version of `md`. HOCT and div-kinematics-as-a-filter are closed. The two-pass variant is untried.

- Hypothesis: whether the peak-finding floor (`DETECT_THRESH` 0.05) is limiting recall, and where the missing recall sits.
- Scope: Zebrahub, 41 crops, every 20th frame, 50,897 GT points. Detection F1 and recall ceiling only, not adj_J.
- Experiment: `det_floor.py` -> `biohub-det-floor` v1, 16 min on a T4.
- Result:
  - Anchor: FULL at floor 0.05, gate 0.15 reads F1 0.7554 against `det_ablate3` v3's 0.7539 (that run used every 10th frame).
  - Recall ceiling = fraction of GT points with any peak within 5 um, before NMS and before any gate.

    | config | floor | peaks | ceiling |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | FULL | 0.05 | 64,584 | 0.8688 |
    | FULL | 0.01 | 68,026 | 0.8690 (+0.0002) |
    | B0 | 0.05 | 61,144 | 0.8610 |
    | B0 | 0.01 | 63,405 | 0.8627 (+0.0017) |
    | B2 | 0.05 | 51,282 | 0.7005 |
    | B2 | 0.01 | 61,604 | 0.7712 (+0.0707) |

    F1 curves are identical for every gate at or above 0.05 and strictly worse below it.

    | | share of GT | recoverable by parameters? |
    |---|---|---|
    | detected today (FULL, gate 0.15) | 0.7738 | -- |
    | has a peak but is discarded | 0.0950 | YES |
    | no peak at any threshold | 0.1312 | NO -- needs a better detector |

  - 9.5 percentage points of recall sit in peaks that exist and are then discarded, by `_physical_nms` (`NMS_UM` 4.0) or by the gate (`UNET_THRESH` 0.15). That is five times the size of what `biohub-thr-sweep` moved by touching the gate. `NMS_UM` has never been swept.
  - Related: `biohub-div-mass` found 44.7% of divisions had both daughters inside one watershed label.
  - `ceiling_hits` counts a GT point as reachable if any peak lies within 5 um, with no 1:1 constraint, so two adjacent cells sharing one peak are both counted. The true 1:1 ceiling is lower than 0.8688; the gap between the two measures how much NMS merges. Not computed.
  - B2 at floor 0.01: the F1-vs-gate curve turns over inside the range -- 0.6712, 0.6744 (gate 0.02), 0.6741, 0.6693 ... B2's true best F1 is 0.6744 against B0's 0.7536 and FULL's 0.7554, still last by about 0.08 (corrected 2026-08-25; `det_ablate3` v2 read B2 at a shared gate 0.15 as "nearly useless" and v3's sweep was censored at the peak-finding floor). B2's recall ceiling rises +0.0707 when the floor drops, consistent with B2's probabilities being systematically lower.
- Conclusion: Lowering the peak-finding floor from 0.05 to 0.01 buys FULL +0.0002; `cache_train.py`'s 0.05 stands and the caches need no rebuild. 13.12% of GT cells have no peak at any threshold; 9.50% have a peak that NMS or the gate discards. B2's ordering as weakest branch survives the corrected gate.

## 2026-08-25 tta probe

- Hypothesis: reverse proof of the claim "the four flip views buy nothing", made from `biohub-det-ablate3` v2's F1 0.7546 (3 passes) against 0.7539 (12 passes).
- Scope: Zebrahub, 41 crops, per-branch per-frame heatmaps; detection F1 and detection sets only, not adj_J.
- Experiment: `tta_probe.py` -> `biohub-tta-probe` v1, 17 min on a T4.
- Result:
  - A. The four views are correlated but not the same volume.

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | Pearson r, view 0 vs views 1-3, per branch per frame (n=1845) | median 0.9781 [p10 0.9402, p90 0.9926] |
    | spread across the 4 views / spread across voxels | median 0.1085 [p10 0.061, p90 0.180] |
    | mean per-voxel abs difference, heatmap(4) vs heatmap(1) | 0.00198 |

    A convolution is translation-equivariant by construction but nothing in the architecture makes it flip-equivariant; flip invariance is learned from augmentation, so it is approximate. `det_ablate3` v3 predicted this before the run: flip-averaging buys about +0.003 F1 for a single branch (B0 +0.0028, B1 +0.0040, B2 +0.0029).
  - B. The F1 difference is inside its own error bar.

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | paired over 41 crops, one view minus four | +0.00109, SE 0.00150 |
    | in units of its own SE | +0.73 |
    | crops where one view wins | 19 of 41 |

  - C. The two configurations find different cells.

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | paired within 2 um | 50,560 |
    | only in the FOUR-view set | 2,786 |
    | only in the ONE-view set | 3,512 |
    | symmetric difference | 6,298 of 56,858 = 11.08% |

    The count gap was 1.3%; the set gap is 11.08%.
  - Retracted: "three forward passes tie twelve, so switch and spend the saved runtime on the lower gate." `biohub-node-filter` measured that detection quality and adj_J do not move together -- removing detections costs edges faster than it removes noise -- and an 11% churn in the node set propagates into linking, the ILP and the division patch.
  - Stands: three passes are not worse than twelve on detection F1, a 4x saving if a pipeline run confirms adj_J holds. Same caution applies to `B0(4)` and `B01(8)`, listed as ties.
  - Untested: whether the disagreement concentrates on low-scoring, near-threshold detections. `set_overlap` counts the symmetric difference but does not record the scores of the 6,298 detections in it.
- Conclusion: One view and four views differ by +0.00109 F1 with SE 0.00150 (0.73 SE), so neither "buys nothing" nor "slightly better" is supported at this sample size. The two configurations disagree on 11.08% of their detections, so they are different detectors with the same summary score.

## 2026-08-25 morph edge

- Hypothesis: whether morphology columns added to the edge ranker improve adj_J.
- Scope: 187 training datasets, 12-dataset `6bba` holdout. Six signed morphology columns derived from this project's own masks; says nothing about orientation/shape, texture, or learned pixel embeddings.
- Experiment: `morph_edge.py` -> `biohub-morph-edge` v2, 106 min on CPU, trained on 187 datasets. Six signed morphology columns appended to the ranker's 18: four child/parent ratios (mean, max, std, MASS) and the two absolute brightness levels.
- Result:
  - BASE reproduced the anchor exactly -- score 0.9386, adj_J 0.9254, div_J 0.1316, TP/FP/FN 5/26/7.

    | arm | cols | score | adj_J | div_J | TP/FP/FN |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | BASE | 18 | 0.9386 | 0.9254 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |
    | MORPH | 24 | 0.9326 | 0.9240 | 0.0857 | 3/23/9 |
    | delta | | -0.0060 | -0.0015 | -0.0459 | |

  - adj_J -0.0015 is below the ~0.003 holdout floor. Stage A agreed in advance: edge AUC 0.9866 against 0.9864, permutation importance for all six columns between +0.0003 and +0.0007.
  - div_J fell 0.0459, which unpacks to TP 5 -> 3: two divisions. Standing warning: five true divisions, every row rests on TP counts of 1-5, far under anything resolvable alone.
  - The orphan-starvation mechanism is ruled out by this run's own Stage A: it requires the model to see the size change, and `MASS_ratio` over 225,861 rows is median 0.994, p10 0.722, p90 1.270, where a daughter should sit near 0.5.
  - The morphology line, end to end:

    | route | measurement | verdict |
    |---|---|---|
    | mass conservation, voxel count | per-fork AUC 0.605 | wrong quantity measured |
    | fringe vs tessellation | 76.8% background-bounded, density slope -0.028 | fringe |
    | mass conservation, brightness | per-fork AUC 0.621, +0.0157 | fringe real, nothing under it |
    | box brightness as a node filter | F10 - S10 adj_J -0.0297 | loses to raising the threshold |
    | morphology in the edge ranker | adj_J -0.0015 | no effect |

    No dataset here annotates cell size, so size is unverifiable rather than merely weak. Brightness has a label and separates real detections from hallucinations at AUC 0.866 on Zebrahub, but does not survive transfer to competition data.
  - 2026-09-02 provenance: the "do not reopen this with a better mask algorithm" sentence was the 2026-08-25 session's own verdict, not the user's instruction. The user, 2026-09-02: a better algorithm can certainly be tried. Tested claim killed: six mask-derived size/brightness ratio columns from this project's own masks add nothing to the edge ranker (AUC 0.9866 vs 0.9864). Untested residue: orientation/shape (inertia tensor, the HOCT/Trackastra feature set), texture, and learned pixel embeddings (the official edge head's U-Net features at node positions -- see the edgeprob line).
- Conclusion: Six mask-derived morphology columns move adj_J by -0.0015, below the holdout floor. The div_J drop is a two-event move this sample cannot resolve, and the orphan-starvation mechanism is ruled out by `MASS_ratio`'s distribution.

## 2026-08-25 node filter

- Hypothesis: whether a learned node filter trained on Zebrahub improves adj_J when used to cut detections.
- Scope: 12-dataset `6bba` holdout, D187 ranker. Percentile cuts within each dataset, so only the ordering had to transfer.
- Experiment: `node_filter.py` -> `biohub-node-filter` v1, 66 min on CPU. Assembled from `poolsize.py` so environment, caches, holdout and ILP are identical to the anchor; the D187 ranker is loaded from `biohub-poolsize`'s pkl rather than retrained, so the linker is submission 55757064's byte for byte.
- Result:
  - BASE reproduced the anchor exactly -- score 0.9386, adj_J 0.9254, div_J 0.1316, TP/FP/FN 5/26/7.

    | arm | cuts | score | adj_J | div_J | TP/FP/FN |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | BASE | nothing | 0.9386 | 0.9254 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |
    | F10 | bottom 10% by node filter | 0.8879 | 0.8736 | 0.1429 | 5/23/7 |
    | S10 | bottom 10% by det score | 0.9168 | 0.9033 | 0.1351 | 5/25/7 |
    | F20 | bottom 20% by node filter | 0.8150 | 0.8029 | 0.1212 | 4/21/8 |
    | S20 | bottom 20% by det score | 0.8878 | 0.8753 | 0.1250 | 4/20/8 |

  - F10 - S10 = -0.0297 adj_J. F20 - S20 = -0.0724. The learned filter led the detection score by +0.1418 AUC offline on Zebrahub.
  - Fifth time an offline gain reversed in the pipeline, after scale-invariant edge features, the division model's four arms, D187's own edge AUC, and div-gate's prune.
  - `morph_cheap`'s rho 0.965 licenses box statistics as a stand-in for mask statistics within a domain; it says nothing about ranking detections across domains.
  - Cutting 10% by the detection score itself costs -0.0221 adj_J; 20% costs -0.0501. The metric counts edges: a real cell carries roughly two and loses both when cut, while a false detection links to little.
  - F10 raised div_J to 0.1429 and cut false divisions 26 -> 23 with TP and FN unchanged. div_J carries a tenth of adj_J's weight, so -0.0518 adj_J buries +0.0113 div_J.
  - Blocked: training the filter on competition data needs a "this detection is spurious" label, which sparse GT cannot give -- an unmatched detection there means unannotated, not false. That absence is why Zebrahub was used.
  - Open question raised, evidence conflicting: `UNET_THRESH` is 0.15 and lowering it would add detections. FOR: this run is a controlled intervention and says removing real cells is what hurts. AGAINST: `corr(edge J, N/N_true) = -0.64` says over-detection tracks worse edge J, but that is a correlation across datasets, confounded by density, not an intervention. A downward threshold sweep has not been run.
- Conclusion: At a matched cut count the learned filter is worse than raising the detection threshold (-0.0297 at 10%, -0.0724 at 20%), despite a +0.1418 offline AUC lead on Zebrahub. Removing detections is expensive under adj_J even by the best existing signal, so any node filter must be far more precise than the detection score to break even.

## 2026-08-25 ruler for mask-based mass

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: masks built from this detector's peaks via watershed, on Zebrahub. Applies to size, shape and brightness features derived from those masks.
- Experiment: no new run; check of the detector's recall/precision against the record, prompted by the user's objection that the detector does not achieve full recall on Zebrahub so its masks cannot be accurate.
- Result:
  - Recall 0.65 / precision 0.64 at the pipeline's det gate (`progress.md`, "the clean ruler's first reading: recall 0.65, not 0.99"). So 35% of cells have no detection at all and 36% of detections are spurious.
  - The watershed's seeds are those peaks: a missed cell leaves its volume unclaimed and a neighbouring basin swallows it, so that neighbour's voxel count and brightness contain a whole extra cell; a spurious peak splits one real cell into two basins.
  - Bias direction matches 1.713: at t there is one seed, at t+1 there are two, and the pair can claim the mother's old territory plus unclaimed ground. The 40% merged-label rate is the same failure -- one peak where there were two cells.
  - `morph_probe` established that our `regionprops` reproduces HOCT's `create_graph` at 0.000e+00; that shows two implementations compute the same quantity, not that the quantity is a cell. Same defect as the diameter anchor earlier the same day (7.08 / 8.83 um, also from watershed-on-heatmap masks). Both instances were caught by the user.
  - A clean subsample does not rescue it: Zebrahub's GT is dense, so keeping only divisions whose local neighbourhood is perfectly detected is roughly 0.65^5 ~ 12% of events, a few hundred. That could answer whether mass is conserved but not the engineering question, because at inference there is no GT to tell a clean neighbourhood from a dirty one.
  - Poor detection was costed at ~1.75% of the score through missed edge endpoints.
- Conclusion: Mass conservation as a division test is closed on masks built from this detector, because the masks are seeded by peaks with recall 0.65 / precision 0.64. Every mask-based morphology feature -- size, shape, brightness -- inherits the same instrument error. Another threshold, weighting or mask floor is downstream of the same seeds.
