## 2026-08-25 mask anatomy

- Hypothesis: the Zebrahub watershed masks are a cell plus a fuzzy fringe, not a tessellation of territory between peaks.
- Scope: `biohub-zh-masks` labels only, 41 Zebrahub crops. Two tests sharing no arithmetic. Says nothing about mass conservation itself.
- Experiment: `mask_anatomy.py` -> `biohub-mask-anatomy` v1, 19 s on CPU, labels only.
- Result:

  Test 1 -- what a mask's boundary faces touch. A fringe ends where the heatmap falls below `MASK_FLOOR`, i.e. at background; a territory boundary is a watershed line halfway to a neighbouring peak, cell on both sides.

  | boundary faces against | count | share |
  |---|---|---|
  | BACKGROUND | 14,911,652 | 76.8% |
  | another mask | 4,508,503 | 23.2% |

  Test 2 -- mask volume against crowding. The 41 crops span 45 to 809 cells per frame, an 18x range.

  | crop | cells/frame | median vol | bg face % |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | ZSNS004_z2y5x5 | 45 | 523 um^3 | 95.7% |
  | ZSNS005_z1y1x5 | 55 | 451 um^3 | 97.5% |
  | ZSNS001_z2y2x7 | 450 | 541 um^3 | 74.3% |
  | ZSNS004_z2y1x3 | 606 | 571 um^3 | 81.4% |
  | ZSNS005_z1y6x3 | 809 | 534 um^3 | 72.1% |

  log(volume) on log(cells per frame): slope -0.028, r -0.127. Territory requires -1. Volume spans 2.4x against density's 18x. The densest crop is still 72% background-bounded.

  Consequence for `div_mass`: mask = core M + fringe H with H = 3.39 M, so ~77% of volume is a shell about 1.3 voxels thick on a 6.62-voxel mask. `div_mass`'s 1.772 does not test mass conservation; mass conservation is still untested.

  Retry planned: `div_intmass.py` -> `biohub-div-intmass`, summing brightness inside the mask instead of counting voxels. A fringe voxel sits at heatmap 0.05-0.1, a core voxel near 0.9, so brightness discounts the fringe with no new threshold; at 6.6 voxels across there is no room to erode. Gated on measuring the discount: the outer shell's share of volume against its share of light, with step 2 suppressed if they are equal.

  The diameter anchor (7.08 / 8.83 um) cannot arbitrate this: those numbers came from watershed-on-heatmap masks and carry the same fringe.
- Conclusion: three quarters of every mask surface is cut by the threshold, not by a neighbour, and mask volume is nearly independent of crowding. The masks are cell plus fringe; the territory reading of `div_mass` is wrong.

## 2026-08-25 div_mass

- Hypothesis: a voxel count on the Zebrahub masks can test whether cell mass is conserved at division, i.e. `(Va+Vb)/Vp` = 1.0.
- Scope: reads only `biohub-zh-masks`; no detector, no images, no competition mount. Zebrahub only.
- Experiment: `div_mass.py` -> `biohub-div-mass` v1, 3 min on CPU.
- Result:

  `(Va+Vb)/Vp` is 1.772 where mass conservation predicts 1.0; a fake fork is 1.984 where it predicts 2.0. Per-fork AUC 0.605.

  | quantity | mass conservation predicts | measured |
  |---|---|---|
  | DIV `(Va+Vb)/Vp` | 1.0 | 1.772 [1.03, 2.93] |
  | DIV `Vchild/Vmother` | 0.5 | 0.878 [0.43, 1.53] |
  | DIV diameter ratio | 0.794 | 0.958 [0.76, 1.15] |
  | CONT `Vnext/Vnow` | 1.0 | 1.000 [0.73, 1.37] |
  | FAKE FORK `(V1+Vq)/V0` | 2.0 | 1.984 [1.31, 3.18] |

  per-FORK AUC (true division vs fake fork) 0.6051; per-EDGE AUC (daughter vs continuation) 0.6247.

  (corrected 2026-08-25; earlier text said the cause was settled -- that the watershed measures territory between peaks rather than cell mass -- and closed the line. The competing reading is that the masks are inflated by a fringe: writing mask = core M + fringe H, a division reads (M+2H)/(M+H), equal to the measured 1.772 at H = 3.39 M, so the cell is 22.8% of the mask, a shell ~1.3 voxels thick on a 6.62-voxel mask, since volume goes as the cube. A fake fork reads 2.0 and a continuation 1.0 under either reading. Both readings fit every number and prescribe opposite next moves: territory means no threshold helps, fringe means strip it. `mask_anatomy.py` -> `biohub-mask-anatomy` decides it; see 2026-08-25 mask anatomy. The measured failure stands, the cause did not. The diameter anchor cannot arbitrate: 7.08 / 8.83 um on the competition data came from watershed-on-heatmap masks too.)

  Gates and anchors:
  - 974,613 of 1,021,008 GT nodes (95.5%) land inside a label.
  - median equivalent diameter 10.76 um [9.00, 13.54]. Anchors: 7.08 um over all competition detections, 8.83 um over GT-matched ones.
  - mining: 7,894 division events, 0 crops empty (15,788 before the daughter-order dedupe). The broken-mining signature -- 68 positives, 26 of 41 crops empty -- did not appear. 945,261 continuations.

  Both control rows hit their predictions: continuations 1.000, fake forks 1.984. One explanation covers every number: the mother is one peak and one basin, the daughters are two peaks and two basins; basins are sized by neighbour spacing, not by the cell.

  Corroborations:
  - CONT diameter ratio 1.000 with p10-p90 [0.900, 1.111].
  - 44.7% of divisions had both daughters inside one label (3,532 of 7,894; a further 678 lost a member to non-detection, leaving 3,684 usable). That fraction is a ceiling on what any size feature could see here.

  Not closed: why. `mask_anatomy.py` asks what a mask's surface touches, using nothing but the label array, and cross-checks with density: across the 41 crops, 44 to 815 cells per frame, territory predicts median mask volume falling as 1/N (log-log slope near -1), fringe predicts near 0.

  Never measured: whether cell mass is conserved at division. An intensity-weighted mass (background-subtracted brightness sum inside the mask, already the 4th column of `morph_edge.py`'s `crop_stats_all`) needs the Zebrahub images mounted alongside the masks, still CPU. The 44.7% ceiling is a detector failure (one peak served two daughters) and neither reading touches it.
- Conclusion: a voxel count on these masks separates true divisions from fake forks at AUC 0.605, which is useless as a feature. The cause was not established by this run.

## 2026-08-25 zh_masks

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: all 41 Zebrahub crops, T=100 each. Watershed on the detector heatmap pooled to an isotropic 1.625 um grid.
- Experiment: `zh_masks.py` -> `biohub-zh-masks` v1, 54 min GPU, 41/41 written, 0 skipped, no degradation warning. One `.npz` per crop carrying `labels` plus GT (`nodes`, `track_id`, `parent_track_id`, `voxel_um`, `t0`), so consumers need this kernel and not the 7.5 GB crops.
- Result: T=100 for every crop. Peaks per crop 4,438 (`ZSNS004_z2y5x5`) to 81,493 (`ZSNS005_z1y6x3`); files 0.5-5.7 MB each.
- Conclusion: `regionprops` on these masks reproduces HOCT's `create_graph` at 0.000e+00 (see 2026-08-25 morph_probe), so one GPU pass buys CPU iteration on size and shape.

## 2026-08-25 morph_confound

- Hypothesis: "morphology separates true from false links" is really "morphology separates real cells from spurious detections", since a false link's far endpoint is usually a spurious detection.
- Scope: Zebrahub dense ground truth, where real-endpoint negatives exist. Negatives split by whether the far endpoint is itself a GT-matched cell. The competition data cannot answer this: its GT is sparse.
- Experiment: `morph_confound.py` -> `biohub-morph-confound`, CPU.
- Result:

  | negative class | n | AUC of \|d intensity\| |
  |---|---|---|
  | N-real (both endpoints real cells, simply not linked) | 2,022,702 | 0.8298 |
  | N-fake (far endpoint spurious) | 88,941 | 0.8640 |

  The detection component is worth 0.034.

  `morph_cheap.py` -> `biohub-morph-cheap`, CPU, Spearman against the verified mask-based `regionprops`:

  | mask feature | best box proxy | rho | usable |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `intensity_mean` | crop mean | 0.965 | yes |
  | `intensity_max` | crop max | 0.968 | yes |
  | `intensity_std` | crop std | 0.946 | yes |
  | `equivalent_diameter_area` | `n_half` | 0.713 | no |
- Conclusion: the morphology edge signal holds at AUC 0.8298 on two million negatives whose both ends are real cells, so it is not detection quality leaking. Intensity features are available from the raw volume without masks; size features are not.

## 2026-08-25 morph_probe

- Hypothesis: cell size and brightness separate GT-matched detections from spurious ones, and separate true edges from false ones.
- Scope: one dataset, 770 nodes, 30 frames, 1 division. Step 2b's edge numbers are unusable (3 negatives).
- Experiment: `morph_probe.py` -> `biohub-morph-probe` v2, 6 min on CPU. Gated: step 2 suppressed unless step 1 proves the extractor reproduces HOCT's node for node.
- Result:

  Step 1: all five columns agree at 0.000e+00 over 770/770 nodes paired by centroid. `skimage.regionprops` on the cached masks is `create_graph`; hoct can be dropped (no 25 MB weights, no offline packaging).

  v1 mismatched: `equivalent_diameter_area` agreed at 0.000e+00 while all four intensity columns differed (worst 9.4e-01). Cause: `create_graph` defaults to `normalize_images=True` and was passed images `_norm` had already normalised, so HOCT normalised twice. Ours read i_mean median 0.6807 against its 0.4948.

  Step 2a: 127 of 770 detections matched GT; 643 unmatched. Medians with [p10, p90]:

  | | matched | unmatched | ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `diam` | 8.83 [7.08, 10.22] | 6.87 [5.35, 8.02] | 1.28 |
  | `i_mean` | 0.856 [0.413, 1.117] | 0.654 [0.305, 0.979] | 1.31 |
  | `i_max` | 1.405 | 1.266 | 1.11 |
  | `i_std` | 0.216 | 0.233 | 0.92 |

  Distributions overlap. `N/N_true` runs to 1.30.

  Step 2b: unusable. 114 candidate pairs, 111 true -- 3 negatives; the printed ratios (0.58 and 0.38) are computed on three samples. Cause: the pairing required both endpoints to be GT-matched, and with sparse GT the only other matched cell within 15 um is nearly always the successor -- the same construction that produced "109 of 109" in the HOCT gates. Fix: draw negatives as "matched parent + any candidate that is not its GT successor", without requiring the candidate to be matched.

  1 division in this dataset's 30 frames, so "does the mother shrink before dividing" cannot be asked here.
- Conclusion: the extractor is verified against HOCT at 0.000e+00. Matched cells are 28% bigger and 31% brighter than unmatched detections. The edge half of the probe produced no usable number.

## 2026-08-25 hoct_score

- Hypothesis: HOCT `general_v0`'s `similarity` score beats distance as an edge feature on this data.
- Scope: one dataset, 30 frames, 364 edges with both endpoints GT-matched, 111 real (30.5% positive). Masks are watershed on a detection heatmap, not real segmentation. `general_v0` was trained on Cell Tracking Challenge plus a bacteria benchmark, not light-sheet embryos; training code is withheld.
- Experiment: `hoct_score.py` -> `biohub-hoct-score` v4, 7 min on CPU. Masks cached in `biohub-hoct-gate` v4 (123 KB npz).
- Result:

  | | AUC |
  |---|---|
  | HOCT `similarity`, blind (v2, no images) | 0.6673 |
  | HOCT `similarity`, with images (v4) | 0.7012 |
  | negative distance, same edges | 0.9091 |

  Images helped 0.034.

  `create_graph` per-node features, CPU, under a second per frame, all live and non-degenerate:

  | column | median | p10 | p90 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `equivalent_diameter_area` | 7.08 | 5.41 | 8.95 |
  | `intensity_mean` | 0.4948 | 0.2347 | 0.7242 |
  | `border_dist` | 0.4812 | 0.0000 | 0.6102 |
  | `orphan_prob` | 0.0775 | 0.0455 | 0.2609 |

  plus `inertia_tensor` and `intensity_min/max/std`. `division_features.py` was written to ask whether these separate a dividing cell and has no recorded result. Reading morphology is a CPU function call over masks already buildable, not a raw-zarr re-read per candidate, so the earlier "needs pixels, too expensive" filing on the division routes was wrong.

  (corrected 2026-08-25: the `create_graph` table is not independent evidence that morphology is measurable here. `create_graph` computes its features from our masks -- watershed on a detection heatmap -- and the 7.08 um came from the same construction `biohub-mask-anatomy` later showed is 76.8% background-bounded. `general_v0` can rely on morphology because Cell Tracking Challenge data has real segmentation ground truth; Zebrahub's GT is points and the competition's is tracks. Bragantini's caveat that results depend on mask quality was in the entry and went unacted on.)

  | `create_graph` column family | depends on the mask boundary | outcome |
  |---|---|---|
  | `equivalent_diameter_area`, `inertia_tensor` | entirely | unverifiable, no size annotation exists |
  | `intensity_mean/min/max/std` | weakly | AUC 0.866 separating hallucinated detections, does not transfer Zebrahub -> competition |
- Conclusion: HOCT `similarity` loses to negative distance by 0.21 AUC and there is no fine-tuning path, so the gate is negative. Its feature extractor is reusable, but every mask-boundary-dependent feature it produces is unvalidatable on this data.

## 2026-08-25 poolsize

- Hypothesis: training the edge ranker on all 187 cached datasets instead of `ranker_fine`'s 32 improves the pipeline.
- Scope: 12 `6bba` holdout datasets. Both arms share the same 18 columns, code, protocol and holdout; rows built once over all 187 and each arm selects by which mount the cache came from, so D32 is `ranker_fine`'s pool exactly.
- Experiment: `poolsize.py` -> `biohub-poolsize`, 39 min on CPU.
- Result:

  | arm | datasets | pairs | edge AUC | score | adj_J | div_J | div TP/FP/FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | D32 | 32 | 39,792 | 0.9884 | 0.9313 | 0.9222 | 0.0909 | 3/21/9 |
  | D187 | 187 | 225,861 | 0.9864 | 0.9386 | 0.9254 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |

  adj_J +0.0032, score +0.0073. Anchors hold: D32's edge AUC 0.9884 is the figure `ranker_fine` recorded, and D32's adj_J 0.9222 sits 0.0002 from div-gate's 0.9220 with the saved pkl.

  (corrected 2026-08-25 by the leaderboard: submission 55757064 scored 0.920 against the D32 baseline's 0.921, with hidden-test output within 0.07%. The +0.0073 is real on the 12 `6bba` holdout datasets and absent on the hidden test.)

  Provenance of the unused data: `ranker_fine` learned on `biohub-edge-ranker`'s 44 caches minus the 12 holdout = 32. `biohub-cache-train` cached the other 155 on 2026-08-23 for the division census and listed the pool going 32 -> 187 as payoff #2; every ranker since loaded the 32-dataset pkl. Requires the submission kernel to train on all 187 or load such a pkl; biohub-cpu-probe2 proved the line runs on CPU.

  D187's edge AUC is lower (0.9864 vs 0.9884) while adj_J is higher -- same inversion as scale-invariant features and as the division model's four arms. Part of the drop is mechanical: a bigger pool means a bigger, harder validation split.

  div_J improved 0.0909 -> 0.1316, divTP 3 -> 5, against the `ranker_fine` header's warning that a more confident 1:1 linker steals second daughters into wrong continuations.

  The run errored at the end on two lines still reading `res["ACC"]`, arm names left over from `accel.py`, after printing every number. Fixed.
- Conclusion: the 187-dataset pool gains +0.0073 score and +0.0032 adj_J on the holdout and nothing on the hidden test. Edge AUC moved opposite to adj_J and is not comparable across configurations.

## 2026-08-24 priority: detection and linking (superseded 2026-08-25 by the entry above)
- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: loss budget decomposed from the det-threshold table; divisions parked.
- Experiment: —
- Result:

| where the score leaks | size |
|---|---|
| detection recall: a GT edge's endpoint was never detected | ~1.75% |
| linking: a reachable edge linked wrong | ~1.6% |
| false edges: predicted where GT has none | ~3.3% |

The last two together are about 3x the first, and adj_J carries 10x div_J's weight. Leads, cheapest first:
- A. Which of the xl detector's 12 forward passes earn their place. `biohub-det-ablate` running. Three branches × four flip views, never ablated. Branches 1 and 2 get pixel-identical input (both top-hat), so their errors should correlate; branch 0 is the only different view and has the worst solo `val_recall`. One inference pass covers 11 configurations.
- B. The ranker never sees `edge_prob`. The transplant dropped yusuketogashi's first-listed feature because `detcache_*.npz` carries only coords and detection scores. Not free: the cached probs index the official detector's nodes, the pipeline runs xl nodes, so it needs the official edge head re-run over the xl node set.
- C. Multi-frame trajectory in linking. The official edge head is `window_size = 2` and structurally cannot use velocity; our ranker has one speed scalar greedily estimated from a single transition. Two public references, neither pursued: Togashi's item 4, acceleration lookahead in motion prediction, never transplanted (`public-solutions-recon.md:313`), pure CPU on existing caches, a component of a 0.915 solution; and HOCT (higher-order cell tracking), forum /726521, posted by Jordão Bragantini as host (co-author, Royer lab, the lab that made this data), paper arxiv 2607.11754, code and pretrained model at `github.com/royerlab/hoct`, training code withheld under peer review so it is inference-only, and he states they have not tried it on the competition dataset. The one recorded attempt is negative: a rank-24 competitor fed it uniform-ball masks and it over-linked into spurious forks (/728551, via `strategy.md`); Bragantini's caveat is that results depend on segmentation mask quality, and this pipeline emits centroids, not masks. Untested idea: watershed the xl detection heatmap seeded at the detected peaks. Submission is offline, so the weights would need packaging as a dataset.
- D. The assignment step, not the scoring. `ranker_scale` measured per-dataset ranker AUC flat against density while adj_J slides hard, so crowding damages the pick, not the score. Untouched.

Why the ordering is structural (user, 2026-08-24): divisions sit downstream of both. Of the 12 holdout GT divisions, 1 parent undetected + 1 daughter undetected + 3 outside `GATE_UM` + 2 below `ILP_FLOOR` = 7 are lost before the division mechanism gets a say, and it already takes all 5 that reach it. The orphan patch feeds on the linker's failures: a second daughter becomes adoptable only if it was detected and the 1:1 assignment left it unclaimed — "1:1 Hungarian steals second daughters into wrong continuations, draining the orphan pool the division patch mines" (`ranker_fine.py` header).

Process notes:
- A static undefined-name pass flagged `gc` as undefined; the push went out anyway and wasted a run. It had earlier caught `class UNet3D` and `_dist_um` missing from an assembled script, both of which would have died at runtime.
- Holdout deltas below ~0.003 are not resolvable on the LB: two submissions whose holdout differed by +0.0014 scored −0.001 apart. The div_w peak at 0.55 was 0.0018 above its neighbours, i.e. under that floor.
- The family-offset rule predicts to about ±0.003, not ±0.001. Two points: −0.0158 and −0.0182.
- `div_train.py` carries `GATE_SWEEP`, `train_at_gate`, `funnel` and two copies of `GATE_XY/GATE_Z` that nothing calls.

State:
- LB best 0.917 (ref 55690436, verbatim xl reproduction). Holdout baseline for the xl family: 0.9318 (adj 0.9185 / div 0.1333); family-specific local-to-LB offset ~−0.015.
- Edge re-ranker line (2026-08-23): v1 failed (sparse-GT labeling gave 97% positives); v2 fixed labels by exclusion negatives (the candidate hitting the GT child is positive, all other in-gate candidates of that source are negative) → 39.8k pairs, 46.8% pos, AUC 0.9884, linker-only adj_J 0.9239 vs Hungarian 0.9185 (+0.0054); v3 full-pipeline composite only 0.9320 vs 0.9318 — the edge gain is eaten by div_J 0.1333 → 0.0800. Diagnosis (user's): 1:1 assignment steals division second-daughters into wrong continuations, draining the orphan pool the division patch mines. v4 (in flight) tests the reconciliation: the ranker's labels already score parent → second-daughter edges high (both GT children were positives), so a capacity-2 ILP fed ranker probs (division surcharge 0.75 / 0.85 / 0.95) can take both daughters natively; plus Hungarian p_min 0.30–0.40. Detection caches for all 44 datasets plus the trained ranker pkl live in the `biohub-edge-ranker` kernel output (iterations cost ~minutes).
- Toolchain: CLI needs `KAGGLE_API_TOKEN` minted per call (kaggle-toolchain.md 1b); pack wheels + `pip -e repo --no-deps` is the proven env for ILP+scoring kernels; ERRORed kernels' outputs are downloadable but not attachable as kernel sources; the official metric needs a GPU machine even to score.
- Uncommitted: two days of docs + scripts (progress/reference/recon restructure, zebrahub_extract rewrite, finetune_detect v3). Commit when the user says so.
- Conclusion: detection and linking were prioritised over divisions on the loss budget and because the division term is downstream of both. Superseded 2026-08-25 by the priority entry above; the loss-budget table is still correct.

## 2026-08-24 div_forks

- Hypothesis: giving the division model SELECTION over the full candidate space, rather than pruning already-selected forks, lets `p_div` improve division recovery.
- Scope: 12-dataset holdout, five true divisions. All three arms start from the same pre-patch graph and the same quotas.
- Experiment: `div_forks.py` -> `biohub-div-forks`, 38 min.
- Result:

  | arm | forks added | score | adj_J | div_J | TP/FP/FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | BASELINE nearest-first | 442 | 0.9363 | 0.9220 | 0.1429 | 5/23/7 |
  | RERANK by `p_div` | 442 | 0.9369 | 0.9222 | 0.1471 | 5/22/7 |
  | GENERATE, filters off | 595 | 0.9342 | 0.9226 | 0.1163 | 5/31/7 |

  BASELINE reproduces div-gate's prune-0% row exactly. RERANK buys one fewer false division, +0.0006, an order of magnitude under the resolution floor. TP is 5 in all three arms. Per fork added the FP rate is identical: 23/442, 22/442, 31/595 = 5.2%, 5.0%, 5.2%.

  The filter stack cuts 14,159 loose proposals to 769 (18x); the quota then takes 442 of 769, a 1.7x selection, and cannot decline to fill the quota. The filters already contain the model's best feature in crude form: `DIV_DIVERGE_UM >= 2.25 um` is one-frame divergence, the hand-set ancestor of `sep_slope` (true 1.155 vs random 0.082 um/frame).

  (corrected 2026-08-24; earlier text said the ranking step had "almost no leverage" and the division line was exhausted. RERANK chooses 442 of 769, so it may exclude 327. Only 23 forks are counted FPs; if those 23 sit inside the 769 and can go without costing a TP, div_J runs 5/35 = 0.143 -> 5/12 = 0.417, worth +0.027. The model removed one of the 23. Discount for replacements drawn from the remaining 327 being FPs themselves -- the true ceiling is lower than +0.027 but not zero.)

  Two untested candidate causes:
  1. Features: the filters already encode one-frame divergence, the crude ancestor of `sep_slope`.
  2. Training data: `biohub-zh-divisions` validated 468,617 Zebrahub divisions; div-train and div-kinematics train on 2001, because only 41 crops were ever extracted (`zebrahub_extract.py`, 7.5 GB) and ~51 of each crop's divisions land on detections. `PER_CROP = 400` is not binding; the crop count is. That is 0.43% of the validated divisions. Extracting more crops is already written; nobody has measured whether the division model's AP scales with it.

  Still established: the funnel's FN 7 (2 detection, 3 gate, 2 floor), and divTP never leaving 5 across every configuration tried.
- Conclusion: all three arms are within noise of each other and no arm found a division another missed. The division model, not the availability of a lever, is what fails.

## 2026-08-24 edge_prob absent from the ranker

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: design note found while answering whether linking already uses multiple frames.
- Experiment: reading `competition-brief.md:179`, `public-solutions-recon.md:300`, `cache_candidates.py`, `cache_train.py`.
- Result:

  Two `window_size`s with opposite meanings:

  | where | what it is | status |
  |---|---|---|
  | `window_size = 2`, the official edge head | how many frames the model sees = two, the minimum; `competition-brief.md:179` says it structurally cannot use velocity | architectural, not a knob |
  | `window_size = 25`, `solve_edges` | ILP time-chunking for speed | reverted; the global solve runs |

  Multi-frame evidence has never entered linking.

  `public-solutions-recon.md:300` describes yusuketogashi's ranker as ~25 engineered features, primary `edge_prob`, raw vs motion-extrapolated distance and their difference. Ours has 18 and `edge_prob` is not among them; its `ps[i]` / `cs[j]` are detection scores from `seeds_of`.

  | cache | keys | read by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `cache_candidates.py` -> `{name}.npz` | coords, src, tgt, prob, dist | the old replay line |
  | `cache_train.py` -> `detcache_*.npz` | `c{t}`, `s{t}` only | ranker_fine, div_train, everything current |

  The current pipeline feeds the ILP a gradient-boosted tree over 18 hand-made geometric numbers and discards the end-to-end-trained edge head (`edge_weight = -EdgeAttr("edge_prob")` where edge_prob is the ranker's output). That replacement moved 0.876 -> 0.921.

  Not free: the cached probs in `{name}.npz` are indexed to the official detector's nodes; the pipeline runs xl detections, which are different nodes. Using `edge_prob` as a ranker feature needs the official edge head re-run over the xl node set -- a GPU inference pass, and the head needs image features at node locations, so it is not a pure cache join.
- Conclusion: the shipped ranker never sees the edge head's opinion of an edge. Adding it requires a GPU inference pass over the xl node set, not a cache join.

## 2026-08-24 div_gate

- Hypothesis: pruning pipeline-selected forks by the division model's `p_div` improves div_J, carrying over div-kinematics' offline AP gain.
- Scope: 12 holdout datasets, 553 selected forks, five true divisions. Every row rests on TP counts of 1-5. Scores only forks the pipeline already chose, not the full candidate set.
- Experiment: `div_gate.py` -> `biohub-div-gate`, 53 min on a T4. Solve each holdout dataset as the recorded pipeline does (div_w 0.55, global), score every fork with the full division model from biohub-div-kinematics, sweep a prune threshold, rescore.
- Result:

  Anchor: prune 0% gives TP/FP/FN 5/23/7, div_J 0.1429, adj_J 0.9220, score 0.9363, against the recorded 5/26/7 / 0.1316 / 0.9214 / 0.9345 at div_w 0.50 -- identical TP and FN, three fewer FP.

  | prune | forks cut | TP | FP | FN | div_J | adj_J | score |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0% | 0 | 5 | 23 | 7 | 0.1429 | 0.9220 | 0.9363 |
  | 25% | 138 | 4 | 22 | 8 | 0.1176 | 0.9222 | 0.9340 |
  | 50% | 276 | 2 | 10 | 10 | 0.0909 | 0.9226 | 0.9317 |
  | 75% | 414 | 1 | 4 | 11 | 0.0625 | 0.9230 | 0.9292 |
  | 90% | 497 | 1 | 3 | 11 | 0.0667 | 0.9229 | 0.9296 |

  Monotone downhill. The bottom 25% of forks by `p_div` holds 20% of the TPs and 4% of the FPs (anti-informative); by the 50% cut it is 60% of TPs against 57% of FPs.

  div-kinematics measured AP 0.0812 and 1.8 FP per TP over every candidate triple `build()` emits, overwhelmingly obvious non-divisions. This kernel scores only the 553 forks that already passed the ILP's division weight or the orphan patch's geometric filters. Second time an offline win did not transfer (first: scale-invariant edge features).

  - Still true: `sep_slope` 1.155 vs 0.082 on the full candidate set.
  - Dead: `p_div` as a post-hoc filter on selected forks.
  - Discouraged, not disproven: re-ranking the orphan patch's proposals by `p_div` instead of `d_pq + 0.15*d_s`; that acts on a larger pool, so it is not strictly the same population.
  - Ceiling unchanged: FN 7 is 2 lost to detection, 3 outside `GATE_UM`, 2 below `ILP_FLOOR`. Perfect FP removal caps div_J at 5/12 = 0.417, worth +0.027.
- Conclusion: pruning by `p_div` is monotonically worse than not pruning; doing nothing wins. The classifier shows zero separation on the population the intervention acts on.

## 2026-08-24 div_kinematics

- Hypothesis: division is a property of a triple over time -- the mother's past and/or the daughters' future add signal over the per-edge features.
- Scope: trained on Zebrahub only (2001 pos), validated on held-out 6bba (83 pos), same protocol as div-train v3. Offline AUC/AP only, not div_J.
- Experiment: `div_kinematics.py` -> `biohub-div-kinematics` v2, ~23 min on a T4. One feature build, four column views.
- Result:

  | arm | cols | AUC | AP | FP per TP @ 10% recall |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | BASE (div_train's 25) | 25 | 0.8275 | 0.0486 | 6.9 |
  | + mother's PAST | 35 | 0.8289 | 0.0375 | 8.8 |
  | + daughters' FUTURE | 35 | 0.8365 | 0.0812 | 2.5 |
  | FULL | 49 | 0.8198 | 0.0747 | 1.8 |

  Backward makes AP worse (0.0486 -> 0.0375); forward nearly doubles AP and cuts FP/TP 2.8x. Positives are 0.25%; AUC moves 0.83 -> 0.84 across every arm while AP doubles, and FULL has the worst AUC and the best FP/TP.

  Physics with no model, medians on 6bba:

  | column | true div | other | ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | fwd `sep_slope` (um/frame) | 1.155 | 0.082 | 14.1 |
  | fwd `sep_end/0` | 1.431 | 1.031 | 1.39 |
  | fwd `score_min` | 0.396 | 0.289 | 1.37 |
  | coup `cent_resid` (um) | 2.872 | 5.053 | 0.57 |
  | back `decel` | 0.905 | 0.934 | 0.97 |
  | back `v_last` | 2.254 | 1.861 | 1.21 |

  - `cent_resid` is the top permutation column (+0.0058, 4x the next).
  - The mitotic slow-down is not present: `decel` 0.905 vs 0.934, and `v_last` runs the other way (dividing mothers slightly faster). Likely mitotic rounding is short against the frame interval and is not sampled. That hypothesis is disproven, not untested.
  - `sep_min/0` ratio 1.05 with negative permutation importance; `surv_both`/`surv_gap` are 5.0/0.0 in both classes at FWD_K=5.
  - `sep_slope` scores +0.0002 permutation importance despite the 14x raw separation, because `sep_end/0` carries the same information inside FULL.

  The metric's marginal budget is ~7 FP per TP; BASE sits at 6.9, FWD at 2.5, FULL at 1.8. Against the forensics funnel (12 GT divisions: 2 lost to detection, 3 outside the gate, 2 below the floor, 5 taken), the 2 below-floor ones are the direct target and the 3 gate ones become reachable if the gate widens and the classifier holds them above the floor.

  `build()` seeds its negative thinning with `np.random.default_rng(hash(name) % 2**31)`. Python randomises `hash()` per process unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is set, so every run keeps a different negative sample: this run got 49586 zebrahub / 46770 competition triples where div-train v3 got 49735 / 46631, and BASE scored 0.8275 here against v3's recorded 0.8083. Arm-to-arm comparisons inside one run are valid (all arms see identical rows); cross-run AUC comparisons in this project carry ~0.02 of sampling noise. Fix with a stable seed (`zlib.crc32(name.encode())`).
- Conclusion: the daughters' forward kinematics add signal (AP 0.0486 -> 0.0812, FP/TP 6.9 -> 2.5) and the mother's backward kinematics do not. AP and FP/TP must be read on this problem, not AUC. div_J is untested.

## 2026-08-24 ranker_scale

- Hypothesis: scale-invariant edge features (distances divided by local spacing) reduce the ranker's density penalty.
- Scope: `ranker_fine`'s own split plus the 12-dataset holdout. One feature build, three column views, so arms differ only in visible columns. The 18 base columns are a transplant of yusuketogashi's public 0.915 ranker (`public-solutions-recon.md`, addendum 2026-08-22b).
- Experiment: `ranker_scale.py` -> `biohub-ranker-scale`, 8.6 min on a T4. Artefacts `edge_ranker_{base,ext,pure}.pkl` in the kernel output; BASE is equivalent to the shipped `edge_ranker.pkl`.
- Result:

  | arm | cols | what |
  |---|---|---|
  | BASE | 18 | the transplant, unchanged |
  | EXT | 28 | + local spacing, `d/sp`, `md/sp`, `gain/sp`, `xy/sp`, `z/sp`, `vel/sp`, and density at an adaptive 2x-spacing radius instead of the hardcoded 7 um |
  | PURE | 17 | scale-free only: no absolute um, no fixed radius, not even the spacing itself |

  Local scale = median distance to the 5 nearest neighbours. Verified before the push: a 6 um lattice gives 6.0, the same lattice at half size gives 3.0, coincident detections do not collapse it to zero.

  | | BASE | EXT | PURE |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | AUC, `ranker_fine`'s own split | 0.9884 | 0.9886 | 0.9875 |
  | corr(per-dataset AUC, density) | +0.053 | +0.021 | -0.083 |
  | sparse-60% -> dense-40% AUC drop (bigger = worse) | 0.0213 | 0.0229 | 0.0258 |
  | holdout linker-only adj_J | 0.9293 | 0.9286 | 0.9269 |
  | corr(adj_J, density) | -0.733 | -0.736 | -0.739 |

  BASE reproduced the recorded 0.9884 exactly. The adj_J spread across arms is 0.0024, below the ~0.003 resolvable floor.

  `corr(adj_J, density) = -0.733` reproduces the recorded -0.68; `corr(AUC, density)` is +0.05. Clearest case `6bba_3abfe10a`, 692 cells/frame, densest holdout dataset by 3x: AUC 0.9773 (mid-pack), adj_J 0.7788 (worst of twelve by 0.15).

  AUC ranks all pairs; adj_J depends on the top-1 choice per cell, and as candidates per cell grow a good ranking still leaves near-ties for 1:1 Hungarian at a fixed `p_min`. `corr(edge J, N/N_true) = -0.64` is on record.

  Two directions that follow: the assignment step rather than the score (candidate count per cell, or a density-dependent `p_min`); and detection under crowding, which adj_J is bounded by.

  Density spans 15x across this train set (46 -> 692 cells/frame) but local spacing spans only 2.1x (10.03 -> 21.23 um), since spacing goes as density^(-1/3) and 15^(1/3) = 2.47.
- Conclusion: no arm differs by more than the resolvable floor; PURE is worst on every line. The density penalty is downstream of edge scoring, not in the feature parametrisation.

## 2026-08-24 windowing reverted

- Hypothesis: the windowed ILP loses points at window seams, and propagating the previous window's refusals across the shared frame fixes it.
- Scope: three LB submissions on the same pipeline, one variable. The visible 4 movies do not reproduce the hidden-test behaviour.
- Experiment: three leaderboard submissions.
- Result:

  | ref | solve | LB | total_bytes (hidden test) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 55707206 | global | 0.921 | 262.6 MB |
  | 55709347 | 25-frame windows | 0.920 | 289.6 MB |
  | 55716291 | windows + seam constraint | 0.920 | 289.3 MB |

  The windowed runs emit 10% more output on the hidden test while emitting 2% less on the visible 4.

  The seam fix propagated the previous window's refusals across the shared frame (the half of ultrack's scheme the first version omitted: sharing a frame stops edge sets colliding but does not stop window k+1 treating a node window k rejected as a fresh track start). It fired -- 25 to 170 candidate edges cut per movie -- and changed nothing: bytes 289.6 -> 289.3, score unchanged.

  Untested alternative: the ILP charges `disappearance_weight` 1.5 at every track end, and under windowing every track appears to end at each seam, so the penalty is paid W times instead of once, biasing the solver toward linking more aggressively, which fits +10% output.

  Windowing existed to buy margin against the 12 h cap; the global solve completed on the hidden test at 0.921.
- Conclusion: the seam hypothesis is disproven -- the constraint fired and moved neither bytes nor score. Windowing costs 0.001 and its purpose no longer applies, so it was reverted.

## 2026-08-24 div-train v1/v2 invalid

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: div-train v1 and v2 runs; every AUC they printed.
- Experiment: review of the Zebrahub division extraction code.
- Result:

  The extraction compared a time against a row index:

  ```python
  if kk not in first or tt < first[kk]:     # tt is a TIME
      first[kk] = r                          # first[kk] is a ROW INDEX
  ```

  so "each track's earliest node" resolved to arbitrary rows and parent-child pairing collapsed. 26 of 41 crops reported no division at all, and Zebrahub yielded 68 positives where hundreds of thousands were expected. Every AUC printed by those runs (0.2255, 0.2161, 0.4332, 0.3417, 0.3145) is meaningless; AUC below 0.5 was the tell.

  Two further design faults:
  - 4,632,084 competition triples for 101 positives, a 0.002% positive rate. v3 keeps every positive and thins negatives to 1%.
  - The split was unusable: training on 44b6 alone gives 18 positives. v3 trains on Zebrahub and validates on 6bba (83 positives), which enters no training set.

  Solid number from the run: 124 of the 151 GT divisions land on detections once all 199 datasets are cached, confirming the earlier projection of ~127.
- Conclusion: div-train v1 and v2 numbers must not be used. The 124/151 detection-coverage figure survives.

## 2026-08-24 division data question, measured end to end

- Hypothesis: widening the candidate set (`GATE_UM`, then Z only) recovers divisions the linker currently cannot reach; and Zebrahub divisions are a usable external source for the competition domain.
- Scope: 12 holdout GT divisions for the funnel; 151 GT divisions across the 199-dataset train split (2 embryos, 44b6 and 6bba); Zebrahub movies ZSNS001, ZSNS001_tail, ZSNS003, ZSNS004, ZSNS005. Geometry comparisons come from GT only (no detector, so no survivorship). Train/test are embryo-disjoint by the rules, so nothing here speaks to unseen embryos.
- Experiment: kernels `biohub-gate-sweep` (round 1), `biohub-gate2` (round 2), `biohub-zgate` (round 3), `biohub-div-census`, `biohub-zh-divisions`, `biohub-zshare`, `biohub-density`.
- Result:

  `GATE_UM` round 1 (`biohub-gate-sweep`): div_w held at 0.55 while the gate widened; divTP 5 -> 2. A wider gate floods training with distant negatives (positives 46.8% -> 21.2% -> 11.4%), dragging the probability scale down: median probability fell 90x, 0.1196 -> 0.0013. div_w and `ILP_FLOOR` are absolute thresholds on that scale, so holding them fixed made them far stricter. The gate is untested by this round, not disproven; the round's number was 0.9301.

  Round 2 (`biohub-gate2`): one training run per gate, div_w swept on the cached probabilities. Best at gate 14 = 0.9357 (floor 0.03, div_w 0.25) against 0.9382 at gate 10. Funnel: gate 14 closes stage 2 (gate 3 -> 0) but those divisions land in stage 3 (floor 2 -> 4) and REACHABLE only moves 5 -> 6. At floor 0.03 divTP reaches 6, one more than gate 10 ever managed, at a cost of +31 division FPs for that one TP against a marginal budget of ~7.

  Round 3 (`biohub-zgate`): Z loosened only, ellipsoid instead of sphere, since missed divisions are z-dominated; volume grows as GZ/GYX = 1.4 instead of (14/10)^3 = 2.74. The isotropic control reproduced 0.9382 exactly. Funnel: gate 3 -> 2 -> 1 as GZ rises, floor 2 -> 3 -> 4, REACHABLE never leaves 5 — widening moves a division from "outside gate" to "below floor". The ranker scores long-z edges low; hengck23 verified independently on the host baseline that long links are almost always wrong. The ranker scores each edge independently while a division is a property of the triple (parent, d1, d2).

  Census (`biohub-div-census`): 151 GT divisions in the whole 199-dataset train split; 87 datasets have any; median 1, max 5. Only 31 sit in the 44 cached datasets, 26 of those fully detected. Caching the rest yields ~127. A forum comment states the training set is 2 embryos split 26 (44b6) + 125 (6bba), matching the census. The same forum thread offers a free CC0 synthetic set with 165,267 divisions; Zebrahub has more.

  Zebrahub divisions (`biohub-zh-divisions`), validated as daughters born on the same frame, both surviving >= 3 frames, non-zero separation — 468,617 validated in total:

  | movie | raw | validated | sisterSep | z share | angle |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | ZSNS001 | 635,041 | 358,314 (56%) | 7.37 | 0.84 | 138 |
  | ZSNS001_tail | 36,878 | 36,246 (98%) | 6.87 | 0.78 | 149 |
  | ZSNS003 | 15,868 | 12,719 (80%) | 6.03 | 0.67 | 148 |
  | ZSNS004 | 30,278 | 24,866 (82%) | 7.78 | 0.65 | 150 |
  | ZSNS005 | 46,026 | 36,472 (79%) | 7.60 | 0.82 | 154 |

  Fragmentation ruled out: across 764k candidates every parent has exactly 2 children (a re-numbered broken track would give 3 and 4 as well). ZSNS001's 2.9% rate is a longer, denser movie.

  Competition geometry from GT alone (`biohub-zshare`), all 151 divisions, split by embryo:

  | | n | sisterSep | z share | angle |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 44b6 | 26 | 8.98 | 0.43 | 135 |
  | 6bba | 125 | 11.47 | 0.55 | 140 |
  | ALL | 151 | 10.57 | 0.53 | 138 |

  Competition sister separation is 10.57 um; Zebrahub at 7.37 is ~30% smaller, not a match (corrected 2026-08-24; earlier text called it a match against "competition 7.24", which was the synthetic dataset author's calibration, not a measurement here).

  `biohub-density` normalised each separation by local cell spacing (median distance to the 5 nearest detections/nodes): sisterSep / local spacing is 0.68-0.85 for the competition and 0.62-0.79 for Zebrahub; the distributions overlap heavily.

  | | count-weighted | equal per unit |
  |---|---|---|
  | competition (0.85 / 0.68) | 0.71 | 0.77 |
  | Zebrahub (0.79/0.72/0.62/0.72/0.69) | 0.77 | 0.71 |

  The gap is 7-8% either way (corrected 2026-08-24; an earlier version claimed agreement "to 2%", 0.72 vs 0.71, by pairing the competition's count-weighted value against Zebrahub's equal-per-movie value, where the Zebrahub side was capped at 4000 divisions per movie so ZSNS001's 358k of the 469k total counted the same as ZSNS003's 13k). The defensible claim is overlap, not equality; 7-8% sits inside the competition's own between-embryo spread (0.68 to 0.85, 20%). The per-movie cap is a legitimate training design — how much of each movie enters training is a free parameter — but a training-design weighting cannot carry a descriptive claim about the domains. Consequence for the build: sweep the mixture (per-movie sampling and the Zebrahub:competition weight ratio, currently 3700:1) and let AUC on the 127 in-domain divisions choose, rather than deriving it analytically.

  Daughters are born roughly 0.7 nearest-neighbour distances apart on both sides; the 30% raw gap is scale, not geometry. Within-dataset correlation of spacing against separation is ~0 (+0.11, +0.04), so this is a between-dataset scaling, not a per-division crowding force.

  An isotropic direction gives median |dz|/||d|| = 0.5 exactly (|cos theta| uniform on [0,1]) (corrected 2026-08-24; an earlier entry said 0.58, which is the RMS). Competition at 0.53 is essentially isotropic; Zebrahub at 0.65-0.84 is z-biased.

  Per-axis normalisation did not reconcile them:

  | | packing sz/sxy | \|dz\|/sz | \|dxy\|/sxy |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 44b6 | 0.55 | 0.32 | 0.61 |
  | 6bba | 0.70 | 0.54 | 0.56 |
  | competition | 0.64 | 0.51 | 0.56 |
  | Zebrahub | 0.52 | 0.75 | 0.33 |

  Packing anisotropy is comparable (0.64 is the isotropic expectation, since E|dz| = r/2 and E||dxy|| = pi*r/4), but the division axis differs and survives normalisation. The competition's own two embryos disagree: 44b6 xy-dominated, 6bba balanced, Zebrahub z-dominated. A feature unstable between the two training embryos has no claim to stability on unseen ones.

  Variance decomposition:

  | quantity | between competition embryos | between Zebrahub embryos | across datasets |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | z share | 0.12 | 0.19 | 0.22 |
  | sister separation | 2.5 um | 1.75 um | ~3 um (scale; normalises away) |
  | daughter angle | 5 deg | 16 deg | ~5 deg |

  Local-to-LB gap: scores are better on sparse data — corr(edge J, density) = -0.68, 0.968 at 50 cells/frame vs 0.771 at 519. Against the same hidden test the two families show offsets -0.042 and -0.015, so most of the larger gap is holdout memorisation by the official weights rather than density. The xl family's -0.015 is the part density explains, and it predicted 0.921 correctly.
- Conclusion: with div_w and `ILP_FLOOR` held on a shifting probability scale, round 1 tested nothing; rounds 2 and 3 are fair and the wider gate still loses to gate 10 (0.9357 / 0.9382). Divisions moved out of the gate bucket land under the floor, so the binding constraint is the per-edge scoring of a triple-valued event, not the gate. Zebrahub reads as one more embryo domain rather than a different problem, with a 7-8% normalised-separation gap and a genuine z-bias difference.

## 2026-08-23 ranker-wincal: ILP windowing and probability calibration

- Hypothesis: W line — windowing the ILP in time is cheaper without costing score. C line — the ranker's labels (both GT children positive) inflate second-daughter probabilities, and div_w 0.55 is paying for that bias.
- Scope: holdout; uncalibrated probabilities at div_w 0.55 for the W line; isotonic fitted on the held-out 10% for the C line. The `wglobal` control is not interchangeable with the fine sweep's number (see caveat).
- Experiment: kernel `biohub-ranker-wincal`, two independent lines.
- Result:

  W line — window the ILP in time (uncalibrated, div_w 0.55):

  | window | score | adj_J | div_J | ILP forks | link | speedup |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | global | 0.9368 | 0.9233 | 0.1351 | 111 | 326 s | 1.00x |
  | 50 | 0.9368 | 0.9230 | 0.1389 | 111 | 213 s | 1.53x |
  | 25 | 0.9382 | 0.9235 | 0.1471 | 108 | 157 s | 2.08x |
  | 10 | 0.9343 | 0.9214 | 0.1290 | 88 | 126 s | 2.59x |

  Window 25 is both faster and better: +0.0014 over the global solve at 2.08x. W=10 loses context. The gain shows in div_J (0.1351 -> 0.1471, division FP 25 -> 22); with `disappearance_weight` 1.5 the global solve is pushed to build very long tracks and a window bounds how far that pressure travels.

  Scheme: window k covers frames [a, b] and k+1 covers [b, c] — they share one frame but never share an edge, since k owns a->a+1 .. (b-1)->b and k+1 owns b->b+1 .. Merged edge sets cannot conflict, so no reconciliation pass is needed. Same as ultrack's `window_size` / `overlap_size` (their default overlap is 1). Mapping solved nodes back to global indices must be done by coordinate, never by `node_id` — node_id is not a stable handle across the solve (progress.md 02f7c8b).

  Control caveat: `wglobal` reads 0.9368 where the fine sweep's div_w 0.55 read 0.9363. `run_config` assembles nodes from all seeds and lets `_short_filter`/`_emit` prune, where the B line built them from the ILP's kept nodes. The window comparison is paired inside this kernel; do not mix these two numbers across kernels.

  C line — isotonic calibration:

  ```
  raw mean 0.4191 -> cal 0.4168;  frac>0.55  0.4214 -> 0.4118
  ```

  Isotonic moved the mean by 0.0023. The calibrated sweep is monotone increasing in div_w and never beats uncalibrated: 0.9258 / 0.9286 / 0.9311 / 0.9343 at div_w 0.05 / 0.15 / 0.30 / 0.55, against 0.9368 uncalibrated at 0.55. Isotonic flattens probabilities into steps, creating ties the ILP then breaks arbitrarily. The ultrack contrast (their `division_weight` default is -0.001) needs a different explanation, most likely that their candidates are segmentation-hypothesis based and mutually exclusive by construction.

  Structural finding: across all twelve sweep points — 8 uncalibrated, 4 calibrated, forks ranging 0 to 1847 — division FN never drops below 6; divTP moves only between 4 and 6 while division FP explodes. The missed divisions are not in the candidate set, so the solver is not refusing them, and the marginal "7 FPs per TP is a bargain" argument (arithmetically correct) has nothing to buy. Anything that moves div_J must act upstream: `GATE_UM`, the detection threshold (`UNET_THRESH` 0.15, a just-divided second daughter being small and dim), or a purpose-built division detector. `biohub-div-forensics` walks every GT division down the funnel.

  Metric note (`reference.md#the-metric`): a fork lying entirely among unannotated cells enters no FP set. From the div_w 0.55 -> 0.20 step, 913 extra forks cost only -0.0027 adj_J, which at ~10.7k holdout edges is roughly 30 visible edge FPs, i.e. about 97% of the extra forks are invisible to the metric. The same step cost -0.0056 on div_J, twice the edge damage. adj_J is a weighted per-dataset average with a node-count penalty, so treat the 30 as an order of magnitude.
- Conclusion: window 25 is adopted — faster and better. Probability calibration is closed: the probabilities were already calibrated and isotonic never beats uncalibrated. Forks are nearly free on edges and not free on divisions.

## 2026-08-23 submission kernel runs; ILP does not fit the 12 h cap

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: visible 4, paired against the 0.917 pipeline; runtime projection to a ~199-200 volume hidden test under a 12 h cap.

- Result:

  | dataset | xl0917 nodes/edges | ranker nodes/edges | ILP forks | runtime xl -> ranker |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 44b6_0113de3b | 23878 / 23152 | 23794 / 23048 | 5 | 82 s -> 120 s |
  | 44b6_0b24845f | 28147 / 26186 | 27599 / 25862 | 20 | 87 s -> 145 s |
  | 6bba_05b6850b | 6135 / 5906 | 6090 / 5894 | 7 | 74 s -> 90 s |
  | 6bba_05db0fb1 | 68259 / 65947 | 66813 / 64421 | 8 | 102 s -> 485 s |

  Nodes -1.7%, edges -1.6%, the drop the ILP's node-dropping predicts. Forks per dataset match the holdout's 111/12.

  Hidden test is ~199-200 volumes (`competition-brief.md:189`), cap 12 h. Measured 210 s/dataset average -> 200 x 210 s = 11.7 h + 10.6 min setup. The 0.917 pipeline runs 86 s/dataset (~5 h), so the excess is entirely the linker.

  Linking cost is superlinear in candidate pairs, ~n^1.5:

  | pairs | features + ILP |
  |---|---|
  | 8.7k | ~16 s |
  | 55.6k | ~38 s |
  | 73.6k | ~58 s |
  | 272.6k | ~383 s |

  3.7x the pairs costs 6.6x the time. `6bba_05db0fb1` is not the worst case in the train set; the densest 6bba movie runs 519 cells/frame.

  Fixes in intended order: (1) window the ILP in time — one global solve costs ~n^1.5, W windows overlapping by a frame cost n^1.5 / sqrt(W), ~3.2x faster at W=10, needs a holdout re-validation (~30 min); (2) raise `ILP_FLOOR` from 0.10 — at AUC 0.9884 true edges score high so 0.25-0.30 should cost nothing and cuts solver edges, but does not cut feature cost since features are built for every in-gate pair and only then filtered by probability; (3) a wall-clock guard — track elapsed time and remaining datasets and fall the rest back to the Hungarian linker already in the file when the projection exceeds the cap, printing how many datasets fell back and from which one.

  The user chose to submit anyway rather than fix first: a timeout does not burn a submission slot, slots are not the scarce resource, and 11.8 h against a 12 h cap may pass. The optimisation work stays queued.
- Conclusion: the offline submission kernel works end to end. Projected runtime is 11.7 h against a 12 h cap, with the excess entirely in the linker and superlinear in candidate pairs.

## 2026-08-23 ranker-fine div_w sweep

- Hypothesis: the div_w curve has an interior optimum in the 0.20-0.75 gap the diag left unmeasured.
- Scope: holdout, 12 GT divisions; xl baseline is adj 0.9185 / div 0.1333.
- Experiment: kernel `biohub-ranker-fine`; eight points total.
- Result:

  | div_w | ILP forks | score | adj_J | div_J | div TP/FP/FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0.20 | 1024 | 0.9280 | 0.9193 | 0.0870 | 6/57/6 |
  | 0.35 | 394 | 0.9309 | 0.9211 | 0.0980 | 5/39/7 |
  | 0.45 | 190 | 0.9344 | 0.9216 | 0.1282 | 5/27/7 |
  | 0.50 | 148 | 0.9345 | 0.9214 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |
  | 0.55 | 111 | 0.9363 | 0.9220 | 0.1429 | 5/23/7 |
  | 0.65 | 49 | 0.9351 | 0.9222 | 0.1290 | 4/19/8 |
  | 0.75 | 12 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |
  | 1.50 | 0 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |

  One unimodal curve, argmax 0.55. At 0.55 both terms beat the xl baseline: adj_J +0.0035 and div_J +0.0096. The peak sits 0.0018 above its neighbours on small counts — div_J moves on FP 27/23/19 and TP 5/5/4 against 12 GT divisions. The computation is deterministic (identical AUC 0.9884 in all three training runs), so this is not run-to-run noise, but 0.45-0.65 are all defensible and 0.55 is simply the best measured. Predicted LB at the -0.015 family offset: ~0.921 vs the standing 0.917.

  Submission kernel built: `biohub-submit-ranker` (`submit_ranker.py`). Detection side is xl-repro verbatim; linker is ranker probs -> capacity-2 ILP at div_w 0.55; post-link patches are ranker-diag's, because those are the code path that measured 0.9363 (xl's gap-close sorts proposals by distance and takes the closest under the cap, ranker's takes them in Hungarian order). Verified before pushing:

  - Detector parity: the ranker trained on `biohub-edge-ranker`'s caches, which mount xiaoleilian's two weight datasets — the same pair xl-repro uses — with identical branches, flip views and POOL/CAND_THR/UNET_THRESH/NMS_UM/SCALE, so the ranker learned on the xl detector's own coordinates.
  - Offline: internet is off at submission; tracksdata/pyscipopt come from the support-pack wheels and `predict_unet_transformer` from the pack's repo copy. No clone anywhere.
  - An AST pass for undefined names caught two graft bugs that compile fine and die at runtime: `class UNet3D` and `_dist_um` were missing, because the block extractor took `def` and not `class`.
  - `submission.csv` is written before scoring, and scoring is wrapped whole. On the hidden rescore the train-GT lookup misses, and scoring says so and skips.
- Conclusion: div_w 0.55 scores 0.9363 and beats the xl baseline on both terms simultaneously. The argmax is not sharply resolved across 0.45-0.65.

## 2026-08-23 ranker-diag div_w sweep

- Hypothesis: v4's B line saw identical rows because `division_weight` had no effect; counting out-degree-2 nodes in the solved graph before any patch will show whether the knob is live.
- Scope: holdout; div_w widened to 0.20-1.50; fork counts taken in the solved graph before post-link patches.
- Experiment: kernel `biohub-ranker-diag`. Scripts in the repo: `ranker_v4.py`, `ranker_diag.py`, `ranker_fine.py`. The diag/fine pair skips the A line via `P_MIN_SWEEP = ()` (measured twice, identical).
- Result:

  | div_w | ILP forks | final forks | patch added | score | adj_J | div_J | div TP/FP/FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0.20 | 1024 | 1423 | 399 | 0.9280 | 0.9193 | 0.0870 | 6/57/6 |
  | 0.50 | 148 | 590 | 442 | 0.9345 | 0.9214 | 0.1316 | 5/26/7 |
  | 0.75 | 12 | 461 | 449 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |
  | 1.50 | 0 | 451 | 451 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |

  Fork count runs 1024 -> 148 -> 12 -> 0, monotone across the range: `division_weight` was always wired correctly. v4's 0.75-0.95 window sat entirely in the dead zone (12 forks at 0.75, zero above), so its three identical rows were one solved graph three times.

  At div_w 0.50 the ILP natively takes 148 forks, div_J returns to near-baseline (0.1316 vs 0.1333) and finds one more true division than baseline (5 TP vs 4), while adj_J holds at 0.9214 (+0.0029 over baseline).

  Decomposition of the +0.0027 over baseline: +0.0013 is the ranker's edges alone (at div_w 1.50 the ILP forks zero times, divisions come purely from `_add_safe_divisions`, and the pipeline still scores 0.9331 vs baseline 0.9318); +0.0014 more is native forking, 0.9331 -> 0.9345 at div_w 0.50.

  div_w 0.20 over-forks: most TPs (6) but division FP 57 and adj_J falls to 0.9193. The curve is peaked between 0.20 and 0.75 with only those two brackets measured, hence `biohub-ranker-fine` at 0.35/0.45/0.55/0.65 before a submission slot is spent.
- Conclusion: `division_weight` is live and monotone; v4's byte-identical rows came from a badly placed window, not a broken knob. Native capacity-2 forking at div_w 0.50 recovers divisions to near-baseline while keeping the ranker's edge gain.

## 2026-08-23 ranker v4

- Hypothesis: A line — a probability threshold p_min on ranker edges improves the composite. B line — a capacity-2 ILP takes both daughters natively, so the ranker's edge gain is not cancelled by division loss.
- Scope: holdout; xl baseline is 0.9318 / adj 0.9185 / div 0.1333, div TP/FP/FN 4/18/8.
- Experiment: two runs. The first errored at 8.5 min: `P` was bound to the pipeline module at import, then clobbered inside the module-level `p_min` loop by `pairs, rows, P, C = feats[t]`, so the B line's `P.build_graph` hit a numpy array; the import is now `as PIPE`. Also hardened: the B line mapped ILP endpoints with `remap[int(a)]`, which KeyErrors on the `edge_endpoint_missing` case `link_replay` has warned about since 2026-08-20 — now dropped loudly as a lower bound. The script is now `ranker_v4.py` in the repo (it previously existed only in a dead session's scratchpad and on Kaggle).
- Result:

  | config | score | adj_J | div_J | div TP/FP/FN |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | xl baseline | 0.9318 | 0.9185 | 0.1333 | 4/18/8 |
  | A line, p_min 0.30 | 0.9305 | 0.9222 | 0.0833 | -- |
  | A line, p_min 0.35 | 0.9284 | 0.9200 | 0.0833 | -- |
  | A line, p_min 0.40 | 0.9278 | 0.9195 | 0.0833 | -- |
  | B line, div_w 0.75 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |
  | B line, div_w 0.85 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |
  | B line, div_w 0.95 | 0.9331 | 0.9224 | 0.1071 | 3/16/9 |

  Composite is exactly `adj_J + 0.1 * div_J` (verified on all seven rows). A line: +0.0037 adj_J against -0.050 div_J = -0.0050, net -0.0013; div_J is 0.0833 at every p_min.

  The three B-line surcharges spanning 0.75-0.95 returned identical score, adj_J, div_J and TP/FP/FN, i.e. one solved graph, so `division_weight` had no effect over that window. With `edge_weight = -1.0 * edge_prob`, a fork is taken iff the second daughter's prob exceeds div_w, so either every accepted fork scored > 0.95 or no fork was accepted and all 3 TPs come from the post-hoc `_add_safe_divisions` patch; B is below baseline on divisions (0.1071 vs 0.1333, 3 TP vs 4), which supports the latter. Predicted LB at the -0.015 family offset: ~0.918 vs the standing 0.917, inside the noise.

  Next: `biohub-ranker-diag` counts forks in the solved graph before any patch, over a div_w sweep widened to 0.2-1.5 (a submission slot is the scarce resource, GPU quota is not).
- Conclusion: the daughter-stealing mechanism is confirmed for the A line, which loses more on div_J than it gains on adj_J. The B line's +0.0013 over baseline means the edge gain is no longer fully cancelled, not that capacity-2 takes both daughters natively; the identical rows leave that unsettled.

## 2026-08-22 from-scratch retraining verdict

- Hypothesis: from-scratch retraining can reach the public weights' quality.
- Scope: session 1 only — 4 full epochs, clean split, official recipe, eval score = acc x recall on the 12-holdout. Target is the public weights' 0.9835 at epoch 402.
- Experiment: resumable trainer harness, 10.3 h, per-epoch full checkpoints, zero incidents. Session-1 checkpoint ferried to dataset `faustine649/biohub-train-ckpt`.
- Result: eval score 0.8980 / 0.9000 / 0.9157 / 0.9121 across four epochs — one epoch buys 0.90, then the curve crawls (+0.016 over three epochs, last epoch negative). Real epoch cost 2.53 h, not the 2.1 h the smoke extrapolation gave; 50 epochs = 127 h. Warm-start surgery stays rejected (0.764 as evidence). Unscheduled appeal path: a 3-epoch LR-schedule probe (3e-4 + cosine), since constant lr 1e-4 may explain some of the crawl.
- Conclusion: the 400-epoch tail is real and parity from scratch is unaffordable. Main line becomes B+C: the learned edge re-ranker plus luxury inference (TTA, ensemble, sub-voxel refinement) plus adopting/ensembling the public xiaoleilian detector. The session-1 checkpoint (clean split, eval 0.9157) is kept as an ensemble-diversity candidate.

## 2026-08-21 sigmoid edge activation; sister separation

- Hypothesis: (a) sigmoid edge activation frees the candidates starved by softmax's per-target normalisation and raises the score; (b) NMS merges newborn daughters, causing missed divisions.
- Scope: holdout-measured (`6bba`), so the negative carries the holdout trust discount; sister curve uses all 151 GT divisions.
- Experiment: `biohub-cache-sigmoid` (edge_activation=sigmoid at dump threshold 0.05, then a 7x3 replay grid); `biohub-sister-curve`.
- Result:
  - With sigmoid, candidates above 0.5 exceed the target count (impossible under softmax) — the mass-splitting starvation is real and softmax-specific.
  - Grid best 0.9314 at threshold 0.70 / disapp 3.5 vs softmax 0.9387 at 0.40 / 3.5; edge_J lower everywhere (0.9316 max vs 0.9363). At threshold 0.9 the sigmoid graph collapses (adj_J 0.05 — probabilities rarely reach 0.9).
  - Salvaged idea from the sigmoid post-mortem (user's): the official softmax normalises per target (candidate parents compete), so a division does not produce a 0.5/0.5 signature — each daughter's column gives the shared parent ~1.0. The transposed statistic can be built from the cache: renormalise each source's outgoing candidate probs; a parent whose top-2 outgoing shares are balanced and whose edge lengths sit in the division band (3.5-11 um) is a synthetic fork signature. CPU only, cache only — a third feature for the orphan-fork scorer (existing: edge length AUC 0.86, parent brightness AUC 0.71).
  - Sister-separation curve, all 151 GT divisions: at k=0 (daughters' first frame) separation p10/p50/p90 = 6.4 / 10.6 / 14.4 um; only 0.7% closer than the 3 um NMS kernel.
  - Kernel-engineering facts (cost ~30 wasted GPU-min): (1) the pack renames `tracking_cellmot` -> `biohub_tracking` and its `evaluate.py` is a different version without `evaluate_pairs`, so `division_recovery.sweep`'s import of it had never executed — score against the official metrics API directly; (2) an ERRORed kernel's output files are downloadable but cannot be attached as a kernel_source; (3) loading all 41 crops decompressed needs ~33 GB RAM (OOM-killed finetune v2) — use /kaggle/tmp memmaps.
- Conclusion: sigmoid activation does not improve the score; the freed candidates are largely the spurious pool the stranded audit predicted and the ILP buys FPs with them. The NMS-merge division hypothesis is refuted: daughters are annotated ~10.6 um apart from birth, so division losses come from detection/linking of the second daughter.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 148,656 | 99,760 | 57,304 | 0.722 | 0.598 |
| 0.9 | 143,621 | 89,911 | 62,339 | 0.697 | 0.615 |
| 0.99 (pipeline) | 133,787 | 76,243 | 72,173 | 0.650 | 0.637 |

  Recall@0.99 by GT-point brightness quartile: Q1 (dimmest) 0.52 (partly Zebrahub label noise); Q4 (brightest) 0.74. Per-crop spread 0.32-0.92; ZSNS004 (a dim movie) is worst, dense ZSNS003/005 crops are fine.

  Three causes stack and this run cannot separate them: (1) the holdout number is inflated (memorization + duplicate frames); (2) genuine domain shift — Zebrahub is a different instrument setup; (3) method deltas (no TTA, approximate NMS), worth a few points at most.

  Correction (user's, accepted): "the hidden test is on the competition instrument" and "same format" were asserted without evidence (corrected 2026-08-21; earlier text asserted both). Nobody has seen the hidden data; the visible test/ files are train copies. "The pipeline read it fine" does not establish similarity — Zebrahub, a different instrument, goes through the same pipeline after resampling. Format compatibility and runtime pin only format family and data volume.

  The load-bearing fact about hidden-test similarity: train-tuned pipelines reach 0.93+ on it — LB #1 0.957 / #20 0.935, read via API 2026-08-20, post-rescore; our own bare config 0.876. (Corrected 2026-08-21; an earlier draft said "the whole field scores 0.9+" — most of the 2560 teams score below 0.9.) The public LB is 29% of the test, so the bound carries that caveat.

  Photometrics differ per batch: the competition's own two batches differ 8x in brightness. Within-instrument photometric brittleness: ZSNS004 (dim) is the worst movie on this bench (crops down to 0.32 recall). User's addition: brightness is only the observed axis — sharpness/PSF width, noise character, scattering with depth and unexamined axes can also differ per batch and are unmeasured. Proposed cheap probe: per-dataset sharpness proxy (Laplacian energy / gradient p95 on a mid frame) across 44b6 / 6bba / Zebrahub.

  Consequences for the fine-tune: (1) augmentation must cover more than gain — random gain/offset/gamma/noise and Gaussian blur of varying width; (2) mix competition sparse-GT frames with Zebrahub dense crops.
- Conclusion: the public detector's recall at the pipeline gate is 0.650 on contamination-free dense GT, with 0.74 even on the brightest quartile. The ruler has ~0.35 of visible headroom, so a real fine-tune effect will be measurable on it. "Detection is solved" does not hold as a general claim; the holdout's node_recall 0.9974 is not compatible with this reading. LB submission remains the only direct read on the hidden domain.

Corollary: if 0.982 detect_ceiling is memorization, hidden-test detection is worse than recorded and detector training is worth more, not less.

## 2026-08-21 competition brightness survey

- Hypothesis: is per-dataset normalisation discarding a real feature, and is the competition's own brightness uniform?
- Scope: 199 competition train datasets; frame-vs-movie caveat noted in `reference.md#train-set-survey-199-datasets`.
- Experiment: `faustine649/competition-brightness-survey`.
- Result: q0.999 spans 8.8x across the 199 train datasets — the same regime as Zebrahub's 10x. The organizers store per-dataset quantiles in the zarr attrs and the official `io.py` normalises with them. Absolute brightness is instrument + expression + bleaching, not biology; a linear per-dataset rescale preserves within-image contrast and ordering. `cell_count.py` had already excluded absolute-intensity features, kept only as a LOGO control.
- Conclusion: per-dataset normalisation is the designed-in policy of the official code, not a local choice, and the competition's brightness is not uniform.

## 2026-08-21 det-threshold sweep

- Hypothesis: det_threshold is a lever on the score.
- Scope: cached replay at the converged linking optimum (edge threshold 0.40, disappearance 3.5), so only `det_threshold` varies; holdout-measured, so this null result is void under the trust tiers.
- Experiment: cache replay.
- Result:

| det | adj_J | edge_J | detect_ceiling | link_rate | nodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.9387 | 0.9363 | 0.9825 | 0.9839 | 161,649 |
| 0.98 | 0.9375 | 0.9362 | 0.9827 | 0.9836 | 164,185 |
| 0.95 | 0.9367 | 0.9365 | 0.9821 | 0.9842 | 166,209 |

  `detect_ceiling` does not move and neither does `edge_J`; the adj_J fall is entirely the node-count penalty on 2.8% more nodes. The extra detections admitted by a lower gate are not the missing endpoints of the ~180 unreachable GT edges — those cells are not peaks in the heatmap at any threshold down to 0.95. The deflation story was wrong on arithmetic: the negative loss term weighs ~2.4e-8 per unannotated voxel.
- Conclusion: the detection ceiling is set by the model's output, not by the threshold. The remaining direction is a better detector, i.e. training.

## 2026-08-20 candidate cache

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: 12-dataset `6bba` holdout, dump threshold 0.05.
- Experiment: `cache_candidates.py` (single GPU inference dumping coords/edges/probs at threshold 0.05), `link_replay.py` (CPU replay; Kaggle entry `run_sweep.py`), `stranded_audit.py`. One 12-dataset pass: 154 s CPU vs 11 min GPU.
- Result:
  - Cache verified faithful: replaying the submitted config reproduces TP/FP/FN 9863/318/450 and adj_J 0.9269 digit for digit.
  - Correction — 0.9953/0.9530 was the greedy decomposition:

| | detect_ceiling | link_rate |
|---|---|---|
| as previously recorded | 0.9953 | 0.9530 |
| ILP+A, measured | 0.9823 | 0.9736 |

  ILP gives up detection reach (the solver discards nodes) to buy linking. Detection's share of the loss is 1.8%, not 0.5% (corrected 2026-08-20; earlier text said 0.5%) — still linking-dominated, but 3.5x the earlier figure.
  - Stranded targets: candidates above 0.5 = 167,398 (everything the submission ever saw); above 0.05 = 338,781 (2.02x); targets = 189,872, of which 22,474 (11.8%) have no candidate above 0.5 — structural false negatives. The softmax normalises over sources, so at most one parent per target can exceed 0.5.
  - Stranded fraction correlates with over-detection (`N/N_true` r=+0.79), not density (r=-0.07). The earlier "density is the primary failure axis" holds for the score, not for this mechanism: a spurious detection has no true parent, its column mass spreads, nothing clears 0.5.
  - Counted with `stranded_audit.py`:
    1. Stranded targets are disproportionately spurious: GT-match rate 1.5% vs 6.1% for confident targets (ratio 0.24, holds in all 12 datasets). Most of the 22,474 should stay unlinked.
    2. 278 of the 450 edge FNs (62%) are real edges stuck behind the 0.5 gate (27 more have an undetected target). Recovering all 278 at F new FPs: +0.026 at F=0, break-even near F=300; the pool holds 22,196 spurious targets, so the real edges are 1.2% of it. Whether it pays depends entirely on ILP selectivity.
    3. Prediction for the 2-D sweep: the winning cell pairs a lower threshold with a lower disappearance weight.
  - `SUPERSEDED 2026-08-21`: the det-threshold knob was swept and is dead as a lever (see 2026-08-21 det-threshold sweep); the over-detection problem stands, but its fix is a better detector, not the threshold.
- Conclusion: the cache makes linking experiments a 154 s CPU replay and reproduces the submitted config exactly. Detection's loss share is 1.8%. 11.8% of targets are structurally unlinkable at the 0.5 gate, but only 278 recoverable real edges hide in that pool.

## 2026-08-20 edge threshold is the binding constraint

- Hypothesis: the edge-candidate gate `threshold=0.5`, with softmax normalisation over sources, is what limits the linker.
- Scope: read from `scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py` (defaults in `reference.md#running-the-official-pipeline`); mechanism read from code, not from the holdout.
- Experiment: code read plus the subsequent threshold x disappearance sweep.
- Result:
  - The gate is the only limit on what the linker sees, and the softmax normalises over sources. A target whose column mass splits between two plausible parents (~0.5/0.5) gets no candidate edge at all.
  - The mechanism predicted, before measurement: the 60% `DROPPED` failure bucket, `corr(edge J, true density) = -0.68`, the densest movie being worst, and detect_ceiling >> link_rate.
  - Arithmetic headroom: the counted recoverable number is 278 edges, +0.026 max at zero cost (corrected 2026-08-20 by the stranded audit; earlier text said up to +0.041 if every dropped edge recovers and retires an FP).
  - Consequences that stand: sweep `threshold` x `disappearance_weight` together (parameters interact; appearance 0.0 / disappearance 1.5 biases towards linking); forks stay impossible throughout (would need edge_prob > 1.0), so the sweep is safe for the division term; `sweep_edge_threshold.py`'s greedy-only monotonicity argument does not transfer to ILP, hence the candidate cache instead of geff replays.
  - The sweep landed at threshold 0.40 / disappearance 3.5 -> local 0.9387. [Recorded 2026-08-21 alongside the det sweep.]
- Conclusion: the 0.5 edge-candidate gate under source-normalised softmax is the binding constraint on the linker, and it explains the density-correlated failures.

Operationally, local scores are for paired deltas only.

The true fork over-prediction factor is unknown (corrected 2026-08-20; earlier text claimed 18x over-prediction, which was circular — 220 = 6+214, never counted from the graph; the metric only sees matched forks). - Conclusion: LB 0.876, up from 0.681 for the classical DoG pipeline, with local 0.9269 on the 12-dataset holdout. The local-to-LB offset is 0.051 with three unseparated causes. Division weight 0.3 loses 8:1 on adj_J, so the default stays at 1.0 and no forks are emitted.

## 2026-08-18 ILP linking pilot

- Hypothesis: ILP linking beats greedy at matched weights.
- Scope: 3 datasets (`3abfe10a`, `2312ac41`, `aeee7805`), paired, same weights, det 0.99.
- Experiment: config sweep over `--use-ilp` and the appearance/disappearance weights.
- Result:

| config | edge J | adj_J | penalty | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy | 0.8956 | 0.8826 | 0.0130 | 0.8857 |
| `--use-ilp` | 0.9150 | 0.9073 | 0.0077 | 0.9073 |
| + app 0.0, disapp 1.5 | 0.9183 | 0.9152 | 0.0031 | 0.9152 |
| + division-weight 0.3 | 0.8999 | 0.8907 | 0.0092 | 0.8937 |
| + disapp 3.0 | 0.9097 | 0.9120 | -0.0023 | 0.9120 |

  Most of the gain is the node-count penalty, not edge J: high disappearance cost makes the solver prefer long tracks and discard scattered nodes (n_pred -12%). At disapp 3.0 the penalty goes negative (n_pred < n_true; the formula has no upper clamp) but node_recall pays more.
- Conclusion: ILP with appearance 0.0 / disappearance 1.5 gains +0.0295 over greedy on this pilot. The disappearance optimum is near 1.5 and the curve is flat.

## 2026-08-18 scorer bug

- Hypothesis: —
- Scope: local scorer vs `tracking_cellmot/metrics.py::_evaluate_matched_graph`; re-measurement on 24 classical-pipeline datasets.
- Experiment: code read of the real scorer, then re-scoring.
- Result:
  - Real rule: an edge counts toward the denominator iff either endpoint matched a GT node of the right degree. Ours required both. Measured on 24 classical-pipeline datasets: FP 2 -> 289; 99.3% of false positives were invisible.
  - Also implemented from the real scorer: t+1-only edges, merge collapse, out-degree cap 2. Full metric rules: `reference.md#the-metric`.
  - Every local number from before 2026-08-18 is void (produced by the broken scorer). In particular the old "0.916 pipeline scores 0.9614 locally" is void.
  - Re-measured on the classical pipeline with the corrected scorer: over-detection still wins (adj_J rising through ratio 2.8 at N_pred/N_true 0.94 — the DoG detector runs out of candidates; `nms_um` is its real lever).
- Conclusion: a missed detection costs twice (FN plus induced FP), so detection recall is worth more than pre-fix measurements implied — consistent with the official U-Net (recall 0.997) beating DoG (0.70) by more than recall alone suggests.
